atrocities-act-2018-arrest-fight-timelin.en:
In 2015 Parliament strengthened the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act. In 2018 a Supreme Court ruling made it harder to use at the police station. Within months Parliament amended the Act to undo the ruling's changes, with a bill that cleared both Houses in under a week. Each side spoke the language of rights: the right of Dalit and Adivasi citizens to protection, and the right of accused people not to be arrested on a false complaint. Here is what changed, and what the case data say. This is general information, not legal advice.

## 2015: rewriting the Act

- **4 August 2015:** the Lok Sabha passes an amendment bill.
- **21 December 2015:** the Rajya Sabha passes it.
- **31 December 2015:** it receives the President's assent and becomes Act No. 1 of 2016 [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]].

The amendment made sexual touching, and sexual words or gestures, towards a Dalit or Adivasi woman by someone who knows her caste a specific atrocity, punishable with six months to five years. It also built deadlines and duties around the stages where cases stall [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]]:

- **Courts:** states must set up Exclusive Special Courts that hear cases day to day and, as far as possible, finish trials within two months of the charge sheet.
- **Police:** a public servant who is not SC or ST and wilfully neglects duties under the Act, including filing a charge sheet within 60 days, faces six months to one year in prison.
- **Victims:** a new Section 15A makes protecting victims, their dependants and witnesses from intimidation, coercion, inducement or violence the state's duty, and gives victims a right to timely notice of court proceedings, including bail hearings.

## 2018: the ruling on arrests and enquiries

In 2018 a Supreme Court ruling changed how the Act worked on the ground. It required approval from senior police officers before anyone accused under the Act could be arrested, and allowed a preliminary enquiry before an FIR was registered [[prs-sc-st-poa-amendment-bill-2018]].

The case for safeguards like these rests on an argument that has followed the Act for years: that it can be used to settle personal or political scores, and that an arrest can wreck an innocent person's life before any court has weighed the evidence. That worry is legitimate for any criminal law.

For the people the Act is meant to protect, the same safeguards looked very different. A preliminary enquiry before an FIR means delay at the moment a complainant is most exposed, sometimes in a village where the accused's family controls land, work and credit. Waiting for senior approval before an arrest means the man she has named may stay next door in the meantime. And the first judgement on whether her complaint even deserves an FIR rests with the same police she may already distrust.

## August 2018: Parliament's reply

- **3 August 2018:** the government introduces an amendment bill.
- **6 August 2018:** the Lok Sabha passes it.
- **9 August 2018:** the Rajya Sabha passes it [[prs-sc-st-poa-amendment-bill-2018]].

The bill inserted a new Section 18A with three plain statements. No preliminary enquiry is required to register an FIR. The investigating officer needs no one's approval to arrest an accused person. And the Act's bar on anticipatory bail, meaning bail before arrest, applies "notwithstanding any judgment or order or direction of any Court" [[prs-sc-st-poa-amendment-bill-2018]].

This timeline follows the text Parliament passed. Before relying on it in a real case, check the current position with a lawyer or free legal aid.

## What the case data say about 'misuse'

If the Act were mostly a tool for false complaints, police investigations would close most cases without charges. They do not. In 2023 police filed charge sheets in 81.2% of the cases of crimes against Scheduled Castes that they disposed of, and in 88.1% of rape cases with SC victims [[ncrb-cii-2023-vol2]]. A charge sheet means police, after investigating, found enough material to send the accused for trial. The rate covers cases police finished that year, not every case registered.

| Year | Crimes against Scheduled Castes registered |
|---|---|
| 2020 | 50,291 |
| 2021 | 50,900 |
| 2022 | 57,582 |
| 2023 | 57,789 |
| 2024 | 55,698 |

Registrations rose every year to 2023 before dipping in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Rising numbers can reflect more crime, more reporting or better policing; on their own, they settle nothing about misuse.

The real weak point is the courts. In 2023 only 31.9% of completed atrocity trials ended in conviction, and 3,11,986 cases, 93.8% of the 3,32,606 before the courts, were still pending at the year's end [[ncrb-cii-2023-vol2]]. That collides head-on with the 2015 promise of trials within two months. Low conviction rates are often quoted as proof of misuse. But an acquittal means a charge was not proved in court, not that the complaint was invented, and years of delay give hostile witnesses, pressure and fading evidence time to work.

## What it means for a survivor deciding to complain

Imagine a 24-year-old Dalit woman in a Rajasthan village in 2018, while the ruling was in force. A dominant-caste neighbour has made sexual remarks at her for months, and one evening he touches her sexually at the handpump. Her complaint could first go to a preliminary enquiry, and his arrest would wait for a senior officer's sign-off while he stayed next door. Under the text Parliament passed, police need no enquiry to register her FIR and no one's approval to arrest him, and the Act's bar on anticipatory bail applies whatever any court has said [[prs-sc-st-poa-amendment-bill-2018]].

For her, the fight over the Act was never abstract. Whether a man can be arrested quickly can decide whether she must face him, and his family, every day while her case moves. That is why arrest rules matter as much as punishments. It is also why the biggest unkept promise now sits in the courtroom: a trial within two months, in a system where 93.8% of atrocity cases before the courts in 2023 were still waiting for a verdict at the year's end [[ncrb-cii-2023-vol2]].
atrocities-act-2018-arrest-fight-timelin.hg:
2015 mein Parliament ne SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act ko mazboot kiya. 2018 mein Supreme Court ke ek faisle ne thane ke level par iska istemaal mushkil bana diya. Kuch hi mahinon mein Parliament ne Act mein amendment karke us faisle ke badlaav khatam kar diye, ek aise bill se jo ek hafte se bhi kam mein dono Houses se paas ho gaya. Dono taraf haq ki baat thi: Dalit aur Adivasi naagrikon ka hifaazat ka haq, aur accused logon ka yeh haq ki unhe kisi jhoothi complaint par arrest na kiya jaaye. Kya badla, aur case data kya kehta hai, yahan dekhiye. Yeh general jaankari hai, legal advice nahi.

## 2015: Act ko naye sire se likha gaya

- **4 August 2015:** Lok Sabha ne amendment bill paas kiya.
- **21 December 2015:** Rajya Sabha ne use paas kiya.
- **31 December 2015:** President ki manzoori mili aur yeh Act No. 1 of 2016 bana [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]].

Amendment ne kisi Dalit ya Adivasi aurat ki caste jaante hue use sexual tareeke se chhoone, ya uski taraf sexual shabd ya ishaare karne ko ek specific atrocity bana diya, jiski sazaa chhah mahine se paanch saal tak hai. Saath hi, jin stages par cases atakte hain, wahan deadlines aur zimmedaariyan bhi tay ki gayin [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]]:

- **Courts:** states ko Exclusive Special Courts banani hain jo roz sunwaai karein aur, jahan tak mumkin ho, charge sheet ke do mahine ke andar trial khatam karein.
- **Police:** jo public servant SC ya ST nahi hai aur Act ke tahat apni duties mein jaanbujhkar laaparwahi karta hai, jaise 60 din ke andar charge sheet file na karna, use chhah mahine se ek saal tak ki jail ho sakti hai.
- **Victims:** nayi Section 15A ke tahat victims, unke dependants aur gawaahon ko dhamki, zabardasti, laalach aur hinsa se bachana state ki zimmedaari hai, aur victims ko bail hearings samet har court proceeding ki samay par jaankari paane ka haq hai.

## 2018: arrest aur enquiry par faisla

2018 mein Supreme Court ke ek faisle ne zameen par Act ke kaam karne ka tareeka badal diya. Isne kaha ki Act ke tahat kisi accused ko arrest karne se pehle senior police officers ki manzoori zaroori hogi, aur FIR darj hone se pehle preliminary enquiry ki ijaazat di [[prs-sc-st-poa-amendment-bill-2018]].

Aise safeguards ke paksh mein woh tark diya jaata hai jo saalon se is Act ke saath chalta aaya hai: ki ise personal ya political hisaab chukaane ke liye istemaal kiya ja sakta hai, aur ki ek arrest kisi begunaah ki zindagi court ke saboot dekhne se pehle hi barbaad kar sakta hai. Yeh chinta kisi bhi criminal law ke liye jaayaz hai.

Jin logon ki hifaazat ke liye yeh Act bana hai, unke liye yahi safeguards bilkul alag dikhe. FIR se pehle preliminary enquiry ka matlab hai deri, theek us waqt jab complaint karne wala sabse zyada asurakshit hota hai, kabhi-kabhi ek aise gaon mein jahan accused ke parivaar ke haath mein zameen, kaam aur karz sab hota hai. Arrest se pehle senior manzoori ka intezaar matlab jis aadmi ka usne naam liya, woh tab tak bagal wale ghar mein hi reh sakta hai. Aur uski complaint FIR ke laayak hai ya nahi, iska pehla faisla usi police ke haath mein rehta hai jis par shayad use pehle se bharosa nahi.

## August 2018: Parliament ka jawaab

- **3 August 2018:** sarkaar ne amendment bill pesh kiya.
- **6 August 2018:** Lok Sabha ne use paas kiya.
- **9 August 2018:** Rajya Sabha ne use paas kiya [[prs-sc-st-poa-amendment-bill-2018]].

Bill ne ek nayi Section 18A jodi, jismein teen seedhi baatein hain. FIR darj karne ke liye koi preliminary enquiry zaroori nahi. Investigating officer ko kisi accused ko arrest karne ke liye kisi ki manzoori nahi chahiye. Aur Act mein anticipatory bail, yaani arrest se pehle ki bail, par jo rok hai, woh "notwithstanding any judgment or order or direction of any Court", yaani kisi bhi court ke kisi bhi faisle, order ya nirdesh ke bawajood laagu rahegi [[prs-sc-st-poa-amendment-bill-2018]].

Yeh timeline Parliament ke paas kiye text par chalti hai. Kisi asli case mein iske bharose kadam uthaane se pehle, kisi lawyer ya free legal aid se aaj ki legal sthiti zaroor check kijiye.

## 'Misuse' ke baare mein case data kya kehta hai

Agar yeh Act zyada tar jhoothi complaints ka hathiyaar hota, toh police ki jaanch zyada tar cases ko bina charge ke band kar deti. Aisa nahi hota. 2023 mein police ne Scheduled Castes ke khilaaf crimes ke jo cases nipataaye, unmein se 81.2% mein charge sheet file ki, aur SC victims wale rape cases mein 88.1% mein [[ncrb-cii-2023-vol2]]. Charge sheet ka matlab hai ki police ko khud jaanch ke baad accused ko trial par bhejne laayak saamagri mili. Yeh rate us saal police ke nipataaye cases par hai, har darj case par nahi.

| Saal | Scheduled Castes ke khilaaf darj crimes |
|---|---|
| 2020 | 50,291 |
| 2021 | 50,900 |
| 2022 | 57,582 |
| 2023 | 57,789 |
| 2024 | 55,698 |

2023 tak har saal registrations badhe, phir 2024 mein thode ghate [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Badhte numbers zyada crime, zyada reporting ya behtar policing, kisi ki bhi wajah se ho sakte hain; akele yeh numbers misuse ke baare mein kuch tay nahi karte.

Asli kamzori courts mein hai. 2023 mein atrocity ke poore hue trials mein se sirf 31.9% mein sazaa hui, aur courts ke saamne maujood 3,32,606 cases mein se 3,11,986, yaani 93.8%, saal ke aakhir tak pending the [[ncrb-cii-2023-vol2]]. Yeh 2015 ke do mahine mein trial ke vaade se seedha takraata hai. Kam conviction rate ko aksar misuse ka saboot bataya jaata hai. Lekin acquittal ka matlab hai ki court mein charge saabit nahi hua, yeh nahi ki complaint gadhi gayi thi, aur saalon ki deri gawaahon ke mukarne, dabaav aur dhundhle padte saboot ko kaam karne ka poora waqt deti hai.

## Complaint karne ka soch rahi survivor ke liye iska matlab

Sochiye, 2018 mein, jab woh faisla laagu tha, Rajasthan ke ek gaon mein 24 saal ki ek Dalit aurat hai. Ek dominant-caste padosi mahinon se us par sexual comments karta aa raha hai, aur ek shaam handpump par use sexual tareeke se chhoota hai. Uski complaint pehle preliminary enquiry mein ja sakti thi, aur uske arrest ke liye kisi senior officer ki manzoori ka intezaar hota, jabki woh bagal wale ghar mein hi rehta. Parliament ke paas kiye text ke mutaabik, uski FIR darj karne ke liye police ko kisi enquiry ki zaroorat nahi, use arrest karne ke liye kisi ki manzoori nahi chahiye, aur Act mein anticipatory bail par jo rok hai, woh kisi bhi court ke faisle ke bawajood laagu hai [[prs-sc-st-poa-amendment-bill-2018]].

Uske liye Act par yeh ladaai kabhi kitaabi nahi thi. Kisi aadmi ko jaldi arrest kiya ja sakta hai ya nahi, isi se tay ho sakta hai ki case chalte waqt use roz us aadmi aur uske parivaar ka saamna karna padega ya nahi. Isiliye arrest ke niyam utne hi maayne rakhte hain jitni sazaayein. Aur isiliye sabse bada adhoora vaada ab courtroom mein hai: do mahine mein trial, ek aise system mein jahan 2023 mein courts ke saamne maujood atrocity cases mein se 93.8% saal ke aakhir tak faisle ka intezaar kar rahe the [[ncrb-cii-2023-vol2]].

atrocities-act-sexual-offences-dalit-adi.en:
Imagine a 22-year-old Dalit woman who cleans a school in a small town in Madhya Pradesh. Every morning a man at the gate makes sexual remarks at her, and drops her caste into them. Under ordinary criminal law, that is sexual harassment. Under a 2015 amendment to the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, it can also be a specific atrocity, with its own punishment of six months to five years in prison and a fine [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]]. Here is what that amendment added, clause by clause. It is general information, not legal advice.

## Why a separate law for caste atrocities

The general law already punishes harassment. The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), in force since 1 July 2024, punishes sexual harassment with up to three years (up to one year for sexually coloured remarks), and words or gestures insulting a woman's modesty with up to three years [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. So why another law?

Because some sexual violence is not only about one man and one woman. It is about putting a woman, and her whole community, back in a "place" someone else has decided for them. The Supreme Court said this plainly in its 2023 handbook on gender stereotypes: "Dominant caste men have historically used sexual violence as a tool to reinforce and maintain caste hierarchies" [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

The Atrocities Act names that caste element. Its offences apply to people who are not themselves from a Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]]. They add to the BNS rather than replacing it, so one complaint can carry sections from both laws. The Act also brings extra duties for police.

## Section 3(1)(w): touch, words and gestures

The clause has two parts [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]]:

- **Touch.** Intentionally touching a Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe woman, knowing that she belongs to that community, when the touching is sexual in nature and without her consent.
- **Words, acts or gestures.** Using words, acts or gestures of a sexual nature towards such a woman, again knowing her caste or tribe.

Both carry six months to five years in prison and a fine. Two details matter. First, the offender must know her caste or tribe. In many places a surname alone signals caste, but that knowledge still has to be shown. Second, the clause does not require any injury or physical struggle. A sexual comment called out across a field can fall within it.

What the clause does not cover is rape itself. Rape is punished under Section 64 of the BNS, with at least 10 years' rigorous imprisonment and up to life [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Section 3(1)(w) is for the everyday harassment that many women are told to ignore.

## Devadasi dedication as an atrocity

Section 3(1)(k) makes it an atrocity to perform or promote the dedication of a Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe woman to a deity, idol, temple or other religious institution as a devadasi, "or any other similar practice", or to permit it [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]]. Like the rest of Section 3(1), it is punishable with six months to five years and a fine.

The wording is wide. It reaches the person who performs the ritual, the relative or elder who promotes it, and the person who allows it to happen. It covers "similar" practices under other names, so changing the label does not open a loophole. The practice is often presented as devotion. The law's position is plain: the dedication itself is the crime, whatever it is called, and any sexual exploitation that follows is a further crime under the general law.

## Consent defined: not resisting is not a yes

For the touching offence, the amendment defines consent as "an unequivocal voluntary agreement": clear, freely given agreement [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]]. Then it closes two old escape routes:

- A Dalit or Adivasi woman who does not physically resist a sexual act is not, for that reason alone, to be treated as consenting.
- Her sexual history, including with the accused, does not imply consent or reduce the offence.

These lines matter because of who usually holds power in the room. A woman who works on a dominant-caste landowner's field, or whose family owes him money, may freeze, stay quiet or force a smile to get through the moment. The proviso exists so that silence of that kind cannot be read as a yes. The same handbook lists, as a stereotype judges must reject, the belief that dominant-caste men would not want sex with oppressed-caste women and that their complaints must therefore be false [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

## Where these crimes are recorded most

Police registered 55,698 crimes against Scheduled Castes in 2024, 3.6% fewer than the 57,789 of 2023, a rate of 27.7 per lakh SC population. Rape made up 7.6% of them, 4,262 cases with Scheduled Caste victims, a count that also includes child victims [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. In 2023 Uttar Pradesh registered the most cases, 15,130, but the highest rates were in Madhya Pradesh, at 72.6 per lakh SC population, and Rajasthan, at 69.1, more than double the national rate of 28.7 [[ncrb-cii-2023-vol2]]. The Act protects Adivasi women too: police registered 1,268 rape cases with Scheduled Tribe victims in 2024, 12.7% of the 9,966 crimes against Scheduled Tribes recorded that year [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Read these numbers as a floor. NCRB counts a crime as an atrocity only when police invoke the Atrocities Act; if an officer registers harassment under the BNS alone, it vanishes from the caste tables [[ncrb-cii-2023-vol2]]. A high state rate can also mean more women are coming forward and more stations are using the Act. NCRB itself cautions against ranking states on crime figures alone.

The practical lesson: the sections written into the FIR decide which protections follow. Under Section 4 of the Act, a public servant who is not SC or ST and wilfully neglects duties under it, such as registering the FIR under the correct sections or filing a charge sheet within 60 days, faces six months to one year in prison [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]]. Ask for the right sections on day one, in writing, and if that feels impossible alone, District Legal Services Authorities offer free legal aid [[nalsa]].
atrocities-act-sexual-offences-dalit-adi.hg:
Sochiye, Madhya Pradesh ke ek chhote shehar mein 22 saal ki ek Dalit aurat ek school mein safai ka kaam karti hai. Har subah gate par khada ek aadmi us par sexual comments karta hai, aur unmein uski caste ka zikr bhi daal deta hai. Aam criminal law mein yeh sexual harassment hai. Lekin SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act mein 2015 ke amendment ke tahat, yeh ek specific atrocity bhi ho sakti hai, jiski apni sazaa hai: chhah mahine se paanch saal tak ki jail aur jurmaana [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]]. Ek-ek clause karke dekhiye ki us amendment ne kya joda. Yeh general jaankari hai, legal advice nahi.

## Caste atrocities ke liye alag kaanoon kyun

General law pehle se harassment ki sazaa deta hai. 1 July 2024 se laagu Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) mein sexual harassment ke liye teen saal tak ki sazaa hai (sexually coloured remarks ke liye ek saal tak), aur kisi aurat ki modesty ka apmaan karne wale shabdon ya ishaaron ke liye bhi teen saal tak [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Toh phir ek aur kaanoon kyun?

Kyunki kuch sexual violence sirf ek aadmi aur ek aurat ke beech ka maamla nahi hota. Uska maqsad hota hai aurat ko, aur uski poori community ko, us "jagah" par wapas dhakelna jo kisi aur ne unke liye tay kar rakhi hai. Supreme Court ne 2023 ki apni gender stereotypes wali handbook mein yeh seedhe shabdon mein kaha: "Dominant caste men have historically used sexual violence as a tool to reinforce and maintain caste hierarchies", yaani dominant caste ke aadmiyon ne itihaas mein sexual violence ko caste ki oonch-neech banaye rakhne ke hathiyaar ki tarah istemaal kiya hai [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

Atrocities Act isi caste wale pehlu ko naam deta hai. Iske offences un logon par laagu hote hain jo khud Scheduled Caste ya Scheduled Tribe se nahi hain [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]]. Yeh BNS ki jagah nahi lete, uske upar judte hain, isliye ek hi complaint mein dono kaanoonon ke sections lag sakte hain. Act lagne se police par extra zimmedaariyan bhi aati hain.

## Section 3(1)(w): chhoona, shabd aur ishaare

Is clause ke do hisse hain [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]]:

- **Chhoona.** Kisi Scheduled Caste ya Scheduled Tribe aurat ko jaanbujhkar chhoona, yeh jaante hue ki woh us community se hai, jab woh chhoona sexual nature ka ho aur uski marzi ke bina ho.
- **Shabd, harkatein ya ishaare.** Aisi aurat ki taraf sexual nature ke shabd, harkatein ya ishaare karna, phir se yeh jaante hue ki woh kis caste ya tribe se hai.

Dono ke liye chhah mahine se paanch saal tak ki jail aur jurmaana hai. Do baatein dhyaan dene wali hain. Pehli, offender ko uski caste ya tribe pata honi chahiye. Kai jagah sirf surname se caste pata chal jaati hai, lekin yeh jaankari phir bhi dikhaani padti hai. Doosri, is clause ke liye na koi chot zaroori hai, na koi physical khinchataani. Khet ke us paar se chillaya gaya ek sexual comment bhi iske daayre mein aa sakta hai.

Yeh clause rape ko cover nahi karta. Rape ki sazaa BNS ki Section 64 mein hai: kam se kam 10 saal ki kathor kaid aur umrqaid tak [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Section 3(1)(w) us roz ke harassment ke liye hai jise kai auraton ko "ignore karo" bolkar taal diya jaata hai.

## Devadasi dedication bhi atrocity hai

Section 3(1)(k) ke tahat kisi Scheduled Caste ya Scheduled Tribe aurat ko devta, murti, mandir ya kisi aur dhaarmik sanstha ke naam par devadasi ke roop mein "dedicate" karna, "or any other similar practice", yaani koi bhi milti-julti pratha, karna ya uska prachaar karna, ya aisa hone dena, atrocity hai [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]]. Section 3(1) ke baaki hisson ki tarah, iski sazaa bhi chhah mahine se paanch saal aur jurmaana hai.

Shabd khule rakhe gaye hain. Yeh us vyakti tak pahunchte hain jo rasm karwata hai, us rishtedaar ya bade-buzurg tak jo iska prachaar karta hai, aur us vyakti tak bhi jo ise hone deta hai. Isme doosre naamon wali "milti-julti" prathayein bhi aati hain, taaki sirf naam badal dene se koi loophole na ban jaaye. Is pratha ko aksar bhakti bataya jaata hai. Kaanoon ka stand saaf hai: dedication khud crime hai, use kuch bhi naam do, aur uske baad jo bhi sexual exploitation ho, woh general law ke tahat ek aur alag crime hai.

## Consent ki definition: virodh na karna 'haan' nahi hai

Chhoone wale offence ke liye amendment consent ko "an unequivocal voluntary agreement" kehta hai, yaani saaf aur apni marzi se di gayi sehmati [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]]. Phir yeh do purane bachaav ke raaste band kar deta hai:

- Jo Dalit ya Adivasi aurat kisi sexual harkat ka physically virodh nahi karti, use sirf isi wajah se raazi nahi maana jaayega.
- Uski sexual history, accused ke saath bhi, consent saabit nahi karti aur offence ko halka nahi karti.

Yeh lines isliye zaroori hain kyunki kamre mein power aksar kiske haath mein hoti hai, yeh sab jaante hain. Jo aurat kisi dominant-caste zameendaar ke khet mein kaam karti hai, ya jiske parivaar par uska karz hai, woh us pal ko kisi tarah guzaarne ke liye jam sakti hai, chup reh sakti hai ya zabardasti muskura sakti hai. Yeh proviso isi liye hai ki aisi chuppi ko 'haan' na samjha jaaye. Wahi handbook ek aur stereotype ko reject karne ko kehti hai: yeh maanna ki dominant-caste aadmi oppressed-caste auraton ke saath sex chahte hi nahi, isliye unki complaints jhoothi hongi [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

## Yeh crimes sabse zyada kahan darj hote hain

2024 mein police ne Scheduled Castes ke khilaaf 55,698 crimes darj kiye, jo 2023 ke 57,789 se 3.6% kam the; yaani har lakh SC aabaadi par 27.7 cases. Inmein se 7.6%, yaani 4,262, Scheduled Caste victims wale rape cases the, aur is ginti mein bachche victims bhi shaamil hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. 2023 mein sabse zyada cases Uttar Pradesh mein darj hue, 15,130, lekin sabse oonche rates Madhya Pradesh mein the, har lakh SC aabaadi par 72.6, aur Rajasthan mein, 69.1. Dono national rate 28.7 ke do guna se bhi zyada hain [[ncrb-cii-2023-vol2]]. Yeh Act Adivasi auraton ki bhi hifaazat karta hai: 2024 mein police ne Scheduled Tribe victims wale 1,268 rape cases darj kiye, jo us saal Scheduled Tribes ke khilaaf darj 9,966 crimes ka 12.7% the [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

In numbers ko neeche ki seema samjhiye, poori tasveer nahi. NCRB kisi crime ko atrocity tabhi ginta hai jab police Atrocities Act lagaati hai; agar koi officer harassment ko sirf BNS mein darj kare, toh woh caste wali tables se gayab ho jaata hai [[ncrb-cii-2023-vol2]]. Kisi state ka oonchha rate yeh bhi dikha sakta hai ki wahan zyada auratein aage aa rahi hain aur zyada thane Act ka istemaal kar rahe hain. NCRB khud kehta hai ki states ko sirf crime figures se rank na kiya jaaye.

Practical seekh yeh hai: FIR mein kaun se sections likhe gaye, isi se tay hota hai ki aage kaun si hifaazat milegi. Act ki Section 4 ke tahat, jo public servant SC ya ST nahi hai aur is Act ke tahat apni duties mein jaanbujhkar laaparwahi karta hai, jaise sahi sections ke saath FIR darj na karna ya 60 din ke andar charge sheet file na karna, use chhah mahine se ek saal tak ki jail ho sakti hai [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]]. Pehle hi din, likhit mein, sahi sections maangiye. Agar akele yeh mushkil lage, toh District Legal Services Authorities free legal aid deti hain [[nalsa]].

campus-harassment-nep-2020-colleges.en:
Imagine a second-year student at a college in Nagpur. The lab instructor who signs off her internal marks has started messaging her at midnight. She does not know whether her college has a complaints committee, who sits on it, or whether it would hear a student at all.

Two documents say she should not have to guess: the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 and a Supreme Court judgment of 12 May 2023. Here is what they give her, and the young guest lecturer down the corridor. This is general information, not legal advice.

## What does NEP 2020 promise on gender and harassment?

Three things. It names girls and transgender students among its "Socio-Economically Disadvantaged Groups". It commits the Government of India to constitute a "Gender-Inclusion Fund" for girls and transgender students. And it asks all higher education institutions to sensitise faculty, counsellors and students on gender identity and to "strictly enforce all no-discrimination and anti-harassment rules" [[nep-2020-full-text]].

NEP is a policy, not a statute. It sets up no committee, no deadline and no penalty, and in its 66 pages it does not once use the word "sexual" [[nep-2020-full-text]]. The rules it wants enforced come from elsewhere, chiefly the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013 (the POSH Act).

## Does my college need a complaints committee?

Yes, because a college is an employer. The POSH Act requires every employer to constitute an Internal Complaints Committee, and its definition of a workplace expressly includes private organisations carrying on "educational" activities. An employer that fails to set one up can be fined up to Rs 50,000, with double the punishment on a repeat [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].

Whether that committee hears students is the question to put in writing. The Act protects any woman "of any age whether employed or not" who alleges sexual harassment at a workplace [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. On those words she need not be on the payroll: a student, a research scholar and a guest lecturer are all women at that workplace. Ask the principal or registrar which committee hears a student, and under which rules.

The Act is written for women. NEP names transgender students as a disadvantaged group, yet the statute spells out no committee route for transgender or male students. They depend on the college's own policy and, for crimes, on the police. Sexual abuse of a transgender person is an offence under Section 18 of the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019, punishable with 6 months to 2 years in prison and a fine [[indiacode-transgender-persons-2019]].

## Who sits on it, and how fast must it act?

The presiding officer must be a woman employed at a senior level. There must be at least two employee members and one external member, from an NGO or someone familiar with sexual harassment issues. At least half the members must be women [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. The outsider matters on a campus, where everyone else on the committee may answer to the same principal.

The Act also sets the clock [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]:

| Step | Time limit |
|---|---|
| Written complaint | within 3 months of the incident, extendable by up to 3 more |
| Inquiry | completed within 90 days |
| Report to the employer | within 10 days |
| Employer acts | within 60 days |
| Appeal | within 90 days |

Set that against a semester. An incident in August has a deadline in November, when internal assessments are due and a student is least likely to challenge the person who marks her.

Two protections are worth knowing. Conciliation can happen only at her request, and never on the basis of a money settlement. And "a mere inability to substantiate a complaint or provide adequate proof need not attract action against the complainant" [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].

## What did the Supreme Court's 'publish it online' order change?

On 12 May 2023 a bench of Justices A.S. Bopanna and Hima Kohli found "serious lapses in the enforcement" of the POSH Act a decade after it was passed, and called it "a sorry state of affairs" [[sc-aureliano-fernandes-2023]].

It issued 11 directions. The Union, states and union territories were to verify whether every ministry, department, public sector undertaking and public body had a properly constituted committee, and to publish each committee's members, contact details and complaint procedure online. The directions also cover universities [[sc-aureliano-fernandes-2023]].

For a student this is a two-minute test. Open the college website and look for names, email IDs, phone numbers and the complaint procedure. If they are missing, that absence is your first piece of information.

Enforcement has been slow. In December 2024 the Court ordered a survey of public and private organisations in every district to see which had Internal Committees [[sc-posh-order-2025-05-21]]. In August 2025 it was told that only the Andaman and Nicobar Islands had completed it [[livelaw-posh-district-survey-2025]].

## If the college does nothing, where do I go next?

Write to the head of the institution and keep a copy. Then go outside.

- **The Local Committee.** Each district's District Officer must set one up for workplaces with fewer than ten workers, or where the complaint is against the employer [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. If the person you are complaining about runs the institution, this is your door.
- **SHe-Box.** The Ministry of Women and Child Development runs an online portal for complaints of sexual harassment at work [[shebox]].
- **The police.** Sexual harassment is a crime under Section 75 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, punishable with up to three years [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Any police station must take the information, whatever the area, and a woman officer must record it [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- **If you are under 18.** Some first-year students are still under 18. Under the POCSO Act, anyone who knows or suspects a sexual offence against a child must report it to the police; heads of institutions who fail to report offences by subordinates face up to one year in jail [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]]. A college cannot keep a minor student's complaint as an internal matter.

The Supreme Court observed that harassed women are often reluctant to report, partly because they do not know whom to approach [[sc-aureliano-fernandes-2023]]. On a campus, the quiet version of quitting a job is changing a guide, dropping an elective or leaving the hostel. NEP's line about strict enforcement becomes real only when students can name their committee. Find yours before you need it.
campus-harassment-nep-2020-colleges.hg:
Socho, Nagpur ke ek college mein second year ki ek student hai. Jo lab instructor uske internal marks sign karta hai, woh ab use aadhi raat ko messages bhejne laga hai. Use nahi pata ki uske college mein complaints committee hai bhi ya nahi, usmein kaun baitha hai, aur kya woh ek student ki baat sunegi bhi.

Do documents kehte hain ki use andaza lagane ki zaroorat nahi honi chahiye: National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 aur Supreme Court ka 12 May 2023 ka judgment. Yahan dekhte hain ki in dono se use, aur corridor ke us paar baithi young guest lecturer ko, asal mein kya milta hai. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## NEP 2020 gender aur harassment par kya promise karti hai?

Teen cheezein. Woh girls aur transgender students ko apne "Socio-Economically Disadvantaged Groups" mein ginti hai. Woh Government of India ki taraf se commitment deti hai ki girls aur transgender students ke liye ek "Gender-Inclusion Fund" banaya jayega. Aur woh sabhi higher education institutions se kehti hai ki faculty, counsellors aur students ko gender identity par sensitise karo aur "strictly enforce all no-discrimination and anti-harassment rules", yaani bhedbhav aur harassment ke khilaf saare rules sakhti se lagu karo [[nep-2020-full-text]].

Par NEP ek policy hai, kanoon nahi. Usmein na koi committee banti hai, na koi deadline hai, na koi penalty. Apne 66 pages mein woh ek baar bhi "sexual" word use nahi karti [[nep-2020-full-text]]. Jin rules ko woh lagu karwana chahti hai, woh kahin aur se aate hain, sabse zyada Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013 se, jise POSH Act kehte hain.

## Kya mere college mein complaints committee hona zaroori hai?

Haan, kyunki college ek employer hai. POSH Act har employer se kehta hai ki Internal Complaints Committee banao, aur Act ki workplace ki definition mein "educational" kaam karne wali private organisations saaf-saaf likhi hain. Jo employer committee nahi banata, us par Rs 50,000 tak ka fine lag sakta hai, aur dobara aisa karne par double saza [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].

Woh committee students ki complaint sunti hai ya nahi, yeh sawaal likhit mein poochna chahiye. Act us har aurat ko protect karta hai jo workplace par sexual harassment ka aarop lagaye, "of any age whether employed or not", yaani kisi bhi umar ki, chahe employed ho ya nahi [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. In words ke hisaab se payroll par hona zaroori nahi: student, research scholar aur guest lecturer, sab us workplace ki women hain. Principal ya registrar se poocho ki student ki complaint kaun si committee sunti hai, aur kin rules ke under.

Yeh Act women ke liye likha gaya hai. NEP transgender students ko disadvantaged group maanti hai, phir bhi is kanoon mein transgender ya male students ke liye committee ka koi rasta likha nahi hai. Unhe college ki apni policy par, aur crime ho toh police par, depend karna padta hai. Transgender person ka sexual abuse, Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019 ke Section 18 ke under offence hai, jiski saza 6 mahine se 2 saal tak ki jail aur fine hai [[indiacode-transgender-persons-2019]].

## Committee mein kaun hota hai, aur use kitni jaldi kaam karna hota hai?

Presiding officer senior level par kaam karne wali ek woman honi chahiye. Employees mein se kam se kam do members hone chahiye, aur ek external member, kisi NGO se ya koi aisa insaan jo sexual harassment ke issues samajhta ho. Kam se kam aadhe members women honi chahiye [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Campus par bahar ka member isliye zaroori hai ki committee ke baaki sab log shayad ek hi principal ko jawab dete hon.

Act ghadi bhi set karta hai [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]:

| Step | Time limit |
|---|---|
| Written complaint | incident ke 3 mahine ke andar; yeh time 3 mahine aur badh sakta hai |
| Inquiry | 90 din ke andar poori |
| Employer ko report | 10 din ke andar |
| Employer ka action | 60 din ke andar |
| Appeal | 90 din ke andar |

Ise ek semester ke saath rakh kar dekho. August mein hue incident ki deadline November mein padti hai, jab internal assessments hote hain aur student us insaan ko challenge karne ki sabse kam himmat kar paati hai jo uske marks deta hai.

Do protections jaan lena kaam aayega. Conciliation sirf tab ho sakta hai jab woh khud maange, aur paise ke settlement ke basis par kabhi nahi. Aur Act kehta hai: "a mere inability to substantiate a complaint or provide adequate proof need not attract action against the complainant". Yaani sirf isliye ki woh complaint saabit nahi kar payi ya poora proof nahi de payi, uske khilaf action nahi banta [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].

## Supreme Court ke 'online publish karo' wale order se kya badla?

12 May 2023 ko Justices A.S. Bopanna aur Hima Kohli ki bench ne paaya ki POSH Act banne ke ek dashak baad bhi uske enforcement mein "serious lapses" hain, aur ise "a sorry state of affairs" kaha [[sc-aureliano-fernandes-2023]].

Court ne 11 directions diye. Union, states aur union territories ko verify karna tha ki har ministry, department, public sector undertaking aur public body mein theek se bani committee hai ya nahi, aur har committee ke members, contact details aur complaint ka procedure online publish karna tha. Yeh directions universities par bhi lagu hote hain [[sc-aureliano-fernandes-2023]].

Student ke liye yeh do minute ka test hai. College ki website kholo aur naam, email IDs, phone numbers aur complaint ka procedure dhundho. Agar yeh sab nahi milta, toh yahi tumhari pehli jaankari hai.

Enforcement dheere chala hai. December 2024 mein Court ne har district mein public aur private organisations ka survey karne ko kaha, yeh dekhne ke liye ki kin mein Internal Committee hai [[sc-posh-order-2025-05-21]]. August 2025 mein Court ko bataya gaya ki sirf Andaman and Nicobar Islands ne yeh survey poora kiya hai [[livelaw-posh-district-survey-2025]].

## Agar college kuch na kare, toh aage kahan jaun?

Institution ke head ko likh kar do aur ek copy apne paas rakho. Phir bahar jao.

- **Local Committee.** Har district ke District Officer ko yeh banani hoti hai, un workplaces ke liye jahan das se kam workers hain ya jahan complaint employer ke hi khilaf hai [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Agar tumhari complaint usi ke khilaf hai jo institution chalata hai, toh tumhara darwaza yahi hai.
- **SHe-Box.** Ministry of Women and Child Development ka online portal, jahan kaam ki jagah par sexual harassment ki complaint ki ja sakti hai [[shebox]].
- **Police.** Sexual harassment, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita ke Section 75 ke under crime hai, jiski saza teen saal tak hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Kisi bhi police station ko, chahe area kisi ka bhi ho, yeh information leni hogi, aur ise ek woman officer record karegi [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- **Agar tum 18 se kam ho.** First year ke kuch students abhi 18 ke nahi hue hote. POCSO Act ke under, jise bhi pata ho ya shak ho ki kisi bachche ke saath sexual offence hua hai, use police ko report karna hi hoga; jo institution heads apne subordinates ke offences report nahi karte, unhe ek saal tak ki jail ho sakti hai [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]]. College kisi minor student ki complaint ko "internal matter" bana kar nahi rakh sakta.

Supreme Court ne kaha tha ki harassment jhelne wali women aksar report karne se hichkichati hain, kuch had tak isliye ki unhe pata hi nahi hota kiske paas jaayein [[sc-aureliano-fernandes-2023]]. Campus par naukri chhodne ka chupchaap wala version hota hai guide badal lena, elective chhod dena ya hostel se nikal jaana. NEP ki "strict enforcement" wali line tabhi sach hoti hai jab students apni committee ka naam le sakein. Zaroorat padne se pehle apni committee dhundh lo.

caste-disability-disbelief-myths-handboo.en:
In 1995 a trial court in Rajasthan acquitted the dominant-caste men accused of the 1992 gang rape of a government social worker from an oppressed caste. One of its stated reasons, as the Supreme Court's 2023 handbook on gender stereotypes records, was that members of a dominant caste would not rape a woman from an oppressed caste [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. The same handbook names that belief for what it is: a stereotype. That belief, and its twin about disabled women, still shape who is believed.

## 1995: a verdict built on a caste belief

The survivor worked in a Rajasthan village for a state programme and had tried to stop a child marriage. In 1992 she filed an FIR saying several dominant-caste men had raped her in retaliation [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. She is not named here.

According to the handbook, the 1995 acquittal observed, among other things, that:

- members of a dominant caste would not rape a woman from an oppressed caste;
- men of different castes would not take part in a gang rape together;
- men aged 60 to 70 could not take part in a gang rape.

None of these is a finding about evidence. Each is a belief about who "would" or "would not" do something. The first does the most damage, because it turns her caste into a reason not to believe her.

On 13 August 1997, in Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan, the Supreme Court named the "alleged brutal gang rape of social worker in a village of Rajasthan" as the petition's "immediate cause" [[sc-vishaka-1997]]. Her case gave working women binding guidelines against harassment. In 2023 the court's own handbook named the belief used to acquit the men she accused.

## 2023: the Supreme Court names the myth

The Handbook on Combating Gender Stereotypes, issued in 2023 with a foreword by Chief Justice D.Y. Chandrachud, was written to help judges stop reasoning from stereotypes about women [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. One entry sets out the caste myth: dominant-caste men do not want sexual relations with oppressed-caste women, so any rape allegation by such a woman against a dominant-caste man is false.

Its answer: "Rape and sexual violence have long been used as a tool of social control. Dominant caste men have historically used sexual violence as a tool to reinforce and maintain caste hierarchies" [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

The myth turns untouchability, the idea that a dominant-caste man avoids contact with a Dalit woman, into proof of innocence. "Social control" means the opposite: violence meant to keep a woman, or her family, in a place someone else has chosen.

## The same myth about disabled women

The handbook names a twin belief: that able-bodied men do not want sex with disabled women, so their complaints against able-bodied men are false. Its reply: able-bodied men may sexually assault or rape disabled women, disability does not lower the likelihood of sexual violence, and some women whose disabilities affect communication are particularly vulnerable [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

Both myths rest on one idea: that rape is about desire, and that some women are too "low" or too "unwanted" to be targets. A woman whose word counts for less is not safer. She is easier to silence.

Under Section 173(1) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), police must record a disabled survivor's complaint at her home or a place she chooses, with an interpreter or special educator, and videograph it [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. The duty dates from a 2013 change to the old Code of Criminal Procedure. Yet in 15 of the 17 rape cases involving disabled women and girls that Human Rights Watch documented in 2018, police and court officials did not follow such accommodation rules [[hrw-invisible-victims-2018]].

## Who gets believed: police, village, court

Consider a 19-year-old Dalit woman with a hearing impairment. She tells her mother that the son of the family whose fields her parents work has assaulted her. In the neighbourhood, people ask why a boy from that family would go near her. At the police station, no interpreter is called and the complaint is written without the Atrocities Act sections, which also erases her from the caste statistics: NCRB counts a crime as an atrocity only when that Act is invoked [[ncrb-cii-2023-vol2]]. In court, she is asked why she did not shout, and about her past.

The law already answers that last line. For the sexual-touching offence under the Atrocities Act, not resisting physically does not by itself mean consent, and a woman's sexual history does not imply it [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]]. The handbook also rejects the beliefs that women are very likely to make false rape allegations and that a delay in reporting means a lie [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. A myth does not need to appear in a judgment to work. It only has to decide who is questioned harder and whose silence looks like consent.

## 1,073 acquittals, 508 convictions: what the record can and cannot show

In 2023, courts acquitted the accused in 1,073 rape cases with Scheduled Caste victims and convicted in 508; another 86 ended in discharge. The conviction rate was 30.5%, and 20,622 cases, 92.3% of those before the courts, were still pending at the year's end [[ncrb-cii-2023-vol2]].

It is tempting to read 1,073 as 1,073 survivors disbelieved because of caste. The record cannot show that. NCRB's tables do not say why a trial ended in acquittal, and acquittals can reflect hostile witnesses, delay, pressure on survivors, weak investigation, or a charge that was not proved. The conviction rate here was in fact higher than the 22.7% for all rape trials completed in India that year [[ncrb-cii-2023]].

What the record does show is a system where most cases age without a verdict, giving doubt and pressure years to work. On disability it is thinner still: of 29,536 rape cases registered in 2024, police recorded only 144 under the aggravated charge for raping a woman with a mental or physical disability [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. When the data cannot see a survivor, the myth about her is harder to challenge.

The 1995 court wrote its belief down, which is why it could be named. The harder task is catching it when nobody writes it down.
caste-disability-disbelief-myths-handboo.hg:
1995 mein Rajasthan ki ek trial court ne un dominant-caste aadmiyon ko bari kar diya jin par 1992 mein ek oppressed caste ki sarkari social worker ke gang rape ka ilzaam tha. Supreme Court ki gender stereotypes par 2023 ki handbook record karti hai ki court ke bataaye kaarnon mein se ek yeh tha ki dominant caste ke log kisi oppressed caste ki aurat ka rape nahi karenge [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. Wahi handbook is soch ko uska sahi naam deti hai: stereotype. Yeh soch, aur disabled auraton ke baare mein iska judwaan myth, aaj bhi tay karte hain ki kis par yakeen kiya jaayega.

## 1995: ek caste wali soch par bana faisla

Survivor Rajasthan ke ek gaon mein ek sarkari programme ke liye kaam karti thi aur usne ek baal vivaah rokne ki koshish ki thi. 1992 mein usne FIR darj karayi ki kai dominant-caste aadmiyon ne badla lene ke liye uska rape kiya [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. Hum yahan uska naam nahi le rahe.

Handbook ke mutaabik, 1995 ke acquittal mein, baaki baaton ke alawa, yeh kaha gaya tha ki:

- dominant caste ke log kisi oppressed caste ki aurat ka rape nahi karenge;
- alag-alag caste ke aadmi milkar gang rape nahi karenge;
- 60 se 70 saal ke aadmi gang rape mein shaamil nahi ho sakte.

Inmein se ek bhi baat saboot par aadhaarit finding nahi hai. Har ek bas ek dhaarna hai ki kaun kya "karega" ya "nahi karega". Pehli baat sabse zyada nuksaan karti hai, kyunki yeh uski caste ko hi us par yakeen na karne ki wajah bana deti hai.

13 August 1997 ko, Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan mein, Supreme Court ne "alleged brutal gang rape of social worker in a village of Rajasthan", yaani Rajasthan ke ek gaon mein ek social worker ke kathit gang rape, ko is petition ka "immediate cause", yaani seedhi wajah, bataya [[sc-vishaka-1997]]. Uske case ki wajah se kaamkaaji auraton ko harassment ke khilaaf binding guidelines mili. 2023 mein court ki apni handbook ne us soch ko naam diya jiske sahaare un aadmiyon ko bari kiya gaya tha jin par usne ilzaam lagaya tha.

## 2023: Supreme Court ne myth ko naam diya

Handbook on Combating Gender Stereotypes 2023 mein Chief Justice D.Y. Chandrachud ke foreword ke saath jaari hui, taaki judges auraton ke baare mein stereotypes par tike tark dena band karein [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. Ek entry caste wala myth saaf likhti hai: dominant-caste aadmi oppressed-caste auraton ke saath sexual rishta nahi chahte, isliye aisi kisi aurat ka kisi dominant-caste aadmi par lagaya gaya rape ka har ilzaam jhootha hai.

Handbook ka jawaab: "Rape and sexual violence have long been used as a tool of social control. Dominant caste men have historically used sexual violence as a tool to reinforce and maintain caste hierarchies." Yaani rape aur sexual violence lambe samay se samaaj ko control karne ka hathiyaar rahe hain, aur dominant caste ke aadmiyon ne caste ki oonch-neech ko banaye rakhne ke liye sexual violence ka istemaal kiya hai [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

Yeh myth chhuachhoot ko, yaani is soch ko ki dominant-caste aadmi Dalit aurat se door rehta hai, begunaahi ka saboot bana deta hai. "Social control" ka matlab iska ulta hai: aisi hinsa jiska maqsad aurat ko, ya uske parivaar ko, us jagah par rakhna hai jo kisi aur ne unke liye chun rakhi hai.

## Disabled auraton ke baare mein wahi myth

Handbook ek judwaan soch ko bhi naam deti hai: ki able-bodied aadmi disabled auraton ke saath sex nahi chahte, isliye able-bodied aadmiyon ke khilaaf unki complaints jhoothi hain. Iska jawaab: able-bodied aadmi disabled auraton par sexual assault ya rape kar sakte hain, disability se sexual violence ki sambhavna kam nahi hoti, aur kuch auratein jinki disability unke baat karne ki kshamta par asar daalti hai, khaas taur par zyada khatre mein hoti hain [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

Dono myths ek hi soch par tike hain: ki rape chahat ka maamla hai, aur kuch auratein itni "neechi" ya itni "unchahi" hain ki unhe koi nishaana nahi banayega. Jis aurat ki baat ki keemat kam aanki jaati hai, woh zyada surakshit nahi hoti. Use chup karaana zyada aasaan hota hai.

Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) ki Section 173(1) ke tahat, police ko disabled survivor ki complaint uske ghar ya uski chuni hui jagah par, interpreter ya special educator ke saath record karni hoti hai, aur uski video recording karni hoti hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Yeh zimmedaari purane Code of Criminal Procedure mein 2013 ke ek badlaav se chali aa rahi hai. Phir bhi 2018 mein Human Rights Watch ne disabled auraton aur ladkiyon ke rape ke jo 17 cases document kiye, unmein se 15 mein police aur court ke officials ne aisi suvidhaaon wale niyamon ka paalan nahi kiya [[hrw-invisible-victims-2018]].

## Kis par yakeen hota hai: police, gaon, court

Sochiye, 19 saal ki ek Dalit aurat hai jise sunne mein dikkat hai. Woh apni maa ko batati hai ki jis parivaar ke kheton mein uske maa-baap kaam karte hain, usi parivaar ke bete ne us par hamla kiya. Mohalle mein log poochhte hain ki us parivaar ka ladka uske paas kyun jaayega. Thane mein koi interpreter nahi bulaya jaata aur complaint Atrocities Act ke sections ke bina likh di jaati hai, jisse woh caste ke aankdon se bhi gayab ho jaati hai: NCRB kisi crime ko atrocity tabhi ginta hai jab yeh Act lagaya jaaye [[ncrb-cii-2023-vol2]]. Court mein usse poochha jaata hai ki woh chillaayi kyun nahi, aur uske ateet ke baare mein sawaal hote hain.

Kaanoon is aakhri sawaal ka jawaab pehle se deta hai. Atrocities Act ke sexual touching wale offence ke liye, sirf physically virodh na karna consent nahi maana jaata, aur aurat ki sexual history se consent saabit nahi hota [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]]. Handbook in dhaarnaon ko bhi reject karti hai ki auratein aksar rape ke jhoothe ilzaam lagaati hain, aur ki report karne mein deri ka matlab jhooth hai [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. Kisi myth ko kaam karne ke liye faisle mein likha jaana zaroori nahi. Use bas itna tay karna hota hai ki kisse zyada sakhti se sawaal hon aur kiski chuppi consent jaisi dikhe.

## 1,073 acquittals, 508 convictions: record kya dikha sakta hai aur kya nahi

2023 mein courts ne Scheduled Caste victims wale 1,073 rape cases mein accused ko bari kiya aur 508 mein sazaa di; 86 aur cases discharge par khatam hue. Conviction rate 30.5% raha, aur 20,622 cases, yaani courts ke saamne maujood aise cases ka 92.3%, saal ke aakhir tak pending the [[ncrb-cii-2023-vol2]].

1,073 ko 1,073 aise survivors ki tarah padhna aasaan hai jin par caste ki wajah se yakeen nahi kiya gaya. Lekin record yeh nahi dikha sakta. NCRB ki tables yeh nahi batatin ki koi trial acquittal par kyun khatam hua, aur acquittal ki wajah gawaahon ka mukar jaana, deri, survivors par dabaav, kamzor jaanch, ya aisa charge bhi ho sakta hai jo saabit nahi hua. Asal mein in cases ka conviction rate us saal India mein poore hue sabhi rape trials ke 22.7% se zyada tha [[ncrb-cii-2023]].

Record jo dikhata hai, woh ek aisa system hai jahan zyada tar cases bina faisle ke saalon tak pade rehte hain, aur shak aur dabaav ko kaam karne ke liye saalon mil jaate hain. Disability par record aur bhi patla hai: 2024 mein darj 29,536 rape cases mein se police ne sirf 144 ko mental ya physical disability wali aurat ke rape ke aggravated charge mein darj kiya [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Jab data survivor ko dekh hi nahi paata, toh uske baare mein bane myth ko chunauti dena aur mushkil ho jaata hai.

1995 ki court ne apni soch likh di thi, isliye use naam diya ja saka. Zyada mushkil kaam hai usi soch ko pakadna jab koi use likhta hi nahi.

community-checklist-panchayat-rwa-colleg.en:
India does not lack provisions against sexual violence. It lacks people who check whether they were ever switched on. Every district is meant to have a committee for domestic workers and small workplaces, every village four teenage peer educators, every government school two trained teachers. Yet a decade after the workplace harassment law, the POSH Act, was passed, the Supreme Court found "serious lapses in the enforcement" and called it "a sorry state of affairs" [[sc-aureliano-fernandes-2023]].

This checklist is for the people who can close that gap: panchayat members, resident welfare association (RWA) office-bearers, principals, college heads and employers. It is general information, not legal advice.

## Why change is local

Each of these provisions ends at a named local person: a District Officer, a principal, an employer, a magistrate. Imagine a domestic worker harassed in a flat in your housing society. The law gives her a district committee. Whether she ever hears of it depends on what is pinned to your notice board.

In December 2024 the Supreme Court still had to order every state to notify a District Officer for each district and to set up Local Committees by 31 January 2025. By May 2025 every state had appointed the officers, but Local Committee compliance was unclear in Delhi, Haryana, Jharkhand and Kerala [[sc-posh-order-2025-05-21]].

We could not verify how many of these are working today. In your district, the only way to find out is to ask.

## Panchayats and RWAs: committees, officers, peer educators

**The Local Committee.** Under the POSH Act, each district's District Officer must set up a Local Committee. It hears complaints from workplaces with fewer than ten workers, complaints against an employer himself, and those of domestic workers. If a domestic worker's complaint shows a prima facie case, the committee must forward it to the police within seven days [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].

- Ask the Collector's office who the District Officer is, and get the Local Committee's address and phone number.
- Put those details on the notice board and in the residents' WhatsApp group, in languages that domestic workers, guards and shop staff read.

**Child marriage.** In October 2024 the Supreme Court told states to appoint district Child Marriage Prohibition Officers with no other duties and to publish their quarterly reports online. It told magistrates to issue injunctions on their own initiative, especially around "auspicious days" known for mass weddings [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]].

- Save the officer's number before the wedding season.
- If a child's wedding is being planned, tell the officer, or call the Child Helpline 1098 or 112.

**Saathiya peer educators.** The national adolescent health programme provides for four peer educators per village or 1,000 population, two boys and two girls, each running a weekly session for 15-20 adolescents [[nhm-peer-education-page-2026]].

- Ask the ASHA worker or primary health centre whether your four have been selected and trained, and give them a room and a fixed hour.

## Schools and colleges: ambassadors and complaint routes

**Government and aided schools.** The School Health and Wellness Programme asks for two teachers per school, trained as Health and Wellness Ambassadors and running a one-hour session a week for 24 weeks a year on 11 health themes [[pib-school-health-ambassador-curriculum-2020]]. Private schools are not covered, but can do the same.

- Name the two teachers on the notice board and put the hour on the timetable.
- Check that this term covered safety from violence and where to get help.

**Every school, coaching centre and hostel.** Under the POCSO Act, anyone who knows or suspects a sexual offence against a child must report it to the Special Juvenile Police Unit or the local police. Failing to report can mean up to six months in jail, a fine or both, and up to one year for the head of an institution who does not report an offence by a subordinate [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]].

- Write the rule down: a disclosure goes to the police or 1098, never to a "compromise" meeting.
- Tell staff plainly that they cannot promise a child total secrecy about abuse.

**Colleges and universities.** The POSH Act protects any woman "of any age whether employed or not" who is harassed at a workplace, so protection does not depend on being on the payroll [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. The Supreme Court's 2023 directions, which also reach universities, require committee members, contact details and the complaint procedure to be published online [[sc-aureliano-fernandes-2023]].

- Put the same details up in every hostel and department.
- The Act covers women. A college's own code should also take complaints from male, transgender and queer students.

## Employers: a committee people actually know about

Every employer must have an Internal Committee headed by a senior woman employee, with at least two employee members and one external member, and at least half its members women. An employer who fails to set one up can be fined up to Rs 50,000, and a repeat offence can cost the business its licence or registration [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].

The Supreme Court observed in 2023 that harassed women are often reluctant to report, and "many of them even drop out from their job", partly because they do not know whom to approach [[sc-aureliano-fernandes-2023]].

- Set up the committee at every office or branch with ten or more employees, with a real external member.
- Display members' names, an email address and the complaint steps where every worker, including contract and night-shift staff, will see them.

## Who to call when a provision exists only on paper

- **No Local Committee:** write to the District Officer through the Collector's office. A woman can also file a workplace complaint on the government's SHe-Box portal [[shebox]].
- **A child marriage is planned and the officer is unreachable:** the Supreme Court's guidelines make the District Collector and the Superintendent of Police responsible for prevention [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]]. Call 1098 or 112.
- **A survivor needs support or a lawyer:** the Women Helpline and One Stop Centres, 985 of them operational in July 2026, are run under Mission Shakti [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-07]] [[wcd-mission-shakti]]. Free legal aid comes through the legal services authorities [[nalsa]].

Put every question in writing and keep a dated copy. Then pick one item from this list and finish it this month.
community-checklist-panchayat-rwa-colleg.hg:
India mein sexual violence ke khilaf provisions ki kami nahi hai. Kami un logon ki hai jo check karein ki yeh provisions kabhi chalu bhi hue ya nahi. Har district mein domestic workers aur chhote workplaces ke liye ek committee honi chahiye, har gaon mein chaar teenage peer educators, har government school mein do trained teachers. Phir bhi, workplace harassment ka kanoon, yaani POSH Act, pass hone ke ek dashak baad Supreme Court ne "serious lapses in the enforcement" paaye aur ise "a sorry state of affairs" kaha [[sc-aureliano-fernandes-2023]].

Yeh checklist un logon ke liye hai jo yeh gap bhar sakte hain: panchayat members, resident welfare association (RWA) ke office-bearers, principals, college heads aur employers. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Badlaav local kyun hai

In sab provisions ka aakhri sira ek local insaan par hota hai jiska naam pata kiya ja sakta hai: District Officer, principal, employer, magistrate. Socho, tumhari housing society ke kisi flat mein ek domestic worker ke saath harassment hota hai. Kanoon use district ki ek committee deta hai. Us committee ke baare mein use kabhi pata chalega ya nahi, yeh is par tika hai ki tumhare notice board par kya laga hai.

December 2024 mein bhi Supreme Court ko har state ko order dena pada ki har district ke liye District Officer notify karo aur 31 January 2025 tak Local Committees banao. May 2025 tak har state ne officers appoint kar diye the, par Delhi, Haryana, Jharkhand aur Kerala mein Local Committee ka compliance saaf nahi tha [[sc-posh-order-2025-05-21]].

Inme se kitne aaj sach mein kaam kar rahe hain, yeh hum verify nahi kar paaye. Tumhare district mein pata karne ka ek hi tareeka hai: poochna.

## Panchayats aur RWAs: committees, officers, peer educators

**Local Committee.** POSH Act ke tahat har district ke District Officer ko ek Local Committee banani hoti hai. Yeh un workplaces ki complaints sunti hai jahan das se kam workers hain, khud employer ke khilaf complaints sunti hai, aur domestic workers ki complaints bhi. Agar domestic worker ki complaint mein prima facie case banta hai, toh committee ko use saat din ke andar police ko bhejna hota hai [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].

- Collector office se poocho ki District Officer kaun hai, aur Local Committee ka address aur phone number le lo.
- Yeh details notice board par aur residents ke WhatsApp group mein daalo, un bhashaon mein jo domestic workers, guards aur dukaan ka staff padh sake.

**Child marriage.** October 2024 mein Supreme Court ne states se kaha ki har district mein aise Child Marriage Prohibition Officers appoint karo jinke paas koi aur duty na ho, aur unki quarterly reports online daalo. Court ne magistrates se kaha ki woh khud pehal karke injunction jaari karein, khaas kar un "auspicious days" ke aas-paas jo mass weddings ke liye jaane jaate hain [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]].

- Officer ka number shaadi ke season se pehle hi save kar lo.
- Agar kisi bachche ki shaadi plan ho rahi hai, toh officer ko batao, ya Child Helpline 1098 ya 112 par call karo.

**Saathiya peer educators.** National adolescent health programme mein har gaon ya 1,000 ki aabadi par chaar peer educators ka provision hai, do ladke aur do ladkiyan, aur har ek ko 15-20 adolescents ke saath hafte ka ek session lena hai [[nhm-peer-education-page-2026]].

- ASHA worker ya primary health centre se poocho ki tumhare chaar Saathiya chune gaye aur train hue ya nahi, aur unhe ek kamra aur ek fixed ghanta do.

## Schools aur colleges: ambassadors aur complaint ke raaste

**Government aur aided schools.** School Health and Wellness Programme har school se do teachers maangta hai, jo Health and Wellness Ambassadors ke roop mein train hon aur saal mein 24 hafte, hafte mein ek ghante ka session lein, 11 health themes par [[pib-school-health-ambassador-curriculum-2020]]. Private schools isme cover nahi hote, par woh bhi yahi kar sakte hain.

- Dono teachers ke naam notice board par likho aur woh ghanta timetable mein daalo.
- Check karo ki is term mein violence se safety aur madad kahan milegi, yeh padhaya gaya ya nahi.

**Har school, coaching centre aur hostel.** POCSO Act ke tahat, jise bhi pata ho ya shak ho ki kisi bachche ke khilaf sexual offence hua hai, use Special Juvenile Police Unit ya local police ko report karna hi hoga. Report na karne par chhe mahine tak ki jail, fine ya dono ho sakte hain, aur us institution head ko ek saal tak ki jo apne subordinate ke offence ki report nahi karta [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]].

- Rule likhkar rakho: bachche ki batayi baat police ya 1098 tak jayegi, kisi "compromise" meeting tak kabhi nahi.
- Staff ko saaf batao ki woh abuse ke baare mein kisi bachche se poori secrecy ka promise nahi kar sakte.

**Colleges aur universities.** POSH Act har us woman ko protect karta hai jo "of any age whether employed or not" ho aur jiske saath workplace par harassment hua ho, isliye protection is baat par tika nahi hai ki woh payroll par hai ya nahi [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Supreme Court ke 2023 ke directions, jo universities tak bhi pahunchte hain, kehte hain ki committee ke members, contact details aur complaint ka procedure online publish ho [[sc-aureliano-fernandes-2023]].

- Yahi details har hostel aur department mein bhi lagao.
- Act women ko cover karta hai. College ke apne code ko male, transgender aur queer students ki complaints bhi leni chahiye.

## Employers: aisi committee jiske baare mein log sach mein jaante hon

Har employer ke paas ek Internal Committee honi chahiye jiski head ek senior woman employee ho, jisme kam se kam do employee members aur ek external member ho, aur jiske kam se kam aadhe members women hon. Jo employer committee nahi banata, us par Rs 50,000 tak ka fine lag sakta hai, aur dobara galti par business ka licence ya registration bhi ja sakta hai [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].

Supreme Court ne 2023 mein kaha ki harassment jhelne wali women aksar report karne se hichkichati hain, aur "many of them even drop out from their job", kuch had tak isliye ki unhe pata hi nahi hota ki jaana kiske paas hai [[sc-aureliano-fernandes-2023]].

- Har us office ya branch mein committee banao jahan das ya zyada employees hain, aur external member sach mein bahar ka ho.
- Members ke naam, ek email address aur complaint ke steps wahan lagao jahan har worker dekh sake, contract aur night-shift staff bhi.

## Jab provision sirf kaagaz par ho, toh kisse baat karein

- **Local Committee hai hi nahi:** Collector office ke zariye District Officer ko likho. Koi bhi woman workplace ki complaint sarkar ke SHe-Box portal par bhi daal sakti hai [[shebox]].
- **Child marriage plan ho rahi hai aur officer tak pahunch nahi ho rahi:** Supreme Court ki guidelines ke mutabik rokne ki zimmedari District Collector aur Superintendent of Police ki hai [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]]. 1098 ya 112 par call karo.
- **Kisi survivor ko support ya lawyer chahiye:** Women Helpline aur One Stop Centres, jinme se 985 July 2026 mein operational the, Mission Shakti ke tahat chalte hain [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-07]] [[wcd-mission-shakti]]. Free legal aid legal services authorities ke zariye milti hai [[nalsa]].

Har sawaal likhkar poocho aur date wali copy apne paas rakho. Phir is list mein se ek kaam chuno aur use isi mahine poora karo.

faith-or-childs-body-nine-judge-bench.en:
On 14 May 2026, after 16 days of hearings, nine Supreme Court judges reserved judgment in what headlines call the Sabarimala case [[scobserver-sabarimala-day16-2026]]. Tied to it is a question about children: when a community says a practice is part of its faith, can a court still ask what it does to a girl's body? The practice is khatna, the genital cutting of girls in the Dawoodi Bohra community.

## The petition and the rights in conflict

In 2017 a public interest petition, Sunita Tiwari v. Union of India, asked the Supreme Court to ban khatna. It argues that the practice violates girls' rights to equality, non-discrimination and bodily autonomy under Articles 14, 15 and 21. Community members argue that it is religious practice protected by Articles 25 and 26 [[scobserver-sunita-tiwari-fgm-case]].

Articles 25 and 26 protect the freedom to practise religion and a denomination's right to manage its own religious affairs, but that freedom is not unlimited. The petitioners' case is that a girl's equality and bodily autonomy are among its limits.

The government has not even agreed that the problem exists. In December 2017 the Ministry of Women and Child Development told the court "there is no official data or study which supports the existence of FGM in India", a position Bohra campaigners rejected [[guardian-fgm-india-study-2018]]. In an online survey by Sahiyo, a group of Dawoodi Bohra women campaigning against khatna, 80% of 385 respondents said they had undergone it and 82% said they were unlikely to continue it on their daughters [[sahiyo-khatna-survey-2017]]. It was a self-selected sample, only 34% of it in India, so it cannot measure prevalence. It does show that some of the strongest opposition comes from women inside the community.

## 2018 and 2019: from one petition to a 'seminal issue'

In 2018 Attorney General K.K. Venugopal told the court that the Union government opposed khatna as a violation of fundamental rights, noting bans in the US, the UK, Australia and around 27 African nations [[toi-fgm-five-judge-bench-2018]]. On 24 September 2018, at the request of the Attorney General and community groups, a three-judge bench led by Chief Justice Dipak Misra sent the case to a larger bench, to consider it "in its entirety from all perspectives" [[sc-sunita-tiwari-order-2018]].

Then it was folded into a bigger case. On 14 November 2019 the bench reviewing the 2018 Sabarimala temple-entry verdict, led by Chief Justice Ranjan Gogoi, referred religious-freedom questions to a larger bench by a 3:2 majority [[ht-fgm-seven-judge-bench-2019]]. The majority called khatna a "seminal issue" about the power of courts to decide whether a practice is essential to religion, needing a bench of "not less than seven judges" [[sc-kantaru-rajeevaru-review-2019]].

## Essential practice and constitutional morality, in plain words

Under what is called the essential religious practices doctrine, Indian courts decide which religious practices to protect by asking whether a practice is "essential" to the faith. In plain words: is this the core of the religion, or a custom that grew around it? An essential practice is protected; a non-essential one can be regulated like any social custom. The 2019 reference asked exactly how far courts may go in making that call.

The other idea is constitutional morality: that the Constitution's values, such as equality, dignity and liberty, set the limits of any custom, whatever a community believes. The nine judges heard arguments on both, and on denominational autonomy, a religious group's right to run its own affairs [[scobserver-sabarimala-day16-2026]].

On 7 May 2026 khatna reached the bench directly. Senior Advocate Siddharth Luthra argued that the genital cutting of seven-year-old girls could not survive constitutional scrutiny merely because it is asserted as faith. Counsel for the review petitioners called it "a symbolic form of circumcision". Justice Joymalya Bagchi responded that male circumcision could not be equated with genital cutting involving the clitoris [[scobserver-sabarimala-day13-2026]]. Remarks from the bench are not rulings, but the question is clear: whose body, whose choice?

## Nine judges, judgment reserved

The nine-judge bench, led by Chief Justice Surya Kant, began hearing the reference on 7 April 2026. The khatna petition is one of three pending cases tagged to it, with Muslim women's entry into mosques and a Parsi woman's entry into a fire temple [[scobserver-sabarimala-reference-2026]]. Judgment was reserved on 14 May 2026 [[scobserver-sabarimala-day16-2026]]. At the time of writing, it had not been delivered.

The judgment will answer general questions about religious freedom; how and when the khatna petition itself is decided depends on the test it sets. Meanwhile, no specific Indian law bans FGM, while, as Supreme Court Observer's report of the 7 May hearing notes, around 59 countries prohibit it [[scobserver-sabarimala-day13-2026]]. This is general information, not legal advice. In February 2026 the UN's women's rights committee (CEDAW) asked India for FGM data and for "any plans and time frame" for a law against it; India's next report is due on 3 February 2027 [[cedaw-india-loipr-2026]].

## Why the answer reaches beyond one community

Whatever test the court sets will apply to every faith. The same reference decides whether women can be kept out of a temple, a mosque or a fire temple: when tradition and a woman's equality collide, who decides? Our story on menstrual exclusion asks the same about homes.

FGM is not one community's secret either. UNFPA says it is documented in at least 94 countries, India among them [[unfpa-fgm-faq-2026]]. More than 230 million girls and women alive today have undergone it [[unicef-fgm-estimates-2024]]; about one in four, some 52 million, were cut by health personnel [[unicef-fgm-topic-page]]. A cut made in a clinic is still made on a child who did not choose it.

So talk about the girl, not the faith. The Dawoodi Bohra community is not one voice: Bohra women are among the clearest voices against khatna, and others sincerely defend the practice. Mockery protects no child; it only hardens positions. If you fear a girl is about to be cut, call the Child Helpline on 1098.
faith-or-childs-body-nine-judge-bench.hg:
14 May 2026 ko, 16 din ki sunwai ke baad, Supreme Court ke nau judges ne us case mein faisla reserve kar liya jise headlines Sabarimala case kehti hain [[scobserver-sabarimala-day16-2026]]. Isi case se bachchon ka ek sawaal juda hai: jab koi community kahe ki ek practice uski aastha ka hissa hai, tab bhi kya court pooch sakti hai ki woh practice ek ladki ki body ke saath kya karti hai? Yeh practice khatna hai, yaani Dawoodi Bohra community mein ladkiyon ki genital cutting.

## Petition, aur aapas mein takraate rights

2017 mein ek public interest petition, Sunita Tiwari v. Union of India, ne Supreme Court se khatna ban karne ki maang ki. Petition ka kehna hai ki yeh practice Articles 14, 15 aur 21 ke tahat ladkiyon ke equality, non-discrimination aur bodily autonomy ke rights ko todti hai. Community ke members ka kehna hai ki yeh religious practice hai, jise Articles 25 aur 26 protect karte hain [[scobserver-sunita-tiwari-fgm-case]].

Articles 25 aur 26 dharm ko practise karne ki freedom aur ek denomination ko apne religious maamle khud chalane ka haq dete hain, lekin yeh freedom bina had ke nahi hai. Petitioners ka case yahi hai ki ek ladki ki equality aur bodily autonomy usi had ka hissa hain.

Sarkar ne toh yeh bhi nahi maana ki problem maujood hai. December 2017 mein Ministry of Women and Child Development ne court se kaha "there is no official data or study which supports the existence of FGM in India", yaani aisa koi official data ya study nahi hai jo India mein FGM ke hone ko support kare. Bohra campaigners ne is position ko reject kiya [[guardian-fgm-india-study-2018]]. Sahiyo, yaani khatna ke khilaaf campaign karne wali Dawoodi Bohra women ke group, ke ek online survey mein 385 respondents mein se 80% ne kaha ki unka khatna hua tha, aur 82% ne kaha ki woh apni betiyon par ise jaari rakhne wali nahi hain [[sahiyo-khatna-survey-2017]]. Yeh self-selected sample tha, jiske sirf 34% log India mein rehte the, isliye isse prevalence nahi naapa ja sakta. Lekin isse yeh zaroor dikhta hai ki iska sabse mazboot virodh community ke andar ki women se bhi aata hai.

## 2018 aur 2019: ek petition se 'seminal issue' tak

2018 mein Attorney General K.K. Venugopal ne court ko bataya ki Union government khatna ko fundamental rights ka violation maanti hai aur iske khilaaf hai. Unhone yeh bhi kaha ki US, UK, Australia aur lagbhag 27 African nations mein is par ban hai [[toi-fgm-five-judge-bench-2018]]. 24 September 2018 ko, Attorney General aur community groups ki request par, Chief Justice Dipak Misra ki aguwai wali teen judges ki bench ne case ek larger bench ko bhej diya, taaki woh is par "in its entirety from all perspectives", yaani poori tarah aur har nazariye se, vichaar kare [[sc-sunita-tiwari-order-2018]].

Phir yeh ek bade case ka hissa ban gaya. 14 November 2019 ko, 2018 ke Sabarimala temple-entry verdict ka review kar rahi bench ne, jiski aguwai Chief Justice Ranjan Gogoi kar rahe the, 3:2 ki majority se religious freedom ke sawaal ek larger bench ko refer kar diye [[ht-fgm-seven-judge-bench-2019]]. Majority ne khatna ko ek "seminal issue" kaha: sawaal yeh ki courts ke paas yeh tay karne ki kitni power hai ki koi practice dharm ke liye essential hai ya nahi. Uske mutabik iske liye "not less than seven judges", yaani kam se kam saat judges ki bench chahiye thi [[sc-kantaru-rajeevaru-review-2019]].

## Essential practice aur constitutional morality, seedhe shabdon mein

Essential religious practices doctrine ke tahat Indian courts yeh tay karne ke liye ki kaun si religious practice protect hogi, ek sawaal poochti hain: kya yeh practice us dharm ke liye "essential" hai? Seedhe shabdon mein: yeh dharm ka core hai, ya uske aas-paas panpa ek rivaaj? Essential practice protected hai; non-essential practice ko kisi bhi social custom ki tarah regulate kiya ja sakta hai. 2019 ka reference thik yahi poochta hai ki courts yeh faisla karne mein kahan tak ja sakti hain.

Doosra idea constitutional morality hai: yaani Constitution ke values, jaise equality, dignity aur liberty, har rivaaj ki had tay karte hain, community chahe jo bhi maanti ho. Nau judges ne in dono par arguments sune, aur denominational autonomy par bhi, yaani ek religious group ka apne maamle khud chalane ka haq [[scobserver-sabarimala-day16-2026]].

7 May 2026 ko khatna seedhe bench ke saamne aaya. Senior Advocate Siddharth Luthra ne argue kiya ki saat saal ki ladkiyon ki genital cutting sirf isliye constitutional scrutiny mein nahi tik sakti ki use aastha kaha ja raha hai. Review petitioners ke counsel ne ise "a symbolic form of circumcision", yaani circumcision ka ek symbolic form kaha.
