Justice Joymalya Bagchi ne jawaab diya ki male circumcision ko us genital cutting ke barabar nahi rakha ja sakta jismein clitoris shaamil ho [[scobserver-sabarimala-day13-2026]]. Bench ki tippaniyan faisle nahi hoti, lekin sawaal saaf hai: body kiski hai, aur choice kiski?

## Nau judges, faisla reserved

Chief Justice Surya Kant ki aguwai wali nau judges ki bench ne 7 April 2026 se is reference ki sunwai shuru ki. Khatna petition isse tagged teen pending cases mein se ek hai; baaki do Muslim women ki mosques mein entry aur ek Parsi woman ki fire temple mein entry ke hain [[scobserver-sabarimala-reference-2026]]. Faisla 14 May 2026 ko reserve hua [[scobserver-sabarimala-day16-2026]]. Yeh likhe jaane tak judgment aaya nahi tha.

Judgment religious freedom ke general sawaalon ka jawaab dega; khatna petition ka faisla kab aur kaise hoga, yeh us test par depend karta hai jo yeh judgment tay karega. Is beech koi bhi specific Indian law FGM ko ban nahi karta, jabki, jaisa 7 May ki sunwai par Supreme Court Observer ki report batati hai, lagbhag 59 countries ise prohibit karti hain [[scobserver-sabarimala-day13-2026]]. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi. February 2026 mein UN ki women's rights committee (CEDAW) ne India se FGM ka data maanga, aur iske khilaaf law ke liye "any plans and time frame", yaani koi plan aur uski time frame; India ki agli report 3 February 2027 ko due hai [[cedaw-india-loipr-2026]].

## Jawaab ek community se aage kyun jaata hai

Court jo bhi test tay karegi, woh har dharm par laagu hoga. Yahi reference tay karega ki women ko temple, mosque ya fire temple se bahar rakha ja sakta hai ya nahi: jab parampara aur ek woman ki equality takraati hain, toh faisla kaun karega? Periods ke dauraan alag rakhe jaane par hamari story yahi sawaal gharon ke baare mein poochti hai.

FGM kisi ek community ka raaz bhi nahi hai. UNFPA ke mutabik yeh kam se kam 94 countries mein documented hai, jinmein India bhi hai [[unfpa-fgm-faq-2026]]. Aaj zinda 230 million se zyada ladkiyan aur women isse guzar chuki hain [[unicef-fgm-estimates-2024]]; lagbhag har chaar mein se ek, yaani kareeb 52 million, ki cutting health personnel ne ki thi [[unicef-fgm-topic-page]]. Clinic mein kiya gaya cut bhi ek aisi bachchi par hota hai jisne ise khud nahi chuna.

Isliye baat ladki ki kijiye, dharm ki nahi. Dawoodi Bohra community ek aawaaz nahi hai: khatna ke khilaaf sabse saaf aawaazon mein Bohra women bhi hain, aur doosre log poori sachchai se is practice ka bachaav karte hain. Mazaak udaane se koi bachchi nahi bachti; isse bas dono taraf ki zid aur sakht hoti hai. Agar aapko darr hai ki kisi ladki ki cutting hone wali hai, toh Child Helpline 1098 par call kijiye.

first-job-internship-harassment-checklis.en:
Imagine a 21-year-old from Indore with her first offer: a six-month internship at a 14-person start-up in Bengaluru. She has read the stipend, the notice period and the dress code. Nothing in the letter says whom she would tell if a senior harassed her.

The Supreme Court noted in 2023 that women harassed at work are often reluctant to report and "many of them even drop out from their job", partly because they do not know whom to approach [[sc-aureliano-fernandes-2023]]. The time to find out is before anything happens. Here are six checks drawn from the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013 (the POSH Act), and a plan for week one. This is general information, not legal advice.

## Before you sign: does a committee exist, and who is on it?

**Check 1: Is there an Internal Committee?** Every office or branch with ten or more workers must have one; smaller ones are covered by the district (Check 4). An employer that does not can be fined up to Rs 50,000, with double the punishment on a repeat [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Email HR one line: "Who are the members of your Internal Committee?"

**Check 2: Is it a real committee?** The law wants a senior woman employee presiding, at least two employee members, and one external member from an NGO or someone familiar with sexual harassment issues. At least half the members must be women [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. "Our founder handles these things personally" is not a committee.

**Check 3: Can you find it without asking your boss?** In May 2023 the Supreme Court found "serious lapses" in enforcing the Act. It ordered governments to verify that every ministry, department, public sector undertaking and public body had a proper committee, and to publish its members, contact details and complaint procedure online [[sc-aureliano-fernandes-2023]]. If you are joining a government office or a PSU, look on its website. In a private firm, look in the handbook or on the intranet.

Do not assume someone has already checked your employer. In December 2024 the Court ordered a survey of Internal Committees in private as well as government institutions; by August 2025 it was told that only the Andaman and Nicobar Islands had completed one [[livelaw-posh-district-survey-2025]].

**Check 4: How many people work there?** Where there are fewer than ten workers, or where the complaint is against the employer, it goes to the district's Local Committee, set up by the District Officer [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. That is the route for a six-person design studio, a clinic or a coaching centre.

## Transport, travel and late shifts: what counts as the workplace

**Check 5: What happens after dark and outside the office?** The Act's definition of a workplace covers any place an employee visits in the course of work, including transport provided by the employer [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. The office cab, a client's site and a work trip are all the workplace. Harassment there is not "after hours" or "personal".

By early 2026 around 22 states and union territories allowed women to work night shifts in factories, and 33 allowed it in commercial establishments. The permissions usually come with duties for the employer: Uttar Pradesh's rules require employer-provided transport, CCTV and security personnel [[es-2025-26-employment-chapter]]. Before you agree to a night roster, ask in writing who provides the drop home.

## Interviews and auditions: the gap in the law

**Check 6: Are you covered before you are hired?** On paper, the Act protects any woman "of any age whether employed or not" who alleges sexual harassment at a workplace [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. That wording is why an intern or someone on probation can complain.

But the Kerala High Court, in proceedings on the Hema Committee report about the Malayalam film industry, has orally remarked that the Act does not cover harassment faced by women who are seeking employment [[livelaw-kerala-hc-hema-draft-law-2025]]. It was a remark, not a ruling, so the question is contested.

So at an interview, an audition or a "trial day", do not count on a committee. Meet at the office in working hours where you can, tell someone where you are going, and keep the call letter and every message. Criminal law does not ask whether you were hired: sexual harassment is an offence under Section 75 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, punishable with up to three years [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

## Week one: noting dates, messages and witnesses

Now suppose that on day four a team lead comments on her body in the office cab and messages her at midnight. She is new, on a stipend, and hoping for a job offer at the end. That imbalance is the reason to start a record the same night.

- Write down the date, time, place, the exact words or act, and who was present. Email the note to your personal account so it carries a date.
- Screenshot messages and save them outside the office laptop, which the company can switch off.
- Tell one person you trust, in writing if you can.
- Do not let anyone "sort it out" over coffee. Conciliation happens only at the complainant's request, and never on the basis of a money settlement [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].

She does not need a perfect file. The Act says a mere inability to substantiate a complaint or provide adequate proof need not attract action against the complainant [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].

## The three-month clock, and where to go without a committee

A complaint must be in writing and made within three months of the incident, or of the last incident in a series. The committee can extend this by up to three more months only if it records in writing why she could not complain in time. Then the inquiry must be completed within 90 days, the report sent to the employer within 10 days, and the employer must act within 60 days [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].

A six-month internship can end before a new joiner decides it was "serious enough". Do not wait for the certificate.

If there is no committee, or the employer is the problem, three doors remain: the district's Local Committee; SHe-Box, the Ministry of Women and Child Development's online portal for workplace harassment complaints [[shebox]]; and the police.

The Act is written for women. If you are a man, or a trans or non-binary person, ask before you join whether the company's own policy covers everyone; criminal acts can still go to the police.

None of the six checks needs a lawyer. They need one email to HR before you sign, and a notes file from day one.
first-job-internship-harassment-checklis.hg:
Socho, Indore ki ek 21 saal ki ladki ko pehla offer mila hai: Bengaluru ke ek 14 logon wale start-up mein chhah mahine ki internship. Usne stipend, notice period aur dress code padh liya hai. Letter mein kahin nahi likha ki agar koi senior use harass kare, toh woh kise bataye.

Supreme Court ne 2023 mein kaha tha ki kaam ki jagah par harassment jhelne wali women aksar report karne se hichkichati hain aur "many of them even drop out from their job", yaani kai toh job hi chhod deti hain. Ek wajah yeh ki unhe pata nahi hota kiske paas jaayein [[sc-aureliano-fernandes-2023]]. Yeh pata karne ka sahi time tab hai jab abhi kuch hua nahi hai. Yahan chhah checks hain, jo Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013 (POSH Act) se nikle hain, aur pehle hafte ka ek plan. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Sign karne se pehle: committee hai ya nahi, aur usmein kaun hai?

**Check 1: Kya Internal Committee hai?** Jis office ya branch mein das ya usse zyada workers hain, wahan yeh honi hi chahiye; usse chhoti jagahon ke liye district ki committee hai (Check 4). Jo employer nahi banata, us par Rs 50,000 tak ka fine lag sakta hai, aur dobara aisa karne par double saza [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. HR ko ek line ka email bhejo: "Aapki Internal Committee ke members kaun hain?"

**Check 2: Kya woh asli committee hai?** Law chahta hai ki presiding officer ek senior woman employee ho, employees mein se kam se kam do members hon, aur ek external member ho, kisi NGO se ya koi aisa insaan jo sexual harassment ke issues samajhta ho. Kam se kam aadhe members women honi chahiye [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. "Yeh sab hamare founder khud dekh lete hain" committee nahi hai.

**Check 3: Kya tum boss se pooche bina use dhundh sakti ho?** May 2023 mein Supreme Court ne paaya ki Act ke enforcement mein "serious lapses" hain. Court ne governments ko order diya ki verify karo ki har ministry, department, public sector undertaking aur public body mein theek se bani committee hai, aur uske members, contact details aur complaint ka procedure online publish karo [[sc-aureliano-fernandes-2023]]. Agar tum kisi government office ya PSU mein join kar rahi ho, toh uski website dekho. Private firm mein handbook ya intranet dekho.

Yeh maan kar mat chalo ki tumhare employer ko kisi ne pehle hi check kar liya hoga. December 2024 mein Court ne private aur government, dono tarah ke institutions mein Internal Committees ka survey karne ko kaha tha; August 2025 tak use bataya gaya ki sirf Andaman and Nicobar Islands ne survey poora kiya hai [[livelaw-posh-district-survey-2025]].

**Check 4: Wahan kitne log kaam karte hain?** Jahan das se kam workers hain, ya jahan complaint employer ke hi khilaf hai, wahan complaint district ki Local Committee ke paas jaati hai, jise District Officer banata hai [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Chhah logon wala design studio, clinic ya coaching centre, in sab ke liye rasta yahi hai.

## Transport, travel aur late shifts: workplace mein kya-kya gina jaata hai

**Check 5: Andhera hone ke baad aur office ke bahar kya hota hai?** Act ki workplace ki definition mein woh har jagah aati hai jahan employee kaam ke silsile mein jaati hai, employer ka diya hua transport bhi [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Office cab, client ki site aur work trip, sab workplace hain. Wahan hua harassment "after hours" ya "personal" maamla nahi hai.

Early 2026 tak lagbhag 22 states aur union territories ne women ko factories mein night shift karne ki ijazat de di thi, aur 33 ne commercial establishments mein. In permissions ke saath aksar employer ki duties bhi aati hain: Uttar Pradesh ke rules mein employer ka diya transport, CCTV aur security personnel zaroori hain [[es-2025-26-employment-chapter]]. Night roster ke liye haan kehne se pehle likhit mein poocho ki ghar tak drop kaun dega.

## Interviews aur auditions: law ka gap

**Check 6: Kya hire hone se pehle bhi tum covered ho?** Kaagaz par, Act us har aurat ko protect karta hai jo workplace par sexual harassment ka aarop lagaye, "of any age whether employed or not", yaani kisi bhi umar ki, chahe employed ho ya nahi [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Inhi words ki wajah se intern ya probation par chal rahi employee bhi complaint kar sakti hai.

Lekin Kerala High Court ne, Malayalam film industry par Hema Committee report se jude proceedings mein, orally kaha hai ki yeh Act un women ke harassment ko cover nahi karta jo abhi kaam dhundh rahi hain [[livelaw-kerala-hc-hema-draft-law-2025]]. Yeh ek remark tha, ruling nahi, isliye yeh sawaal abhi contested hai.

Toh interview, audition ya "trial day" par committee ke bharose mat raho. Jahan ho sake, office mein working hours ke dauraan milo, kisi ko batao ki kahan ja rahi ho, aur call letter aur har message sambhal kar rakho. Criminal law yeh nahi poochta ki tumhe hire kiya gaya tha ya nahi: sexual harassment, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita ke Section 75 ke under offence hai, jiski saza teen saal tak hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

## Pehla hafta: dates, messages aur witnesses note karna

Ab maan lo ki chauthe din ek team lead office cab mein uske body par comment karta hai aur aadhi raat ko message bhejta hai. Woh nayi hai, stipend par hai, aur umeed kar rahi hai ki end mein job offer milega. Yahi imbalance wajah hai ki record usi raat se shuru ho jana chahiye.

- Date, time, jagah, exact words ya harkat, aur wahan kaun-kaun tha, sab likh lo. Yeh note apne personal email par bhej do taaki us par date aa jaye.
- Messages ke screenshots lo aur unhe office laptop ke bahar save karo, kyunki company laptop ka access band kar sakti hai.
- Kisi ek bharosemand insaan ko batao, ho sake toh likh kar.
- Kisi ko bhi maamla coffee par "sort out" mat karne do. Conciliation sirf complainant ki request par hota hai, aur paise ke settlement ke basis par kabhi nahi [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].

Use perfect file ki zaroorat nahi hai. Act kehta hai ki sirf isliye ki koi complaint saabit nahi kar payi ya poora proof nahi de payi, complainant ke khilaf action nahi banta [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].

## Teen mahine ki ghadi, aur committee na ho toh kahan jayein

Complaint likhit mein honi chahiye, incident ke teen mahine ke andar; kai incidents hue hon toh aakhri incident ke teen mahine ke andar. Committee yeh time teen mahine aur tabhi badha sakti hai jab woh likhit mein record kare ki woh time par complaint kyun nahi kar payi. Phir inquiry 90 din ke andar poori honi chahiye, report 10 din ke andar employer ko jaani chahiye, aur employer ko 60 din ke andar action lena hota hai [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].

Chhah mahine ki internship is se pehle khatam ho sakti hai ki nayi joiner tay kar paye ki baat "serious enough" thi ya nahi. Certificate ka wait mat karo.

Agar committee hai hi nahi, ya problem khud employer hai, toh teen darwaze bachte hain: district ki Local Committee; SHe-Box, jo Ministry of Women and Child Development ka workplace harassment complaints ka online portal hai [[shebox]]; aur police.

Yeh Act women ke liye likha gaya hai. Agar tum man ho, ya trans ya non-binary person ho, toh join karne se pehle poocho ki company ki apni policy sabko cover karti hai ya nahi; criminal acts ke liye police ka rasta phir bhi khula hai.

In chhah checks mein se kisi ke liye lawyer nahi chahiye. Chahiye toh bas sign karne se pehle HR ko ek email, aur day one se ek notes file.

hema-report-aftermath-posh-gap-auditions.en:
A film set has a crew, a call sheet and a producer who answers for it. An audition can be a hotel room or a late call from a casting coordinator, and it happens before anyone has signed anything. That is the stage the Hema Committee described in Malayalam cinema. Junior artists, it found, were told they would get a chance in films if they complied with demands for sex, and women who agreed were given a code name: "cooperating artists" [[nie-hema-report-release-2024]].

## Auditions: the moment the law does not reach

India's workplace harassment law, the POSH Act, is built around a workplace and an employer. Its definition of workplace expressly covers private entertainment businesses [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. In 2022 the Kerala High Court held that each film's production unit is a workplace and must have an Internal Complaints Committee if it engages more than 10 workers [[kerala-hc-wcc-judgment-2022]].

A casting couch operates earlier. The demand arrives when a woman has no role, no contract and no unit. In the hearings that followed the report, the Kerala High Court pointed to this orally: the Act, it said, does not take within its purview sexual harassment faced by women who are seeking employment [[livelaw-kerala-hc-hema-draft-law-2025]].

That was a remark from the bench, not a ruling, and the point is contested. The Act's text protects a woman "of any age whether employed or not" who is harassed at a workplace [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Consider a 22-year-old who travels to Kochi for an audition she heard about in a WhatsApp group. The man who meets her is not her employer. The film may not have a unit yet, let alone a committee. If he names a price for the role, there is no committee door she can knock on, and refusing ends the audition.

## Five years 'inactive or silent'

The committee gave its report to the Kerala government in December 2019. The public saw it on 19 August 2024, nearly five years later, and only after the State Information Commission ordered its release and the Kerala High Court rejected a challenge [[nie-hema-report-release-2024]].

On 10 September 2024 the High Court put the question to the state directly: why had it been "inactive or silent" since 31 December 2019? The state police chief had held a copy since February 2021. The court ordered the full, unredacted report handed to a Special Investigation Team (SIT) [[livelaw-kerala-hc-hema-sit-2024]].

Many women the committee approached were at first afraid to speak, because "they were afraid they would lose their jobs". The panel found that fear strange in the beginning, then concluded it was "well-founded", and said it was concerned for the safety of the witnesses and their close relatives [[bbc-hema-report-2024]]. Women took that risk and testified, and for years nothing they could see happened. That teaches the next woman to stay quiet.

## An actors' association with no committee

In 2018 the Women in Cinema Collective (WCC) went to the Kerala High Court, arguing that the Association of Malayalam Movie Artists (AMMA) was bound by the Vishaka guidelines and the POSH Act to have an Internal Complaints Committee or grievance cell, and had none. By 2022 the collective said AMMA and the Cine and TV Artists Association still had none [[livelaw-kwc-wcc-pil-2022]].

The court answered on 17 March 2022. Film associations such as AMMA are not the employers of actors, it held, so the Act binds them only for their own office staff. The duty sits with each production unit, film by film. AMMA volunteered to set up a committee of its own [[kerala-hc-wcc-judgment-2022]].

Follow that logic to the audition. A unit forms for one film and dissolves after it. The associations that outlast every film are not employers. Casting happens before the unit exists. For the woman auditioning, the only body the law clearly binds has not hired her and may not exist yet.

## After the report: the SIT and a promised cinema law

What changed after August 2024 is a short list: the unredacted report went to the SIT on the court's order [[livelaw-kerala-hc-hema-sit-2024]]. On 8 October 2025 the Kerala government told the High Court that the SIT's investigation was over, and that a draft law for the entertainment industry would be placed before the state cabinet in the first week of November [[livelaw-kerala-hc-hema-draft-law-2025]].

We could not confirm how many of the SIT's cases ended in chargesheets, or whether the draft law was approved or enacted after November 2025. Until a law is in force, the promise is a statement made by a government lawyer in a courtroom.

A Kerala cinema law would also cover only Kerala's cinema. Auditions and look tests happen in television, advertising and modelling, in every state, and the gap the court named is in a national law.

## If you are auditioning: what protection exists

This is general information, not legal advice.

- The police route does not need a job. A demand for sexual favours has been named as sexual harassment since the Supreme Court's Vishaka guidelines of 1997 [[sc-vishaka-1997]]. Under Section 75 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, sexual harassment is a crime punishable with up to three years in prison [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. It can be reported at any police station, wherever it happened [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- The POSH route is arguable, so use it. Where the establishment has fewer than ten workers and so no Internal Committee, or the complaint is against the employer, it goes to the district's Local Committee, in writing, within three months of the incident [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. A complaint can also be filed on SHe-Box, the government's portal [[shebox]].
- Leave a trail. Ask in writing which production the audition is for and who is conducting it. Keep every message. Tell one person where you are going.

The POSH Act hears complaints only from women; a male or transgender actor asked for the same price has even fewer routes.

None of this should be the job of the person auditioning. It is the job of whoever is casting. But a written trail is the one thing a casting couch is built to avoid.
hema-report-aftermath-posh-gap-auditions.hg:
Film set par crew hota hai, call sheet hoti hai aur ek producer hota hai jo jawabdeh hai. Audition kisi hotel ke kamre mein ho sakta hai, ya casting coordinator ke der raat ke phone call par, aur ye tab hota hai jab kisi ne kuch sign nahi kiya hota. Hema Committee ne Malayalam cinema mein isi stage ki baat ki. Committee ne paaya ki junior artists se kaha jaata tha ki agar woh sex ki demands maan lein toh unhe films mein chance milega, aur jo aurtein maan jaati thin unhe ek code name diya jaata tha: "cooperating artists" [[nie-hema-report-release-2024]].

## Audition: woh pal jahan law nahi pahunchta

India ka workplace harassment law, yaani POSH Act, do cheezon par tika hai: ek workplace aur ek employer. Iski 'workplace' ki definition mein private entertainment businesses saaf-saaf shaamil hain [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. 2022 mein Kerala High Court ne kaha ki har film ki production unit ek workplace hai, aur agar usme 10 se zyada workers hain toh usme Internal Complaints Committee honi hi chahiye [[kerala-hc-wcc-judgment-2022]].

Casting couch isse pehle kaam karta hai. Demand tab aati hai jab aurat ke paas na role hota hai, na contract, na unit. Report ke baad hui hearings mein Kerala High Court ne orally isi taraf ishaara kiya: court ke mutabik ye Act un aurton ke sexual harassment ko apne daayre mein nahi leta jo abhi employment dhoondh rahi hain [[livelaw-kerala-hc-hema-draft-law-2025]].

Ye bench ki ek oral tippani thi, koi ruling nahi, aur is point par behes hai. Act ka text us aurat ko protect karta hai jo "of any age whether employed or not" ho, yaani kisi bhi umar ki, naukri par ho ya na ho, aur jise workplace par harass kiya gaya ho [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Ab ek situation sochiye: 22 saal ki ek aurat Kochi aati hai, ek aise audition ke liye jiske baare mein use WhatsApp group se pata chala. Jo aadmi usse milta hai, woh uska employer nahi hai. Film ki shayad abhi unit hi nahi bani, committee toh door ki baat hai. Agar woh role ki keemat bata de, toh wahan koi committee nahi jiska darwaza woh khatkhata sake, aur mana karte hi audition khatam.

## Paanch saal 'inactive or silent'

Committee ne apni report December 2019 mein Kerala sarkar ko di. Public ne ise 19 August 2024 ko dekha, kareeb paanch saal baad, aur woh bhi tab jab State Information Commission ne ise release karne ka order diya aur Kerala High Court ne us order ke khilaaf challenge reject kar diya [[nie-hema-report-release-2024]].

10 September 2024 ko High Court ne state se seedha poocha: 31 December 2019 se ab tak sarkar "inactive or silent", yaani nishkriya ya chup, kyun rahi? State police chief ke paas February 2021 se report ki copy thi. Court ne order diya ki poori, unredacted report Special Investigation Team (SIT) ko saunpi jaaye [[livelaw-kerala-hc-hema-sit-2024]].

Committee jin aurton ke paas gayi, unme se kai shuru mein bolne se darti thin, kyunki "they were afraid they would lose their jobs", yaani unhe kaam chhin jaane ka darr tha. Panel ko ye darr pehle ajeeb laga, phir usne maana ki ye "well-founded" tha, yaani bilkul jaayaz, aur kaha ki use gawahon aur unke kareebi rishtedaaron ki safety ki chinta hai [[bbc-hema-report-2024]]. Aurton ne ye risk lekar gawahi di, aur saalon tak unhe kuch hota hua nahi dikha. Agli aurat isse yahi seekhti hai ki chup rehna behtar hai.

## Actors ki association, jisme committee hi nahi thi

2018 mein Women in Cinema Collective (WCC) Kerala High Court gaya. Uski daleel thi ki Association of Malayalam Movie Artists (AMMA) par Vishaka guidelines aur POSH Act ke tahat Internal Complaints Committee ya grievance cell banana zaroori hai, aur uske paas aisa kuch nahi tha. 2022 tak collective ka kehna tha ki AMMA aur Cine and TV Artists Association mein ab bhi koi cell nahi bana [[livelaw-kwc-wcc-pil-2022]].

Court ne 17 March 2022 ko jawab diya. Usne kaha ki AMMA jaisi film associations actors ki employer nahi hain, isliye Act un par sirf unke apne office staff ke liye laagu hota hai. Committee ki zimmedaari har production unit ki hai, film dar film. AMMA ne apni taraf se committee banane ki peshkash ki [[kerala-hc-wcc-judgment-2022]].

Ab yahi logic audition par laga kar dekhiye. Unit ek film ke liye banti hai aur film ke baad khatam ho jaati hai. Jo associations har film ke baad bhi bani rehti hain, woh employer nahi hain. Casting unit banne se pehle hoti hai. Audition dene wali aurat ke liye law jis body ko saaf taur par baandhta hai, usne use abhi hire nahi kiya, aur ho sakta hai woh abhi bani hi na ho.

## Report ke baad: SIT aur cinema law ka vaada

August 2024 ke baad jo badla, uski list chhoti hai: court ke order par unredacted report SIT ke paas gayi [[livelaw-kerala-hc-hema-sit-2024]]. 8 October 2025 ko Kerala sarkar ne High Court ko bataya ki SIT ki investigation poori ho chuki hai, aur entertainment industry ke liye ek draft law November ke pehle hafte mein state cabinet ke saamne rakha jaayega [[livelaw-kerala-hc-hema-draft-law-2025]].

Hum ye confirm nahi kar paaye ki SIT ke kitne cases chargesheet tak pahunche, ya November 2025 ke baad draft law approve ya enact hua ya nahi. Jab tak law laagu nahi hota, ye vaada bas ek sarkari vakeel ka courtroom mein diya gaya bayaan hai.

Kerala ka cinema law vaise bhi sirf Kerala ke cinema ko cover karega. Auditions aur look tests television, advertising aur modelling mein bhi hote hain, har state mein, aur court ne jis gap ka naam liya woh ek national law mein hai.

## Agar aap audition de rahe hain: kya protection hai

Ye general information hai, legal advice nahi.

- Police ka raasta job par depend nahi karta. Sexual favours ki demand ko Supreme Court ki 1997 ki Vishaka guidelines ke time se sexual harassment maana gaya hai [[sc-vishaka-1997]]. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita ke Section 75 ke tahat sexual harassment ek crime hai, jisme teen saal tak ki jail ho sakti hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Iski report kisi bhi police station mein ki ja sakti hai, chahe ghatna kahin bhi hui ho [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- POSH ke raaste par behes ho sakti hai, isliye use zaroor aazmaiye. Jahan establishment mein das se kam workers hain aur isliye Internal Committee nahi hai, ya complaint employer ke khilaaf hai, wahan complaint district ki Local Committee ko jaati hai, likhit mein, incident ke teen mahine ke andar [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Complaint sarkar ke portal SHe-Box par bhi file ki ja sakti hai [[shebox]].
- Record banaiye. Likh kar poochiye ki audition kis production ke liye hai aur kaun le raha hai. Har message sambhal kar rakhiye. Ek insaan ko bata kar jaaiye ki aap kahan ja rahe hain.

india-sex-education-timeline-2005-2024.en:
Imagine you were 14 and in school in Maharashtra in April 2007. The state government had just banned sex education in the state's schools, and with it the CBSE's sex-education textbooks [[thehindu-maharashtra-sex-ed-ban-2007]]. Nobody asked you. In under 20 years, India's school sex education has been launched, banned, attacked, folded into a wellness programme and finally recommended by the Supreme Court. Here is each turn, and where it leaves a teenager in 2026.

## 2005-2006: a programme for every school

**2005.** The Ministry of Human Resource Development and the National AIDS Control Organisation (NACO) launch the Adolescence Education Programme (AEP) for schools [[srhm-pattathil-roy-sexuality-education-india-2023]]. Its curriculum is rolled out in 2006-07.

**2006.** Two quieter starts. Jharkhand begins Udaan, a state-run adolescence education programme in its schools [[unesco-cse-global-status-report-2021]]. And the health system opens Adolescent Reproductive and Sexual Health clinics, the forerunners of today's Adolescent Friendly Health Centres [[nhm-afhc-page-2026]]. Both will outlast the storm that follows.

## 2007: Maharashtra and the wave of bans

**Late March 2007.** After Shiv Sena and BJP legislators raise the issue in the Assembly, Maharashtra bans sex education in the state's schools. It bans the CBSE's sex-education textbooks in the state and drops a planned adolescence life-skills programme [[thehindu-maharashtra-sex-ed-ban-2007]].

**May 2007.** Reuters counts six states, including Gujarat, Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and Karnataka, that have banned the curriculum or refused to run it, calling it too explicit or against Indian culture. Madhya Pradesh says sex education has "no place in Indian culture" and plans yoga instead. NACO's head, Sujatha Rao, warns that the bans put young lives at risk, and has asked MPs who are also doctors whether they are "more concerned about culture than the lives of young people" [[reuters-nbc-india-states-ban-sex-ed-2007]].

**2007, in all.** Counts differ. A 2020 study in the journal Reproductive Health says 12 states banned all AEP and comprehensive sexuality education programmes amid the backlash [[reprodhealth-plesons-jharkhand-cse-2020]]. There is no official list, and the study does not name them, so the honest figure is a range: six to 12 states. Our investigation of the 2007 culture argument tests their reasons against the evidence.

## 2012-2014: a child-protection law, a health programme, a minister's verdict

**14 November 2012.** The POCSO Act comes into force. It defines a child as anyone under 18 and protects boys and girls alike [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Sexual offences against children now have their own law, five years after several states banned the classes that could help children name those offences.

**7 January 2014.** The Health Ministry launches the Rashtriya Kishor Swasthya Karyakram (RKSK) to reach 253 million adolescents. It widens adolescent health beyond sexual and reproductive health to nutrition, injuries, violence including gender-based violence, mental health and substance misuse [[nhm-adolescent-health-rksk-page-2026]]. It is run by the health ministry, not the education system.

**June 2014.** Union Health Minister Harsh Vardhan denies proposing a ban on sex education. But he calls the original 2007 programme "so-called sex education" marked by "crudity", and says chief ministers had objected to it before it was modified [[thehindu-harsh-vardhan-sex-education-2014]]. Seven years after the bans, the objection comes from the Union health minister himself.

## 2018-2021: the evidence arrives, the bans stay, a new programme

**2018.** The UN's revised technical guidance, resting mainly on two evidence reviews (87 studies in 2008; 22 systematic reviews and 77 randomised trials in 2016), states that sexuality education does not increase sexual activity, sexual risk-taking or STI/HIV infection rates [[unesco-itgse-2018]].

**2019.** In Jharkhand, Udaan has reached over one million students by September [[unesco-cse-global-status-report-2021]]. We found no reliable, up-to-date list of which states still keep the AEP out.

**2019-21.** The fifth National Family Health Survey finds only 20.1% of young women and 28.5% of young men aged 15-24 have comprehensive knowledge of HIV/AIDS, down from 22% and 32% in 2015-16 [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

**12 February 2020.** The curriculum of the School Health and Wellness Programme is released under Ayushman Bharat. Two teachers in every government and government-aided school, preferably one man and one woman, are to be trained as "Health and Wellness Ambassadors" and run one-hour weekly sessions on 11 health themes for 24 weeks a year, starting with schools in aspirational districts [[pib-school-health-ambassador-curriculum-2020]]. UNESCO notes that Udaan served as a blueprint for the national initiative [[unesco-cse-global-status-report-2021]]. The programme that survived the backlash in one state became the model for the country, this time framed as "health and wellness". The themes include gender equality, reproductive health and HIV prevention, safety against violence and injuries, and safe use of the internet and social media; none is titled consent or sexuality. Private schools are not covered.

**Also 2020.** The National Education Policy 2020 does not once use the words "sex", "sexuality", "puberty" or "menstruation" in its 66 pages, though it lists "health and nutrition" and "gender sensitivity" among skills for every student [[nep-2020-full-text]]. Adolescent sexual health stays with health-ministry programmes.

## 2024-2026: the Supreme Court steps in

**23 September 2024.** In the Just Rights for Children Alliance case on child sexual exploitation material, the Supreme Court recommends comprehensive sex education that gives young people a clear understanding of consent and the impact of exploitation, and suggests an expert committee on health and sex education and POCSO awareness for children from an early age [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]]. These are suggestions, not orders, and we could not confirm whether such a committee exists.

**October 2025.** The Health Ministry renames Adolescent Friendly Health "Clinics" as "Centres", saying the word "clinic" carried stigma and a teenager's visit was "looked upon with suspicion". It says about 1.7 crore adolescents used the services in 2024-25, a figure that may count visits rather than people [[mohfw-afhc-rename-2025]].

**30 January 2026.** In Dr Jaya Thakur v. Government of India, the Supreme Court makes menstrual health part of the right to life. It orders functional, separate toilets with water, free sanitary napkins and safe disposal in all schools, and calls for gender-responsive curricula and for boys and male teachers to be sensitised [[livelaw-sc-jaya-thakur-judgment-2026]]. We track state compliance separately.

**Where it stands in November 2026.** We found no national rule that has changed what UNESCO reported in 2021: responsibility for sexuality education in India is decentralised to the states [[unesco-cse-global-status-report-2021]]. The national school programme is meant for government and aided schools only, and depends on two teachers being trained and given the time. Who decides what your child learns? State governments, which have banned and adopted programmes before; school managements; and now, through recommendations, the Supreme Court. Until one of them makes it a guarantee, what a teenager learns depends on where they happen to go to school.
india-sex-education-timeline-2005-2024.hg:
Socho, April 2007 mein tum 14 saal ke the aur Maharashtra ke kisi school mein padhte the. State sarkar ne abhi-abhi state ke schools mein sex education par ban laga diya tha, aur saath mein CBSE ki sex education textbooks par bhi [[thehindu-maharashtra-sex-ed-ban-2007]]. Tumse kisi ne nahi poocha. 20 saal se kam mein India ki school sex education launch hui, ban hui, us par hamle hue, woh ek wellness programme mein sama gayi, aur aakhir mein Supreme Court ne uski recommendation di. Yahan har mod hai, aur yeh bhi ki 2026 mein teenagers kahan khade hain.

## 2005-2006: har school ke liye ek programme

**2005.** Ministry of Human Resource Development aur National AIDS Control Organisation (NACO) ne schools ke liye Adolescence Education Programme (AEP) launch kiya [[srhm-pattathil-roy-sexuality-education-india-2023]]. Iska curriculum 2006-07 mein schools tak pahuncha.

**2006.** Do cheezein chupchaap shuru hui. Jharkhand ne apne schools mein Udaan shuru kiya, jo state sarkar ka apna adolescence education programme hai [[unesco-cse-global-status-report-2021]]. Aur health system ne Adolescent Reproductive and Sexual Health clinics khole, jinse aaj ke Adolescent Friendly Health Centres bane [[nhm-afhc-page-2026]]. Aage jo toofan aaya, yeh dono usse bach nikle.

## 2007: Maharashtra aur ban ki lehar

**March 2007 ka aakhir.** Assembly mein Shiv Sena aur BJP ke legislators ke mudda uthane ke baad Maharashtra ne state ke schools mein sex education ban kar di. State mein CBSE ki sex education textbooks ban hui, aur adolescence life-skills ka jo programme aane wala tha, woh cancel ho gaya [[thehindu-maharashtra-sex-ed-ban-2007]].

**May 2007.** Reuters ne chhe states gine jinhone curriculum ban kiya ya chalane se mana kiya; inme Gujarat, Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh aur Karnataka the. Wajah: yeh bahut explicit hai, ya Indian culture ke khilaaf hai. Madhya Pradesh ne kaha ki sex education ki "Indian culture mein koi jagah nahi" hai, aur iski jagah yoga laane ka plan bataya. NACO ki head Sujatha Rao ne chetaya ki yeh ban young logon ki jaan ko khatre mein daal rahe hain; woh un MPs se, jo khud doctor bhi the, pooch chuki thi ki kya woh young logon ki zindagi se zyada culture ki fikr karte hain [[reuters-nbc-india-states-ban-sex-ed-2007]].

**2007, kul milakar.** Gintiyan alag-alag hain. Journal Reproductive Health mein 2020 mein chhapi ek study ke mutabik us backlash mein 12 states ne AEP aur comprehensive sexuality education ke saare programmes band kar diye [[reprodhealth-plesons-jharkhand-cse-2020]]. Koi official list nahi hai aur study states ke naam nahi deti, isliye imaandaar figure ek range hai: chhe se 12 states. 2007 ke culture wale argument par hamari investigation in wajahon ko evidence par parakhti hai.

## 2012-2014: child protection ka kanoon, ek health programme, aur minister ki raay

**14 November 2012.** POCSO Act lagoo hua. Isme 18 saal se kam umar ka har insaan child hai, aur ladke-ladkiyon dono ko barabar protection milta hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Bachchon ke khilaaf sexual offences ke liye ab alag kanoon tha. Par yeh tab aaya jab paanch saal pehle hi kai states woh classes band kar chuke the jo bachchon ko aise offences pehchaanna sikha sakti thi.

**7 January 2014.** Health Ministry ne Rashtriya Kishor Swasthya Karyakram (RKSK) launch kiya, 253 million (25.3 crore) adolescents tak pahunchne ke target ke saath. Isne adolescent health ko sirf sexual aur reproductive health tak seemit nahi rakha: nutrition, injuries, violence (gender-based violence bhi), mental health aur substance misuse bhi jode [[nhm-adolescent-health-rksk-page-2026]]. Yeh programme health ministry chalati hai, education system nahi.

**June 2014.** Union Health Minister Harsh Vardhan ne is baat se inkaar kiya ki unhone sex education par ban ka proposal diya tha. Lekin unhone 2007 ke original programme ko "so-called sex education" kaha, jisme "crudity" thi, aur kaha ki chief ministers ne ispar aitraaz kiya tha, jiske baad ise badla gaya [[thehindu-harsh-vardhan-sex-education-2014]]. Ban ke saat saal baad, aitraaz ab khud Union health minister ki taraf se tha.

## 2018-2021: evidence aaya, ban bane rahe, naya programme aaya

**2018.** UN ki revised technical guidance aayi, jo mainly do reviews par tiki hai: 2008 ka review (87 studies) aur 2016 ka review (22 systematic reviews aur 77 randomised trials). Guidance kehti hai: sexuality education se na sexual activity badhti hai, na risky behaviour, na STI/HIV infection [[unesco-itgse-2018]].

**2019.** Jharkhand ka Udaan September tak 10 lakh se zyada students tak pahunch chuka tha [[unesco-cse-global-status-report-2021]]. Kaun se states ab bhi AEP ko bahar rakhe hue hain, iski koi bharosemand, taaza list humein nahi mili.

**2019-21.** NFHS-5, yaani fifth National Family Health Survey, mein pata chala ki 15-24 saal ki sirf 20.1% young women aur 28.5% young men ko HIV/AIDS ki comprehensive knowledge hai, jabki 2015-16 mein yeh 22% aur 32% thi [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

**12 February 2020.** Ayushman Bharat ke tahat School Health and Wellness Programme ka curriculum jaari hua. Har government aur government-aided school mein do teachers ko, ho sake toh ek male aur ek female, "Health and Wellness Ambassadors" ki training milni hai. Woh saal mein 24 hafte, har hafte ek ghante ke sessions mein 11 health themes padhayenge, aur shuruaat aspirational districts ke schools se hogi [[pib-school-health-ambassador-curriculum-2020]]. UNESCO ke mutabik yeh national initiative Udaan ke blueprint par bani [[unesco-cse-global-status-report-2021]]. Yaani jo programme ek state mein backlash jhelkar bacha raha, wahi poore desh ka model bana, is baar "health and wellness" ke roop mein. Themes mein gender equality, reproductive health aur HIV se bachaav, violence aur injuries se safety, aur internet aur social media ka safe use shaamil hain; kisi theme ka naam consent ya sexuality nahi hai. Private schools isme cover nahi hote.

**2020 mein hi.** National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 ke 66 pages mein "sex", "sexuality", "puberty" ya "menstruation" shabd ek baar bhi nahi aata, halaanki isme "health and nutrition" aur "gender sensitivity" ko har student ki zaroori skills mein gina gaya hai [[nep-2020-full-text]]. Adolescent sexual health ka kaam Health Ministry ke programmes ke bharose hi raha.

## 2024-2026: Supreme Court aage aaya

**23 September 2024.** Child sexual exploitation material se jude Just Rights for Children Alliance case mein Supreme Court ne comprehensive sex education programmes ki recommendation di, jo young logon ko consent aur exploitation ke asar ki saaf samajh dein. Court ne suggest kiya ki Union sarkar ek expert committee banane par vichaar kare, jo bachchon ke liye chhoti umar se health aur sex education aur POCSO awareness ka programme banaye [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]]. Yeh sirf suggestions hain, aise orders nahi jinhe maanna zaroori ho, aur aisi koi committee bani ya nahi, hum confirm nahi kar paaye.

**October 2025.** Health Ministry ne Adolescent Friendly Health "Clinics" ka naam badalkar "Centres" kar diya, yeh kehkar ki "clinic" shabd ke saath stigma juda tha aur wahan jaane walon ko shak ki nazar se dekha jaata tha. Ministry ke mutabik 2024-25 mein lagbhag 1.7 crore adolescents ne yeh services li; ho sakta hai yeh ginti logon ki nahi, visits ki ho [[mohfw-afhc-rename-2025]].

**30 January 2026.** Dr Jaya Thakur v. Government of India case mein Supreme Court ne kaha ki menstrual health right to life ka hissa hai. Court ne saare schools ko ladkiyon aur ladkon ke liye alag, chaalu toilets, paani, free sanitary napkins aur safe disposal ka intezaam karne ko kaha, aur gender-responsive curriculum aur ladkon va male teachers ki sensitisation ki baat ki [[livelaw-sc-jaya-thakur-judgment-2026]]. States ise kitna maan rahe hain, us par hamari alag coverage hai.

**November 2026 mein haal.** UNESCO ne 2021 mein kaha tha ki India mein sexuality education ki zimmedari states par chhodi gayi hai [[unesco-cse-global-status-report-2021]], aur humein aisa koi national rule nahi mila jisne yeh badla ho. National school programme sirf government aur aided schools ke liye hai, aur yeh is par tika hai ki do teachers ko training aur time mila ya nahi. Toh tum, ya tumhare chhote bhai-behen, kya seekhenge, yeh kaun tay karta hai? State sarkarein, jo pehle programmes ban bhi kar chuki hain aur apna bhi chuki hain; school managements; aur ab, recommendations ke zariye, Supreme Court. Jab tak inme se koi ise guarantee nahi banata, tab tak teenager kya seekhega, yeh is par tika rahega ki woh kis school mein padhta hai.

izzat-honour-language-rape-shame.en:
"Uski izzat lut gayi." Read the sentence the way a grammar teacher would. The subject is her honour. The verb says it was looted. The man who committed the crime does not appear anywhere. This is how Hindi and Hinglish have long described a rape, in headlines, film dialogue and family kitchens: as the theft of something she was supposed to guard.

The silence that follows rape is not a guess; it shows up in national survey data. In the National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5), 77.2% of women aged 18-49 who had faced physical or sexual violence had never sought help or told anyone [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

## 'Izzat', 'muh dikhane layak nahi': the words we inherit

The vocabulary is large. "Izzat lut gayi." "Ghar ki izzat mitti mein mil gayi." "Kahin muh dikhane layak nahi rahi." "Ab isse shaadi kaun karega?" English has its own set: she was "ravished", "violated", "dishonoured", "ruined".

All of them rest on one idea: that a family's standing is stored in the bodies of its women, and that a daughter's job is to keep it intact until marriage. Once that is believed, three things follow from a rape. The loss is hers, because the thing taken was hers to protect. The injured party becomes the family, whose name is now "spoiled". And the event stops being a crime to report and becomes a secret to manage.

Notice what these phrases never do. They never make the offender the subject. "He raped her" is a sentence about what a man did. "Her izzat was looted" is a sentence about what a woman no longer has.

## When a court retired 'chaste' and 'fallen'

Indian judgments used the same register, in English. On 16 August 2023 the Supreme Court released its Handbook on Combating Gender Stereotypes, with a foreword by Chief Justice D.Y. Chandrachud, to help judges identify and stop using language built on stereotypes about women [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

Its glossary takes "chaste woman", "fallen woman", "seductress" and "woman of easy virtue" and replaces every one of them with a single word: "woman". For "ravished" and "violated" it gives "sexually harassed / assaulted or raped" [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

Those entries are the English cousins of izzat. "Chaste" and "fallen" sort women into those who have honour to lose and those who supposedly have none left, and then weigh the crime by which shelf she stood on. The handbook's one-word answer removes the shelf.

## 'Marriage is not a remedy'

If rape is a loss of honour, then honour can in theory be returned, and the logic of izzat has always known how: marry her to the man. The handbook lists that belief among the stereotypes judges must reject. "Rape does not taint the honour of the survivor / victim or her family," it says, and: "Marriage is not a remedy to the violence of rape." [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]

Look at who the honour argument protects. In 96.8% of rape cases registered in India in 2024, 28,597 of 29,536, the offender was known to the victim [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. These are police-registered cases only, but the pattern is clear: the man is usually a relative, a neighbour, a partner or someone else she knows. When a family says "ghar ki izzat ka sawaal hai", the person kept safe by the silence is very often someone the family knows.

## How honour talk produces silence

In 2021 a Delhi court, deciding a #MeToo defamation case, put the mechanism on record: "Most of the women who suffer abuse do not speak up about it or against it for simple reason 'The Shame' or the social stigma attached with the sexual harassment and abuse." [[delhi-court-metoo-defamation-judgment-2021]]

The surveys agree. Besides the 77.2% who told no one, NFHS-5 found that only 14.1% of women who had faced physical or sexual violence ever sought help [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. A 2022 paper in BMC Public Health cites estimates that only about 1% of victims of sexual violence in India report it to the authorities, and gives reasons such as false beliefs that place responsibility on the victim, and stigma around rape and female sexuality [[bmcph-dandona-rape-data-2022]]. That figure is an estimate taken from earlier studies, not a measurement.

Imagine a 19-year-old in Kanpur who tells her mother that a relative raped her. The first reply is "kisi ko mat batana". In four words the crime has been refiled as her secret. Meanwhile a medical clock is running: HIV post-exposure medicine has to start within 72 hours [[who-pep]], and emergency contraception works for up to 5 days, the sooner the better [[who-ec]]. Honour does not only delay justice. It delays medicine.

The same script gags boys, men, and transgender and queer survivors, who are told that being assaulted makes them less of a man, or that nobody will believe them.

## Words to use instead

| Instead of | Say |
|---|---|
| "Uski izzat lut gayi" | "Us aadmi ne uska rape kiya" (he raped her) |
| "Ghar ki izzat ka sawaal hai" | "Yeh tumhari galti nahi hai. Hum tumhare saath hain." |
| "Muh dikhane layak nahi rahi" | "Sharm usko aani chahiye jisne yeh kiya." |
| "Ab shaadi kaun karega?" | "Tumhe abhi kya chahiye: doctor, police, ya bas koi sunne wala?" |
| "Ravished", "violated", "lost her honour" | "Raped", "sexually assaulted" |

In the news, make the accused the subject of the sentence. On "survivor" or "victim", the handbook says both terms apply and the person's own preference decides [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

On WhatsApp, do not forward a name, a photo, a street or a school "so that people know". Publishing anything that identifies a rape survivor is a crime under Section 72 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, punishable with up to two years in prison [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. This is general information, not legal advice.

At home, the next time someone says a girl's izzat is gone, ask one calm question back: what did she do? The honest answer is nothing. The disgrace in a rape belongs to the person who committed it, and our sentences should put it there.
izzat-honour-language-rape-shame.hg:
"Uski izzat lut gayi." Is sentence ko waise padhiye jaise grammar ki teacher padhti. Subject hai uski izzat. Verb kehta hai ki woh loot li gayi. Jis aadmi ne crime kiya, woh is sentence mein kahin nahi hai. Hindi aur Hinglish mein rape ko barson se aise hi bola gaya hai, headlines mein, film ke dialogues mein aur ghar ki rasoi mein: jaise koi aisi cheez chori ho gayi jiski rakhwali uski apni zimmedari thi.

Rape ke baad ki chuppi koi andaaza nahi hai; woh national survey data mein dikhti hai. National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5) mein 18-49 saal ki jin auraton ne physical ya sexual violence jheli thi, unme se 77.2% ne kabhi madad nahi maangi aur kisi ko bataya tak nahi [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

## 'Izzat', 'muh dikhane layak nahi': woh shabd jo humein virasat mein mile

Shabdon ki list lambi hai. "Izzat lut gayi." "Ghar ki izzat mitti mein mil gayi." "Kahin muh dikhane layak nahi rahi." "Ab isse shaadi kaun karega?" English ke paas apna set hai: aurat "ravished" hui, "violated" hui, "dishonoured" hui, "ruined" ho gayi.

In sabke neeche ek hi soch hai: ki parivaar ki izzat uski auraton ke shareer mein rakhi hoti hai, aur beti ka kaam hai use shaadi tak sambhaal kar rakhna. Ek baar ye maan liya, toh rape ke baad teen baatein apne aap nikal aati hain. Nuksaan ladki ka hai, kyunki jo cheez gayi uski rakhwali usi ko karni thi. Peedit parivaar ban jaata hai, jiska naam ab "kharaab" ho gaya. Aur jo hua woh report karne wala crime nahi rehta, sambhaal kar chhupaane wala raaz ban jaata hai.

Dhyaan dijiye ki ye phrases kya kabhi nahi karte. Ye offender ko kabhi sentence ka subject nahi banate. "Us aadmi ne uska rape kiya" batata hai ki ek aadmi ne kya kiya. "Uski izzat lut gayi" batata hai ki ek aurat ke paas ab kya nahi raha.

## Jab ek court ne 'chaste' aur 'fallen' ko retire kiya

Indian judgments bhi isi sur mein likhe jaate rahe, bas English mein. 16 August 2023 ko Supreme Court ne apni Handbook on Combating Gender Stereotypes jaari ki, jiska foreword Chief Justice D.Y. Chandrachud ne likha, taaki judges auraton ke baare mein stereotypes par tiki bhasha ko pehchaan sakein aur use likhna band karein [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

Iski glossary "chaste woman", "fallen woman", "seductress" aur "woman of easy virtue" ko uthati hai aur har ek ki jagah ek hi shabd rakh deti hai: "woman". "Ravished" aur "violated" ki jagah woh deti hai "sexually harassed / assaulted or raped" [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

Ye entries izzat ke hi English rishtedaar hain. "Chaste" aur "fallen" auraton ko do khaanon mein baant dete hain, ek woh jinke paas khone ke liye izzat hai aur ek woh jinke paas kehne ko kuch bacha hi nahi, aur phir crime ko is se tola jaata hai ki woh kis khaane mein khadi thi. Handbook ka ek shabd wala jawab woh khaana hi hata deta hai.

## 'Marriage is not a remedy'

Agar rape izzat ka nuksaan hai, toh izzat 'wapas' bhi laayi ja sakti hai, aur izzat ka logic hamesha se jaanta hai kaise: ladki ki shaadi usi aadmi se kara do. Handbook is soch ko un stereotypes mein ginti hai jinhe judges ko khaarij karna hai. Woh kehti hai, "Rape does not taint the honour of the survivor / victim or her family", yaani rape se survivor ya uske parivaar ki izzat par koi daag nahi lagta, aur: "Marriage is not a remedy to the violence of rape", yaani shaadi rape ki hinsa ka ilaaj nahi hai [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

Ab dekhiye ki izzat wali daleel kise bachati hai. 2024 mein India mein darj rape cases mein se 96.8% mein, yaani 29,536 mein se 28,597 mein, offender victim ka jaan-pehchaan wala tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Ye sirf police mein darj cases hain, lekin pattern saaf hai: woh aadmi aksar koi rishtedaar, padosi, partner ya koi aur jaanne wala hota hai. Jab parivaar kehta hai "ghar ki izzat ka sawaal hai", toh is chuppi se jo insaan bachta hai woh bahut baar parivaar ka hi koi jaanne wala hota hai.

## Izzat ki baatein chuppi kaise paida karti hain

2021 mein Delhi ki ek court ne ek #MeToo defamation case ka faisla dete hue ye mechanism record par rakha: "Most of the women who suffer abuse do not speak up about it or against it for simple reason 'The Shame' or the social stigma attached with the sexual harassment and abuse." Yaani abuse jhelne wali zyadatar auratein ek seedhi si wajah se nahi bolti: 'sharm', ya woh kalank jo samaaj sexual harassment aur abuse ke saath jod deta hai [[delhi-court-metoo-defamation-judgment-2021]].

Surveys bhi yahi kehte hain. Jin 77.2% ne kisi ko nahi bataya, unke alawa NFHS-5 ne paaya ki physical ya sexual violence jhelne wali auraton mein se sirf 14.1% ne kabhi madad maangi [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. BMC Public Health mein 2022 mein chhapa ek paper un estimates ka hawala deta hai jinke mutabik India mein sexual violence ke sirf about 1% victims, yaani kareeb sau mein se ek, authorities ko report karte hain. Paper kuch wajahein bhi ginata hai, jaise woh galat maanyataayein jo zimmedari victim par daal deti hain, aur rape aur auraton ki sexuality se juda stigma [[bmcph-dandona-rape-data-2022]]. Ye figure purani studies se liya gaya ek estimate hai, koi naap nahi.

Sochiye Kanpur ki ek 19 saal ki ladki ke baare mein, jo apni maa ko batati hai ki ek rishtedaar ne uska rape kiya. Pehla jawab milta hai: "kisi ko mat batana". Chaar shabdon mein crime ko uska apna raaz bana diya gaya. Udhar ek medical ghadi chal rahi hai: HIV se bachaav ki dawa (PEP) 72 ghante ke andar shuru karni hoti hai [[who-pep]], aur emergency contraception 5 din tak kaam karti hai, jitni jaldi utna behtar [[who-ec]]. Izzat sirf insaaf mein der nahi karwati. Woh ilaaj mein bhi der karwati hai.

Yahi script ladkon, mardon aur transgender aur queer survivors ka bhi muh band karti hai. Unhe kaha jaata hai ki assault hona unhe 'kam mard' bana deta hai, ya ki un par koi yakeen nahi karega.

## Iski jagah kya bolein

| Iski jagah | Ye kahiye |
|---|---|
| "Uski izzat lut gayi" | "Us aadmi ne uska rape kiya" |
| "Ghar ki izzat ka sawaal hai" | "Yeh tumhari galti nahi hai. Hum tumhare saath hain." |
| "Muh dikhane layak nahi rahi" | "Sharm usko aani chahiye jisne yeh kiya." |
| "Ab shaadi kaun karega?" | "Tumhe abhi kya chahiye: doctor, police, ya bas koi sunne wala?" |
| "Ravished", "violated", "lost her honour" | "Raped", "sexually assaulted" |

News mein accused ko sentence ka subject banaiye. "Survivor" ya "victim" par handbook kehti hai ki dono shabd sahi hain aur jis insaan ke saath hua hai, uski apni pasand maani jaaye [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

WhatsApp par kisi ka naam, photo, gali ya school "taaki logon ko pata chale" keh kar forward mat kijiye. Aisi koi bhi cheez publish karna jisse rape survivor ki pehchaan ho sake, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita ke Section 72 ke under crime hai, jisme do saal tak ki jail ho sakti hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Ye general information hai, legal advice nahi.

Ghar par, agli baar jab koi kahe ki ladki ki izzat chali gayi, toh shaanti se ek sawaal wapas poochiye: usne kya kiya? Sachcha jawab hai: kuch nahi. Rape mein sharm usi ki hai jisne crime kiya, aur humare sentences ko sharm wahin rakhni chahiye.

media-identifying-rape-survivors-kathua-.en:
On 18 April 2018, the Delhi High Court ordered 12 media houses to pay Rs 10 lakh each into Jammu and Kashmir's victim compensation fund. They had revealed the identity of the eight-year-old girl raped and murdered in Kathua. Their lawyers told the court the outlets had acted on a mistaken belief: that a victim who had died could be named [[thehindu-delhi-hc-kathua-media-2018]]. The law they broke was not new. Disclosing a rape victim's identity had been a crime in India since 25 December 1983 [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. Knowing the rule is the easy part. The harder question is whether newsrooms recognise every way a story can break it.

## April 2018: 12 media houses and a costly belief

Nobody had to file a petition. The High Court took up the matter on its own [[thehindu-delhi-hc-kathua-media-2018]].

Look closely at the mistake. The outlets did not claim the child's name was needed for the story. They assumed her protection ended with her life. That assumption treats privacy as something only the living can use, and it turns the gravest cases, the ones where the victim cannot speak for herself, into the ones with the least protection. Each of the 12 was told to pay separately, into a fund for victims.

## 'Even if she is dead': the December 2018 ruling

Eight months later, the Supreme Court settled the very question the outlets had got wrong. In Nipun Saxena v. Union of India, decided on 11 December 2018, it said no person may print or publish, in print, electronic or social media, a rape victim's name, "or even in a remote manner disclose any facts which can lead to the victim being identified" [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]].

On the Kathua mistake it was explicit. When the victim is dead or of unsound mind, her identity must not be disclosed even with her family's authorisation, unless a Sessions Judge decides that disclosure is justified [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]].

The court also dealt with the argument that a movement needs a name. Without her true identity being revealed, it noted, "Nirbhaya" became "the most effective symbol of protest the country has ever known" [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. A campaign can carry a case, a place and a demand. It does not need her face.

The rule now sits in Section 72 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS): publishing a survivor's name, or anything that may make her identity known, carries up to two years in prison and a fine. An adult survivor may authorise it in writing [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. That choice is hers to make, not a channel's or a page's. This is general information, not legal advice.

## Identification without a name: ranks, villages, relatives

The 2018 judgment described two reports that identified survivors without naming them. One said the victim had topped her state board exam and named the state; it "would not require rocket science" to find her, the court said. The other was TV footage that blurred her face but clearly showed her relatives, her neighbours and the name of her village. Both, the court held, disclosed her identity [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]].

Those examples come from TV and print. The same test applies to what a phone makes easy today:

- a reel shot outside her house, with the street sign in the frame;
- a screenshot of the FIR, though the court ordered that FIRs in rape and POCSO cases must not be put in the public domain [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]];
- her college, course and year, or her father's job and the name of his shop;
- a "justice for" hashtag built from her first name;
- the name of the accused when he is her father, uncle or brother.

The last is the easiest to miss. In 2024 police recorded 2,134 rape cases in which the accused was a family member, and in 96.8% of all rape cases the accused was someone the survivor knew [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Name the accused father, and you have named the daughter.

## Children: what POCSO Section 23 forbids

For children, the law spells it out. Section 23 of the POCSO Act bars any media report from disclosing a child victim's name, address, photograph, family details, school or neighbourhood. The punishment is six months to a year in prison, a fine, or both, and the publisher or owner is jointly liable; only the Special Court can allow disclosure, and only in the child's interest [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. It protects boys exactly as it protects girls [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

Read that list the way an editor should. A school uniform in a video is the school. A shot of the lane is the neighbourhood. "Daughter of a local shopkeeper" is family details. And joint liability means an owner cannot simply blame a stringer.

## A newsroom checklist, and the survivor-or-victim question

Police registered just 11 cases under Section 72 in the BNS's first six months, July to December 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The protection that works is the one applied before you publish. For every story, post or reel:

- **Recognition test.** Could her neighbours, classmates, colleagues or relatives recognise her? If yes, cut it.
- **Frame check.** Look past the blurred face: house, street, shop sign, uniform, vehicle, relatives.
- **No documents.** No FIR, medical record or court paper that carries her details.
- **The accused.** If he is a relative or a close neighbour, leave his name out.
- **Death and consent.** Death does not end the protection, and her family's consent does not lift it; only a Sessions Judge can allow disclosure.
- **Her choice.** If an adult survivor wants to speak publicly, get her written authorisation and agree exactly what she wants shown.
- **Words.** The Supreme Court's 2023 handbook replaces "ravished" and "violated" with "sexually harassed", "assaulted" or "raped", and "forcible rape" with plain "rape" [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

Last, survivor or victim? The same handbook says both terms apply, and that if the person has a preference, it should be respected [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. So ask her, or the lawyer or organisation supporting her. It is a small question that holds the whole checklist: the story is about her, but how she is seen is not yours to decide.
media-identifying-rape-survivors-kathua-.hg:
18 April 2018 ko Delhi High Court ne 12 media houses ko order diya ki har ek Rs 10 lakh Jammu and Kashmir ke victim compensation fund mein jama kare. Inhone Kathua mein rape aur murder ki shikaar aath saal ki bachchi ki identity reveal kar di thi. Unke lawyers ne court mein kaha ki outlets ek galatfehmi mein the: unhe laga tha ki jis victim ki maut ho chuki hai, uska naam chhapa ja sakta hai [[thehindu-delhi-hc-kathua-media-2018]]. Jo law unhone toda, woh naya nahi tha. India mein rape victim ki identity kholna 25 December 1983 se crime hai [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. Rule jaanna aasaan hissa hai. Mushkil sawaal yeh hai ki kya newsrooms pehchaante hain ki ek story kitne tareekon se yeh rule tod sakti hai.

## April 2018: 12 media houses aur ek mehngi galatfehmi

Kisi ko petition file nahi karni padi. High Court ne khud yeh matter uthaya [[thehindu-delhi-hc-kathua-media-2018]].

Galti ko dhyaan se dekhiye. Outlets ne yeh claim nahi kiya ki story ke liye bachchi ka naam zaroori tha. Unhone bas maan liya ki uski protection uski zindagi ke saath khatam ho gayi. Is soch mein privacy sirf zinda logon ka haq ban jaati hai, aur sabse gambhir cases, jinme victim apne liye bol hi nahi sakti, unhi mein use sabse kam protection milti hai. 12 mein se har ek ko alag se pay karne ko kaha gaya, aur yeh paisa victims ke fund mein jaana tha.

## 'Maut ke baad bhi': December 2018 ka faisla

Aath mahine baad Supreme Court ne theek wahi sawaal settle kar diya jis par outlets galat the. 11 December 2018 ko Nipun Saxena v. Union of India mein court ne kaha ki koi bhi insaan print, electronic ya social media mein rape victim ka naam publish nahi kar sakta, aur "even in a remote manner", yaani door se bhi, aisi koi baat nahi bata sakta jisse uski pehchaan ho jaye [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]].

Kathua wali galti par court bilkul clear tha. Agar victim ki maut ho chuki hai ya uski mental condition theek nahi hai, toh family ki permission se bhi uski identity nahi kholi ja sakti, jab tak Sessions Judge yeh decide na karein ki disclosure justified hai [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]].

Court ne us argument ka bhi jawab diya ki movement ko naam chahiye. Court ne yaad dilaya ki asli identity saamne aaye bina hi "Nirbhaya" desh mein protest ka ab tak ka sabse effective symbol bani [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. Campaign ko case chahiye, jagah chahiye, demand chahiye. Uska chehra nahi chahiye.

Ab yeh rule Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke Section 72 mein hai: survivor ka naam, ya koi bhi aisi baat publish karna jisse uski identity khul sakti hai, uski saza do saal tak ki jail aur fine hai. Adult survivor chahe toh likh kar iski permission de sakti hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Yeh choice uski hai, kisi channel ya page ki nahi. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Naam ke bina pehchaan: rank, gaon, rishtedaar

2018 ke judgment mein court ne do aisi reports ka zikr kiya jinhone naam liye bina survivor ki pehchaan khol di. Ek mein likha tha ki ladki ne apne state ke board exam mein top kiya tha, aur state ka naam bhi diya tha; court ne kaha, use dhoondhne ke liye "rocket science" nahi chahiye. Doosri TV footage thi jisme victim ka chehra blur tha, lekin uske rishtedaar, padosi aur gaon ka naam saaf dikh rahe the. Court ne kaha ki dono hi baar uski identity disclose ho gayi [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]].

Yeh examples TV aur print ke hain. Lekin aaj phone se jo kaam aasaan ho gaye hain, un par bhi yahi test lagta hai:

- uske ghar ke bahar shoot hui reel, jiske frame mein gali ka board dikh raha ho;
- FIR ka screenshot, jabki court ka order hai ki rape aur POCSO cases ki FIR public domain mein nahi daali jayengi [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]];
- uska college, course aur year, ya uske papa ka kaam aur unki dukaan ka naam;
- uske first name se bana "justice for..." hashtag;
- accused ka naam, jab woh uska papa, chacha ya bhai ho.

Aakhri wali baat sabse aasaani se chhoot jaati hai. 2024 mein police ne rape ke 2,134 aise cases register kiye jinme accused family ka hi member tha, aur sabhi rape cases mein se 96.8% mein accused koi aisa tha jise survivor jaanti thi [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Accused papa ka naam chhapa, toh samajhiye beti ka naam chhap gaya.

## Bachche: POCSO Section 23 kya mana karta hai

Bachchon ke liye law aur bhi clear hai. POCSO Act ka Section 23 kehta hai ki koi bhi media report victim bachche ka naam, address, photo, family details, school ya mohalla disclose nahi kar sakti. Iski saza chhe mahine se ek saal tak ki jail, fine, ya dono hai, aur publisher ya owner bhi barabar ka zimmedaar hai; identity batane ki permission sirf Special Court de sakti hai, aur woh bhi tabhi jab isme bachche ki bhalai ho [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Yeh law ladkon ko bhi bilkul waise hi protect karta hai jaise ladkiyon ko [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

Is list ko ek editor ki nazar se padhiye. Video mein dikhi school uniform matlab school. Gali ka ek shot matlab mohalla. "Ek local dukaandaar ki beti" matlab family details. Aur joint liability ka matlab hai ki owner saara blame kisi stringer par daal kar nahi bach sakta.

## Newsroom checklist, aur 'survivor ya victim' ka sawaal

BNS ke pehle chhe mahino mein, July se December 2024 tak, police ne Section 72 mein sirf 11 cases register kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Jo protection sach mein kaam karti hai, woh publish karne se pehle wali hai. Har story, post ya reel se pehle:

- **Recognition test.** Kya uske padosi, classmates, colleagues ya rishtedaar use pehchaan lenge? Agar haan, toh woh hissa kaat dijiye.
- **Frame check.** Blur chehre se aage dekhiye: ghar, gali, dukaan ka board, uniform, gaadi, rishtedaar.
- **Koi documents nahi.** FIR, medical record ya court ka koi bhi paper jisme uski details hon, bilkul nahi.
- **Accused.** Agar woh rishtedaar ya paas ka padosi hai, toh uska naam mat chhapiye.
- **Maut aur consent.** Maut se yeh protection khatam nahi hoti, aur family ki haan se bhi khatam nahi hoti; disclosure ki permission sirf Sessions Judge de sakte hain.
- **Uski choice.** Agar koi adult survivor khud saamne aakar bolna chahe, toh uski written permission lijiye aur pehle tay kar lijiye ki woh kya-kya dikhana chahti hai.
- **Words.** Supreme Court ki 2023 handbook kehti hai ki "ravished" aur "violated" ki jagah "sexually harassed", "assaulted" ya "raped" likhiye, aur "forcible rape" ki jagah sirf "rape" [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

Aakhir mein, survivor ya victim? Wahi handbook kehti hai ki dono terms theek hain, aur agar insaan ki apni koi preference hai toh uski respect honi chahiye [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. Toh unse poochiye, ya unke lawyer ya support kar rahi organisation se. Yeh chhota sa sawaal poori checklist ka saar hai: story uske baare mein hai, lekin woh kaise dikhegi, yeh decide karna aapka kaam nahi.

metoo-delay-posh-three-month-limit.en:
In late 2018, India's #MeToo movement gathered momentum in the Hindi film industry and spread within weeks, as women in the news media, films and government publicly made allegations of sexual harassment [[bbc-hema-report-2024]]. Many of those accounts were about things that had happened years earlier. The law built for workplace complaints, the POSH Act, counts time differently: three months from the incident, extendable by three more [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. This is general information, not legal advice.

## 2018: old stories, new courage

The Supreme Court's Vishaka guidelines came on 13 August 1997 [[sc-vishaka-1997]]. The POSH Act was enacted on 22 April 2013 and came into force on 9 December 2013, more than 15 years later [[sc-aureliano-fernandes-2023]]. A woman harassed before 1997 had no complaints committee to go to at all.

A law on paper did not make speaking cheap. The Supreme Court observed in 2023 that women harassed at work are often reluctant to report it, and that "many of them even drop out from their job" [[sc-aureliano-fernandes-2023]]. A Delhi court named the other reason in two words: "The Shame" [[delhi-court-metoo-defamation-judgment-2021]].

What changed in 2018 was not the law but the number of women speaking at once.

## The POSH clock: three months plus three

The Act's first deadline falls on the complainant. A written complaint must be made within three months of the incident. If there was a series of incidents, the three months run from the last one. The committee can extend the limit by up to three more months, but only if it records in writing that circumstances prevented the woman from complaining in time [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].

| Step | Time the Act allows |
|---|---|
| Written complaint | 3 months from the incident, or the last in a series |
| Extension by the committee | up to 3 more months, reasons in writing |
| Inquiry | 90 days |
| Inquiry report to the employer | 10 days |
| Employer acts on the report | 60 days |
| Appeal | 90 days |

So the outer limit is six months, and the second half is at a committee's discretion. If the same person is still harassing you, the clock restarts with each incident.

Consider a 26-year-old analyst in Gurugram whose manager's comments began in her first month. She says nothing for a year, because he signs her appraisal. If his last comment was in March, her three months run from March. But if she resigned in January and found the words only the following December, the committee's door is shut. The POSH route is also open only to women; a harassed man or transgender worker has no committee clock at all.

## 'Even after decades': what a court said in 2021

In October 2018 a Union minister of state filed a criminal defamation case in a Delhi court against a woman journalist who had accused him of sexual harassment. Several other women also accused him; he denied the allegations and resigned days later [[livelaw-ramani-acquittal-2021]]. We name neither: no court has found him guilty of any offence, and she is a woman who reported harassment.

On 17 February 2021 the court acquitted her. One sentence of the judgment answers the clock directly: "The woman has a right to put her grievance at any platform of her choice and even after decades" [[delhi-court-metoo-defamation-judgment-2021]].

The POSH deadline is a rule for one forum, the workplace committee. The court's sentence is about a person's right to speak. The first can expire while the second does not. The Supreme Court's 2023 handbook on gender stereotypes makes a related point about rape: the belief that a woman who delays reporting is lying is a stereotype [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

Two cautions. This is a trial court's ruling, so other courts are not bound by it. And the former minister's appeal, admitted by the Delhi High Court in January 2022, was listed for final hearing on 24 September 2026; we could not confirm what happened that day [[livelaw-akbar-appeal-2026]].

## Speaking late: the routes that remain

The police. Sexual harassment of a woman is a crime, punishable under Section 75 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita with up to three years in prison [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Acts committed before 1 July 2024, when the new code came into force, fall under the older Indian Penal Code [[air-new-criminal-laws-2024]]. Whether an old incident can still be taken to the police, and whether any other claim is possible, are questions for a lawyer. A complaint can be given at any police station [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Be realistic about speed. In 2024 courts convicted in 41.9% of the sexual harassment trials they completed, and 1,22,888 such cases were still pending at the end of the year [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Speaking. To a friend, a counsellor, a lawyer or the public. This is the route the 2021 verdict protected, and the one that carries the risk below.

## The defamation risk, and how to weigh it

In India defamation can be prosecuted as a crime, and then the person who spoke becomes the accused, as the journalist did in 2018. The 2018 case shows what even winning costs: filed in October 2018, decided in February 2021, and an appeal listed for final hearing more than five years after the verdict [[livelaw-akbar-appeal-2026]].

So weigh it deliberately:

- Decide what you want: an apology, his removal, a warning to others, or to be heard. Not every aim needs his name in public.
- Say only what you can stand behind as your own experience, and keep what supports it: messages, emails, diary entries, the people you told at the time.
- Speak to a lawyer before you post, not after. Legal services authorities give free legal aid [[nalsa]].

If an old incident still weighs on your sleep or your work, Tele-MANAS offers free counselling round the clock on 14416 [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].

The law allows three months. People take years. A court has said the right to speak does not expire, and it is worth planning how you use it.
metoo-delay-posh-three-month-limit.hg:
2018 ke aakhir mein India ka #MeToo movement Hindi film industry mein zor pakadne laga aur kuch hi hafton mein phail gaya, jab news media, films aur sarkar mein kaam karne wali aurton ne khul kar sexual harassment ke ilzaam lagaye [[bbc-hema-report-2024]]. Inme se kai baatein saalon purani ghatnaon ke baare mein thin. Workplace complaints ke liye bana law, yaani POSH Act, waqt ko alag tarah se ginta hai: incident se teen mahine, jo teen mahine aur badh sakte hain [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Ye general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## 2018: purani kahaniyan, nayi himmat

Supreme Court ki Vishaka guidelines 13 August 1997 ko aayin [[sc-vishaka-1997]]. POSH Act 22 April 2013 ko bana aur 9 December 2013 ko laagu hua, yaani 15 saal se bhi zyada baad [[sc-aureliano-fernandes-2023]]. 1997 se pehle harass hui aurat ke paas jaane ke liye koi complaints committee thi hi nahi.

Kaagaz par law aa jaane se bolna sasta nahi ho gaya. Supreme Court ne 2023 mein kaha ki kaam ki jagah par harass hone wali aurtein aksar report karne se jhijhakti hain, aur "many of them even drop out from their job", yaani kai toh naukri hi chhod deti hain [[sc-aureliano-fernandes-2023]]. Delhi ki ek court ne doosri wajah do shabdon mein batayi: "The Shame", yaani sharm [[delhi-court-metoo-defamation-judgment-2021]].

2018 mein law nahi badla tha. Badli thi ek saath bolne wali aurton ki ginti.

## POSH ki clock: teen mahine plus teen

Act ki pehli deadline complaint karne wali par hi aati hai. Likhit complaint incident ke teen mahine ke andar deni hoti hai. Agar incidents ki series thi, toh teen mahine aakhri incident se gine jaate hain. Committee ye limit teen mahine tak aur badha sakti hai, lekin tabhi jab woh likh kar record kare ki haalaat ne aurat ko waqt par complaint karne se roka [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].

| Step | Act kitna waqt deta hai |
|---|---|
| Likhit complaint | incident se, ya series ke aakhri incident se, 3 mahine |
| Committee ka extension | 3 mahine tak aur, wajah likhit mein |
| Inquiry | 90 din |
| Inquiry report employer ko | 10 din |
| Employer ka report par action | 60 din |
| Appeal | 90 din |
