Yaani bahari seema chhe mahine hai, aur uska doosra aadha hissa committee ki marzi par hai. Agar wahi insaan aapko ab bhi harass kar raha hai, toh har incident ke saath clock dobara shuru hoti hai.

Sochiye Gurugram ki ek 26 saal ki analyst ke baare mein, jiske manager ke comments uske pehle hi mahine se shuru ho gaye. Woh ek saal tak kuch nahi kehti, kyunki uska appraisal wahi sign karta hai. Agar manager ka aakhri comment March mein tha, toh uske teen mahine March se gine jaayenge. Lekin agar usne January mein resign kar diya aur bolne ke shabd use agle December mein mile, toh committee ka darwaza band ho chuka hai. POSH ka raasta vaise bhi sirf aurton ke liye khula hai; harass hue kisi aadmi ya transgender worker ke liye committee ki koi clock hai hi nahi.

## 'Even after decades': 2021 mein ek court ne kya kaha

October 2018 mein ek Union minister of state ne Delhi ki ek court mein us woman journalist ke khilaaf criminal defamation ka case kiya jisne un par sexual harassment ka ilzaam lagaya tha. Kai aur aurton ne bhi un par ilzaam lagaye; unhone ilzaamon se inkaar kiya aur kuch din baad istifa de diya [[livelaw-ramani-acquittal-2021]]. Hum dono mein se kisi ka naam nahi lete: kisi court ne unhe kisi offence ka doshi nahi paaya hai, aur woh ek aurat hain jinhone harassment report kiya.

17 February 2021 ko court ne journalist ko bari kar diya. Faisle ki ek line seedhe clock ka jawab deti hai: "The woman has a right to put her grievance at any platform of her choice and even after decades", yaani aurat ko haq hai ki woh apni shikaayat apni pasand ke kisi bhi platform par, dashkon baad bhi, rakhe [[delhi-court-metoo-defamation-judgment-2021]].

POSH ki deadline ek forum ka rule hai: workplace committee ka. Court ki line insaan ke bolne ke haq ke baare mein hai. Pehli cheez expire ho sakti hai, doosri nahi. Supreme Court ki 2023 ki gender stereotypes wali handbook rape ke baare mein isse judi baat kehti hai: ye maanna ki der se report karne wali aurat jhooth bol rahi hai, ek stereotype hai [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

Do saavdhaaniyan. Ye ek trial court ka faisla hai, isliye doosri courts is par chalne ke liye bandhi nahi hain. Aur purane minister ki appeal, jise Delhi High Court ne January 2022 mein admit kiya tha, 24 September 2026 ko final hearing ke liye list hui thi; us din kya hua, ye hum confirm nahi kar paaye [[livelaw-akbar-appeal-2026]].

## Der se bolna: jo raaste bache hain

Police. Aurat ka sexual harassment ek crime hai, jisme Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita ke Section 75 ke tahat teen saal tak ki jail ho sakti hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Naya code 1 July 2024 ko laagu hua; usse pehle ki ghatnaon par purana Indian Penal Code lagta hai [[air-new-criminal-laws-2024]]. Koi purani ghatna ab bhi police ke paas le jaayi ja sakti hai ya nahi, aur koi aur claim mumkin hai ya nahi, ye sawaal vakeel se poochne ke hain. Complaint kisi bhi police station mein di ja sakti hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Raftaar ko lekar realistic rahiye. 2024 mein courts ne sexual harassment ke jitne trials poore kiye, unme se 41.9% mein conviction hui, aur saal ke aakhir mein aise 1,22,888 cases pending the [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Bolna. Kisi dost se, counsellor se, vakeel se, ya public mein. Yahi woh raasta hai jise 2021 ke faisle ne protect kiya, aur isi mein neeche wala risk hai.

## Defamation ka risk, aur use kaise taulein

India mein defamation par criminal case ho sakta hai, aur tab bolne wala hi accused ban jaata hai, jaise 2018 mein journalist bani. 2018 ka case dikhata hai ki jeetne ki bhi keemat hoti hai: October 2018 mein case file hua, February 2021 mein faisla aaya, aur appeal faisle ke paanch saal se zyada baad final hearing ke liye list hui [[livelaw-akbar-appeal-2026]].

Isliye soch-samajh kar tauliye:

- Tay kariye ki aap kya chahti hain: maafi, uska hataya jaana, doosron ko chetavni, ya bas ye ki aapki baat suni jaaye. Har maqsad ke liye uska naam public mein lena zaroori nahi.
- Wahi kahiye jo aapka apna anubhav hai aur jis par aap tiki reh sakti hain, aur jo use support kare woh sambhal kar rakhiye: messages, emails, diary ki entries, woh log jinhe aapne us waqt bataya tha.
- Post karne se pehle vakeel se baat kariye, baad mein nahi. Legal services authorities free legal aid deti hain [[nalsa]].

Agar koi purani ghatna ab bhi aapki neend ya kaam par bhaari pad rahi hai, toh Tele-MANAS 14416 par chaubees ghante free counselling deta hai [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].

Law teen mahine deta hai. Logon ko saal lag jaate hain. Ek court keh chuki hai ki bolne ka haq expire nahi hota; use kaise istemaal karna hai, iski planning karna samajhdari hai.

night-shifts-women-employer-duties.en:
Indian labour law long dealt with the risks of the night by keeping women out of it. That is changing. By early 2026 around 22 states and union territories allowed women to work night shifts in factories, 33 allowed it in commercial establishments, and 17 had lifted bans on women in industries classed as "hazardous", according to the Economic Survey 2025-26 [[es-2025-26-employment-chapter]].

A permission is not a protection. Here is what an employer owes a woman who works after dark, and how she can insist on it.

## Night work opens up: 22, 33 and 17

The three numbers describe jobs the law used to close to women: the night line in a factory, the late counter in a mall, work in plants labelled hazardous. India needs them to open. In 2023-24 only 28.0% of urban women aged 15 and above were in the labour force [[mospi-plfs-annual-2023-24]]. The International Labour Office estimated in 2017 that in middle-income countries, the group that includes India, limited access to safe transport lowers a woman's probability of taking part in the labour market by 5.7 percentage points, and abuse, harassment or discrimination at work by 2.0 points [[ilo-weso-trends-women-2017]]. These are cross-country estimates, not Indian measurements, but the direction is plain.

That is why the permissions usually come with conditions. Uttar Pradesh's night-shift rules, for example, require employer-provided transport, CCTV surveillance and security personnel [[es-2025-26-employment-chapter]]. Conditions differ by state, so the first document to ask for is your own state's order.

## The RG Kar warning

The case that showed what is at stake did not happen in a factory. On 9 August 2024 a trainee doctor was raped and murdered at RG Kar Medical College and Hospital in Kolkata. On 20 August the Supreme Court, taking up the case on its own, set up a National Task Force on the safety of medical professionals [[livelaw-rg-kar-task-force-2024]].

"If women cannot go to a place of work and feel safe, we are denying them equal opportunity," Chief Justice D.Y. Chandrachud said in court, as LiveLaw reported his words. The Court's order added: "The nation cannot await a rape or murder for real changes on the ground" [[livelaw-rg-kar-task-force-2024]].

Hospitals never shut, and women have always worked nights in them. Letting women in after dark and making the place safe after dark are two different jobs, and the second can be left undone for years.

## Transport is part of the workplace

Imagine a 22-year-old who joins the night line at an electronics plant near Noida. Her shift ends at 2 am. The company cab drops five workers, and because she lives farthest, the last stretch is just her and a male colleague, who starts commenting on her body. The next day a supervisor tells her it happened "outside work".

The POSH Act of 2013 says otherwise. It defines the workplace to include "any place visited by the employee arising out of or during the course of employment including transportation provided by the employer" [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Harassment in the company cab is workplace harassment, and her complaint goes to the same committee as one from the shop floor.

Note the words "provided by the employer". The Act makes the company answerable for a vehicle it arranges. It does not itself order the company to arrange one. That duty, where it exists, comes from the state's night-shift conditions.

On a bus or auto you arrange yourself, the remedy you can count on is the criminal law: sexual harassment is an offence under Section 75 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), punishable with up to three years, or up to one year for sexually coloured remarks [[indiacode-bns-2023]], and it can be reported at any police station [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

## A complaints committee that works at 2 am

Every employer must set up an Internal Committee, headed by a woman employed at a senior level, with at least two employee members and one outside member from an NGO or familiar with sexual harassment issues. At least half the members must be women. Workplaces with fewer than ten workers are covered by the district's Local Committee [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. An employer who fails to constitute a committee can be fined up to Rs 50,000, doubled for a repeat offence, which can also cost the business its licence [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].

That is the law on paper. In May 2023 the Supreme Court found "serious lapses in the enforcement" of the Act and warned that unless it was strictly enforced it would "remain an empty formality" [[sc-aureliano-fernandes-2023]]. In August 2025, LiveLaw reported, the Court was told that only the Andaman and Nicobar Islands had completed the district-wise survey of committees it had ordered in December 2024 [[livelaw-posh-district-survey-2025]]. Nobody can say how many workplaces now opening a night shift have a committee at all.

A night shift adds its own test. A committee whose members all work days, reachable through an email read on Monday, is little use to a woman harassed at 2 am on a Saturday. The Act is silent on how a committee is reached at night, so ask.

The committee also hears complaints only from women. Men, transgender and queer workers are harassed at night too. Ask whether the company's own policy covers them.

## What to ask before you take a night shift

- **The order.** Which state notification allows this shift, and what does it require on transport, security and cameras?
- **The cab.** Is transport provided both ways, to your door? Who decides the drop order?
- **The committee.** Who are the members, and how do you reach one of them during the shift?
- **The night in-charge.** Who on site at 2 am has the authority to move a harasser off your line or out of your cab?

Ask in writing and keep the replies. A complaint to the committee must also be in writing, within three months of the incident [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. An employer who cannot answer these questions has taken the permission and skipped the duties. This is general information, not legal advice.
night-shifts-women-employer-duties.hg:
Indian labour law ne lambe samay tak raat ke khatron ka ek hi ilaaj rakha: auraton ko raat se hi bahar rakho. Ab yeh badal raha hai. Economic Survey 2025-26 ke mutabik, early 2026 tak lagbhag 22 states aur union territories auraton ko factories mein night shift ki ijaazat de chuke the, 33 ne commercial establishments mein yeh ijaazat di thi, aur 17 ne "hazardous" maani jaane wali industries mein auraton par laga ban hata diya tha [[es-2025-26-employment-chapter]].

Lekin permission milna protection milna nahi hai. Yahan samjhiye ki andhere ke baad kaam karne wali aurat ke prati employer ki kya zimmedaari hai, aur woh ise kaise maang sakti hai.

## Night work khul raha hai: 22, 33 aur 17

Yeh teen numbers un jobs ke baare mein hain jo law ne auraton ke liye band rakhi thin: factory ki night line, mall ka late counter, "hazardous" kahe jaane wale plants ka kaam. India ko zaroorat hai ki yeh jobs khulen. 2023-24 mein 15 saal aur usse upar ki urban auraton mein se sirf 28.0% labour force mein thin [[mospi-plfs-annual-2023-24]]. International Labour Office ne 2017 mein estimate kiya ki middle-income countries mein, jis group mein India aata hai, safe transport tak kam pahunch aurat ke labour market mein hissa lene ki probability 5.7 percentage points ghata deti hai, aur kaam par abuse, harassment ya discrimination 2.0 points [[ilo-weso-trends-women-2017]]. Yeh cross-country estimates hain, India ke apne measurements nahi, lekin disha saaf hai.

Isiliye permissions ke saath aksar conditions aati hain. Jaise Uttar Pradesh ke night-shift rules employer ki taraf se transport, CCTV surveillance aur security personnel zaroori karte hain [[es-2025-26-employment-chapter]]. Conditions har state mein alag hain, isliye sabse pehle apne state ka order maangiye.

## RG Kar ki chetavni

Jis case ne dikhaya ki daav par kya hai, woh kisi factory mein nahi hua. 9 August 2024 ko Kolkata ke RG Kar Medical College and Hospital mein ek trainee doctor ka rape aur murder hua. 20 August ko Supreme Court ne khud is case ko uthaate hue medical professionals ki safety par ek National Task Force banayi [[livelaw-rg-kar-task-force-2024]].

LiveLaw ki report ke mutabik Chief Justice D.Y. Chandrachud ne court mein kaha: "If women cannot go to a place of work and feel safe, we are denying them equal opportunity." Yaani agar auratein kaam ki jagah par jaakar safe mehsoos nahi kar saktin, toh hum unhe barabar ka mauka dene se inkaar kar rahe hain. Court ke order mein likha tha: "The nation cannot await a rape or murder for real changes on the ground" [[livelaw-rg-kar-task-force-2024]].

Hospitals kabhi band nahi hote, aur auratein unmein hamesha se raat ko kaam karti aayi hain. Andhere ke baad auraton ko andar aane dena aur andhere ke baad us jagah ko safe banana, yeh do alag kaam hain, aur doosra kaam saalon tak adhoora chhoda ja sakta hai.

## Transport bhi workplace ka hissa hai

Sochiye, 22 saal ki ek ladki Noida ke paas ek electronics plant ki night line join karti hai. Uski shift raat 2 baje khatam hoti hai. Company cab paanch workers ko drop karti hai, aur kyunki uska ghar sabse door hai, aakhri hisse mein cab mein sirf woh aur ek male colleague bachte hain, jo uske body par comments karne lagta hai. Agle din supervisor kehta hai ki yeh toh "kaam ke bahar" hua.

2013 ka POSH Act kuch aur kehta hai. Uski definition mein workplace ke andar "any place visited by the employee arising out of or during the course of employment including transportation provided by the employer" bhi aata hai, yaani employer ka diya hua transport bhi [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Company cab mein harassment workplace harassment hai, aur uski complaint usi committee ke paas jaayegi jiske paas shop floor ki complaint jaati hai.

"Provided by the employer" shabdon par dhyan dijiye. Act company ko us gaadi ke liye jawabdeh banata hai jiska intezaam company karti hai. Act khud company ko gaadi dene ka order nahi deta. Yeh duty, jahan hai, state ki night-shift conditions se aati hai.

Jis bus ya auto ka intezaam aap khud karti hain, wahan bharose ka raasta criminal law hai: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke Section 75 ke tahat sexual harassment crime hai, jismein teen saal tak ki saza ho sakti hai, aur sexually coloured remarks par ek saal tak [[indiacode-bns-2023]], aur iski report kisi bhi police station mein ki ja sakti hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

## Aisi complaints committee jo raat 2 baje bhi kaam kare

Har employer ko Internal Committee banani hoti hai. Iski head senior level par kaam karne wali ek aurat hoti hai, ismein kam se kam do employee members hote hain, aur ek bahar ka member jo kisi NGO se ho ya sexual harassment ke issues ko samajhta ho. Kam se kam aadhe members auratein honi chahiye. Jin workplaces mein das se kam workers hain, woh district ki Local Committee ke under aate hain [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Jo employer committee nahi banata, us par Rs 50,000 tak ka fine lag sakta hai, dobara galti par double, aur business ka licence bhi ja sakta hai [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].

Yeh kaagaz par likha law hai. May 2023 mein Supreme Court ne Act ke "serious lapses in the enforcement" paaye, aur chetaya ki agar ise sakhti se laagu nahi kiya gaya toh yeh "remain an empty formality" hoga, yaani bas ek khokhli formality [[sc-aureliano-fernandes-2023]]. LiveLaw ki report ke mutabik, August 2025 mein Court ko bataya gaya ki December 2024 mein jis district-wise survey ka order diya gaya tha, woh sirf Andaman and Nicobar Islands ne poora kiya tha [[livelaw-posh-district-survey-2025]]. Koi nahi bata sakta ki jo workplaces ab night shift khol rahe hain, unmein se kitnon mein committee hai bhi.

Night shift ek alag test jodti hai. Jis committee ke saare members din mein kaam karte hain, aur jis tak pahunchne ka raasta ek email hai jo Monday ko padha jaata hai, woh us aurat ke kisi kaam ki nahi jise Saturday raat 2 baje harass kiya gaya. Act is par chup hai ki raat ko committee tak kaise pahuncha jaaye, isliye poochhiye.

Committee sirf auraton ki complaints sunti hai. Raat ko men, transgender aur queer workers ke saath bhi harassment hota hai. Poochhiye ki company ki apni policy unhe cover karti hai ya nahi.

## Night shift lene se pehle kya poochhen

- **Order.** Kaun sa state notification is shift ki ijaazat deta hai, aur transport, security aur cameras par kya zaroori karta hai?
- **Cab.** Kya transport dono taraf milega, ghar ke darwaze tak? Drop order kaun tay karta hai?
- **Committee.** Members kaun hain, aur shift ke dauraan unmein se kisi tak kaise pahunchen?
- **Night in-charge.** Raat 2 baje site par kiske paas yeh authority hai ki harasser ko aapki line ya cab se hata sake?

Likhit mein poochhiye aur jawab sambhaal kar rakhiye. Committee ko complaint bhi likhit mein deni hoti hai, ghatna ke teen mahine ke andar [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Jo employer in sawaalon ka jawab nahi de sakta, usne permission le li hai aur duties chhod di hain. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

office-harassment-rarely-reaches-police.en:
The National Crime Records Bureau's (NCRB) figures for where sexual harassment is reported begin in 2017. That year police across India recorded 479 cases at work or office premises [[ncrb-cii-2018]]. In 2024 they recorded 388 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. That is about one police case a day for all of India's offices combined. The figure says little about how much harassment happens at work, and a great deal about where complaints go.

## Eight years of office numbers

| Year | Cases | Year | Cases |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2017 | 479 | 2021 | 418 |
| 2018 | 401 | 2022 | 419 |
| 2019 | 504 | 2023 | 381 |
| 2020 | 485 | 2024 | 388 |

The line barely moves [[ncrb-cii-2018]] [[ncrb-cii-2021]] [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. It peaks at 504 in 2019, slips to 485 and 418 in the lockdown years of 2020 and 2021, and has stayed between 381 and 419 since. Over the same period urban women's labour force participation rose from 20.4% in 2017-18 to 28.0% in 2023-24 [[mospi-plfs-annual-2023-24]]. The police count did not follow.

The series has limits. These are FIRs only, each counted once under its most serious offence, so harassment that is part of a graver case is filed elsewhere. The 2024 report shortens the label from "work or office premises" to "office premises", and from July 2024 shops, factories and homes get a line of their own, so the 2024 figure may not cover exactly what earlier years did. The series counts harassment of women only; a man or a transgender person harassed in an office is not in it. And the place column is blunt: of the 15,609 sexual harassment cases registered in 2024, 12,592, or 81%, sit under "other places" [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Three states with zero

Kerala recorded the most office cases in 2024, with 89, followed by Himachal Pradesh with 58 and Maharashtra with 57. Rajasthan, Odisha and West Bengal recorded none [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

That does not mean three states with harassment-free offices. Odisha's police recorded 549 sexual harassment cases at public places in the second half of 2024, the most in India, and not one in an office [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

A zero measures what was reported and what was written down. NCRB itself warns that a rise in registered crime is not the same as a rise in crime, and that steps such as e-FIR facilities or women's help desks can push the numbers up [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A higher count can mean that more women were heard.

## 512 cases beyond the office

When the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) replaced the Indian Penal Code on 1 July 2024, NCRB added a new head for cases under it: sexual harassment at work premises such as shops, malls, factories and homes. In six months it recorded 512 cases, more than offices produced in the full year [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Until then the statistics had no separate line for a saleswoman, a factory hand or a domestic worker. One possible explanation, which the data alone cannot prove, lies in the law's design. A small shop or a private home has no in-house committee. The complaint goes to the district's Local Committee, and for a domestic worker that committee must forward a prima facie case to the police within seven days [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. There is no internal process to absorb the complaint first.

## A committee or the police? Two different routes

The POSH Act route is internal. A woman gives her employer's Internal Committee a written complaint within three months of the incident, a limit the committee can extend by up to three more. The inquiry must finish within 90 days, the report goes to the employer within 10 days, and the employer must act within 60 days [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. What comes out is workplace action. Unless she also goes to the police, no FIR is written and nothing enters NCRB's tables.

The police route is criminal. Sexual harassment is an offence under Section 75 of the BNS, earlier Section 354A of the IPC, punishable with up to three years, or up to one year for sexually coloured remarks [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Police investigate and a court decides, slowly: courts convicted in 41.9% of the sexual harassment trials they completed in 2024, while 1,22,888 cases, more than nine in ten, were still pending at the end of the year [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Consider a 24-year-old analyst in Pune whose team lead comments on her body and messages her at night. She writes to the Internal Committee. It inquires; the company warns him or moves him. Whatever the result, no police station hears of it.

Many women use neither route. The Supreme Court observed in 2023 that women harassed at work are often reluctant to report, and that "many of them even drop out from their job", partly because they do not know whom to approach and lack confidence in the process [[sc-aureliano-fernandes-2023]]. Behind the 388 are complaints that went to a committee, complaints that went nowhere, and women who resigned.

## When to file an FIR as well

This is general information, not legal advice. The two routes are not either/or: a committee complaint does not stop a woman from going to the police. Go to the police as well when:

- **There is touching or force.** Assault to outrage modesty carries one to five years under Section 74 of the BNS [[indiacode-bns-2023]].
- **He follows you or keeps contacting you after a clear no.** Stalking is an offence under Section 78, punishable with up to three years on a first conviction [[indiacode-bns-2023]].
- **There is no committee, or the harasser is the employer.** The district's Local Committee, the government's SHe-Box portal [[shebox]] and the police are all open to you.
- **You fear for your safety.** In an emergency call 112.

You can report at any police station, whatever area the office is in, or electronically if you sign the complaint within three days, and you must be given a copy of the FIR free of cost [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. The three-month clock belongs to the committee route. If it has run out, ask a lawyer or the Women Helpline about a police complaint.

Use the committee for what it can do quickly: stop the behaviour and protect your job. Use the police for what only a criminal court can do. One office case a day in a country this size is not evidence of safe offices. It is a count of how rarely a complaint leaves the building.
office-harassment-rarely-reaches-police.hg:
National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) ke woh figures jo batate hain ki sexual harassment kahan report hua, 2017 se shuru hote hain. Us saal poore India ki police ne work ya office premises par 479 cases record kiye [[ncrb-cii-2018]]. 2024 mein 388 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yaani India ke saare offices milakar din mein lagbhag ek police case. Yeh figure yeh bahut kam batata hai ki kaam ki jagah par kitna harassment hota hai, aur yeh bahut kuch batata hai ki complaints jaati kahan hain.

## Office ke aath saal ke numbers

| Year | Cases | Year | Cases |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2017 | 479 | 2021 | 418 |
| 2018 | 401 | 2022 | 419 |
| 2019 | 504 | 2023 | 381 |
| 2020 | 485 | 2024 | 388 |

Line lagbhag hilti hi nahi [[ncrb-cii-2018]] [[ncrb-cii-2021]] [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. 2019 mein yeh 504 par sabse upar jaati hai, lockdown wale saalon 2020 aur 2021 mein 485 aur 418 par aati hai, aur uske baad se 381 aur 419 ke beech rahi hai. Isi dauraan urban women ka labour force participation 2017-18 ke 20.4% se badhkar 2023-24 mein 28.0% ho gaya [[mospi-plfs-annual-2023-24]]. Police ka count uske saath nahi badha.

Is series ki apni limits hain. Yeh sirf FIRs hain, aur har FIR ek hi baar, apne sabse serious offence ke neeche gini jaati hai, isliye jo harassment kisi zyada gambhir case ka hissa hai, woh kahin aur darj hota hai. 2024 ki report mein label "work or office premises" se chhota hokar "office premises" ho gaya hai, aur July 2024 se shops, factories aur gharon ki apni alag line hai, isliye 2024 ka figure shayad theek wahi cheez nahi ginta jo pichhle saal ginte the. Series sirf auraton ke harassment ko ginti hai; office mein harass hua koi mard ya transgender insaan ismein hai hi nahi. Aur jagah wala column bhi mota-mota hai: 2024 mein register hue sexual harassment ke 15,609 cases mein se 12,592, yaani 81%, "other places" ke neeche pade hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Teen states jahan count zero hai

2024 mein office cases sabse zyada Kerala mein record hue, 89, uske baad Himachal Pradesh mein 58 aur Maharashtra mein 57. Rajasthan, Odisha aur West Bengal mein ek bhi nahi [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Iska matlab yeh nahi ki in teen states ke offices harassment-free hain. Odisha ki police ne 2024 ke doosre half mein public places par sexual harassment ke 549 cases record kiye, jo India mein sabse zyada the, aur office mein ek bhi nahi [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Zero yeh naapta hai ki kya report hua aur kya likha gaya. NCRB khud chetavni deta hai ki registered crime ka badhna aur crime ka badhna ek hi baat nahi hai, aur e-FIR facilities ya women's help desks jaise kadam numbers ko upar le ja sakte hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Zyada count ka matlab yeh bhi ho sakta hai ki zyada auraton ki baat suni gayi.

## Office ke bahar 512 cases

1 July 2024 ko jab Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ne Indian Penal Code ki jagah li, toh NCRB ne uske cases ke liye ek naya head joda: shops, malls, factories aur gharon jaise work premises par sexual harassment. Chhe mahine mein ismein 512 cases record hue, jo poore saal ke office cases se zyada hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Tab tak statistics mein saleswoman, factory worker ya domestic worker ke liye koi alag line thi hi nahi. Aise workplaces se police tak zyada cases pahunchne ki ek sambhav wajah, jise sirf data se saabit nahi kiya ja sakta, law ka apna design hai. Chhoti dukaan ya private ghar mein koi in-house committee nahi hoti. Complaint district ki Local Committee ke paas jaati hai, aur domestic worker ke case mein us committee ko prima facie case saat din ke andar police ko bhejna hota hai [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Wahan complaint ko pehle andar hi sambhaal lene wala koi internal process nahi hota.

## Committee ya police? Do alag raaste

POSH Act wala raasta internal hai. Aurat incident ke teen mahine ke andar apne employer ki Internal Committee ko likhit complaint deti hai; committee yeh limit teen mahine tak aur badha sakti hai. Inquiry 90 din mein poori honi chahiye, report 10 din mein employer ke paas jaati hai, aur employer ko 60 din ke andar action lena hota hai [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Isse jo nikalta hai, woh workplace ka action hai. Jab tak woh police ke paas bhi nahi jaati, koi FIR nahi likhi jaati aur NCRB ki tables mein kuch nahi aata.

Police wala raasta criminal hai. Sexual harassment BNS ke Section 75 ke tahat offence hai, jo pehle IPC ka Section 354A tha; ismein teen saal tak ki saza hai, aur sexually coloured remarks par ek saal tak [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Police investigate karti hai aur court faisla karta hai, dheere-dheere: 2024 mein jin sexual harassment trials ka faisla hua, unmein se 41.9% mein conviction hua, jabki 1,22,888 cases, yaani das mein se nau se zyada, saal ke aakhir mein bhi pending the [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Sochiye, Pune mein 24 saal ki ek analyst hai jiska team lead uske shareer par comments karta hai aur raat ko messages bhejta hai. Woh Internal Committee ko likhti hai. Committee inquiry karti hai; company use warning deti hai ya uski team badal deti hai. Nateeja jo bhi ho, kisi police station tak yeh baat pahunchti hi nahi.

Bahut si auratein dono mein se koi raasta nahi leti. Supreme Court ne 2023 mein kaha ki workplace par harassment jhelne wali auratein aksar report karne se hichkichati hain, aur "many of them even drop out from their job", yaani kai toh naukri hi chhod deti hain; iski ek wajah yeh hai ki unhe pata nahi hota kiske paas jaana hai, aur process par bharosa nahi hota [[sc-aureliano-fernandes-2023]]. Us 388 ke peeche woh complaints hain jo committee ke paas gayin, woh jo kahin nahi gayin, aur woh auratein jinhone resign kar diya.

## FIR bhi kab karni chahiye

Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi. Yeh dono raaste ek-doosre ki jagah nahi lete: committee mein complaint karne se police ke paas jaane ka raasta band nahi hota. Police ke paas bhi jaiye jab:

- **Chhoona ya zabardasti ho.** Aurat ki modesty outrage karne ke liye assault par BNS ke Section 74 ke tahat ek se paanch saal ki saza hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].
- **Woh aapka peechha kare ya saaf mana karne ke baad bhi contact karta rahe.** Stalking Section 78 ke tahat offence hai, jismein pehli conviction par teen saal tak ki saza ho sakti hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].
- **Committee hai hi nahi, ya harass karne wala khud employer hai.** District ki Local Committee, sarkar ka SHe-Box portal [[shebox]] aur police, teeno raaste aapke liye khule hain.
- **Aapko apni safety ka darr ho.** Emergency mein 112 par call kijiye.

Aap kisi bhi police station mein report kar sakti hain, chahe office kisi bhi area mein ho, ya electronically bhi, agar aap complaint par teen din ke andar sign kar dein, aur FIR ki copy aapko free milni chahiye [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Teen mahine wali ghadi committee wale raaste ki hai. Agar woh nikal chuki hai, toh kisi lawyer ya Women Helpline se police complaint ke baare mein poochhiye.

Committee ka istemaal us kaam ke liye kijiye jo woh jaldi kar sakti hai: harassment rokna aur aapki naukri bachana. Police ka istemaal us kaam ke liye kijiye jo sirf criminal court kar sakta hai. Itne bade desh mein din ka ek office case safe offices ka saboot nahi hai. Yeh is baat ki ginti hai ki complaint building se bahar kitni kam baar nikalti hai.

outrage-cases-versus-typical-rape.en:
Three cases mark how India has talked about rape since 2012: the Delhi gang rape case of that year, the Hyderabad case of 2019 and Kolkata's RG Kar Medical College case of 2024. Each was a rape and a murder. Police keep a separate head for that crime, murder with rape or gang rape, and in 2024 it held 266 cases [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The same year they registered 29,536 cases of rape. In 28,597 of them, 96.8%, the accused was someone the survivor knew [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. India's picture of rape is drawn from its smallest category.

## The cases that become movements

The cases that fill the streets share a pattern. The victim was killed. And the story could be told without a husband, a boyfriend or a relative in it, so the crowd could rage at the accused without recognising anyone it knew.

Such attention moves the state. After the Delhi case, the Justice J.S. Verma Committee was set up in December 2012 and reported on 23 January 2013 [[thehindu-verma-2013]]. After RG Kar, the Supreme Court set up a National Task Force eleven days after the crime [[livelaw-rg-kar-task-force-2024]].

None of this needed a name. In 2018 the Supreme Court observed that "without disclosing her true identity 'Nirbhaya' became the most effective symbol of protest the country has ever known" [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. So anonymity is not what keeps the other cases quiet.

A 2022 study in BMC Public Health notes that under NCRB's principal offence rule, the 2012 Delhi case was itself recorded as murder, not rape [[bmcph-dandona-rape-data-2022]]. The case that defined rape for a generation is not in the rape count.

## The case that never trends: a boyfriend, a husband, a relative

Of the 28,597 cases with a known offender in 2024, 13,879 involved friends, online friends, live-in partners "on the pretext of marriage" or separated husbands. Another 12,584 involved family friends, neighbours, employers or other known persons, and 2,134 involved family members [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. In just 939 cases was the offender unknown or not identified.

Wives are mostly missing even here. In NFHS-5 (2019-21), 82% of ever-married women who had faced sexual violence named their current husband, and 14% a former husband [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Exception 2 to Section 63 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) says sex by a man with his own wife, if she is 18 or older, is not rape. The same section defines rape as an act by a man against a woman, which leaves out adult men and transgender survivors too [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. None of that produces a rape FIR that could trend.

Consider a 23-year-old in Nagpur whose former boyfriend rapes her after she ends the relationship. There is no public crime scene and no stranger. Her identity is protected, as it should be, so a newsroom has nothing to show. Her relatives ask why she met him. His family offers to "settle". Nobody marches. Hers is the typical case.

## What the selection teaches

A country that notices rape mainly when the victim is killed learns three wrong lessons.

**That danger lives outside.** The Supreme Court's 2023 handbook on gender stereotypes lists the belief that rapists are usually strangers as a false stereotype [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. In 2012 itself, offenders were known to the victim in 98.2% of recorded rape cases [[ncrb-cii-2012-snapshots]]. Yet the money followed the street: by July 2026, Safe City projects in eight cities had received Rs 1,686.73 crore from the Nirbhaya Fund, against Rs 1,299.10 crore for One Stop Centres [[theprint-nirbhaya-fund-rajya-sabha-2026]].

**That harsher punishment is the fix.** The Verma Committee advised against the death penalty for rape, noting it "may not have a deterrent effect", and recommended deleting the marital rape exception [[thehindu-verma-2013]]. Parliament followed neither recommendation. The 2013 amendment allowed death where a rape kills the victim or leaves her in a persistent vegetative state, and kept the exception [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]].

**That a rapist is a monster.** So when a woman names a husband, a cousin or a colleague, people who marched for a stranger's victim find reasons to doubt her.

> The march is for the stranger's victim. The register is full of boyfriends, husbands and neighbours.

## 'Instant justice' and what the inquiry found

Anger aimed at monsters ends in a demand to kill them. In 2019, police shot dead four men accused of a rape and murder near Hyderabad before any court had heard evidence. A Supreme Court-appointed commission found that the four were "deliberately fired upon with an intent to cause their death", that three of them were minors, and recommended that all ten officers involved be tried for murder [[livelaw-hyderabad-encounter-commission-2022]]. The men were accused, never tried. No court will now say who committed that crime.

Courts have refused to let anger set the sentence. Commuting the Shakti Mills death sentences in 2021, the Bombay High Court held that a constitutional court cannot award punishment based on public opinion [[barandbench-shakti-mills-hc-2021]]. In January 2025 the Sealdah court gave the RG Kar convict life imprisonment, not death, warning against "the temptation to bow to public pressure or emotional appeals" [[tribune-rg-kar-sentence-2025]]. The CBI has appealed to the Calcutta High Court seeking death.

A bullet or a noose offers nothing in the typical case. A woman reporting her partner or her uncle is not asking for an encounter. She is asking to be believed, and for a trial that ends.

## An outrage that matches the data

When a rape-murder trial finishes, it usually ends in conviction. A rape trial usually does not: the 2024 conviction rate was 24.4%, and 1,85,785 rape cases were awaiting a verdict at the year's end [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Outrage that matched the data would ask for unglamorous things.

- **Judges, prosecutors and forensic labs**, so the waiting cases reach a verdict.
- **An end to the marital rape exception.** As of 20 November 2026 the Supreme Court had not ruled on the challenge [[livelaw-marital-rape-final-hearing-2026]].
- **Police who write down complaints against familiar men.** Failing to record a rape FIR is a crime under Section 199 of the BNS [[indiacode-bns-2023]].
- **Belief at home.** In NFHS-5, of women who had faced physical or sexual violence, 77% never sought help or told anyone [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

The next time a case fills your feed, grieve for it. Then ask about the 28,597.
outrage-cases-versus-typical-rape.hg:
2012 ke baad se India rape ke baare mein jaise baat karta hai, use teen cases ne shape kiya hai: usi saal ka Delhi gang rape case, 2019 ka Hyderabad case, aur 2024 ka Kolkata ka RG Kar Medical College case. Teeno mein rape ke saath murder hua. Police is crime ko ek alag head mein ginti hai, murder with rape ya gang rape, aur 2024 mein is head mein 266 cases the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Usi saal police ne rape ke 29,536 cases register kiye. Inmein se 28,597 mein, yaani 96.8% mein, accused koi aisa tha jise survivor jaanti thi [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. India ke dimaag mein rape ki jo tasveer hai, woh sabse chhoti category se bani hai.

## Woh cases jo movement ban jaate hain

Jo cases sadkon ko bhar dete hain, unmein ek pattern hai. Victim ki jaan gayi. Aur yeh kahani kisi husband, boyfriend ya rishtedaar ke bina sunayi ja sakti thi, isliye bheed accused par gussa kar sakti thi, bina unmein apni jaan-pehchaan ka koi chehra dekhe.

Aisa attention state ko hila deta hai. Delhi case ke baad Justice J.S. Verma Committee December 2012 mein bani aur 23 January 2013 ko usne apni report de di [[thehindu-verma-2013]]. RG Kar case mein Supreme Court ne crime ke gyarah din baad hi ek National Task Force bana di [[livelaw-rg-kar-task-force-2024]].

Iske liye kisi naam ki zaroorat nahi padi. 2018 mein Supreme Court ne kaha ki "without disclosing her true identity 'Nirbhaya' became the most effective symbol of protest the country has ever known", yaani asli pehchaan saamne aaye bina hi 'Nirbhaya' desh ka ab tak ka sabse asardaar protest ka symbol ban gayi [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. Matlab, baaki cases ko jo cheez chup rakhti hai, woh anonymity nahi hai.

BMC Public Health mein chhapi 2022 ki ek study batati hai ki NCRB ke principal offence rule ki wajah se 2012 ka Delhi case khud murder ki tarah record hua, rape ki tarah nahi [[bmcph-dandona-rape-data-2022]]. Jis case ne ek poori generation ke liye rape ka matlab tay kiya, woh rape ki ginti mein hai hi nahi.

## Woh case jo kabhi trend nahi karta: boyfriend, husband, rishtedaar

2024 mein jin 28,597 cases mein offender jaan-pehchaan ka tha, unmein se 13,879 mein woh dost, online friend, "on the pretext of marriage" yaani shaadi ke bahaane wala live-in partner, ya separated husband tha. 12,584 cases mein family friends, padosi, employer ya doosre jaan-pehchaan wale the, aur 2,134 mein family ke members [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Sirf 939 cases mein offender anjaan tha ya uski pehchaan nahi ho paayi.

Patniyan toh is list mein bhi zyada tar gayab hain. NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein jin ever-married women ne sexual violence jhela tha, unmein se 82% ne apne current husband ka naam liya aur 14% ne former husband ka [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ki Section 63 ka Exception 2 kehta hai ki agar patni 18 saal ya usse badi hai, toh pati ka apni patni ke saath sex rape nahi hai. Yahi section rape ko ek aadmi ka ek woman ke khilaaf kiya gaya act maanti hai, isliye adult men aur transgender survivors bhi bahar reh jaate hain [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Is sab mein se kisi ki bhi rape FIR nahi banti jo trend kar sake.

Sochiye, Nagpur ki ek 23 saal ki ladki, jiska former boyfriend relationship khatam karne ke baad uska rape karta hai. Yahan na koi public crime scene hai, na koi stranger. Uski identity protected hai, jaisa hona bhi chahiye, isliye newsroom ke paas dikhane ko kuch nahi hai. Uske rishtedaar poochte hain ki woh usse milne gayi hi kyun. Ladke ki family "settle" karne ka offer deti hai. Koi march nahi nikalta. Aur typical case yahi hai.

## Yeh selection hamein kya sikhata hai

Jo desh rape ko zyada tar tabhi dekhta hai jab victim ki jaan chali jaaye, woh teen galat sabak seekhta hai.

**Ki khatra bahar rehta hai.** Supreme Court ki 2023 ki gender stereotypes wali handbook is soch ko false stereotype ginti hai ki rapist aam taur par stranger hote hain [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. Khud 2012 mein, recorded rape cases ke 98.2% mein offender victim ka jaan-pehchaan wala tha [[ncrb-cii-2012-snapshots]]. Phir bhi paisa sadak ke peeche gaya: July 2026 tak aath cities ke Safe City projects ko Nirbhaya Fund se Rs 1,686.73 crore mil chuke the, jabki One Stop Centres ko Rs 1,299.10 crore [[theprint-nirbhaya-fund-rajya-sabha-2026]].

**Ki sakht sazaa hi ilaaj hai.** Verma Committee ne rape ke liye death penalty ke khilaaf salaah di thi, yeh note karte hue ki iska "may not have a deterrent effect", yaani crime rokne wala asar shayad na ho, aur marital rape exception hataane ki sifaarish ki thi [[thehindu-verma-2013]]. Parliament ne dono mein se koi bhi sifaarish nahi maani. 2013 ke amendment ne wahan death ki ijaazat di jahan rape se victim ki maut ho jaaye ya woh persistent vegetative state mein chali jaaye, aur exception ko jaisa tha waisa rakha [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]].

**Ki rapist ek monster hota hai.** Isliye jab koi woman apne husband, cousin ya colleague ka naam leti hai, toh wahi log us par shak karne ki wajah dhoondh lete hain jo ek stranger ki victim ke liye march mein gaye the.

> March stranger ki victim ke liye nikalta hai. Register boyfriends, husbands aur padosiyon se bhara hai.

## 'Instant justice', aur inquiry ne kya paaya

Monsters par nikla gussa aakhir mein unhe maar daalne ki maang ban jaata hai. 2019 mein police ne Hyderabad ke paas hue ek rape aur murder ke chaar accused ko goli maar di, isse pehle ki koi court saboot sun paati. Supreme Court ke banaye commission ne paaya ki chaaron par "deliberately fired upon with an intent to cause their death", yaani jaan lene ke iraade se jaanbujhkar goli chalayi gayi, ki unmein se teen minor the, aur sifaarish ki ki ismein shaamil sabhi das police officers par murder ka trial chale [[livelaw-hyderabad-encounter-commission-2022]]. Woh aadmi accused the, un par trial kabhi chala hi nahi. Ab koi court nahi batayegi ki woh crime kisne kiya.

Courts ne gusse ko sazaa tay karne dene se mana kiya hai. 2021 mein Shakti Mills ki death sentences ko commute karte hue Bombay High Court ne kaha ki constitutional court public opinion ke aadhaar par sazaa nahi de sakti [[barandbench-shakti-mills-hc-2021]]. January 2025 mein Sealdah ki court ne RG Kar ke convict ko death nahi, life imprisonment di, aur "the temptation to bow to public pressure or emotional appeals", yaani public pressure ya emotional appeals ke aage jhukne ke laalach, ke khilaaf warn kiya [[tribune-rg-kar-sentence-2025]]. CBI ne death ki maang ke saath Calcutta High Court mein appeal ki hai.

Typical case mein goli ya phaansi ke paas dene ko kuch nahi hai. Apne partner ya chacha-mama ko report karne wali woman encounter nahi maang rahi. Woh maang rahi hai ki us par yakeen kiya jaaye, aur trial kabhi khatam bhi ho.

## Woh gussa jo data se mel khaaye

Jab rape-murder ka trial poora hota hai, toh aam taur par conviction hota hai. Rape ke trial mein aam taur par aisa nahi hota: 2024 mein conviction rate 24.4% tha, aur saal ke end mein rape ke 1,85,785 cases faisle ke intezaar mein the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Data se mel khaata gussa aisi cheezein maangta jinmein koi glamour nahi hai.

- **Judges, prosecutors aur forensic labs**, taaki intezaar mein pade cases faisle tak pahunchein.
- **Marital rape exception ka khatma.** 20 November 2026 tak Supreme Court ne is exception ke challenge par faisla nahi diya tha [[livelaw-marital-rape-final-hearing-2026]].
- **Aisi police jo jaan-pehchaan ke aadmiyon ke khilaaf complaint likhe.** Rape ki FIR record na karna BNS ki Section 199 ke tahat crime hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].
- **Ghar mein yakeen.** NFHS-5 mein, jin women ne physical ya sexual violence jhela tha, unmein se 77% ne kabhi help nahi maangi aur kisi ko bataya bhi nahi [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Agli baar jab koi case aapki feed bhar de, toh uska dukh zaroor manaiye. Phir un 28,597 ke baare mein poochiye.

outraging-modesty-law-language-1860.en:
In 2024, police in India registered 48,303 cases of assault on a woman "with intent to outrage her modesty", 7.1 cases for every lakh women [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Another 9,338 cases were registered for words, gestures or acts "intended to insult the modesty of a woman" [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. In plain words: he groped her, grabbed her, or made sexual remarks and gestures at her. The law's wording says that the thing damaged was her modesty.

## 48,303 and 9,338: the 'modesty' offences in 2024

Both counts were higher in 2024 than in the two years before. Assault to outrage modesty went from 44,867 cases in 2022 to 45,086 in 2023 and 48,303 in 2024. Insult to modesty went from 8,972 to 8,823 to 9,338 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. For scale, police registered 29,536 rape cases in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

These are FIRs, not incidents. The National Crime Records Bureau counts each FIR once, under its most serious offence, so an assault that came with a graver crime disappears from this row. The 2024 figure joins two codes: the old one until 30 June, the new one from 1 July [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## From 1860 to 2024: the words that survived

The phrase comes from the Indian Penal Code of 1860, where it sat in Section 354 (assault) and Section 509 (words and gestures). On 1 July 2024 the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita replaced that code [[pib-new-criminal-laws-highlights-2024]]. The sections got new numbers, 74 and 79. The Victorian noun stayed [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Parliament knows how to do it differently. In 2013 it added offences to the old code that are named for what the offender does: sexual harassment (Section 354A), disrobing (354B), voyeurism (354C) and stalking (354D) [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]]. The new code keeps them as Sections 75 to 78 [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Both times, the phrase in the parent section was left alone.

On 16 August 2023, the year the new code was passed, the Supreme Court released its Handbook on Combating Gender Stereotypes to help judges replace language that promotes stereotypes [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. A handbook can change the adjectives in a judgment. It cannot rename the offence the judgment is about.

## What Sections 74 and 79 actually cover

| BNS section | What it covers | Prison term |
|---|---|---|
| 74 | Assault or criminal force on a woman "to outrage her modesty" | 1 to 5 years |
| 75 | Sexual harassment | up to 3 years |
| 76 | Assault to disrobe | 3 to 7 years |
| 77 | Voyeurism | 1 to 3 years; 3 to 7 on a repeat |
| 78 | Stalking | up to 3 years; up to 5 on a repeat |
| 79 | Words or gestures meant to "insult the modesty of a woman" | up to 3 years |

Section 74 is not a small charge: it carries a minimum of one year in prison [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. It is the section police reach for when a man gropes or grabs a woman, sexual touching without consent that the law does not class as rape. Section 79 covers the sexual comment and the gesture, the things still waved away as "eve teasing".

Two things are missing. The first is a definition: modesty is not among the terms the code defines, so its meaning is left to each police officer and judge. The second is everyone who is not a woman. The code defines a woman as a female human being of any age [[indiacode-bns-2023]], and Sections 74 to 79 protect only women, so a man who is groped has no matching section among them. Sexual abuse of a transgender person is punished under a separate law, with six months to two years [[indiacode-transgender-persons-2019]]. Only children are covered whatever their gender, under POCSO [[pocso-act-2012]].

## Why the word matters at the police station and in court

In ordinary English, modesty is a quality of the woman: reserve in dress, speech and conduct. A law built on it invites a question about her before any question about him: was she modest, and so was there anything to outrage? Consent puts the question to the man: did she agree to be touched?

The Supreme Court's handbook stands with consent. It rejects the belief that a woman's clothes, drinking or smoking invite sexual contact, and says: "A man who touches a woman without her consent must not be permitted to take the defence that the woman invited his touch by dressing in a particular way" [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. The statute's vocabulary pulls the other way.

Consider a 22-year-old in Pune who is groped on a crowded bus. At the police station, what was done to her body is written up as an outrage to her modesty. At home, the family hears that their daughter's "modesty" is now a police matter and starts to worry about the neighbours. One word has moved attention from his hands to her reputation.

Of the 22,796 trials for assault to outrage modesty completed in 2024, 20.1% ended in conviction, and 3,17,491 cases, 92.3% of those on trial, were still pending when the year ended. For insulting modesty the conviction rate was 15.4%. For sexual harassment, the offence Parliament named plainly in 2013, it was 41.9% [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

The data cannot show that a word causes acquittals: these are different offences, with different evidence and different defences. They do show that roughly four of every five "modesty" assault trials completed in 2024 did not end in a conviction.

## Saying it plainly

An FIR will cite the section numbers. The rest of us can describe the act.

- Say "he groped her", "he sexually assaulted her", "he sexually harassed her". The handbook itself replaces "eve teasing" with "street sexual harassment" [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].
- In a complaint, write what he did, where, when, and that you did not consent. You do not have to prove that you are modest.
- You can report at any police station, whatever the area, or electronically if you sign within three days, and you must be given a free copy of the FIR [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

The repair is a drafting job. Section 74 could be called what it is, sexual assault, defined by the absence of consent and written to protect every person. Until then, the 1860 word keeps putting the question to the wrong person. This is general information, not legal advice.
outraging-modesty-law-language-1860.hg:
2024 mein India ki police ne aurat par "with intent to outrage her modesty", yaani uski modesty ko thes pahunchane ki niyat se kiye gaye assault ke 48,303 cases darj kiye, har ek lakh auraton par 7.1 cases [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Iske alawa 9,338 cases un shabdon, ishaaron ya harkaton ke darj hue jo "intended to insult the modesty of a woman" the, yaani aurat ki modesty ka apmaan karne ke liye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Seedhi bhasha mein: usne use grope kiya, pakda, ya us par sexual comments aur ishaare kiye. Law ke shabd kehte hain ki nuksaan uski modesty ka hua.

## 48,303 aur 9,338: 2024 mein 'modesty' wale offences

2024 mein dono ginti pichhle do saalon se zyada thi. Assault to outrage modesty ke cases 2022 mein 44,867 the, 2023 mein 45,086 aur 2024 mein 48,303. Insult to modesty ke cases 8,972 se 8,823 aur phir 9,338 hue [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Andaaza lagane ke liye: 2024 mein police ne rape ke 29,536 cases darj kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Ye FIRs hain, ghatnaayein nahi. National Crime Records Bureau har FIR ko ek hi baar ginta hai, uske sabse gambhir offence ke under, isliye jo assault kisi zyada gambhir crime ke saath hua woh is row se gayab ho jaata hai. 2024 ka figure do codes ko jodta bhi hai: 30 June tak purana, 1 July se naya [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## 1860 se 2024 tak: woh shabd jo bache rahe

Ye phrase 1860 ke Indian Penal Code se aaya hai, jahan ye Section 354 (assault) aur Section 509 (shabd aur ishaare) mein tha. 1 July 2024 ko Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita ne us code ki jagah le li [[pib-new-criminal-laws-highlights-2024]]. Sections ko naye number mile, 74 aur 79. Victorian zamaane ka shabd wahin raha [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Parliament ko doosra tareeka aata hai. 2013 mein usne purane code mein aise offences jode jinka naam is par rakha gaya ki offender kya karta hai: sexual harassment (Section 354A), disrobing (354B), voyeurism (354C) aur stalking (354D) [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]]. Naye code mein ye Sections 75 se 78 hain [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Dono baar parent section ka phrase jyon ka tyon chhod diya gaya.

16 August 2023 ko, usi saal jab naya code paas hua, Supreme Court ne apni Handbook on Combating Gender Stereotypes jaari ki, taaki judges stereotype badhaane wali bhasha ko badal sakein [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. Handbook judgment ke adjectives badal sakti hai. Jis offence par judgment hai, uska naam nahi badal sakti.

## Sections 74 aur 79 asal mein kya cover karte hain

| BNS section | Kya cover karta hai | Jail |
|---|---|---|
| 74 | Aurat par assault ya criminal force "to outrage her modesty" | 1 se 5 saal |
| 75 | Sexual harassment | 3 saal tak |
| 76 | Assault to disrobe | 3 se 7 saal |
| 77 | Voyeurism | 1 se 3 saal; dobara hone par 3 se 7 |
| 78 | Stalking | 3 saal tak; dobara hone par 5 tak |
| 79 | Shabd ya ishaare jinka maqsad "insult the modesty of a woman" ho | 3 saal tak |

Section 74 koi chhota charge nahi hai: isme kam se kam ek saal ki jail hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Police isi section ka sahaara leti hai jab koi aadmi kisi aurat ko grope karta hai ya pakadta hai, yaani bina consent ka sexual touch jise law rape nahi maanta. Section 79 sexual comment aur ishaaron ko cover karta hai, wahi sab jise aaj bhi "eve teasing" keh kar taal diya jaata hai.

Do cheezein gayab hain. Pehli hai definition: code jin shabdon ki definition deta hai, unme modesty nahi hai, isliye iska matlab har police officer aur judge par chhod diya gaya hai. Doosri hain woh sab log jo aurat nahi hain. Code ke mutabik woman ka matlab hai kisi bhi umar ki female human being [[indiacode-bns-2023]], aur Sections 74 se 79 sirf auraton ko protect karte hain, isliye jis aadmi ko grope kiya jaaye uske liye inme koi section nahi hai. Transgender person ke sexual abuse ki saza ek alag law mein hai, chheh mahine se do saal [[indiacode-transgender-persons-2019]]. Sirf bachche, gender koi bhi ho, POCSO ke under cover hote hain [[pocso-act-2012]].

## Police station aur court mein is shabd se farq kyun padta hai

Aam English mein modesty aurat ka ek gun hai: kapdon, bol-chaal aur bartaav mein sharm-lihaaz. Is par bana law aadmi se pehle aurat ke baare mein sawaal poochne ka nyota deta hai: kya woh modest thi, aur kya outrage hone ke liye kuch tha bhi? Consent sawaal aadmi se poochta hai: kya aurat chhue jaane ke liye raazi thi?

Supreme Court ki handbook consent ke saath khadi hai. Woh is soch ko khaarij karti hai ki aurat ke kapde, sharaab peena ya smoking sexual contact ko nyota dete hain, aur kehti hai: "A man who touches a woman without her consent must not be permitted to take the defence that the woman invited his touch by dressing in a particular way", yaani bina consent aurat ko chhoone wale aadmi ko ye bachaav nahi lene diya ja sakta ki aurat ne apne kapdon se use nyota diya [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. Statute ki bhasha ulti taraf kheenchti hai.

Sochiye Pune ki ek 22 saal ki ladki ke baare mein, jise bheed wali bus mein grope kiya jaata hai. Police station mein, uske shareer ke saath jo hua woh uski modesty ke outrage ke naam se likha jaata hai. Ghar par parivaar sunta hai ki beti ki "modesty" ab police ka maamla hai, aur padosiyon ki fikar shuru ho jaati hai. Ek shabd ne dhyaan us aadmi ke haathon se hata kar ladki ki reputation par laga diya.

2024 mein assault to outrage modesty ke jo 22,796 trials poore hue, unme se 20.1% conviction par khatm hue, aur 3,17,491 cases, yaani trial par chal rahe cases ke 92.3%, saal ke aakhir mein bhi pending the. Insulting modesty mein conviction rate 15.4% tha. Sexual harassment mein, jis offence ko Parliament ne 2013 mein seedha naam diya, ye 41.9% tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Data ye saabit nahi kar sakta ki ek shabd ki wajah se log bari hote hain: ye alag-alag offences hain, jinke saboot aur bachaav bhi alag hote hain. Data itna zaroor dikhata hai ki 2024 mein poore hue "modesty" assault ke har paanch trials mein se kareeb chaar conviction par khatm nahi hue.

## Seedhe shabdon mein kehna

FIR mein section ke number hi likhe jaayenge. Baaki hum sab bata sakte hain ki hua kya.

- Kahiye "usne use grope kiya", "usne use sexually assault kiya", "usne use sexually harass kiya". Handbook khud "eve teasing" ki jagah "street sexual harassment" likhti hai [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].
- Complaint mein likhiye ki usne kya kiya, kahan, kab, aur ye ki aapka consent nahi tha. Aapko ye saabit nahi karna ki aap modest hain.
- Aap kisi bhi police station mein report kar sakte hain, ilaaka koi bhi ho, ya electronically, agar teen din ke andar sign kar dein, aur FIR ki free copy aapko milni hi chahiye [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Ilaaj drafting ka kaam hai. Section 74 ko wahi kaha ja sakta hai jo woh hai, sexual assault, jiski definition consent ke na hone par tiki ho aur jo har insaan ko protect kare. Tab tak 1860 ka shabd sawaal galat insaan se poochta rahega. Ye general information hai, legal advice nahi.

parliament-speed-gender-laws-waiting.en:
On 13 March 2026 a bill to amend India's law on transgender persons was introduced in the Lok Sabha. The Lok Sabha passed it on 24 March and the Rajya Sabha on 25 March [[prs-transgender-amendment-bill-2026]]. Twelve days. The law against sexual harassment at work arrived more than 15 years after the Supreme Court wrote stop-gap rules and left the rest to Parliament [[sc-aureliano-fernandes-2023]]. Parliament is not simply slow. It chooses what to hurry, and the choices follow a pattern.

## Twelve days: when Parliament hurries

The 2026 amendment deleted the right to self-perceived gender identity and made a transgender certificate depend on a medical board's recommendation. It left the punishment for sexual abuse of a transgender person where it was: six months to two years in prison [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]]. The amendment is under challenge in the Supreme Court [[scobserver-transgender-amendment-hearing-2026]].

In 2018 the government did not wait for Parliament at all. An ordinance of 21 April 2018 brought in the death penalty for the rape of a girl under 12. The Act that followed, assented to on 11 August 2018, was deemed to have been in force from that April date [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2018]].

| Law or proposal | Key dates | The wait |
|---|---|---|
| Transgender amendment | Introduced 13 March 2026; passed 25 March 2026 | 12 days |
| Death penalty for rape of girls under 12 | Ordinance 21 April 2018; Act 11 August 2018 | None |
| Workplace harassment law | Court guidelines 13 August 1997; Act 22 April 2013 | More than 15 years |
| Abortion-law amendment | Lok Sabha 17 March 2020; Rajya Sabha 16 March 2021 | Almost a year between Houses |
| Law against "honour" crimes | Law Commission report, August 2012 | No separate offence yet |
| Offence for sexual assault of men and transgender persons | Committee advice, 10 November 2023 | Not accepted |

## Fifteen years, one year, still waiting

On 13 August 1997, in Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan, the Supreme Court laid down guidelines against sexual harassment of working women and declared them binding until Parliament passed a law [[sc-vishaka-1997]]. Parliament's law was enacted on 22 April 2013 and came into force on 9 December 2013 [[sc-aureliano-fernandes-2023]]. A woman who took her first job that year was in mid-career before her employer's duty was written into a statute.

The amendment that widened access to abortion passed the Lok Sabha on 17 March 2020. The Rajya Sabha approved it on 16 March 2021, almost a year later [[pib-mtp-amendment-bill-rs-2021]].

In August 2012 the Law Commission proposed a special law against interference with marriages in the name of "honour". It was still unimplemented in January 2018, when the Supreme Court's amicus curiae urged its adoption [[livelaw-honour-killing-amicus-2018]]. The BNS has no separate offence either [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

A bill introduced on 21 December 2021 would have raised women's minimum marriage age from 18 to 21 and made the child marriage law override any other law, custom or practice. In October 2024 the Supreme Court declined to decide the personal-law question, noting that the issue "is pending consideration before Parliament" [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]]. Bills pending in the Lok Sabha lapse when the House is dissolved, and a new Lok Sabha was elected in 2024. We could not confirm what became of this one.

## Expert advice set aside

Delay is one way to stall a protection. Declining advice is another. On 10 November 2023 Parliament's own Standing Committee on Home Affairs warned that dropping Section 377 of the IPC from the new penal code would leave non-consensual sexual offences against men and transgender persons unpunished, and recommended keeping it [[prs-standing-committee-bns-2023]]. The government did not accept this. Under the BNS, non-consensual penetrative sex against an adult man or a transgender person is not rape, and no specific offence replaced Section 377 [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Imagine a 24-year-old man assaulted this way in his hostel: the police have no rape section to write in his FIR.

Courts have pointed at the gap and stopped there. On 28 August 2024 the Delhi High Court asked the Centre to decide within six months, remarking that "there can't be a vacuum to an offence" [[barandbench-delhi-hc-unnatural-offences-bns-2024]]. In October 2024 the Supreme Court refused a similar plea, saying it cannot direct Parliament to create an offence [[livelaw-sc-bns-sexual-offences-men-pil-2024]]. In March 2026 the High Court revived its case because "the decision is nowhere in sight" [[theprint-pti-delhi-hc-restores-pil-2026]].

## What decides which bills move

These cases are too few to prove a rule, and no record states a motive. But three features repeat.

**Ownership.** Each fast law was the government's own bill or ordinance. The longest waits began as someone else's advice: a court's, the Law Commission's, a committee's. Government bills can drift too: the abortion amendment waited almost a year for the second House.

**Direction.** The fast laws added punishment or state control: a death sentence, a medical board. The slow ones would put duties on employers, families and communities, or protect people the law does not see: men and transgender survivors, couples who marry against their families' wishes, girls married as children.

**Courts cannot finish the job.** Vishaka's guidelines stood in for a statute for more than 15 years. On the missing offence, the Supreme Court said it cannot direct Parliament to create one.

Speed is not reserved for harsh laws: in August 2018 Parliament took days to undo a Supreme Court ruling that had made arrests under the SC/ST Atrocities Act harder [[prs-sc-st-poa-amendment-bill-2018]].

> When a government wants a law, time is found. When it does not, a court's reminder is not enough.

## How citizens push a stalled law

This is general information, not legal advice.

- **Follow the bill, not the headline.** The PRS Legislative Research bill tracker at prsindia.org lists the date of every stage.
- **Write to your MPs.** Name the bill or report and ask for one thing: a question in the House, or a date.
- **Answer committees.** Standing committees often invite written comments when they examine a bill. Anyone can send one.
- **Back the petitions.** Vishaka began as a petition, and a public-interest case has kept the missing offence on a court's record.
- **Use what exists.** POCSO protects any child under 18, boys included [[pocso-act-2012]].

A stalled law does not announce itself. Someone has to keep asking where it is.
parliament-speed-gender-laws-waiting.hg:
13 March 2026 ko transgender persons wale kaanoon ko badalne ka ek bill Lok Sabha mein introduce hua. Lok Sabha ne use 24 March ko pass kiya aur Rajya Sabha ne 25 March ko [[prs-transgender-amendment-bill-2026]]. Baarah din. Workplace par sexual harassment ke khilaaf kaanoon tab aaya jab Supreme Court ke stop-gap rules likhne aur baaki kaam Parliament par chhodne ko 15 saal se zyada ho chuke the [[sc-aureliano-fernandes-2023]]. Parliament sirf slow nahi hai. Woh chunti hai ki kis cheez mein jaldi karni hai, aur is chunaav mein ek pattern dikhta hai.

## Baarah din: jab Parliament jaldi karti hai

2026 ke amendment ne self-perceived gender identity ka haq hata diya, aur transgender certificate ko ek medical board ki recommendation par tika diya. Transgender vyakti ke sexual abuse ki saza usne wahin rehne di jahan thi: chhe mahine se do saal ki jail [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]]. Is amendment ko Supreme Court mein challenge kiya gaya hai [[scobserver-transgender-amendment-hearing-2026]].

2018 mein toh sarkar ne Parliament ka intezaar hi nahi kiya. 21 April 2018 ke ek ordinance ne 12 saal se kam umar ki bachchi ke rape par death penalty la di. Uske baad jo Act aaya, use 11 August 2018 ko assent mila, aur use usi April wali taareekh se laagu maana gaya [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2018]].

| Kaanoon ya proposal | Zaroori taareekhein | Intezaar |
|---|---|---|
| Transgender amendment | 13 March 2026 ko introduce; 25 March 2026 ko pass | 12 din |
| 12 saal se kam umar ki bachchiyon ke rape par death penalty | Ordinance 21 April 2018; Act 11 August 2018 | Koi nahi |
| Workplace harassment ka kaanoon | Court ki guidelines 13 August 1997; Act 22 April 2013 | 15 saal se zyada |
| Abortion-law amendment | Lok Sabha 17 March 2020; Rajya Sabha 16 March 2021 | Dono Houses ke beech lagbhag ek saal |
| "Honour" crimes ke khilaaf kaanoon | Law Commission ki report, August 2012 | Abhi tak koi alag offence nahi |
| Mardon aur transgender logon par sexual assault ka offence | Committee ki salaah, 10 November 2023 | Maani nahi gayi |

## Pandrah saal, ek saal, aur abhi tak intezaar

13 August 1997 ko Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan mein Supreme Court ne kaam karne wali aurton ke sexual harassment ke khilaaf guidelines di, aur kaha ki jab tak Parliament kaanoon nahi banati, yahi binding rahengi [[sc-vishaka-1997]]. Parliament ka kaanoon 22 April 2013 ko bana aur 9 December 2013 ko laagu hua [[sc-aureliano-fernandes-2023]]. Jis aurat ne usi saal apni pehli naukri shuru ki thi, woh apne career ke beech mein pahunch chuki thi jab uske employer ki zimmedaari kisi statute mein likhi gayi.

Abortion tak pahunch badhaane wala amendment Lok Sabha se 17 March 2020 ko pass hua. Rajya Sabha ne use 16 March 2021 ko manzoor kiya, lagbhag ek saal baad [[pib-mtp-amendment-bill-rs-2021]].

August 2012 mein Law Commission ne "honour" ke naam par shaadiyon mein dakhal dene ke khilaaf ek special kaanoon ka proposal diya. January 2018 mein, jab Supreme Court ke amicus curiae ne use apnaane ki maang ki, tab tak woh laagu nahi hua tha [[livelaw-honour-killing-amicus-2018]]. BNS mein bhi aisa koi alag offence nahi hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

21 December 2021 ko introduce hua ek bill aurton ki shaadi ki minimum umar 18 se badha kar 21 karta, aur child marriage wale kaanoon ko kisi bhi doosre kaanoon, custom ya practice se upar rakhta. October 2024 mein Supreme Court ne personal law wale sawaal par faisla nahi diya, aur note kiya ki yeh mudda "is pending consideration before Parliament", yaani Parliament ke saamne vichaar ke liye pending hai [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]]. Lok Sabha mein pending bills House ke dissolve hone par lapse ho jaate hain, aur 2024 mein nayi Lok Sabha chuni gayi. Is bill ka aage kya hua, yeh hum confirm nahi kar paaye.

## Experts ki salaah, jo kinaare kar di gayi

Kisi protection ko atkaane ka ek tareeka deri hai. Doosra tareeka hai salaah ko na maanna. 10 November 2023 ko Parliament ki apni Standing Committee on Home Affairs ne chetaavni di ki naye penal code se IPC ka Section 377 hataane par mardon aur transgender logon ke khilaaf non-consensual sexual offences bina saza ke reh jaayenge, aur use rakhne ki sifaarish ki [[prs-standing-committee-bns-2023]]. Sarkar ne yeh baat nahi maani. BNS ke tahat kisi adult mard ya transgender vyakti ke saath non-consensual penetrative sex rape nahi hai, aur Section 377 ki jagah koi specific offence nahi aaya [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Sochiye, 24 saal ke ek ladke par uske hostel mein isi tarah ka assault hota hai: police ke paas uski FIR mein likhne ke liye rape ka koi section hi nahi hai.

Courts ne is gap ki taraf ishaara kiya, aur wahin ruk gayi. 28 August 2024 ko Delhi High Court ne Centre se chhe mahine ke andar faisla lene ko kaha, aur tippani ki ki "there can't be a vacuum to an offence", yaani kisi offence ki jagah khaali nahi chhodi ja sakti [[barandbench-delhi-hc-unnatural-offences-bns-2024]]. October 2024 mein Supreme Court ne aisi hi ek plea sunne se mana kar diya, yeh kehte hue ki woh Parliament ko offence banane ka direction nahi de sakti [[livelaw-sc-bns-sexual-offences-men-pil-2024]]. March 2026 mein High Court ne apna case phir se zinda kiya, kyunki "the decision is nowhere in sight", yaani faisla door-door tak nazar nahi aa raha tha [[theprint-pti-delhi-hc-restores-pil-2026]].

## Kaun sa bill aage badhega, yeh kis se tay hota hai

Yeh cases itne kam hain ki inse koi rule saabit nahi hota, aur kisi record mein neeyat likhi nahi hoti. Lekin teen baatein baar-baar dikhti hain.

**Bill kiska hai.** Har tez kaanoon sarkar ka apna bill ya ordinance tha. Sabse lambe intezaar kisi aur ki salaah se shuru hue: court ki, Law Commission ki, committee ki. Sarkari bills bhi latak sakte hain: abortion amendment ne doosre House ke liye lagbhag ek saal intezaar kiya.

**Kaanoon kis taraf jaata hai.** Tez kaanoonon ne saza ya state ka control badhaya: death sentence, medical board. Dheeme kaanoon employers, families aur communities par zimmedaari daalte, ya un logon ko protect karte jinhe kaanoon dekhta hi nahi: mard aur transgender survivors, parivaar ki marzi ke khilaaf shaadi karne wale couples, aur bachpan mein byaahi gayi ladkiyan.

**Courts kaam poora nahi kar sakti.** Vishaka ki guidelines 15 saal se zyada tak ek statute ki jagah khadi rahi. Missing offence par Supreme Court ne kaha ki woh Parliament ko use banane ka direction nahi de sakti.

Tezi sirf sakht kaanoonon ke liye nahi hoti: August 2018 mein Parliament ne kuch hi dinon mein Supreme Court ke us faisle ko palat diya jisne SC/ST Atrocities Act ke tahat arrest ko mushkil bana diya tha [[prs-sc-st-poa-amendment-bill-2018]].

> Jab sarkar koi kaanoon chahti hai, toh waqt nikal aata hai. Jab nahi chahti, toh court ka yaad dilana kaafi nahi hota.

## Atke hue kaanoon ko citizens kaise aage badhaayein

Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

- **Headline nahi, bill ko follow kijiye.** PRS Legislative Research ka bill tracker, prsindia.org par, har stage ki taareekh dikhata hai.
- **Apne MPs ko likhiye.** Bill ya report ka naam lijiye aur ek hi cheez maangiye: House mein ek sawaal, ya ek taareekh.
- **Committees ko jawaab dijiye.** Standing committees jab kisi bill ko examine karti hain, toh aksar likhit comments maangti hain. Koi bhi bhej sakta hai.
- **Petitions ka saath dijiye.** Vishaka ek petition se shuru hua tha, aur ek public-interest case ne hi missing offence ko court ke record par banaye rakha hai.
- **Jo maujood hai, use istemaal kijiye.** POCSO 18 se kam umar ke har bachche ko protect karta hai, ladkon ko bhi [[pocso-act-2012]].

Atka hua kaanoon khud nahi batata ki woh atka hai. Kisi ko poochhte rehna padta hai ki woh kahan hai.

pink-tax-women-commute-safety.en:
Ask a woman in Mumbai what stops her from travelling to a job, and she is unlikely to say "the train is unsafe". In a 2019 World Bank survey of 2,388 non-working women in the city, 31% said commuting was a barrier to working. Most pointed to domestic duties (19%) and childcare (13%). Only 1.6% named unsafe commuting [[worldbank-mumbai-gender-transport-2021]].

It would be easy to conclude that safety is a small problem. The same study shows where the problem went. Safety is being paid for, in rupees and in hours, and the bill has a name: the pink tax.

## 31% and 1.6%: what Mumbai's women said

The survey spoke to women aged 18 to 45 who were not working, and they could give more than one reason [[worldbank-mumbai-gender-transport-2021]].

Nearly one in three saw the commute as an obstacle, and their reasons were about time. A woman who must cook before she leaves and be back at the school gate by afternoon has no hours to spare for a crowded train. The commute is a barrier because the housework and the child are treated as hers alone.

Two cautions. This is one city, and the report itself notes that Mumbai is seen as one of India's safer cities for women, so safety may weigh more elsewhere. And these are women who are not travelling to work. The price of unsafe transport is paid by the ones who are.

## The pink tax

Between 2004 and 2019, the World Bank note records, satisfaction with Mumbai's trains and buses fell steeply. Women shifted to auto-rickshaws and taxis, which tend to cost more per trip than two-wheelers [[worldbank-mumbai-gender-transport-2021]]. The authors call this a "pink tax" on women's mobility: when public transport fails to deal with barriers such as a lack of security, women choose safer but more expensive ways to travel.

The tax is collected in small amounts. It can look like this: the auto taken because the last stretch from the station is unlit. The job across the city that is never applied for, because the only way home after 9 pm costs too much or feels too exposed.

> Women are not telling surveyors that the bus is unsafe. They are quietly paying not to be on it.

None of this reaches the police. Across India, police registered 459 cases of sexual harassment of women on public transport in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. What women spend to avoid harassment is recorded nowhere.

## A fifth of a wage on the commute

For a salaried professional the pink tax is an irritation. For a woman earning very little, it decides whether working is worth it.

Jagori surveyed 270 women domestic workers in Delhi-NCR between May and November 2024. Those earning under Rs 5,000 a month spent about 20% of their income on commuting: one rupee in every five, gone before any food is bought [[jagori-domestic-workers-report-2025]]. In the same study 45% said they felt very unsafe in the city at night, a further 17% felt somewhat unsafe, and 24% had experienced sexual harassment in the previous two years [[jagori-domestic-workers-report-2025]].

Imagine a woman who cleans three homes in south Delhi and lives an hour away. A fourth home would raise her income, but she would leave it after dark. She weighs the fare for a shared auto against the extra wage, and the walk from the stop against both. She says no. No survey will record that refusal as a safety problem.

This is a small sample from one region, not a picture of all Indian women. It does show who pays this tax at the highest rate: the women with the least to spare.

## 16.5 points or 5.7: transport and women's work

How much work does this cost? The figure usually quoted comes from the International Labour Office, which estimated in 2017 that limited access to safe transport lowers a woman's probability of taking part in the labour market by 16.5 percentage points [[ilo-weso-trends-women-2017]]. The World Bank's Mumbai note cites it too.

That number is for low-income countries. India sits in the ILO's middle-income group, where the estimate is 5.7 points, with a further 2.0 points for abuse, harassment or discrimination at work [[ilo-weso-trends-women-2017]]. Both are cross-country estimates from survey data, not Indian measurements. Quoting the larger one for India overstates what the source says.

Even the smaller number matters where so few urban women are in paid work. In 2023-24 only 28.0% of urban women aged 15 and above were in the labour force, up from 20.4% in 2017-18. Rural women's participation nearly doubled over the same years, from 24.6% to 47.6% [[mospi-plfs-annual-2023-24]]. The city, with its buses, trains and salaried jobs, is where women's work has grown more slowly.

## A city built for women's journeys

Money is being spent on safety. Safe City projects in eight cities had received Rs 1,686.73 crore from the Nirbhaya Fund by July 2026 [[theprint-nirbhaya-fund-rajya-sabha-2026]]. The Mumbai and Delhi numbers suggest how to judge that spending: by whether a woman can make an ordinary trip cheaply, quickly and without planning around fear.

That means frequent buses outside rush hour, when school runs and part-time shifts happen. Lit, staffed stops, and a last stretch home that does not need an auto. Fares that do not punish a journey made in three short legs. Staff who act on a complaint, and transport bodies that count harassment complaints and publish them.

Part of the fix is not transport policy at all. The first reasons Mumbai's women gave were domestic duties and childcare. A home where men share both gives a woman back the hours a commute needs.

The figures here are all about women. None of these surveys tells us what transgender commuters pay to move through a city safely.

Until cities are planned around the journeys women and other commuters actually make, the pink tax will go on being paid in money, time and the jobs women do not take.
pink-tax-women-commute-safety.hg:
Mumbai ki kisi aurat se poochhiye ki naukri tak pahunchne mein use kya rokta hai, toh "train unsafe hai" sunne ki ummeed kam hai. World Bank ke 2019 ke survey mein shehar ki 2,388 non-working auraton mein se 31% ne kaha ki commuting kaam karne mein rukaavat hai. Zyada tar ne wajah domestic duties (19%) aur childcare (13%) batayi. Sirf 1.6% ne unsafe commuting ka naam liya [[worldbank-mumbai-gender-transport-2021]].

Isse yeh nateeja nikaalna aasaan hai ki safety chhoti problem hai. Lekin wahi study dikhati hai ki problem gayi kahan. Safety ki keemat chukayi ja rahi hai, rupayon mein aur ghanton mein, aur is bill ka ek naam hai: pink tax.

## 31% aur 1.6%: Mumbai ki auraton ne kya kaha

Survey ne 18 se 45 saal ki un auraton se baat ki jo kaam nahi kar rahi thin, aur woh ek se zyada wajah bata sakti thin [[worldbank-mumbai-gender-transport-2021]].
