Lagbhag har teen mein se ek ne commute ko rukaavat maana, aur unki wajahein time ke baare mein thin. Jis aurat ko nikalne se pehle khana banana hai aur dopahar tak school gate par wapas pahunchna hai, uske paas bheed bhari train ke liye ghante nahi bachte. Commute isliye rukaavat hai kyunki ghar ka kaam aur bachcha sirf uski zimmedaari maane jaate hain.

Do baatein dhyan mein rakhiye. Yeh sirf ek shehar hai, aur report khud kehti hai ki Mumbai ko auraton ke liye India ke zyada safe shehron mein gina jaata hai, toh baaki jagah safety ka wazan zyada ho sakta hai. Aur yeh woh auratein hain jo kaam par safar nahi kar rahin. Unsafe transport ki keemat woh chukati hain jo safar karti hain.

## Pink tax

World Bank ka note darj karta hai ki 2004 se 2019 ke beech Mumbai ki trains aur buses se satisfaction tezi se gira. Auratein auto-rickshaws aur taxis ki taraf shift huin, jo per trip two-wheelers se mehenge padte hain [[worldbank-mumbai-gender-transport-2021]]. Authors ise auraton ki mobility par "pink tax" kehte hain: jab public transport security ki kami jaisi rukaavaton ko door nahi karta, toh auratein zyada safe lekin zyada mehenge raaste chunti hain.

Yeh tax chhoti-chhoti kishton mein vasool hota hai. Kuch aisa dikhta hai: station se ghar tak ka aakhri hissa andhera hai, isliye auto liya. Shehar ke doosre kone wali job ke liye apply hi nahi kiya, kyunki raat 9 baje ke baad ghar lautne ka raasta ya toh bahut mehenga hai ya bahut asurakshit lagta hai.

> Auratein survey karne walon se yeh nahi keh rahin ki bus unsafe hai. Woh chupchaap paise de rahi hain taaki us bus mein hona hi na pade.

Ismein se kuch bhi police tak nahi pahunchta. Poore India mein police ne 2024 mein public transport par auraton ke sexual harassment ke 459 cases register kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Harassment se bachne ke liye auratein jo kharch karti hain, woh kahin darj nahi hota.

## Kamaai ka paanchwa hissa sirf commute par

Salaried professional ke liye pink tax ek jhanjhat hai. Bahut kam kamaane wali aurat ke liye yahi tay karta hai ki kaam karna faayde ka hai bhi ya nahi.

Jagori ne May se November 2024 ke beech Delhi-NCR ki 270 women domestic workers ka survey kiya. Rs 5,000 mahine se kam kamaane wali workers apni income ka lagbhag 20% commuting par kharch karti thin: har paanch mein se ek rupaya, khana khareedne se pehle hi kharch [[jagori-domestic-workers-report-2025]]. Isi study mein 45% ne kaha ki raat ko shehar mein woh very unsafe mehsoos karti hain, 17% aur ne somewhat unsafe kaha, aur 24% ne pichhle do saal mein sexual harassment jhela tha [[jagori-domestic-workers-report-2025]].

Sochiye, ek aurat south Delhi ke teen gharon mein safai karti hai aur ek ghante door rehti hai. Chautha ghar uski kamaai badha dega, lekin wahan se woh andhera hone ke baad niklegi. Woh shared auto ke kiraye ko extra kamaai se tolti hai, aur stop se ghar tak ke paidal raaste ko dono se. Woh mana kar deti hai. Koi survey is inkaar ko safety problem ke taur par darj nahi karega.

Yeh ek region ka chhota sample hai, saari Indian auraton ki tasveer nahi. Lekin yeh dikhata hai ki yeh tax sabse oonchi rate par kaun bharta hai: woh auratein jinke paas bachaane ko sabse kam hai.

## 16.5 points ya 5.7: transport aur auraton ka kaam

Iski keemat kaam mein kitni hai? Aam taur par jo figure quote hota hai woh International Labour Office ka hai, jisne 2017 mein estimate kiya ki safe transport tak kam pahunch aurat ke labour market mein hissa lene ki probability 16.5 percentage points ghata deti hai [[ilo-weso-trends-women-2017]]. World Bank ka Mumbai note bhi isi ko cite karta hai.

Lekin yeh number low-income countries ke liye hai. India ILO ke middle-income group mein aata hai, jahan estimate 5.7 points hai, aur kaam par abuse, harassment ya discrimination ke liye 2.0 points aur [[ilo-weso-trends-women-2017]]. Dono survey data se nikle cross-country estimates hain, India ke apne measurements nahi. India ke liye bada wala number quote karna source ki baat ko badha-chadha kar kehna hai.

Chhota number bhi maayne rakhta hai, kyunki paid work mein urban auratein itni kam hain. 2023-24 mein 15 saal aur usse upar ki urban auraton mein se sirf 28.0% labour force mein thin, jo 2017-18 mein 20.4% tha. Inhi saalon mein rural auraton ki participation lagbhag double hui, 24.6% se 47.6% [[mospi-plfs-annual-2023-24]]. Shehar, jahan buses, trains aur salaried jobs hain, wahin auraton ka kaam zyada dheere badha hai.

## Aisa shehar jo auraton ke safar ke hisaab se bana ho

Safety par paisa kharch ho raha hai. July 2026 tak aath shehron ke Safe City projects ko Nirbhaya Fund se Rs 1,686.73 crore mil chuke the [[theprint-nirbhaya-fund-rajya-sabha-2026]]. Mumbai aur Delhi ke numbers batate hain ki is kharch ko kis kasauti par parkha jaaye: kya ek aurat ek aam safar sasta, jaldi aur darr ke hisaab se plan kiye bina kar sakti hai.

Iska matlab hai rush hour ke bahar bhi frequent buses, kyunki school run aur part-time shifts tabhi hote hain. Roshni wale, staff wale stops, aur ghar tak ka aakhri hissa jiske liye auto na lena pade. Aise fares jo teen chhote hisson mein kiye gaye safar ko saza na den. Aisa staff jo complaint par action le, aur aisi transport bodies jo harassment complaints ginen aur publish karen.

Ilaaj ka ek hissa transport policy hai hi nahi. Mumbai ki auraton ne sabse pehle domestic duties aur childcare ka naam liya. Jis ghar mein mard yeh dono kaam baant-te hain, wahan aurat ko woh ghante wapas milte hain jo commute maangta hai.

Yahan ke saare figures auraton ke baare mein hain. In surveys mein se koi nahi batata ki transgender commuters shehar mein safely chalne ke liye kya keemat chukate hain.

Jab tak shehar un safaron ke hisaab se plan nahi hote jo auratein aur baaki commuters asal mein karte hain, tab tak pink tax paise, time aur un jobs mein bhara jaata rahega jo auratein nahi letin.

posh-act-compliance-one-of-36.en:
In August 2025, lawyers for India's states and union territories told the Supreme Court that a survey it had ordered eight months earlier was not finished. The survey asks one basic question: in each district, which workplaces have the sexual harassment committee the law has required since 2013? Only the Andaman and Nicobar Islands had completed it, the Court was told, LiveLaw reported [[livelaw-posh-district-survey-2025]]. India has 28 states and 8 union territories. That is 1 of 36.

## The law since December 2013

The Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, the POSH Act, was enacted on 22 April 2013 and came into force on 9 December 2013 [[sc-aureliano-fernandes-2023]]. That was more than 15 years after the Supreme Court's binding Vishaka guidelines of 13 August 1997 [[sc-vishaka-1997]].

Every employer must set up an Internal Committee headed by a senior woman employee, with at least two employee members and one external member; at least half the members must be women. For workplaces with fewer than ten workers, and for complaints against the employer himself, each district's District Officer must set up a Local Committee [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].

An employer who ignores this can be fined up to Rs 50,000. A repeat offence doubles the punishment and can cost the business its licence [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. But a court can take up the offence only on a complaint by the aggrieved woman, or by someone a committee authorises. Where the employer has no committee and the district's is missing or silent, the only person left who can set the penalty in motion is the woman who was harassed. That is one reason the law is easy to ignore.

## 'A sorry state of affairs': the 2023 judgment

The Court was chasing compliance before the Act existed. On 19 October 2012 it found that several state governments had not complied with the Vishaka guidelines and warned that "laws with sloppy enforcement are not enough" [[sc-aureliano-fernandes-2023]].

On 12 May 2023, a decade into the Act, a bench of Justices A.S. Bopanna and Hima Kohli found "serious lapses in the enforcement of the Act even after such a long passage of time" [[sc-aureliano-fernandes-2023]].

> "This is indeed a sorry state of affairs." Supreme Court of India, 12 May 2023

So it told governments to audit themselves. The Union, every state and every union territory had to verify whether each ministry, department, public sector undertaking and public body had a properly constituted committee, and to publish its members, contact details and complaint procedure online. Affidavits were due within eight weeks. Without strict enforcement, the Court warned, the Act would "remain an empty formality" [[sc-aureliano-fernandes-2023]].

## Deadlines in 2024, one survey by 2025

More than a year and a half later, the Court was still on the same case. On 3 December 2024 it set dates. Every state was to notify a District Officer for each district by 31 December 2024, constitute Local Committees and government Internal Committees by 31 January 2025, and survey public and private organisations in every district to see which had Internal Committees [[sc-posh-order-2025-05-21]].

By May 2025 the affidavits gave half an answer. Every state had appointed District Officers. But Local Committee compliance was unclear in Delhi, Haryana, Jharkhand and Kerala, and several states gave no information on the survey. Jharkhand reported Local Committees in 22 of its 24 districts [[sc-posh-order-2025-05-21]].

In August, only the Andaman and Nicobar Islands was reported to have finished the survey. On 12 August 2025 the Court gave states and union territories six more weeks, with help from their labour departments [[livelaw-posh-district-survey-2025]].

Two cautions about "1 of 36". The Andaman detail comes from a report of the hearing; the written order records only that the survey was incomplete. And the six weeks ran out in September 2025: we could not verify a public, state-by-state record of what followed. Even a finished survey is only a count. It does not make one employer set up a committee.

## Who is left with no committee

The gaps fall on the women with the least power to push back. The Internal Committee belongs to offices with HR departments. The Local Committee is for everyone else: the woman in a five-person shop, the worker whose harasser is the owner, the domestic worker in a private home [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].

"Everyone else" takes in a great many working women, especially outside the cities. In 2023-24, 73.5% of rural women workers were self-employed and just 7.8% had regular salaried jobs [[mospi-plfs-annual-2023-24]].

Imagine a 22-year-old who stitches garments in a unit of eight workers in a small Haryana town. The owner's brother, her supervisor, messages her late at night. Her unit is too small for an Internal Committee, so her complaint must go to the district's Local Committee. If nobody at the district office can tell her where it sits, the Act has given her a right with no door.

The Act is also written only for an "aggrieved woman" [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Men, and transgender workers whose employers do not treat them as covered, have no statutory committee at all.

## How to check your workplace

This is general information, not legal advice.

- **Ask in writing.** Email HR or the head of office for the order constituting the Internal Committee and its members' names. The law requires a senior woman in the chair, at least two employee members, one outsider and at least half women [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].
- **Check the website.** Under the 2023 directions, government bodies must publish their committee's members, contact details and complaint procedure online. The directions also cover universities, hospitals and professional bodies [[sc-aureliano-fernandes-2023]].
- **Small workplace, or the harasser is the employer?** Ask the district administration where the Local Committee sits.
- **No committee is not the end.** The government's SHe-Box portal takes workplace sexual harassment complaints [[shebox]]. Sexual harassment is also a crime under Section 75 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, punishable with up to three years [[indiacode-bns-2023]], and can be reported at any police station [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

The Supreme Court has spent the years since 2023 asking governments to count committees. Until that count exists, the checking is left to the people the law was meant to protect. Ask in writing, before you need the answer.
posh-act-compliance-one-of-36.hg:
August 2025 mein India ke states aur union territories ke lawyers ne Supreme Court ko bataya ki jis survey ka order Court ne aath mahine pehle diya tha, woh abhi poora nahi hua hai. Survey ek seedha sa sawaal poochhta hai: har district mein kin workplaces ke paas woh sexual harassment committee hai jo law 2013 se maang raha hai? LiveLaw ki report ke mutabik Court ko bataya gaya ki sirf Andaman and Nicobar Islands ne yeh survey poora kiya hai [[livelaw-posh-district-survey-2025]]. India mein 28 states aur 8 union territories hain. Yaani 36 mein se 1.

## December 2013 se law kya kehta hai

Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, yaani POSH Act, 22 April 2013 ko bana aur 9 December 2013 se laagu hua [[sc-aureliano-fernandes-2023]]. Yeh Supreme Court ki 13 August 1997 ki binding Vishaka guidelines ke 15 saal se bhi zyada baad hua [[sc-vishaka-1997]].

Har employer ko ek Internal Committee banani hai, jiski head ek senior woman employee ho, jismein kam se kam do employee members aur ek external member ho, aur jiske kam se kam aadhe members auratein hon. Jin workplaces mein das se kam workers hain, aur jahan complaint khud employer ke khilaaf hai, unke liye har district ke District Officer ko Local Committee banani hai [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].

Jo employer yeh nahi karta, us par Rs 50,000 tak ka fine lag sakta hai. Dobara wahi galti par saza double ho jaati hai aur business ka licence bhi ja sakta hai [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Lekin court is offence ko tabhi le sakta hai jab complaint khud aggrieved woman kare, ya koi aisa insaan jise committee ne authorise kiya ho. Jahan employer ke paas committee hi nahi hai, aur district ki committee gayab ya chup hai, wahan penalty ko chaalu karne wala sirf ek insaan bachta hai: wahi aurat jiske saath harassment hua. Yeh ek wajah hai ki is law ko ignore karna itna aasaan hai.

## 'A sorry state of affairs': 2023 ka judgment

Court is law ke banne se pehle se compliance ke peeche laga hua hai. 19 October 2012 ko usne paaya ki kai state governments ne Vishaka guidelines ka paalan nahi kiya, aur chetavni di ki "laws with sloppy enforcement are not enough", yaani dheele enforcement wale kanoon kaafi nahi hain [[sc-aureliano-fernandes-2023]].

12 May 2023 ko, Act ke ek dashak baad, Justices A.S. Bopanna aur Hima Kohli ki bench ne paaya ki "serious lapses in the enforcement of the Act even after such a long passage of time" hain, yaani itna lamba waqt beetne ke baad bhi Act ko laagu karne mein gambhir kamiyan hain [[sc-aureliano-fernandes-2023]].

> "This is indeed a sorry state of affairs." Supreme Court of India, 12 May 2023

Isliye Court ne sarkaron se kaha ki pehle apna hi audit karein. Union, har state aur har union territory ko verify karna tha ki har ministry, department, public sector undertaking aur public body mein theek se bani hui committee hai ya nahi, aur committee ke members, contact details aur complaint procedure online publish karne the. Affidavits aath hafton ke andar dene the. Court ne chetavni di ki sakht enforcement ke bina yeh Act "remain an empty formality" rahega, yaani sirf ek khokhli formality [[sc-aureliano-fernandes-2023]].

## 2024 mein deadlines, 2025 tak ek survey

Dedh saal se zyada baad bhi Court usi case par tha. 3 December 2024 ko usne dates tay kar di. Har state ko 31 December 2024 tak har district ke liye District Officer notify karna tha, 31 January 2025 tak Local Committees aur government Internal Committees banani thin, aur har district mein public aur private organisations ka survey karna tha ki kin ke paas Internal Committee hai [[sc-posh-order-2025-05-21]].

May 2025 tak affidavits se aadha jawab mila. Har state ne District Officers appoint kar diye the. Lekin Delhi, Haryana, Jharkhand aur Kerala mein Local Committee ka compliance saaf nahi tha, aur kai states ne survey ke baare mein koi jaankari hi nahi di. Jharkhand ne apne 24 mein se 22 districts mein Local Committees hone ki report di [[sc-posh-order-2025-05-21]].

August mein sirf Andaman and Nicobar Islands ke baare mein report hua ki usne survey poora kar liya hai. 12 August 2025 ko Court ne states aur union territories ko chhe hafte aur diye, aur kaha ki labour departments ki madad lein [[livelaw-posh-district-survey-2025]].

"36 mein se 1" ke saath do savdhaniyan zaroori hain. Andaman wali baat hearing ki report se aati hai; likhit order sirf itna record karta hai ki survey adhoora tha. Aur woh chhe hafte September 2025 mein khatam ho gaye: uske baad kya hua, iska koi public, state-by-state record hum verify nahi kar paaye. Poora hua survey bhi sirf ek ginti hai. Usse kisi ek employer ke yahan bhi committee nahi ban jaati.

## Kis ke paas koi committee nahi hai

Yeh gaps unhi auraton par girte hain jinke paas virodh karne ki taaqat sabse kam hai. Internal Committee un offices ki cheez hai jahan HR department hota hai. Local Committee baaki sab ke liye hai: paanch logon ki dukaan mein kaam karne wali aurat, woh worker jise harass karne wala khud maalik hai, kisi ke ghar mein kaam karne wali domestic worker [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].

Aur is "baaki sab" mein bahut saari kaam-kaaji auratein aati hain, khaas kar shehron ke bahar. 2023-24 mein rural women workers mein se 73.5% self-employed thin aur sirf 7.8% ke paas regular salaried job thi [[mospi-plfs-annual-2023-24]].

Sochiye, Haryana ke ek chhote sheher mein 22 saal ki ek ladki aath workers wali unit mein kapde silti hai. Maalik ka bhai, jo uska supervisor hai, use der raat messages bhejta hai. Uski unit itni chhoti hai ki wahan Internal Committee nahi banegi, isliye uski complaint district ki Local Committee ke paas hi jaani hai. Agar district office mein koi use yeh nahi bata sakta ki woh committee kahan baithti hai, toh Act ne use ek aisa haq diya hai jiska koi darwaza hi nahi.

Act likha bhi sirf "aggrieved woman" ke liye gaya hai [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Mardon ke liye, aur un transgender workers ke liye jinhe unka employer covered nahi maanta, law mein koi committee hai hi nahi.

## Apna workplace kaise check karein

Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

- **Likhit mein poochhiye.** HR ya head of office ko email karke Internal Committee banane ka order aur members ke naam maangiye. Law ke hisaab se head ek senior woman honi chahiye, kam se kam do employee members, ek bahar ka member, aur kam se kam aadhi auratein [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].
- **Website dekhiye.** 2023 ke directions ke tahat government bodies ko apni committee ke members, contact details aur complaint procedure online publish karne hain. Yeh directions universities, hospitals aur professional bodies par bhi laagu hote hain [[sc-aureliano-fernandes-2023]].
- **Chhota workplace hai, ya harass karne wala khud employer hai?** District administration se poochhiye ki Local Committee kahan baithti hai.
- **Committee nahi hai toh bhi raasta band nahi hai.** Sarkar ka SHe-Box portal workplace sexual harassment ki complaints leta hai [[shebox]]. Sexual harassment Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita ke Section 75 ke tahat crime bhi hai, jismein teen saal tak ki saza ho sakti hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]], aur ise kisi bhi police station mein report kiya ja sakta hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Supreme Court 2023 se sarkaron se bas yahi keh raha hai ki committees gin lo. Jab tak yeh ginti nahi hoti, check karne ka kaam unhi logon par chhoota hua hai jinki hifazat ke liye yeh law bana tha. Likhit mein poochhiye, aur tab poochhiye jab jawab ki zaroorat abhi padi na ho.

posh-act-excludes-men-transgender-worker.en:
Imagine two colleagues in a Pune office, harassed by the same manager: the same messages, the same comments, the same threats about appraisals. One is a woman. She can take it to the Internal Committee the company is required to have. The other is a man, or a transgender person. For them, that committee has no clear legal duty to listen. The reason is in the law's own name: the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, enacted on 22 April 2013 and in force since 9 December 2013 [[sc-aureliano-fernandes-2023]]. This is general information, not legal advice.

## Does the POSH Act protect me if I'm a man?

No. The Act gives its remedy to an "aggrieved woman": a woman "of any age whether employed or not" who alleges sexual harassment at a workplace. The written complaint, the 90-day inquiry and the employer's duty to act all start from her complaint [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. A man reporting the same conduct is outside the statute.

Criminal law does not fill the space. The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) offences a harassed woman can use are written around women: assault to outrage a woman's modesty (Section 74), words or gestures insulting a woman's modesty (Section 79). Sexual harassment (Section 75, up to three years) and stalking (Section 78) can, by their wording, be committed only by a man [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

What is left for a man are general offences that depend on the facts, such as hurt, grievous hurt or wrongful confinement. Voluntarily causing hurt carries at most one year in prison [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. None of them calls what happened sexual harassment.

## I'm transgender: which law covers harassment at work?

In 2014 the Supreme Court, in NALSA v. Union of India, recognised transgender persons as a "third gender" protected by Articles 14, 15, 16, 19 and 21 of the Constitution [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]]. The law that followed, the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019, gave every person recognised as transgender "a right to self-perceived gender identity" [[indiacode-transgender-act-2019]]. Against harassment, its clearest protection is a criminal one, and it is thin. Section 18(d) of the Act puts physical, sexual, verbal, emotional and economic abuse of a transgender person in a single clause, punishable with 6 months to 2 years in prison and a fine. The 2026 amendment rewrote the section and left that range unchanged [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]]. Compare it with the BNS: sexual harassment of a woman carries up to three years, and rape at least 10 years [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. For a transgender person, sexual abuse of any gravity sits in the same bracket as a verbal insult.

Two further catches. The 2026 amendment deleted the right to self-perceived gender identity and narrowed who counts as a transgender person under the Act, saying the term does not include "persons with different sexual orientations and self-perceived sexual identities" [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]]. It is under challenge in the Supreme Court, which heard the petitions on 17 August 2026 [[scobserver-transgender-amendment-hearing-2026]]. And by November 2025 only 20 states and union territories had set up the Transgender Protection Cells that the 2020 Rules require of every state [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]].

## Didn't the government say the new criminal laws are gender-neutral?

It did. In a July 2024 note, the Home Ministry said "various offences against women and children have been made gender-neutral in BNS, covering all victims and perpetrators regardless of gender", and that the definition of gender "now includes transgender individuals" [[pib-new-criminal-laws-2024]].

The second half is true in a narrow sense. The code says the pronoun "he" covers any person, "whether male, female or transgender". But it also defines "man" as a male and "woman" as a female human being, and those are the words the sexual offences use [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Rape stays limited to a man assaulting a woman, and sexual harassment and stalking to acts by a man.

So the claim does not reach the offences a harassed worker would look for. A pronoun was widened. The sections were not.

## What can I do today?

- Write it down: date, place, exact words, who saw it. Save messages and emails somewhere your employer cannot delete them.
- Ask HR in writing whether the company's harassment policy covers every gender. An employer can choose to write one that does; if yours has, use it.
- If you are transgender, ask your employer in writing who handles harassment complaints from transgender staff, and keep the reply. A police complaint under Section 18(d) of the Transgender Persons Act is also open to you [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]].
- For assault, threats or confinement, go to the police. Information about a cognizable offence can be given at any police station, wherever it happened [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Legal services authorities give free legal aid [[nalsa]].
- If you are under 18, the law is different: POCSO protects every child below 18, whatever their gender [[pocso-act-2012]].
- Tele-MANAS offers free counselling on 14416 to anyone, including transgender persons [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].

## What would close the gap?

Parliament would. In November 2023 its own Standing Committee on Home Affairs warned that dropping Section 377 of the old penal code would leave non-consensual sexual offences against men and transgender persons unpunished, and recommended keeping it. The government did not [[prs-standing-committee-bns-2023]]. On 14 October 2024 the Supreme Court refused to entertain a plea to create such offences, saying it cannot direct Parliament to make one [[livelaw-sc-bns-sexual-offences-men-pil-2024]].

Three changes would do most of the work: a workplace law whose committee hears any worker, harassment and stalking offences that do not depend on anyone's gender, and a penalty for sexual abuse of transgender persons that matches the harm. None of this takes anything from women. The committee, the deadlines and the employer's duties stay; more people get to use them.

It matters to everyone because of what the present wording teaches. A law that hears only women tells men that what happened to them does not count, tells transgender workers that it counts for less, and tells every office that harassment is a women's issue to be managed, not conduct to be stopped.
posh-act-excludes-men-transgender-worker.hg:
Sochiye Pune ke ek office mein do colleagues hain, jinhe ek hi manager harass karta hai: wahi messages, wahi comments, appraisal ko lekar wahi dhamkiyan. Ek aurat hai. Woh ye baat us Internal Committee ke paas le ja sakti hai jo company ko banani hi padti hai. Doosra ek aadmi hai, ya ek transgender person. Unke liye us committee par sunne ki koi saaf legal zimmedaari nahi hai. Wajah law ke naam mein hi hai: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, jo 22 April 2013 ko bana aur 9 December 2013 se laagu hai [[sc-aureliano-fernandes-2023]]. Ye general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Main aadmi hoon: kya POSH Act mujhe protect karta hai?

Nahi. Act apna remedy "aggrieved woman" ko deta hai: woh aurat jo "of any age whether employed or not" ho, yaani kisi bhi umar ki, naukri par ho ya na ho, aur jo workplace par sexual harassment ka ilzaam lagaye. Likhit complaint, 90 din ki inquiry aur employer ki action lene ki duty, sab usi ki complaint se shuru hote hain [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Wahi bartaav report karne wala aadmi is law ke bahar hai.

Criminal law ye khaali jagah nahi bharta. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke jo offences harass hui aurat istemaal kar sakti hai, woh aurton ko dhyaan mein rakh kar likhe gaye hain: aurat ki modesty outrage karne ke liye assault (Section 74), aurat ki modesty ka apmaan karne wale shabd ya ishaare (Section 79). Sexual harassment (Section 75, teen saal tak) aur stalking (Section 78), apne shabdon ke hisaab se, sirf ek aadmi hi kar sakta hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Aadmi ke liye jo bachta hai woh general offences hain, jo facts par depend karte hain, jaise hurt, grievous hurt ya wrongful confinement. Voluntarily causing hurt mein zyada se zyada ek saal ki jail hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Inme se koi bhi us cheez ko sexual harassment nahi kehta jo asal mein hui.

## Main transgender hoon: kaam par harassment ke liye kaun sa law hai?

2014 mein Supreme Court ne NALSA v. Union of India mein transgender persons ko "third gender" maana aur kaha ki unhe Constitution ke Articles 14, 15, 16, 19 aur 21 ki protection haasil hai [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]]. Iske baad aaya Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019, jisne transgender maane gaye har insaan ko "a right to self-perceived gender identity", yaani apni pehchaan khud tay karne ka haq diya [[indiacode-transgender-act-2019]]. Harassment ke khilaaf iski sabse saaf protection criminal hai, aur woh kamzor hai. Act ka Section 18(d) transgender person ke physical, sexual, verbal, emotional aur economic abuse ko ek hi clause mein rakhta hai, jiski saza 6 mahine se 2 saal ki jail aur fine hai. 2026 ke amendment ne ye section dobara likha, lekin range wahi rakhi [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]]. Iski tulna BNS se kijiye: aurat ke sexual harassment par teen saal tak, aur rape par kam se kam 10 saal [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Transgender person ke liye kitna bhi gambhir sexual abuse usi bracket mein hai jisme ek verbal insult hai.

Do pech aur hain. 2026 ke amendment ne apni pehchaan khud tay karne ka haq hata diya, aur ye daayra chhota kar diya ki Act ke tahat transgender person kise maana jaayega; ab is term mein "persons with different sexual orientations and self-perceived sexual identities" shaamil nahi hain [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]]. Is amendment ko Supreme Court mein challenge kiya gaya hai, jisne 17 August 2026 ko petitions suni [[scobserver-transgender-amendment-hearing-2026]]. Aur November 2025 tak sirf 20 states aur union territories ne woh Transgender Protection Cells banaye the jo 2020 ke Rules har state ke liye zaroori batate hain [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]].

## Sarkar ne toh kaha tha ki naye criminal laws gender-neutral hain?

Kaha tha. July 2024 ke ek note mein Home Ministry ne kaha ki "various offences against women and children have been made gender-neutral in BNS, covering all victims and perpetrators regardless of gender", yaani aurton aur bachchon ke khilaaf kai offences BNS mein gender-neutral kar diye gaye hain, aur ye bhi ki gender ki definition mein "now includes transgender individuals", yaani ab transgender log bhi shaamil hain [[pib-new-criminal-laws-2024]].

Doosri baat ek chhote se maayne mein sach hai. Code kehta hai ki pronoun "he" kisi bhi insaan ke liye hai, "whether male, female or transgender". Lekin wahi code "man" ko male aur "woman" ko female human being define karta hai, aur sexual offences inhi shabdon mein likhe gaye hain [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Rape ab bhi aadmi dwara aurat par assault tak seemit hai, aur sexual harassment aur stalking aadmi ke kiye gaye acts tak.

Yaani ye daava un offences tak pahunchta hi nahi jinhe ek harass hua worker dhoondhega. Pronoun ka daayra badha. Sections ka nahi.

## Aaj kya kiya ja sakta hai?

- Likh lijiye: date, jagah, exact shabd, kisne dekha. Messages aur emails aisi jagah save kariye jahan se employer unhe delete na kar sake.
- HR se likh kar poochiye ki company ki harassment policy har gender ko cover karti hai ya nahi. Employer chahe toh aisi policy likh sakta hai; agar aapki company ne likhi hai, toh use istemaal kariye.
- Agar aap transgender hain, toh employer se likh kar poochiye ki transgender staff ki harassment complaints kaun sunta hai, aur jawab sambhal kar rakhiye. Transgender Persons Act ke Section 18(d) ke tahat police complaint ka raasta bhi aapke liye khula hai [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]].
- Maar-peet, dhamki ya confinement ke liye police ke paas jaaiye. Cognizable offence ki information kisi bhi police station mein di ja sakti hai, chahe ghatna kahin bhi hui ho [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Legal services authorities free legal aid deti hain [[nalsa]].
- Agar aap 18 se kam umar ke hain, toh law alag hai: POCSO 18 se kam ke har bachche ko protect karta hai, gender koi bhi ho [[pocso-act-2012]].
- Tele-MANAS 14416 par har kisi ko free counselling deta hai, transgender persons ko bhi [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].

## Ye gap kaise band hoga?

Ye Parliament ka kaam hai. November 2023 mein Parliament ki apni Standing Committee on Home Affairs ne chetaya tha ki purane penal code ka Section 377 hatane se aadmiyon aur transgender persons ke khilaaf non-consensual sexual offences bina saza ke reh jaayenge, aur use rakhne ki sifaarish ki thi. Sarkar ne ye sifaarish nahi maani [[prs-standing-committee-bns-2023]]. 14 October 2024 ko Supreme Court ne aise offences banane ki maang wali plea sunne se mana kar diya, ye kehte hue ki woh Parliament ko offence banane ka direction nahi de sakta [[livelaw-sc-bns-sexual-offences-men-pil-2024]].

Teen badlaav zyadatar kaam kar denge: ek aisa workplace law jiski committee har worker ki sune, harassment aur stalking ke aise offences jo kisi ke gender par depend na karein, aur transgender persons ke sexual abuse ke liye aisi saza jo nuksaan ke barabar ho. Isse aurton ka kuch nahi chhinta. Committee, deadlines aur employer ki duties wahi rehti hain; bas unhe istemaal karne wale log badh jaate hain.

Ye sabke liye maayne rakhta hai, kyunki abhi ke shabd kuch sikhate hain. Jo law sirf aurton ki sunta hai, woh aadmiyon se kehta hai ki unke saath jo hua woh ginti mein nahi aata, transgender workers se kehta hai ki unka maamla kam ginti ka hai, aur har office se kehta hai ki harassment aurton ka issue hai jise manage karna hai, aisa bartaav nahi jise rokna hai.

prevention-evidence-what-stops-violence.en:
Almost everything a government does about sexual violence happens after it. A camera records it. A crisis centre receives the survivor. A court tries the accused, often years later. All three are needed, and none of them stops the first assault. The work that tries to do that is called prevention, and in 2022 programmes to prevent violence against women received 0.2% of the world's development aid [[who-vaw-estimates-2025]].

## 0.2% and 0.2%: the prevention gap

Two small numbers from the World Health Organization (WHO) belong side by side. The first is the 0.2% of aid that went to programmes focused on preventing violence against women in 2022. WHO says such funding fell further in 2025 [[who-vaw-estimates-2025]].

The second: over the past 20 years, violence against women by their partners has declined by only about 0.2% a year on average. WHO says the "one in three" figure has stagnated, and that the global goal of eliminating violence against women and girls by 2030 is very unlikely to be met [[who-vaw-factsheet-2026]].

The matching digits are a coincidence, and money is not the only reason violence has barely moved. But little can be expected from work that is barely paid for.

In India, WHO's modelled estimate is that 29.9% of women aged 15-49 who have ever been married or partnered have faced physical or sexual violence from a partner at some point, and 22.4% in the past 12 months [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]].

## Where India's safety money goes

Aid is not a national budget, so look at India's own purse for women's safety, the Nirbhaya Fund. A written reply in the Rajya Sabha, reported in July 2026, shows that three schemes took 63% of all the money released: Safe City projects in eight cities (Rs 1,686.73 crore), One Stop Centres (Rs 1,299.10 crore) and fast-track courts for rape and POCSO cases (Rs 1,234.55 crore) [[theprint-nirbhaya-fund-rajya-sabha-2026]].

Safe City projects aim to make public places safer, through urban infrastructure and faster access to police [[pib-wcd-nirbhaya-fund-2025]]. A One Stop Centre helps a woman after violence. A fast-track court tries a case after an FIR. Survivors need all of them. But none of the three pays to change what boys and men learn about power and consent before anyone is hurt.

The same reply lists a Panchayati Raj programme to sensitise men as "ongoing", with zero spending. And of Rs 7,990.85 crore set aside for the fund since 2013-14, Rs 1,287.83 crore, about 16%, was still unused in July 2026 [[theprint-nirbhaya-fund-rajya-sabha-2026]]. The money existed. The one listed programme aimed at men had spent none of it.

A camera can be counted, inaugurated and audited. A change in what a 13-year-old boy believes about girls cannot be photographed, and its result, an assault that never happens, appears in no register. Budgets tend to follow what can be shown.

## What schools can do

The first place the evidence points to is the classroom. UNESCO's 2018 international guidance found that curriculum-based sexuality education contributes to later first sex, less frequent sex, fewer partners, less risk-taking and more use of condoms and contraception. It also states that such education does not increase sexual activity [[unesco-itgse-2018]].

These are measures of sexual behaviour and health, not of assault, and most of the trials were run outside India. The case for the classroom as violence prevention rests on what good teaching contains: the words for your own body, the rule that sex needs agreement, and where help is. Boys and queer children, who are also assaulted, need those lessons as much as girls do. That is a reasoned argument, not yet a measured Indian result, and the missing measurement is itself a symptom of the 0.2%.

India has a programme on paper: under the School Health and Wellness Programme, whose curriculum was launched in February 2020, two teachers in every government and government-aided school are to run a one-hour session a week, for 24 weeks a year, on 11 themes that include gender equality and safety against violence [[pib-school-health-ambassador-curriculum-2020]]. Private schools are not covered. UNESCO's 2021 status report found sexuality education in India left to the states, with Jharkhand's Udaan the only state-run programme at scale [[unesco-cse-global-status-report-2021]].

## What homes can do

The second place is the home, and here the evidence is Indian. In 2014 the International Center for Research on Women and UNFPA surveyed 9,205 men and 3,158 women in seven states. 60% of the men said they had acted violently towards a wife or partner at some point, a count that includes emotional and economic violence [[icrw-unfpa-masculinity-ipv-son-preference-2014]].

In the same study, men who had frequently faced discrimination as children were four times more likely to be violent to their partners. Men raised in families where the father did household chores were two times more likely to hold gender-equitable attitudes [[icrw-unfpa-masculinity-ipv-son-preference-2014]].

A survey like this shows association, not proof of cause, and it is twelve years old. It also linked men's economic stress to violence. Still, a boy who grows up treated unfairly learns one lesson about how power is used. A boy who watches his father cook and clean learns another about what men do.

## A budget for before, not after

No costed Indian prevention plan sits in our verified data, so what follows is a list of items, not rupees.

- Teacher time and training, so the weekly hour is actually taught, with consent and violence on the timetable, in private schools too.
- Work with men and boys through panchayats, youth clubs and workplaces, the kind of line that showed zero spending.
- Support for parents, since the Indian evidence points at fathers and at how boys are treated at home.
- Measurement: trials in Indian schools and districts, published, so the next budget pays for what worked here.

None of this replaces One Stop Centres or courts. But paying only afterwards is the expensive choice. WHO notes that in some countries violence against women costs between 1% and 6% of GDP in police, justice, social protection and health services [[who-vaw-factsheet-2026]].

Until budgets change, the two places the evidence points to are open to anyone: the school your family uses, and your own home.
prevention-evidence-what-stops-violence.hg:
Sexual violence ke baare mein sarkar jo kuch karti hai, woh lagbhag sab violence ke baad hota hai. Camera use record karta hai. Crisis centre survivor ko sambhalta hai. Court accused par trial chalata hai, aksar saalon baad. Teeno zaroori hain, par inme se koi bhi pehle assault ko nahi rokta. Jo kaam yeh koshish karta hai use prevention kehte hain, aur 2022 mein women ke khilaf violence rokne wale programmes ko duniya ke development aid ka sirf 0.2% mila [[who-vaw-estimates-2025]].

## 0.2% aur 0.2%: prevention ka gap

World Health Organization (WHO) ke do chhote numbers saath rakhkar dekhne chahiye. Pehla hai aid ka woh 0.2% jo 2022 mein women ke khilaf violence rokne par focused programmes ko gaya. WHO ke mutabik 2025 mein yeh funding aur gir gayi [[who-vaw-estimates-2025]].

Doosra: pichhle 20 saal mein women par unke partners ki violence average mein saal ka sirf lagbhag 0.2% ghati hai. WHO kehta hai ki "one in three" wala figure wahin atka hua hai, aur 2030 tak women aur girls ke khilaf violence khatam karne ka global goal poora hona bahut mushkil hai [[who-vaw-factsheet-2026]].

Dono digits ka milna ek ittefaq hai, aur violence ke mushkil se hilne ki wajah sirf paisa nahi hai. Par jis kaam ke liye mushkil se paisa diya jaata hai, usse zyada ummeed bhi nahi ki ja sakti.

India ke liye WHO ka modelled estimate yeh hai ki 15-49 saal ki jin women ki kabhi shaadi hui ya partner raha, unme se 29.9% ne kabhi na kabhi partner ki physical ya sexual violence jheli hai, aur 22.4% ne pichhle 12 mahino mein [[who-vaw-prevalence-report-2025]].

## India ka safety ka paisa kahan jaata hai

Aid kisi desh ka budget nahi hota, isliye India ka apna women's-safety ka fund dekho, yaani Nirbhaya Fund. Rajya Sabha ke ek written reply se, jo July 2026 mein report hua, pata chalta hai ki release hue saare paise ka 63% teen schemes ko gaya: aath shehron ke Safe City projects (Rs 1,686.73 crore), One Stop Centres (Rs 1,299.10 crore) aur rape aur POCSO cases ke fast-track courts (Rs 1,234.55 crore) [[theprint-nirbhaya-fund-rajya-sabha-2026]].

Safe City projects ka maqsad urban infrastructure aur police tak jaldi pahunch ke zariye public places ko safe banana hai [[pib-wcd-nirbhaya-fund-2025]]. One Stop Centre violence ke baad ek aurat ki madad karta hai. Fast-track court FIR ke baad case sunta hai. Survivors ko in sabki zaroorat hai. Par in teeno mein se koi bhi is par paisa nahi lagata ki ladke aur men taakat aur consent ke baare mein kya seekhte hain, kisi ko chot pahunchne se pehle.

Usi reply mein men ko sensitise karne ka ek Panchayati Raj programme "ongoing" likha hai, aur uska kharcha zero hai. Aur 2013-14 se fund ke liye rakhe gaye Rs 7,990.85 crore mein se Rs 1,287.83 crore, yaani lagbhag 16%, July 2026 tak use hi nahi hua tha [[theprint-nirbhaya-fund-rajya-sabha-2026]]. Paisa tha. Men ke liye list hue us ek programme ne usme se kuch bhi kharch nahi kiya.

Camera gina ja sakta hai, uska inauguration ho sakta hai, audit ho sakta hai. Ek 13 saal ka ladka ladkiyon ke baare mein jo maanta hai, usme aaye badlaav ki photo nahi kheenchi ja sakti. Aur uska result, yaani woh assault jo kabhi hua hi nahi, kisi register mein nahi aata. Budget aksar usi cheez ke peeche jaata hai jo dikhayi ja sake.

## Schools kya kar sakte hain

Evidence sabse pehle classroom ki taraf ishara karta hai. UNESCO ki 2018 ki international guidance ne paaya ki curriculum-based sexuality education se pehla sex der se hota hai, sex kam baar hota hai, partners kam hote hain, risk-taking ghatti hai aur condom aur contraception ka use badhta hai. Guidance yeh bhi kehti hai ki aisi education se sexual activity nahi badhti [[unesco-itgse-2018]].

Yeh sab sexual behaviour aur health ke measures hain, assault ke nahi, aur zyada tar trials India ke bahar hue the. Classroom ko violence prevention maanne ka case is baat par tika hai ki achhi teaching mein kya hota hai: apni body ke sahi shabd, yeh rule ki sex ke liye dono ki haan zaroori hai, aur yeh jaankari ki madad kahan milegi. Ladkon aur queer bachchon par bhi assault hota hai, aur unhe yeh lessons utne hi chahiye jitne ladkiyon ko. Yeh ek soch-samajhkar banaya gaya argument hai, abhi tak India mein naapa gaya result nahi, aur is measurement ka na hona khud us 0.2% ka ek symptom hai.

Kaagaz par India ke paas ek programme hai: School Health and Wellness Programme ke tahat, jiska curriculum February 2020 mein launch hua, har government aur government-aided school mein do teachers ko hafte mein ek ghante ka session lena hai, saal mein 24 hafte, 11 themes par, jinme gender equality aur violence se safety shamil hain [[pib-school-health-ambassador-curriculum-2020]]. Private schools isme cover nahi hote. UNESCO ki 2021 status report ne paaya ki India mein sexuality education states par chhodi gayi hai, aur bade scale par chalne wala ek hi state-run programme hai, Jharkhand ka Udaan [[unesco-cse-global-status-report-2021]].

## Ghar kya kar sakte hain

Doosri jagah ghar hai, aur yahan evidence Indian hai. 2014 mein International Center for Research on Women aur UNFPA ne saat states mein 9,205 men aur 3,158 women ka survey kiya. 60% men ne kaha ki unhone kabhi na kabhi apni wife ya partner ke saath violence ki hai; is ginti mein emotional aur economic violence bhi shamil hai [[icrw-unfpa-masculinity-ipv-son-preference-2014]].

Usi study mein, jin men ne bachpan mein baar-baar discrimination jhela tha, unke apne partner par violence karne ke chances chaar guna the. Aur jin parivaaron mein papa ghar ka kaam karte the, wahan pale-badhe men ke gender-equitable soch rakhne ke chances do guna the [[icrw-unfpa-masculinity-ipv-son-preference-2014]].

Aisa survey association dikhata hai, cause ka pakka saboot nahi, aur yeh barah saal purana hai. Isne men ke economic stress ko bhi violence se joda tha. Phir bhi, jis ladke ke saath bachpan mein na-insaafi hoti hai, woh taakat ke istemal ke baare mein ek sabak seekhta hai. Jo ladka apne papa ko khana banate aur safai karte dekhta hai, woh mard kya karte hain is baare mein doosra sabak seekhta hai.

## Baad ka nahi, pehle ka budget

Hamare verified data mein India ka koi aisa prevention plan nahi hai jiska kharcha joda gaya ho. Isliye neeche cheezon ki list hai, rupayon ki nahi.

- Teachers ka time aur training, taaki hafte ka woh ghanta sach mein padhaya jaye, timetable mein consent aur violence ho, aur private schools mein bhi.
- Panchayats, youth clubs aur workplaces ke zariye men aur boys ke saath kaam, yaani usi tarah ki line jisme zero kharcha dikha.
- Parents ke liye support, kyunki Indian evidence papa ki taraf aur is taraf ishara karta hai ki ghar mein ladkon ke saath kaisa bartaav hota hai.
- Measurement: Indian schools aur districts mein trials, jo publish hon, taaki agla budget us cheez par kharch ho jo yahan kaam aayi.

Inme se kuch bhi One Stop Centres ya courts ki jagah nahi leta. Par sirf baad mein paisa dena hi mehnga raasta hai. WHO ke mutabik kuch deshon mein women ke khilaf violence ka kharcha, police, justice, social protection aur health services ko jodkar, GDP ke 1% se 6% ke beech hota hai [[who-vaw-factsheet-2026]].

Jab tak budgets nahi badalte, evidence jin do jagahon ki taraf ishara karta hai woh sabke liye khuli hain: woh school jahan tumhare ghar ke bachche padhte hain, aur tumhara apna ghar.

public-transport-harassment-delhi-18-cas.en:
Eighteen. That is how many cases of sexual harassment on public transport were registered in Delhi in the whole of 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. In the same year police in Delhi city registered 13,396 crimes against women, more than any other metropolitan city [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The first number cannot describe the evening bus. It describes how rarely what happens on that bus is ever written down.

## 459 cases, and Delhi's 18

Across India, police registered 459 cases of sexual harassment of women in public transport in 2024, against 525 in 2023 and 422 in 2022 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. That is a little more than one case a day for the whole country.

Kerala recorded the most, 100. Madhya Pradesh had 65, Maharashtra 61 and Uttar Pradesh 54. Delhi had 18 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Read as a safety ranking, this says Kerala's buses are India's most dangerous and Delhi's among the safest. The National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) itself warns against that reading: a rise in registered crime is not the same as a rise in crime, and steps such as e-FIR facilities or women's help desks can push the numbers up [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A state where a woman can complain easily and is taken seriously will log more cases than one where she is told to let it go. A low count says more about reporting than about safety.

## Eight years of small numbers

NCRB's figures for sexual harassment by place start in 2017. Since then the public transport row has read:

| Year | Cases | Year | Cases |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2017 | 599 | 2021 | 357 |
| 2018 | 730 | 2022 | 422 |
| 2019 | 607 | 2023 | 525 |
| 2020 | 375 | 2024 | 459 |

The figures come from three editions of Crime in India: 2018 [[ncrb-cii-2018]], 2021 [[ncrb-cii-2021]] and 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Even the peak, 730 in 2018, works out to two cases a day. The dip in 2020 and 2021 coincides with the COVID-19 lockdowns, when fewer people travelled. It is not evidence that behaviour changed.

Three things keep this row small. First, it counts FIRs, not incidents. Second, NCRB counts each FIR once, under its most serious offence [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Sexual harassment under Section 75 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) carries up to three years, while assault to outrage a woman's modesty under Section 74 carries one to five [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. An FIR that invokes both is counted under the graver offence, not in this row. Third, most cases are never tied to a named place: of 15,609 sexual harassment cases registered in 2024, 12,592, or 81%, were filed under "other places" [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

The row also counts only women. Section 75 can, by its wording, be committed only by a man, and NCRB files it under crimes against women. A boy, a man or a transgender person harassed on a train does not appear here at all.

## The 200-times gap

How far is the police count from what people live through? The clearest measurement is old, and it is about neighbourhoods, not buses. In 2005, 12% of households told the India Human Development Survey that unmarried girls in their neighbourhood were "sometimes" or "often" harassed. NCRB records implied a figure of only 0.06% of households [[aej-iyer-political-voice-2012]]. That is a gap of about 200 times.

A newer, smaller study points the same way. Of 270 women domestic workers surveyed in Delhi-NCR between May and November 2024, 24% had experienced sexual harassment in the previous two years [[jagori-domestic-workers-report-2025]]. It is one small group in one region, and the figure is not limited to buses and trains. Set it beside 18 FIRs anyway.

Imagine a 19-year-old on a packed Delhi bus at 6 pm. A man behind her presses against her and does not move when she shifts. She tells him to step back. Another passenger says it is crowded and she should adjust. The conductor is at the other end. Her stop comes and she gets off. Nobody has taken a name or a bus number. In NCRB's table, nothing happened.

> The table does not count harassment. It counts the times a woman went to the police and an officer registered a case.

## From 'eve teasing' to street sexual harassment

The word India uses may be part of why so little is reported. On 16 August 2023 the Supreme Court released its Handbook on Combating Gender Stereotypes, which tells judges to replace "eve teasing" with "street sexual harassment" [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

"Teasing" is what siblings do. The word tells the woman she is overreacting, the co-passenger that it is not his business and the constable that there is nothing to register. It does its damage long before a case reaches any judge.

The law has no offence called eve teasing. It has sexual harassment (Section 75, up to three years, or up to one year for sexually coloured remarks), words or gestures intended to insult a woman's modesty (Section 79, up to three years) and stalking (Section 78) [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Those are the names to use at a police station.

## What a safer ride needs

Nobody who is harassed owes the system a complaint. But a ride gets safer only when more of what happens on it is recorded.

- **The person harassed.** Note the bus or coach number, route, time and stop. You can report at any police station, wherever the offence took place, or by electronic communication [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- **Fellow passengers.** Stand next to her, ask if she is okay, tell the conductor and offer your name as a witness. Do not film her.
- **Conductors and drivers.** A complaint reports a crime, not a quarrel between passengers. Call 112 and note the time and place.
- **Transport police and operators.** Register the FIR instead of counselling both sides. Display a complaint number in every bus and coach, and publish complaints by route.
- **Apps.** A complaint button helps only if it creates a record that someone is required to answer.

This is general information, not legal advice. A Delhi that registers ten times as many cases next year will not have become ten times more dangerous. It will have started counting.
public-transport-harassment-delhi-18-cas.hg:
Sirf 18. 2024 ke poore saal mein Delhi mein public transport par sexual harassment ke itne hi cases register hue [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Usi saal Delhi city mein police ne auraton ke khilaaf 13,396 crimes register kiye, kisi bhi doosre metropolitan city se zyada [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Pehla number shaam ki bus ka haal nahi ho sakta. Yeh batata hai ki us bus mein jo hota hai, woh kitni kam baar kahin likha jaata hai.

## 459 cases, aur Delhi ke 18

Poore India mein police ne 2024 mein public transport mein auraton ke sexual harassment ke 459 cases register kiye, jabki 2023 mein 525 aur 2022 mein 422 the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yaani poore desh ke liye din mein ek se thoda zyada case.

Sabse zyada cases Kerala mein darj hue, 100. Madhya Pradesh mein 65, Maharashtra mein 61 aur Uttar Pradesh mein 54. Delhi mein 18 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Agar ise safety ranking ki tarah padhen, toh Kerala ki buses India mein sabse khatarnaak hain aur Delhi ki sabse safe buses mein se. National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) khud is tarah padhne se mana karta hai: registered crime ka badhna crime ka badhna nahi hai, aur e-FIR facilities ya women's help desks jaise kadam numbers ko upar le ja sakte hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Jis state mein aurat aasaani se complaint kar sakti hai aur uski baat seriously li jaati hai, wahan zyada cases darj honge, us state ke muqaable jahan use kaha jaata hai ki jaane do. Kam count safety se zyada reporting ke baare mein batata hai.

## Aath saal, chhote numbers

NCRB ke jagah ke hisaab se sexual harassment ke figures 2017 se shuru hote hain. Tab se public transport wali row kuch aisi rahi hai:

| Saal | Cases | Saal | Cases |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2017 | 599 | 2021 | 357 |
| 2018 | 730 | 2022 | 422 |
| 2019 | 607 | 2023 | 525 |
| 2020 | 375 | 2024 | 459 |

Yeh figures Crime in India ke teen editions se hain: 2018 [[ncrb-cii-2018]], 2021 [[ncrb-cii-2021]] aur 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Sabse ooncha saal, 2018 ke 730 cases bhi, din ke do cases bante hain. 2020 aur 2021 ki giraavat COVID-19 lockdowns ke saath aati hai, jab kam log safar kar rahe the. Yeh is baat ka saboot nahi ki bartaav badla.

Teen cheezein is row ko chhota rakhti hain. Pehli, yeh FIRs ginti hai, ghatnaayein nahi. Doosri, NCRB har FIR ko ek hi baar ginta hai, uske sabse serious offence ke under [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke Section 75 ke tahat sexual harassment par teen saal tak ki saza hai, jabki Section 74 ke tahat aurat ki modesty outrage karne ke iraade se assault par ek se paanch saal [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Jis FIR mein dono sections lagte hain, woh zyada serious offence ke under gini jaati hai, is row mein nahi. Teesri, zyada tar cases kisi naam wali jagah se jude hi nahi hote: 2024 mein register hue sexual harassment ke 15,609 cases mein se 12,592, yaani 81%, "other places" ke under darj hue [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Yeh row sirf auraton ko ginti hai. Section 75, apne shabdon ke hisaab se, sirf ek mard hi commit kar sakta hai, aur NCRB ise crimes against women ke under rakhta hai. Train mein harass hua ladka, mard ya transgender insaan yahan dikhta hi nahi.

## 200 guna ka gap

Police ki ginti aur logon ki asal zindagi ke beech kitna faasla hai? Sabse saaf measurement purana hai, aur woh mohallon ke baare mein hai, buses ke baare mein nahi. 2005 mein 12% households ne India Human Development Survey ko bataya ki unke mohalle mein unmarried ladkiyon ko "sometimes" ya "often" harass kiya jaata hai. NCRB ke records se sirf 0.06% households ka figure nikalta tha [[aej-iyer-political-voice-2012]]. Yaani lagbhag 200 guna ka gap.

Ek nayi, chhoti study bhi isi taraf ishaara karti hai. May se November 2024 ke beech Delhi-NCR mein survey ki gayi 270 women domestic workers mein se 24% ne pichhle do saal mein sexual harassment jhela tha [[jagori-domestic-workers-report-2025]]. Yeh ek region ka ek chhota group hai, aur yeh figure sirf buses aur trains tak seemit nahi hai. Phir bhi ise 18 FIRs ke saamne rakh kar dekhiye.

Sochiye, 19 saal ki ek ladki shaam 6 baje Delhi ki ek khachakhach bhari bus mein hai. Peeche khada aadmi us se sat kar khada hai aur uske hatne par bhi nahi hatta. Woh use peeche hone ko kehti hai. Ek aur passenger kehta hai ki bheed hai, adjust kar lo. Conductor bus ke doosre sire par hai. Uska stop aata hai aur woh utar jaati hai. Kisi ne na naam liya, na bus number. NCRB ki table mein kuch hua hi nahi.

> Yeh table harassment nahi ginti. Yeh un mauqon ko ginti hai jab ek aurat police ke paas gayi aur officer ne case register kiya.

## 'Eve teasing' se street sexual harassment tak

Itna kam report kyun hota hai, iski ek wajah shaayad woh shabd bhi hai jo India istemaal karta hai. 16 August 2023 ko Supreme Court ne apni Handbook on Combating Gender Stereotypes jaari ki, jo judges se kehti hai ki "eve teasing" ki jagah "street sexual harassment" likhen [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

"Teasing" toh bhai-behen karte hain. Yeh shabd aurat se kehta hai ki woh overreact kar rahi hai, co-passenger se kehta hai ki yeh uska maamla nahi, aur constable se kehta hai ki register karne laayak kuch hai hi nahi. Case kisi judge tak pahunche, usse bahut pehle yeh shabd apna nuksaan kar chuka hota hai.

Law mein eve teasing naam ka koi offence nahi hai. Law mein sexual harassment hai (Section 75, teen saal tak, ya sexually coloured remarks par ek saal tak), aurat ki modesty ka apmaan karne ke iraade se kahe gaye shabd ya ishaare hain (Section 79, teen saal tak), aur stalking hai (Section 78) [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Police station mein inhi naamon ka istemaal kijiye.

## Safe ride ke liye kya chahiye

Jiske saath harassment hua, us par system ko complaint dene ka koi karz nahi hai. Lekin ride tabhi safe hoti hai jab usmein jo hota hai uska zyada hissa record ho.

- **Jiske saath harassment hua.** Bus ya coach number, route, time aur stop note kijiye. Aap kisi bhi police station mein report kar sakte hain, offence chahe kahin bhi hua ho, ya electronic communication se [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- **Saath ke passengers.** Uske paas jaakar khade ho jaiye, poochhiye ki woh theek hai, conductor ko bataiye aur witness ke taur par apna naam dijiye. Uska video mat banaiye.
- **Conductors aur drivers.** Complaint ek crime ki report hai, passengers ka aapsi jhagda nahi. 112 par call kijiye aur time aur jagah note kijiye.
- **Transport police aur operators.** Dono taraf ko samjhaane ke bajaye FIR register kijiye. Har bus aur coach mein complaint number lagaiye, aur route ke hisaab se complaints publish kijiye.
- **Apps.** Complaint button tabhi kaam ka hai jab usse aisa record bane jiska jawab dena kisi ki zimmedaari ho.

Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi. Jo Delhi agle saal das guna cases register karegi, woh das guna zyada khatarnaak nahi ho gayi hogi. Usne ginna shuru kiya hoga.

queer-students-sex-education-silence.en:
Imagine a 16-year-old in Lucknow who has known for a while that he likes boys. If his school holds a session on growing up, he may hear about periods, pimples and "attraction to the opposite sex". He hears nothing about anyone like him, except perhaps a joke from the back of the room. Every school is different, and some teachers handle this well. But silence is common far beyond India. In a UNESCO survey of countries in Asia-Pacific, sub-Saharan Africa and Latin America, sexual orientation and gender identity was among the three topics least included in secondary-school curricula, alongside safe abortion and online media [[unesco-cse-global-status-report-2021]].

## The topics curricula skip

That is a finding across many countries, so it cannot tell us how Indian classrooms compare [[unesco-cse-global-status-report-2021]]. What we can check is the national policy. India's National Education Policy 2020 does not once use the words "sex", "sexual" or "sexuality" in its 66 pages. It does mention gender identities, lists gender sensitivity among the skills every student should learn, and asks for safe ways for adolescents to report discrimination and harassment [[nep-2020-full-text]].

So gender gets a few lines. Sexual orientation, which cannot be named without the word "sexual", is simply absent.

## What Indian law now says about queer lives

The law has moved faster than the syllabus. On 15 April 2014, in NALSA, the Supreme Court recognised transgender persons as a "third gender" and upheld their right to self-identify their gender [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]]. On 6 September 2018, in Navtej Singh Johar, a five-judge bench unanimously read down Section 377 of the IPC, decriminalising consensual sex between adults of the same sex [[scobserver-navtej-johar-2018]]. In August 2022 the National Medical Commission told state medical councils that "conversion therapy" on LGBTQIA+ people is professional misconduct [[scroll-nmc-conversion-therapy-2022]].

Then part of it moved back. The Transgender Persons Amendment Act, 2026, in force from 25 May 2026, deletes the right to self-perceived gender identity. A District Magistrate now issues a transgender certificate only after examining a medical board's recommendation [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]]. The new definition also says the term does not include "persons with different sexual orientations and self-perceived sexual identities" [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]]. The amendment is under challenge: on 17 August 2026 the Union told the Supreme Court that identity cards already issued under the 2019 Act would continue to operate while the case is pending [[scobserver-transgender-amendment-hearing-2026]]. This is general information, not legal advice.

So a trans student in 2026 could learn that the Supreme Court said she may name her own gender, and that Parliament has since handed that decision to a medical board. Unless someone tells her, she may learn neither.

## NEP 2020: transgender students and gender identity on campus

NEP 2020 does name transgender students. It lists girls and transgender students among "Socio-Economically Disadvantaged Groups", creates a Gender-Inclusion Fund for them, and asks all higher education institutions to sensitise faculty, counsellors and students on gender identity and to strictly enforce no-discrimination and anti-harassment rules [[nep-2020-full-text]].

That matters, but notice the limits. The sensitisation clause is written for colleges and universities. It speaks of gender identity, so a gay, lesbian or bisexual student whose gender is not in question is not who these lines are about. For schools, a court has gone further. In 2021 the Madras High Court, in S. Sushma v. Commissioner of Police, ordered a ban on attempts to medically "cure" LGBTQIA+ people, and sensitisation of schools, along with police, the judiciary and health workers [[livelaw-madras-hc-sushma-2021]].

## What silence teaches a queer teenager

Silence is not neutral. A student who hears only boy-girl examples learns that the normal story has no place for them. A student who never hears that being queer is not an illness has no way to recognise a "cure" for what it is. The NMC's rule binds registered doctors [[scroll-nmc-conversion-therapy-2022]], but it only helps a family that knows it exists.

Silence also leaves gaps in safety. Consent lessons that imagine only boy-girl couples skip the questions queer teenagers actually face. And the law they meet as adults is uneven. Under 18, the POCSO Act protects every child, whatever their gender [[pocso-act-2012]]. After 18, Section 63 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita defines rape as an act by a man against a woman, so an adult man cannot legally be a victim of rape [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. When the BNS replaced the IPC on 1 July 2024, it dropped Section 377, which had punished non-consensual "carnal intercourse against the order of nature", and put nothing in its place [[scroll-delhi-hc-unnatural-offences-bns-2024]]. Under the Transgender Persons Act, sexual abuse of a transgender person carries only six months to two years in prison [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]]. A student who has never heard any of this cannot know what protection exists, or where it is missing.

And silence isolates, so help should not be a secret. Tele-MANAS, the Health Ministry's free 24x7 mental-health helpline on 14416, offers counselling to anyone in need, including transgender persons [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]]. The Mental Healthcare Act, 2017 bars discrimination in mental health care on grounds including sexual orientation [[indiacode-mhca-2017]].

## What inclusive teaching sounds like

It does not need a new syllabus. It needs a few sentences said out loud, by a teacher who means them:

- "Some of you will be attracted to girls, some to boys, some to more than one gender, and some to no one. All of these are normal."
- "Consent works the same way in every relationship: a clear yes, and the right to stop."
- "Being gay, lesbian, bisexual or transgender is not an illness, and doctors in India may not try to 'cure' it."
- "If someone tells you the name they go by, use it."
- "Slurs are abuse. In this room, we stop them."

Some teachers already talk like this; for the rest, the first step is one sentence. Students who cannot wait for their school will find a session plan in our guide for peer educators.
queer-students-sex-education-silence.hg:
Socho, Lucknow ka ek 16 saal ka ladka hai jise kuch time se pata hai ki use ladke pasand hain. Agar uske school mein growing up par koi session hota hai, toh usme periods, pimples aur "opposite sex ki taraf attraction" ki baat ho sakti hai. Uske jaise kisi insaan ki koi baat nahi hoti, bas shayad peeche ki bench se koi joke. Har school alag hai, aur kuch teachers ise achhe se handle bhi karte hain. Lekin yeh chuppi sirf India mein nahi hai. UNESCO ke Asia-Pacific, sub-Saharan Africa aur Latin America ke deshon ke ek survey mein, secondary school curriculum mein sabse kam shaamil teen topics mein se ek tha sexual orientation aur gender identity. Baaki do the safe abortion aur online media [[unesco-cse-global-status-report-2021]].

## Curriculum kin topics ko skip karta hai

Yeh kai deshon ko milakar nikla finding hai, isliye isse yeh pata nahi chalta ki Indian classrooms kaise hain [[unesco-cse-global-status-report-2021]]. Hum yeh zaroor check kar sakte hain ki national policy kya kehti hai. National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 ke 66 pages mein "sex", "sexual" ya "sexuality" word ek baar bhi nahi aata. Haan, isme gender identities ka zikr hai, yeh gender sensitivity ko un skills mein ginti hai jo har student ko seekhni chahiye, aur kehti hai ki teenagers ke liye discrimination aur harassment report karne ke safe tareeke hon [[nep-2020-full-text]].

Yaani gender par kuch lines hain. Lekin sexual orientation, jiska naam "sexual" word ke bina liya hi nahi ja sakta, poori tarah gaayab hai.

## Indian law aaj queer logon ke baare mein kya kehta hai

Law syllabus se tez chala hai. 15 April 2014 ko NALSA judgment mein Supreme Court ne transgender logon ko "third gender" maana aur unke apna gender khud identify karne ke haq ko uphold kiya [[pib-transgender-rights-backgrounder-2025]]. 6 September 2018 ko Navtej Singh Johar case mein paanch judges ki bench ne unanimously IPC ki Section 377 ko read down kiya, aur do adults ke beech consent se bane same-sex relations crime nahi rahe [[scobserver-navtej-johar-2018]]. August 2022 mein National Medical Commission ne state medical councils se kaha ki LGBTQIA+ logon par "conversion therapy" karna professional misconduct hai [[scroll-nmc-conversion-therapy-2022]].

Phir iska kuch hissa peeche bhi gaya. 25 May 2026 se lagu Transgender Persons Amendment Act, 2026 ne apni gender identity khud decide karne ka haq hata diya hai. Ab District Magistrate transgender certificate tabhi denge jab woh medical board ki recommendation dekh lein [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]]. Nayi definition yeh bhi kehti hai ki transgender mein "persons with different sexual orientations and self-perceived sexual identities" shaamil nahi hain [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]]. Is amendment ko challenge kiya gaya hai: 17 August 2026 ko Union ne Supreme Court se kaha ki 2019 ke Act ke under pehle se bane identity cards case chalne tak valid rahenge [[scobserver-transgender-amendment-hearing-2026]]. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

Yaani 2026 mein ek trans student yeh jaan sakti hai ki Supreme Court ne use apna gender khud batane ka haq diya tha, aur phir Parliament ne yeh faisla ek medical board ko de diya. Agar koi use na bataye, toh shayad woh in dono mein se kuch bhi na jaane.

## NEP 2020: campus par transgender students aur gender identity

NEP 2020 transgender students ka naam leti hai. Yeh girls aur transgender students ko "Socio-Economically Disadvantaged Groups" mein ginti hai, unke liye ek Gender-Inclusion Fund banati hai, aur saare higher education institutions se kehti hai ki woh faculty, counsellors aur students ko gender identity par sensitise karein aur no-discrimination aur anti-harassment rules sakhti se lagu karein [[nep-2020-full-text]].

Yeh important hai, par iski limits bhi dekho. Sensitisation wali line colleges aur universities ke liye likhi gayi hai. Yeh gender identity ki baat karti hai, toh ek gay, lesbian ya bisexual student, jiske gender par koi sawaal nahi hai, in lines ke daayre mein nahi aata. Schools ke maamle mein ek court isse aage gaya hai. 2021 mein Madras High Court ne S. Sushma v. Commissioner of Police case mein LGBTQIA+ logon ka medically "ilaaj" karne ki koshishon par ban ka order diya, aur police, judiciary aur health workers ke saath-saath schools ko bhi sensitise karne ko kaha [[livelaw-madras-hc-sushma-2021]].

## Chuppi ek queer teenager ko kya sikhaati hai

Chuppi neutral nahi hoti. Jo student sirf ladka-ladki wale examples sunta hai, woh seekhta hai ki "normal" kahani mein uski koi jagah nahi. Jisne kabhi nahi suna ki queer hona bimaari nahi hai, woh kisi "cure" ko pehchaan hi nahi paata ki woh asal mein kya hai. NMC ka rule registered doctors par lagu hota hai [[scroll-nmc-conversion-therapy-2022]], lekin yeh usi family ke kaam aata hai jise iske baare mein pata ho.

Chuppi safety mein bhi gaps chhod deti hai. Consent ki jo class sirf ladka-ladki couples ko imagine karti hai, woh un sawaalon ko skip kar deti hai jo queer teenagers ke saamne sach mein aate hain. Aur adult hone par jo law milta hai, woh sabke liye barabar nahi hai. 18 se kam umar mein POCSO Act har bachche ko protect karta hai, chahe uska gender kuch bhi ho [[pocso-act-2012]]. 18 ke baad, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita ki Section 63 rape ko aisa act maanti hai jo ek aadmi ek aurat ke saath karta hai, yaani law ki nazar mein ek adult aadmi rape ka victim nahi ho sakta [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. 1 July 2024 ko jab BNS ne IPC ki jagah li, toh Section 377 hata di gayi, jo bina consent ke "carnal intercourse against the order of nature" ki saza deti thi, aur uski jagah kuch nahi joda gaya [[scroll-delhi-hc-unnatural-offences-bns-2024]]. Transgender Persons Act ke under kisi transgender person ke sexual abuse ki saza sirf chhe mahine se do saal ki jail hai [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]]. Jis student ne in mein se kuch bhi nahi suna, woh nahi jaan sakta ki protection kahan hai aur kahan nahi.

Aur chuppi akela kar deti hai, isliye help ki jaankari chhupi nahi rehni chahiye. Tele-MANAS, Health Ministry ki free 24x7 mental health helpline 14416, har zaroorat-mand ko counselling deti hai, transgender logon ko bhi [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]]. Mental Healthcare Act, 2017 mental health care mein discrimination par rok lagata hai, jisme sexual orientation ke basis par discrimination bhi shaamil hai [[indiacode-mhca-2017]].

## Inclusive teaching kaisi sunai deti hai

Iske liye naya syllabus nahi chahiye. Bas kuch sentences chahiye, jo koi teacher dil se aur khulkar bole:

- "Tum mein se kuch ko ladkiyan pasand aayengi, kuch ko ladke, kuch ko ek se zyada gender ke log, aur kuch ko koi nahi. Yeh sab normal hai."
- "Consent har relationship mein ek jaisa hota hai: saaf 'haan', aur rukne ka haq."
- "Gay, lesbian, bisexual ya transgender hona bimaari nahi hai, aur India mein doctors iska 'ilaaj' karne ki koshish nahi kar sakte."
- "Koi tumhe bataye ki use kis naam se bulaya jaaye, toh usi naam se bulao."
- "Slurs abuse hain. Is class mein hum inhe rokte hain."

Kuch teachers pehle se aise baat karte hain; baaki ke liye pehla step bas ek sentence hai. Jo students apne school ka intezaar nahi kar sakte, unke liye hamari peer educators wali guide mein session chalane ka poora plan hai.

reporting-rape-trial-what-media-can-publ.en:
A rape trial is one of the few places in Indian public life that the public is not allowed to watch. That is deliberate. It protects the survivor at the moment she is most exposed: giving evidence about what was done to her. But these cases matter, and reporters, YouTubers and Instagram pages will keep covering them. Here are five questions they ask, answered from the law and the record. This is general information, not legal advice.

## Can I report what happens inside the courtroom?

Not without the court's permission. Under Section 366 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), the trial of rape and of the main POCSO offences must be held in camera, as far as practicable before a woman judge, and nothing about those proceedings may be published without it [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Rape trials have been held behind closed doors since 25 December 1983 [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]].

In camera means the public and press stay outside. What a witness said, what the survivor was asked, how she answered: none of it is yours to publish unless the court allows it.

Closed does not mean secret, or slow. When the Supreme Court moved the Kathua rape and murder trial out of Jammu and Kashmir to Pathankot in Punjab on 7 May 2018, it ordered the hearings held in camera and day to day [[theprint-kathua-transfer-2018]]. On 10 June 2019 the Pathankot court convicted six of the seven accused and acquitted one [[theprint-kathua-verdict-2019]]. The verdict was reported. The testimony stayed inside.

## What exactly does Section 73 forbid?

Section 73 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) punishes anyone who prints or publishes "any matter in relation to any proceeding" before a court in a rape or other sexual-offence case without the court's previous permission. The penalty is up to two years in prison and a fine [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Three things follow.

- **It is separate from Section 72.** That section bans identifying the survivor, also with up to two years in prison [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Permission to report proceedings is not permission to identify her.
- **High Court and Supreme Court judgments are exempt.** You may report and quote them [[indiacode-bns-2023]], still without identifying her.
- **It begins with "whoever".** It does not say newspaper or channel. A reel is a publication too.

## Can I name the accused before a verdict?

The law bans naming the survivor, not, as a rule, an adult accused. But naming him carries three risks.

The first is to her. In 2024, the accused was a family member in 2,134 rape cases, and a neighbour, employer or other known person in 12,584 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. When he is her uncle, landlord or boss, his name can identify her as surely as her own, and that makes it a Section 72 problem.

The second is accuracy. Courts completed 20,587 rape trials in 2024: 5,032 ended in conviction and 13,980 in acquittal [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. An acquittal is not proof that a complaint was false; trials collapse for many reasons, as our myth-check on "false cases" explains. But a man you called a rapist before the verdict may walk out with a court record that says otherwise. Until a court convicts, write "accused" or "charged with", and attribute every claim.

The third is defamation, which can follow a story for years. In October 2018, during India's #MeToo movement, a Union minister of state filed a criminal defamation case in a Delhi court against a woman journalist who had accused him of sexual harassment; he denied the allegations [[livelaw-ramani-acquittal-2021]]. On 17 February 2021 the court acquitted her, ruling that "the right of reputation cannot be protected at the cost of the right of life and dignity of woman" [[delhi-court-metoo-defamation-judgment-2021]]. His appeal, admitted by the Delhi High Court in January 2022, was listed for final hearing on 24 September 2026, more than five years after the verdict; we could not confirm the outcome of that listing [[livelaw-akbar-appeal-2026]]. The trial court backed a woman's right to speak about what happened to her. That is not a licence for anyone else to declare a person guilty.

## The case is already "everywhere" online: does the law still apply?

Yes. The Supreme Court's 2018 direction in Nipun Saxena v. Union of India begins with "no person" and names social media alongside print and TV: no one may publish a rape victim's name, or disclose "even in a remote manner" facts that could identify her [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. Nothing in Section 72 or in that ruling makes an exception for a name that is already circulating.

The Kathua case showed what this costs. In April 2018 the Delhi High Court ordered 12 media houses to pay Rs 10 lakh each for revealing the child's identity [[thehindu-delhi-hc-kathua-media-2018]]. Each was fined for its own report.

The same goes for FIRs. The court ordered that FIRs in rape and POCSO cases must not be put in the public domain [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. A copy doing the rounds on WhatsApp does not change that. Don't post it.

## Writing about a case fairly, from FIR to verdict

Most of the real story sits outside the courtroom, and you are free to tell it.

- **At the FIR.** Report that a case was registered, under which law, and what the police did next. Leave out anything that points to her.
- **During investigation.** The BNSS gives police two months to complete a rape investigation [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Whether they met that deadline is a fair story.
- **During trial.** The BNSS says a rape trial should finish within two months of the chargesheet [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
