At the end of 2024, 1,85,785 rape cases were still pending trial, 89.8% of all those before the courts [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. You can tell that story without a word from inside the courtroom.
- **At the verdict.** Report the outcome and the sentence. Name a convicted man only if that cannot identify her, say which court convicted him and when, and check whether an appeal is pending. Never present an acquitted person as guilty.

The survivor, whether a woman, a girl or a boy, is a person with rights, not a plot. Her name, face, village, school and testimony are not your content. The failures of police, courts and families are.
reporting-rape-trial-what-media-can-publ.hg:
Rape trial India ki public life ki un gini-chuni jagahon mein se hai jahan public ko dekhne ki ijaazat nahi hai. Yeh jaan-boojh kar hai. Isse survivor us waqt protected rehti hai jab woh sabse zyada exposed hoti hai: jab woh court mein bata rahi hoti hai ki uske saath kya hua. Lekin yeh cases sabke liye matter karte hain, aur reporters, YouTubers aur Instagram pages inhe cover karte rahenge. Yeh rahe unke paanch sawaal, law aur record se jawab ke saath. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Kya courtroom ke andar ki baat report ki ja sakti hai?

Court ki permission ke bina nahi. Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) ke Section 366 ke hisaab se rape aur POCSO ke main offences ka trial in camera hoga, jahan tak ho sake woman judge ke saamne, aur court ki permission ke bina in proceedings ki koi baat publish nahi ki ja sakti [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Rape trials 25 December 1983 se band kamre mein hote aa rahe hain [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]].

In camera ka matlab hai public aur press bahar rahenge. Witness ne kya kaha, survivor se kya poocha gaya, usne kya jawab diya: court ki permission ke bina isme se kuch bhi publish karna aapka kaam nahi.

Band kamra matlab secret nahi, aur slow bhi nahi. 7 May 2018 ko Supreme Court ne Kathua rape aur murder ka trial Jammu and Kashmir se bahar, Punjab ke Pathankot shift kiya, aur order diya ki hearings in camera aur day-to-day hon [[theprint-kathua-transfer-2018]]. 10 June 2019 ko Pathankot court ne saat mein se chhe accused ko convict kiya aur ek ko bari kiya [[theprint-kathua-verdict-2019]]. Verdict report hua. Testimony andar hi rahi.

## Section 73 exactly kya mana karta hai?

Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ka Section 73 kehta hai ki rape ya aise doosre sexual-offence case mein court proceedings se judi "any matter", yaani koi bhi baat, court ki pehle se permission ke bina print ya publish karna crime hai. Saza do saal tak ki jail aur fine hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Isse teen baatein nikalti hain.

- **Yeh Section 72 se alag hai.** Section 72 survivor ki identity kholne par ban lagata hai, aur usme bhi do saal tak ki jail hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Proceedings report karne ki permission, uski identity kholne ki permission nahi hai.
- **High Court aur Supreme Court ke judgments exempt hain.** Aap unhe report aur quote kar sakte hain [[indiacode-bns-2023]], lekin tab bhi survivor ki identity nahi khol sakte.
- **Section "whoever" se shuru hota hai.** Usme newspaper ya channel nahi likha. Reel bhi publication hi hai.

## Kya verdict se pehle accused ka naam liya ja sakta hai?

Law survivor ka naam lene par ban lagata hai, aam taur par adult accused ka naam lene par nahi. Lekin uska naam lene mein teen risks hain.

Pehla risk survivor ko hai. 2024 mein 2,134 rape cases mein accused family member tha, aur 12,584 mein padosi, employer ya koi aur jaan-pehchaan wala [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Jab woh uska chacha, makaan-maalik ya boss ho, toh uska naam bhi utni hi aasaani se survivor ki identity khol deta hai jitna uska apna naam. Tab yeh Section 72 ka maamla ban jaata hai.

Doosra risk accuracy ka hai. 2024 mein courts ne 20,587 rape trials poore kiye: 5,032 mein conviction hua aur 13,980 mein accused bari hue [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Bari hone ka matlab yeh nahi ki complaint jhoothi thi; trials kai wajahon se gir jaate hain, jaisa humare "false cases" wale myth-check mein samjhaya gaya hai. Lekin jise aapne verdict se pehle rapist bol diya, woh aise court record ke saath bahar aa sakta hai jo kuch aur kehta ho. Jab tak court convict na kare, "accused" ya "charged with" likhiye, aur har claim ka source batayiye.

Teesra risk defamation ka hai, jo saalon tak peecha kar sakta hai. October 2018 mein, India ke #MeToo movement ke dauraan, ek Union minister of state ne Delhi ki ek court mein ek woman journalist ke khilaaf criminal defamation case kiya, jisne un par sexual harassment ka allegation lagaya tha; minister ne allegations se inkaar kiya [[livelaw-ramani-acquittal-2021]]. 17 February 2021 ko court ne journalist ko bari kar diya aur kaha ki "the right of reputation cannot be protected at the cost of the right of life and dignity of woman" [[delhi-court-metoo-defamation-judgment-2021]]. Minister ki appeal Delhi High Court ne January 2022 mein admit ki thi, aur verdict ke paanch saal se zyada baad, 24 September 2026 ko final hearing ke liye list hui thi; us listing mein kya hua, yeh hum confirm nahi kar paaye [[livelaw-akbar-appeal-2026]]. Trial court ne ek aurat ke apne saath hui baat bolne ke haq ka saath diya. Iska matlab yeh nahi ki koi aur kisi ko bhi guilty declare kar de.

## Case pehle se online "har jagah" hai: kya tab bhi law laagu hota hai?

Haan. Nipun Saxena v. Union of India mein Supreme Court ka 2018 ka direction "no person" se shuru hota hai, aur print aur TV ke saath social media ka naam bhi leta hai: koi bhi rape victim ka naam publish nahi kar sakta, ya "even in a remote manner", yaani door se bhi, aisi baatein nahi bata sakta jisse uski pehchaan ho [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. Section 72 mein ya us ruling mein aisi koi chhoot nahi hai ki jo naam pehle se ghoom raha hai, use dobara chhapa ja sake.

Kathua case ne dikhaya ki iski keemat kya hoti hai. April 2018 mein Delhi High Court ne 12 media houses ko bachchi ki identity reveal karne par Rs 10 lakh each bharne ka order diya [[thehindu-delhi-hc-kathua-media-2018]]. Har ek par uski apni report ke liye fine laga.

FIR ke saath bhi yahi baat hai. Court ne order diya hai ki rape aur POCSO cases ki FIR public domain mein nahi daali jayengi [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. WhatsApp par ghoomti copy se yeh rule nahi badalta. Use post mat kijiye.

## FIR se verdict tak: case ke baare mein fair tareeke se kaise likhein

Asli story ka zyada hissa courtroom ke bahar hai, aur use batane ki aapko poori azaadi hai.

- **FIR ke waqt.** Batayiye ki case register hua, kis law mein, aur police ne aage kya kiya. Aisi koi baat mat likhiye jo survivor ki taraf ishaara kare.
- **Investigation ke dauraan.** BNSS ke hisaab se police ko rape investigation do mahine mein poori karni hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Police ne yeh deadline meet ki ya nahi, yeh ek fair story hai.
- **Trial ke dauraan.** BNSS kehta hai ki rape trial chargesheet ke baad do mahine mein khatam ho jaana chahiye [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. 2024 ke end mein 1,85,785 rape cases abhi bhi trial ke intezaar mein the, yaani courts ke saamne aise sabhi cases ka 89.8% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yeh story aap courtroom ke andar ka ek bhi shabd bataye bina suna sakte hain.
- **Verdict ke waqt.** Faisla aur saza batayiye. Convict ka naam tabhi lijiye jab usse survivor ki pehchaan na khule, batayiye ki kis court ne kab convict kiya, aur check kijiye ki appeal pending toh nahi. Jo bari ho gaya, use kabhi guilty ki tarah mat dikhaiye.

Survivor, chahe woh aurat ho, bachchi ho ya bachcha, ek insaan hai jiske apne rights hain, koi plot nahi. Uska naam, chehra, gaon, school aur testimony aapka content nahi hain. Police, courts aur families ki failures hain.

school-health-wellness-programme-explain.en:
Consider a 15-year-old in a government school in a district town. She has questions she cannot ask at home: whether her period pain is normal, whether the messages an older cousin keeps sending are okay, and where a girl her age can talk to a doctor. On paper, India has built three answers: a weekly health hour at school, a teenage peer educator nearby, and an adolescent clinic in the public health system. Here is what each promises, and what it cannot do.

## Two Health and Wellness Ambassadors per school

The School Health and Wellness Programme, part of Ayushman Bharat, got its curriculum on 12 February 2020. It asks every government and government-aided school to have two teachers, preferably one man and one woman, trained as "Health and Wellness Ambassadors". They are to run one-hour weekly sessions on 11 themes for 24 weeks a year, starting with schools in aspirational districts [[pib-school-health-ambassador-curriculum-2020]].

The model has an Indian precedent. UNESCO's 2021 global status report says Jharkhand's Udaan, a school-based adolescence education programme running since 2006, had reached over one million students by September 2019 and served as a blueprint for the national ambassador initiative [[unesco-cse-global-status-report-2021]].

The 11 themes, as the government listed them, are: growing up healthy; emotional well-being and mental health; interpersonal relationships; values and responsible citizenship; gender equality; nutrition, health and sanitation; healthy lifestyles; preventing and managing substance misuse; reproductive health and HIV prevention; safety and security against violence and injuries; and safe use of the internet, media and social media [[pib-school-health-ambassador-curriculum-2020]]. Several of them could carry what our 15-year-old needs. None is titled consent or sexuality, so what gets said depends on the material and the teacher.

One more caveat. The programme is meant for government and aided schools; had our 15-year-old been in a private school, it would not cover her.

## RKSK: from reproductive health to violence and mental health

The school hour sits inside a bigger health effort. The Health Ministry launched the Rashtriya Kishor Swasthya Karyakram (RKSK) on 7 January 2014 to reach 253 million adolescents, married and unmarried, in school and out of it [[nhm-adolescent-health-rksk-page-2026]]. That is a target, not a count of those reached.

Its real shift was in scope. Adolescent health had been limited to sexual and reproductive health; RKSK widened it to nutrition, injuries and violence, including gender-based violence, along with non-communicable diseases, mental health and substance misuse [[nhm-adolescent-health-rksk-page-2026]].

That widening matters, because in police data the offender is rarely a stranger. In 96.6% of POCSO penetrative sexual assault cases registered in 2024, the offender was someone the child knew: a family member in 8.3% of cases, a family friend, neighbour, employer or other known person in 37.8%, and a friend, online friend or live-in partner in 50.6% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. That last group also includes teenage relationships, because POCSO makes sexual activity with anyone under 18 an offence whatever the "consent". Either way, a programme about periods and pimples alone would miss the risks that sit inside a teenager's own circle and phone.

RKSK's clinical arm is the Adolescent Friendly Health Centre. These began in 2006 as Adolescent Reproductive and Sexual Health clinics and now offer counselling and care at primary and community health centres, district hospitals and medical colleges. National guidance says they should not sit next to labour rooms or STI and HIV testing centres, so that adolescents can visit without hesitation [[nhm-afhc-page-2026]]. In October 2025 the Ministry renamed them from "Clinics" to "Centres" because the word "clinic" carried stigma, and said about 1.7 crore adolescents used them in 2024-25, a figure that may count visits rather than people [[mohfw-afhc-rename-2025]].

## Saathiya: four teenage peer educators per village

RKSK's most local layer is a teenager. Four peer educators called Saathiya, two boys and two girls, are to be selected for every village, every 1,000 people or every ASHA habitation. Each forms a group of 15-20 boys or girls and runs weekly one- to two-hour sessions with a peer education kit, covering all six RKSK themes [[nhm-peer-education-page-2026]].

The logic is sound: many teenagers will ask someone their own age what they would never ask a teacher. The limit is just as clear. A teenage volunteer is not a counsellor, and anything serious, such as a disclosure of abuse, has to go to an adult who can act. Our guide for peer educators covers running such sessions safely.

We could not confirm how many Saathiyas have actually been selected and trained. The official page describes the design, not the reach [[nhm-peer-education-page-2026]].

## What these programmes are not

They are programmes, not a curriculum with legal force. UNESCO notes that in India responsibility for sexuality education is decentralised to the states [[unesco-cse-global-status-report-2021]]. After the 2007 backlash, the older national Adolescence Education Programme was banned or refused by somewhere between six and 12 states, depending on the count [[reprodhealth-plesons-jharkhand-cse-2020]]; our timeline of India's school sex education traces how it got there. Education policy is quieter still: the National Education Policy 2020 does not once use the words "sex", "sexuality", "puberty" or "menstruation" [[nep-2020-full-text]].

In 2024 the Supreme Court recommended comprehensive sex education covering consent, and suggested an expert committee on health and sex education and POCSO awareness. Those were suggestions to the government, not binding directions [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]].

So a weekly wellness hour is not automatically comprehensive sexuality education. Whether it reaches consent, contraception or abuse depends on the themes, the teacher's training and the teacher's comfort. Privacy also has a legal limit. If a child discloses sexual abuse, the POCSO Act requires anyone who knows or suspects it, a teacher or doctor included, to report it to the police or the Special Juvenile Police Unit [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]]. That duty exists to protect the child. (This is general information, not legal advice.)

## How to check what your school offers

Ask the principal, in writing if you need a record:

- Who are the school's two Health and Wellness Ambassadors, and have they been trained?
- When is the weekly hour, and which themes has it covered this term?
- Does any session cover body changes, consent, violence and where to get help?
- In a private school: what does the school run instead?

Outside school, ask the ASHA worker or ANM whether a Saathiya group meets in your area, and where the nearest Adolescent Friendly Health Centre is. The National Health Mission's RKSK page is the official starting point [[nhm-rksk]].

If the answers are "nobody" and "never", that is information too. Write it down, and take it to the district education officer. A programme that exists only on a government web page has not yet reached the 15-year-old it was built for.
school-health-wellness-programme-explain.hg:
Socho, ek 15 saal ki ladki hai jo kisi district town ke government school mein padhti hai. Uske paas kuch sawaal hain jo woh ghar par nahi pooch sakti: kya period mein itna dard normal hai, kya bade cousin ke lagatar aate messages theek hain, aur uski umar ki ladki doctor se baat karne kahan jaaye? Kaagaz par sarkar ne uske liye teen jawab banaye hain: school mein hafte mein ek ghante ki health class, aas-paas ek teenage peer educator, aur sarkari health system mein adolescents ka clinic. Chalo dekhte hain ki har ek kya promise karta hai, aur kya nahi kar sakta.

## Har school mein do Health and Wellness Ambassadors

Ayushman Bharat ke School Health and Wellness Programme ka curriculum 12 February 2020 ko jaari hua. Yeh har government aur government-aided school se kehta hai ki do teachers ko, ho sake toh ek male aur ek female, "Health and Wellness Ambassadors" ki training mile. Yeh saal mein 24 hafte, har hafte ek ghante ke sessions mein 11 themes padhayenge, aur shuruaat aspirational districts ke schools se hogi [[pib-school-health-ambassador-curriculum-2020]].

Yeh idea India mein aazmaya ja chuka hai. UNESCO ki 2021 global status report ke mutabik Jharkhand ka Udaan, jo 2006 se schools mein chal raha adolescence education programme hai, September 2019 tak 10 lakh se zyada students tak pahunch chuka tha, aur national ambassador initiative isi ke blueprint par bani [[unesco-cse-global-status-report-2021]].

Sarkar ki list ke hisaab se 11 themes yeh hain: growing up healthy; emotional well-being aur mental health; interpersonal relationships; values aur responsible citizenship; gender equality; nutrition, health aur sanitation; healthy lifestyle; substance misuse se bachaav aur uska management; reproductive health aur HIV se bachaav; violence aur injuries se safety aur security; aur internet, media aur social media ka safe use [[pib-school-health-ambassador-curriculum-2020]]. Inme se kai themes mein woh baatein aa sakti hain jo hamari 15 saal ki ladki ko chahiye. Par kisi theme ka naam consent ya sexuality nahi hai, isliye kya bola jaayega, yeh material aur teacher par tika hai.

Ek aur baat. Programme government aur aided schools ke liye hai; agar hamari 15 saal ki ladki private school mein hoti, toh yeh use cover nahi karta.

## RKSK: reproductive health se aage, violence aur mental health tak

School ka yeh ghanta ek bade health programme ka hissa hai. Health Ministry ne 7 January 2014 ko Rashtriya Kishor Swasthya Karyakram (RKSK) shuru kiya, 253 million (25.3 crore) adolescents tak pahunchne ke target ke saath: married aur unmarried, school jaane wale aur na jaane wale, sab [[nhm-adolescent-health-rksk-page-2026]]. Yeh target hai, is baat ki ginti nahi ki asal mein kitnon tak pahuncha.

Asli badlaav scope mein tha. Pehle adolescent health ka matlab sirf sexual aur reproductive health tha; RKSK ne isme nutrition, injuries aur violence jode, gender-based violence samet, aur saath mein non-communicable diseases, mental health aur substance misuse bhi [[nhm-adolescent-health-rksk-page-2026]].

Yeh bada scope zaroori hai, kyunki teenagers ko khatra aksar kisi stranger se nahi hota. 2024 mein POCSO ke tahat darj penetrative sexual assault ke 96.6% cases mein offender bachche ka jaan-pehchaan wala tha: 8.3% cases mein family member, 37.8% mein family friend, padosi, employer ya koi aur jaan-pehchaan wala, aur 50.6% mein dost, online dost ya live-in partner [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Is aakhri group mein teenagers ke apne rishte bhi aate hain, kyunki POCSO ke hisaab se 18 se kam umar ke kisi ke saath sexual activity offence hai, "consent" ho ya na ho. Jo bhi ho, jo programme sirf periods aur pimples ki baat kare, woh teenager ke apne daayre aur phone mein chhupa khatra miss kar dega.

RKSK ka clinic wala hissa hai Adolescent Friendly Health Centre (AFHC). Yeh 2006 mein Adolescent Reproductive and Sexual Health clinics ke roop mein shuru hue the, aur ab primary aur community health centres, district hospitals aur medical colleges mein counselling aur ilaaj dete hain. National guidance kehti hai ki yeh labour rooms ya STI aur HIV testing centres ke paas nahi hone chahiye, taaki adolescents bina jhijhak aa sakein [[nhm-afhc-page-2026]]. October 2025 mein Ministry ne inka naam "Clinics" se badalkar "Centres" kar diya, kyunki "clinic" shabd ke saath stigma juda tha. Ministry ke mutabik 2024-25 mein lagbhag 1.7 crore adolescents ne inki services li; ho sakta hai yeh ginti logon ki nahi, visits ki ho [[mohfw-afhc-rename-2025]].

## Saathiya: har gaon mein chaar teenage peer educators

RKSK ki sabse local kadi khud ek teenager hai. Har gaon, har 1,000 logon ya har ASHA habitation par chaar peer educators chune jaane hain, jinhe Saathiya kehte hain: do ladke aur do ladkiyan. Har Saathiya 15-20 ladkon ya ladkiyon ka group banata hai aur har hafte ek se do ghante ka session leta hai, peer education kit ke saath, RKSK ke saare chhe themes par [[nhm-peer-education-page-2026]].

Logic sahi hai: bahut se teenagers apni umar wale se woh pooch lete hain jo teacher se kabhi nahi poochenge. Par limit bhi utni hi saaf hai. Ek teenage volunteer counsellor nahi hota, aur koi serious baat, jaise koi abuse ke baare mein bataye, kisi aise bade tak jaani chahiye jo kuch kar sake. Aise sessions safely kaise chalayein, is par hamari peer educators wali guide hai.

Kitne Saathiya asal mein chune gaye aur kitnon ko training mili, yeh hum confirm nahi kar paaye. Official page design batata hai, reach nahi [[nhm-peer-education-page-2026]].

## Yeh programmes kya nahi hain

Yeh programmes hain, legal taakat wala curriculum nahi. UNESCO ke mutabik India mein sexuality education ki zimmedari states par chhodi gayi hai [[unesco-cse-global-status-report-2021]]. 2007 ke backlash ke baad purane national Adolescence Education Programme ko, ginti ke hisaab se, chhe se 12 states ne ban kiya ya lagoo karne se mana kiya [[reprodhealth-plesons-jharkhand-cse-2020]]; yeh naubat kaise aayi, yeh hamari school sex education timeline mein hai. Education policy toh aur bhi chup hai: National Education Policy 2020 mein "sex", "sexuality", "puberty" ya "menstruation" shabd ek baar bhi nahi aata [[nep-2020-full-text]].

2024 mein Supreme Court ne consent sikhane wali comprehensive sex education ki recommendation di, aur health aur sex education aur POCSO awareness ke liye ek expert committee ka suggestion diya. Lekin yeh sarkar ke liye suggestions the, aise orders nahi jinhe maanna zaroori ho [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]].

Isliye hafte ka ek wellness ghanta apne aap comprehensive sexuality education nahi ban jaata. Usme consent, contraception ya abuse ki baat hogi ya nahi, yeh themes, teacher ki training aur teacher ke comfort par tika hai. Privacy ki bhi ek legal limit hai. Agar koi bachcha sexual abuse ke baare mein batata hai, toh POCSO Act ke hisaab se jise bhi iska pata hai ya shak hai, teacher ho ya doctor, use police ya Special Juvenile Police Unit ko report karna hi hoga [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]]. Yeh duty bachche ki safety ke liye hai. (Yeh general jaankari hai, legal advice nahi.)

## Tumhare school mein kya hai, yeh kaise check karo

Principal se poocho, aur record chahiye toh likhkar:

- School ke do Health and Wellness Ambassadors kaun hain, aur kya unhe training mili hai?
- Hafte ka woh ghanta kab hota hai, aur is term mein kaun se themes cover hue?
- Kya kisi session mein body changes, consent, violence aur madad kahan milegi, in par baat hoti hai?
- Private school hai, toh wahan iski jagah kya chalta hai?

School ke bahar, ASHA worker ya ANM se poocho ki tumhare area mein koi Saathiya group chalta hai ya nahi, aur sabse paas ka Adolescent Friendly Health Centre kahan hai. National Health Mission ka RKSK page official starting point hai [[nhm-rksk]].

Agar jawab ho "koi nahi" aur "kabhi nahi", toh yeh bhi ek jaankari hai. Ise likh lo, aur district education officer tak le jao. Jo programme sirf sarkari website par hai, woh abhi tak us 15 saal ki ladki tak nahi pahuncha jiske liye woh bana tha.

sex-education-ban-2007-culture-argument.en:
In the spring of 2007, Indian states began shutting a classroom door. The new school sex-education course, introduced the year before under the Adolescence Education Programme, was banned or refused across a widening map. That year, the Ministry of Women and Child Development published its Study on Child Abuse: 53.22% of the 12,447 children it surveyed across 13 states reported one or more forms of sexual abuse [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. One arm of the state was recording what was happening to children. Others were deciding that children should not get the words to describe it.

## Spring 2007: the bans spread

In late March 2007, after Shiv Sena and BJP legislators raised the issue in the Assembly, the Maharashtra government banned sex education in the state's schools. It banned the CBSE's sex-education textbooks in the state and dropped a planned adolescence life-skills programme [[thehindu-maharashtra-sex-ed-ban-2007]]. By May, Reuters counted six states, including Gujarat, Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and Karnataka, that had banned the curriculum or refused to implement it [[reuters-nbc-india-states-ban-sex-ed-2007]].

Later counts were higher, and they do not agree. A 2020 study in the journal Reproductive Health, on how Jharkhand dealt with resistance to sexuality education, says that amid the backlash 12 states banned all Adolescence Education Programme and comprehensive sexuality education programmes [[reprodhealth-plesons-jharkhand-cse-2020]]. There is no official list, the study does not name the states, and refusing a curriculum is not the same as banning it. The safest statement is a range: soon after reaching classrooms, the programme was shut out of somewhere between six and 12 states.

## 'Too explicit', 'against Indian culture': the arguments

The reasons given were short: the course material was too explicit, or against Indian culture [[reuters-nbc-india-states-ban-sex-ed-2007]]. Madhya Pradesh put it most plainly: sex education had "no place in Indian culture", and the state planned to introduce yoga in schools instead. The Reproductive Health study notes that such claims were bolstered by parents and community members [[reprodhealth-plesons-jharkhand-cse-2020]].

Under the slogans sat three testable assumptions. First, that Indian children did not face the risks the course described. Second, that talking about sex pushes teenagers towards it. Third, that something gentler, like yoga or silence, would protect them instead.

India's own AIDS agency pushed back at the time. In May 2007 the head of the National AIDS Control Organisation (NACO), Sujatha Rao, warned that the bans put young lives at risk. To MPs who were also doctors, she had put it more bluntly: "Are you more concerned about culture than the lives of young people?" [[reuters-nbc-india-states-ban-sex-ed-2007]]

## What the government's own study found that year

The first assumption had already been tested, by the government itself. In the 2007 Study on Child Abuse, 21.90% of the children surveyed reported severe forms of sexual abuse and 5.69% said they had been sexually assaulted [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Half the abusers were people the child knew or who held a position of trust and responsibility. Boys made up 52.94% of the children who reported abuse. The abuse began as early as age 5, gained momentum from age 10 and peaked between 12 and 15: the very years an adolescence education programme exists for [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]].

Most children carried it alone. Of those who reported sexual assault, 72.1% had told no one, and only 3.4% had gone to the police [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]].

The study has limits. It was not a national prevalence survey: it used a purposive sample that deliberately included street children, working children and children in institutions, and its definition of abuse was broad. But it was official evidence from the year of the bans, and it showed the opposite of the culture argument's picture: abuse by familiar people, and children with no words and no adult to tell.

## The other two arguments, against the UN's evidence

The other two assumptions have been tested too. The UN's International Technical Guidance on Sexuality Education, revised in 2018 by UNESCO and five other UN agencies, rests mainly on two evidence reviews: one of 87 studies in 2008, and a 2016 Oxford review of 22 systematic reviews and 77 randomised trials. It states that sexuality education, in or out of school, does not increase sexual activity, sexual risk-taking or STI/HIV infection rates [[unesco-itgse-2018]]. Curriculum-based programmes contribute to later first sex, fewer partners, less risk-taking and more use of condoms and contraception [[unesco-itgse-2018]].

Nor does the gentler alternative work. The same guidance found abstinence-only programmes ineffective at delaying first sex, reducing how often young people have sex or reducing their number of partners [[unesco-itgse-2018]]. Yoga may be good for a teenager. It cannot teach a 13-year-old the difference between a safe touch and an unsafe one, or which adult to tell.

Most of the trials behind that evidence were run outside India. But India has its own counter-example. Jharkhand's state-run Udaan programme, in schools since 2006, kept running while other states banned similar programmes. By September 2019 it had reached over one million students, and UNESCO calls it the only at-scale, state-run initiative of its kind in India [[unesco-cse-global-status-report-2021]]. A state that chose to answer resistance rather than ban the subject showed it could be taught at scale.

## The cost: a generation that knows less

The 15-to-24-year-olds in the fifth National Family Health Survey, carried out in 2019-21, were children in 2007. They went through school in the years after the bans, when what a teenager was taught depended on which state they lived in.

What they know is thin. In 2019-21, only 20.1% of young women and 28.5% of young men aged 15-24 had comprehensive knowledge of HIV/AIDS, down from 22% and 32% in 2015-16 [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Only 54.4% of young women knew where to get a condom, against 87.3% of young men [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

No survey can isolate what one banned lesson would have changed in one life, and the survey itself calls the fall among young women marginal. But the numbers show what the silence defended in 2007 looks like years later: most young Indians lack complete, basic knowledge of HIV, and young women are left furthest behind.

Seventeen years after the bans, the Supreme Court recommended comprehensive sex education that gives young people a clear understanding of consent [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]]. It was a recommendation, not a binding order. The question NACO's chief asked in 2007 has not gone away. It now sits with a new generation of legislators.
sex-education-ban-2007-culture-argument.hg:
2007 mein India ke kai states school ka ek darwaza band kar rahe the. Woh darwaza tha sex education ka naya course, jo ek saal pehle hi Adolescence Education Programme ke tahat schools mein aaya tha. Ek-ek karke states use ban kar rahe the, ya lagoo karne se mana kar rahe the. Usi saal Ministry of Women and Child Development ne child abuse par ek study chhaapi. Isme 13 states ke 12,447 bachchon se baat hui, aur unme se 53.22% ne bataya ki unke saath kisi na kisi tarah ka sexual abuse hua hai [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Sochiye. Sarkar ka ek hissa likh raha tha ki bachchon ke saath kya ho raha hai. Aur baaki hisse tay kar rahe the ki bachchon ko uske baare mein bolne ke shabd bhi na milein.

## 2007: ek ke baad ek ban

March 2007 ke aakhir mein, Assembly mein Shiv Sena aur BJP ke legislators ke mudda uthane ke baad, Maharashtra sarkar ne state ke schools mein sex education par rok laga di. Usne state mein CBSE ki sex education textbooks ban kar di aur adolescence life-skills ka jo programme aane wala tha, use bhi cancel kar diya [[thehindu-maharashtra-sex-ed-ban-2007]]. May tak news agency Reuters ne chhe aise states gine jinhone yeh course ban kar diya tha ya lagoo karne se mana kar diya tha. Inme Gujarat, Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh aur Karnataka the [[reuters-nbc-india-states-ban-sex-ed-2007]].

Baad ki gintiyan isse badi nikli, aur aapas mein mel nahi khaati. 2020 mein journal Reproductive Health mein ek study chhapi, is baare mein ki Jharkhand ne sex education ke virodh ko kaise sambhala. Iske mutabik us backlash ke daur mein 12 states ne Adolescence Education Programme aur comprehensive sexuality education ke saare programmes band kar diye [[reprodhealth-plesons-jharkhand-cse-2020]]. Koi official list nahi hai, study states ke naam nahi deti, aur course lagoo na karna ban karne jaisa nahi hota. Isliye sabse safe baat ek range hai: classrooms tak pahunchne ke kuch hi samay baad yeh programme chhe se 12 states ke beech kahin bahar ho gaya.

## 'Bahut explicit', 'culture ke khilaaf': ban ke arguments

Wajahein chhoti si thi: course material bahut explicit hai, ya Indian culture ke khilaaf hai [[reuters-nbc-india-states-ban-sex-ed-2007]]. Madhya Pradesh sarkar ne sabse seedhi baat kahi: sex education ki "Indian culture mein koi jagah nahi" hai, aur state ka plan tha ki iski jagah schools mein yoga laaya jaaye. Reproductive Health wali study batati hai ki aisi baaton ko parents aur community ke logon ka bhi saath mila [[reprodhealth-plesons-jharkhand-cse-2020]].

In naaron ke peeche teen assumptions thi, aur teeno ko test kiya ja sakta hai. Pehli: Indian bachchon ko woh khatre hain hi nahi jinki baat yeh course karta hai. Doosri: sex par baat karne se teenagers sex ki taraf badhte hain. Teesri: koi naram raasta, jaise yoga ya chuppi, unhe bacha lega.

Desh ki apni AIDS agency ne usi waqt iska virodh kiya. May 2007 mein National AIDS Control Organisation (NACO) ki head Sujatha Rao ne chetaya ki yeh ban young logon ki jaan ko khatre mein daal rahe hain. Usse pehle woh un MPs se, jo khud doctor bhi the, seedha pooch chuki thi: "Are you more concerned about culture than the lives of young people?" Yaani, kya aapko young logon ki zindagi se zyada culture ki fikr hai? [[reuters-nbc-india-states-ban-sex-ed-2007]]

## Usi saal sarkar ki apni study ne kya bataya

Pehli assumption ko sarkar ki apni study pehle hi parakh chuki thi. 2007 ki Study on Child Abuse mein 21.90% bachchon ne severe sexual abuse ki baat batayi, aur 5.69% ne kaha ki unpar sexual assault hua [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Abuse karne walon mein aadhe log bachche ke jaan-pehchaan wale the, ya aise log jin par bachche ke bharose aur dekhbhaal ki zimmedari thi. Abuse ki baat batane wale bachchon mein 52.94% ladke the. Abuse 5 saal ki umar se hi shuru ho jaata tha, 10 saal ke baad tez hota tha, aur 12 se 15 saal ki umar mein sabse zyada tha. Yahi toh woh umar hai jiske liye adolescence education bani hai [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]].

Zyada tar bachche yeh bojh akele utha rahe the. Jin bachchon ne sexual assault ki baat batayi, unme se 72.1% ne usse pehle kisi ko kuch nahi bataya tha, aur sirf 3.4% police tak gaye the [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]].

Is study ki apni limits hain. Yeh poore desh ki tasveer dene wala survey nahi tha. Isme jaan-boojhkar street children, kaam karne wale bachche aur institutions mein rehne wale bachche bhi shaamil kiye gaye the, aur abuse ki definition kaafi badi rakhi gayi thi. Phir bhi yeh sarkari evidence tha, aur ban wale saal mein hi aaya tha. Yeh culture wale argument ki ulti tasveer dikhata tha: jaan-pehchaan walon ke haathon abuse, aur aise bachche jinke paas na shabd the, na koi bada jise woh bata sakein.

## Baaki do arguments, UN ke evidence ke saamne

Baaki do assumptions bhi test ho chuki hain. Sexuality education par UN ki International Technical Guidance 2018 mein revise hui, jise UNESCO ne paanch aur UN agencies ke saath milkar jaari kiya. Yeh mainly do reviews par tiki hai: 2008 ka ek review jisme 87 studies dekhi gayi, aur 2016 ka Oxford review jisme 22 systematic reviews aur 77 randomised trials dekhe gaye. Guidance saaf kehti hai: sexuality education, school mein ho ya bahar, sexual activity, risky behaviour ya STI/HIV infection nahi badhati [[unesco-itgse-2018]]. Ulta, curriculum wale programmes ke achhe nateeje dikhe hain: pehla sex der se, kam partners, kam risk, aur condom aur contraception ka zyada use [[unesco-itgse-2018]].

Naram raasta bhi kaam nahi karta. Isi guidance ke mutabik sirf abstinence sikhane wale programmes bekaar hain: na pehla sex taalte hain, na sex kam karte hain, na partners kam karte hain [[unesco-itgse-2018]]. Yoga teenagers ke liye achha ho sakta hai. Par yoga ek 13 saal ke bachche ko safe touch aur unsafe touch ka fark nahi sikha sakta, na yeh bata sakta hai ki kis bade se baat karni hai.

Is evidence ke peeche ke zyada tar trials India ke bahar hue the. Lekin India ke paas apni misaal bhi hai. Jharkhand sarkar ka Udaan programme 2006 se schools mein hai, aur jab doosre states aise programmes ban kar rahe the, tab bhi yeh chalta raha. September 2019 tak yeh 10 lakh se zyada students tak pahunch chuka tha, aur UNESCO ise desh mein apni tarah ka akela bada, state-run programme kehta hai [[unesco-cse-global-status-report-2021]]. Jis state ne ban lagane ki jagah virodh ka jawab dena chuna, usne dikha diya ki yeh padhai bade scale par ho sakti hai.

## Keemat: ek generation jo kam jaanti hai

NFHS-5, yaani fifth National Family Health Survey, 2019-21 mein hua. Usme jo young log 15 se 24 saal ke the, woh 2007 mein bachche the. Unki schooling ban ke baad ke saalon mein hui, jab teenager ko kya padhaya jaayega, yeh is par tika tha ki woh kis state mein rehta hai.

Unki jaankari kamzor hai. 2019-21 mein 15-24 saal ki sirf 20.1% young women aur 28.5% young men ko HIV/AIDS ki comprehensive knowledge thi, jabki 2015-16 mein yeh 22% aur 32% thi [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Sirf 54.4% young women ko pata tha ki condom kahan milta hai; young men mein yeh 87.3% tha [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Koi survey yeh alag se nahi naap sakta ki ek band ki gayi class kisi ek zindagi mein kya badal deti, aur survey khud young women mein aayi is girawat ko marginal kehta hai. Lekin yeh numbers dikhate hain ki 2007 mein jis chuppi ko bachaya gaya, woh saalon baad kaisi dikhti hai: zyada tar young Indians ke paas HIV ki poori, basic jaankari nahi hai, aur ladkiyan sabse peeche chhoot gayi hain.

Ban ke 17 saal baad Supreme Court ne recommend kiya ki aisi comprehensive sex education di jaaye jo young logon ko consent ki saaf samajh de [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]]. Yeh ek recommendation thi, maanna zaroori wala order nahi. NACO chief ne 2007 mein jo sawaal poocha tha, woh khatam nahi hua. Ab woh legislators ki nayi generation ke saamne khada hai.

sex-education-parents-culture-questions.en:
Consider a father in Patna whose 12-year-old daughter brings home a school worksheet called "Growing up". His first reaction is about trust, not evidence: who decided my child needs this, what else are they teaching, and why was I not asked? Parents, teachers and religious leaders hold the keys to sex education in India. In 2007, amid a nationwide backlash backed by parents and community members, somewhere between six and 12 states, depending on who was counting, banned or refused to run school sexuality-education programmes [[reprodhealth-plesons-jharkhand-cse-2020]]. Worries like his deserve answers, not ridicule. Here are five.

## Will it make children curious, or 'spoil' them?

Children are curious already; the question is where that curiosity goes. The UN's 2018 guidance on sexuality education rests mainly on two evidence reviews: a 2008 review of 87 studies, and a 2016 Oxford review of 22 systematic reviews and 77 randomised trials. It states that sexuality education does not increase sexual activity, sexual risk-taking or STI and HIV infection rates [[unesco-itgse-2018]]. Curriculum-based programmes work the other way: they contribute to later first sex, fewer partners and more condom and contraceptive use [[unesco-itgse-2018]].

What does not work is telling teenagers only to stay away from sex. Abstinence-only programmes do not delay first sex or reduce the number of partners [[unesco-itgse-2018]]. Most of these trials ran outside India, which is a reason to test Indian programmes, not to ignore the evidence.

## At what age should it start?

Earlier than most parents expect, but it does not start with sex. In the government's 2007 Study on Child Abuse, sexual abuse reported by children began as early as age 5, gained momentum from age 10 and peaked between 12 and 15 [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. The study used a non-random sample and is nearly two decades old; India has not run a national survey since. UNICEF's 2024 global estimates point the same way: most childhood sexual violence happens in adolescence, with a spike between 14 and 17 [[unicef-sexual-violence-children-2024]].

So the teaching has to arrive before those years. For young children, sexuality education does not mean teaching about sex. It means knowing their bodies, naming their feelings, and knowing what to do about violence or abuse. In 2024 the Supreme Court suggested an expert committee for health and sex education, and for POCSO awareness among children "from an early age" [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]].

A rough ladder: in the early school years, correct names for body parts, safe and unsafe touch, and "no secrets about your body"; before puberty, periods and wet dreams, for girls and boys alike; in the teens, consent, relationships, contraception, online safety and the law. Sons need this as much as daughters. The POCSO Act protects every child under 18, boys included [[pocso-act-2012]].

## Isn't this the family's job, not the school's?

It is both. Children are safest when they hear the same clear message from more than one trusted adult: parents and family, but also teachers. Families can start early; schools make sure no child is left out.

Families are not managing it alone. In a 2016 analysis of 88 Indian studies, only 48% of adolescent girls had been told about periods before their first one [[bmjopen-van-eijk-mhm-india-2016]]. That is the most basic conversation there is, and about half of girls did not get it in time.

There is a harder reason too. In the 2007 study, 50% of abusers were people the child knew or who held a position of trust and responsibility [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. When the person harming a child is inside the family circle, the child needs a safe adult outside it, such as a teacher who has talked openly about body safety. Our data story on why "stranger danger" is the wrong lesson has today's police figures.

## Does it go against religion and culture?

Nothing in good sexuality education asks a family to give up its faith. Its content is families and relationships; respect, consent and bodily autonomy; anatomy, puberty and menstruation; contraception and pregnancy; and infections including HIV. Respect, honesty and keeping children safe are values most families already hold, whatever their faith. At home, parents can add what their family believes.

The "against Indian culture" argument was used to ban school programmes in 2007; our investigation of those bans tests it against the evidence. Since then, Indian institutions have moved the other way. The Health Ministry's adolescent health programme, launched on 7 January 2014, covers violence, including gender-based violence, and mental health alongside sexual and reproductive health [[nhm-adolescent-health-rksk-page-2026]]. The Supreme Court has recommended comprehensive sex education that explains consent [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]], and in January 2026 it ordered that boys and male teachers in schools be sensitised about menstruation [[livelaw-sc-jaya-thakur-judgment-2026]]. This is not an import. India's own courts and ministries are asking for it.

## What do children learn when nobody tells them?

They still learn. They learn from friends, forwards and porn, which is not made to teach consent, protection or care. They learn that some things cannot be said: in the 2007 study, only 26.8% of young adults who had been sexually assaulted in childhood had ever told anyone [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. And periods still cost girls school days: about a quarter (24%) of adolescent girls in India missed school during them [[bmjopen-van-eijk-mhm-india-2016]].

Myths that nobody corrects in school can last a lifetime. In 2019-21, 35.1% of Indian men aged 15-49 agreed that contraception is women's business, and 19.6% agreed that women who use contraception may become promiscuous [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

A child who is told nothing is not protected by innocence, only left alone with their questions. Parents do not need every answer. They need to go first.
sex-education-parents-culture-questions.hg:
Patna ke ek father ke baare mein sochiye. Unki 12 saal ki beti school se ek worksheet laati hai jiska naam hai "Growing up". Unka pehla reaction evidence ka nahi, bharose ka hota hai: yeh kisne decide kiya ki meri bachchi ko iski zaroorat hai, aur kya-kya padha rahe hain, aur mujhse poocha kyon nahi gaya? India mein sex education ki chaabi parents, teachers aur dharm-guruon ke haath mein hai. 2007 mein desh bhar mein sex education ke khilaaf backlash hua, jise parents aur community ke logon ka bhi saath mila, aur kaun gin raha tha uske hisaab se 6 se 12 states ne schools ke sexuality education programmes ban kar diye ya chalane se mana kar diya [[reprodhealth-plesons-jharkhand-cse-2020]]. Aisi chintaon ka mazaak nahi, jawab banta hai. Yahan aise paanch sawaal hain.

## Kya isse bachchon mein curiosity badhegi, ya woh 'bigad' jayenge?

Bachchon ke mann mein sawaal toh pehle se hote hain. Asli baat yeh hai ki woh jawab kahan dhoondhte hain. UN ki 2018 ki sexuality education guidance mainly do evidence reviews par tiki hai: 2008 ka ek review jisme 87 studies thi, aur 2016 ka Oxford review jisme 22 systematic reviews aur 77 randomised trials the. Guidance saaf kehti hai: sexuality education se na sexual activity badhti hai, na risk lena, na STI aur HIV ke infection rates [[unesco-itgse-2018]]. Ulta, curriculum-based programmes se pehli baar sex der se hota hai, partners kam hote hain, aur condom aur contraception ka use badhta hai [[unesco-itgse-2018]].

Jo tareeka kaam nahi karta, woh hai teenagers se bas itna kehna ki sex se door raho. Sirf abstinence sikhane wale programmes na pehli baar sex ko taal paate hain, na partners ki ginti ghata paate hain [[unesco-itgse-2018]]. Inmein se zyada tar trials India ke bahar hue. Iska matlab hai ki Indian programmes ko bhi test kiya jaaye, yeh nahi ki evidence ko ignore kar diya jaaye.

## Yeh kis umar se shuru hona chahiye?

Aap jitna sochte hain, usse pehle. Par iski shuruaat sex se nahi hoti. Sarkar ki 2007 ki Study on Child Abuse mein bachchon ne jo sexual abuse report kiya, woh 5 saal ki umar se hi shuru ho jaata tha, 10 saal ke baad tezi se badhta tha, aur 12 se 15 saal ki umar mein sabse zyada tha [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Yeh study random sample par nahi thi aur lagbhag do dashak purani hai; uske baad India ne aisa koi national survey nahi kiya. UNICEF ke 2024 ke global estimates bhi yahi dikhate hain: bachpan ki zyada tar sexual violence teenage mein hoti hai, aur 14 se 17 saal ke beech yeh kaafi badh jaati hai [[unicef-sexual-violence-children-2024]].

Isliye yeh padhai un saalon se pehle pahunchni chahiye. Chhote bachchon ke liye sexuality education ka matlab sex ke baare mein padhana nahi hai. Iska matlab hai apni body ko jaanna, apni feelings ko naam dena, aur yeh jaanna ki violence ya abuse ho toh kya karein. 2024 mein Supreme Court ne suggest kiya ki health aur sex education ke liye ek expert committee bane, jo bachchon mein "early age se hi" POCSO ki awareness bhi failaye [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]].

Mote taur par seedhi kuch aisi hai. School ke shuruaati saalon mein: body parts ke sahi naam, kaunsa touch theek hai aur kaunsa nahi, aur "body se judi koi baat chhupani nahi hai". Puberty se pehle: periods aur nightfall, ladkiyon aur ladkon dono ke liye. Teenage mein: consent, rishte, contraception, online safety aur law. Beton ko iski utni hi zaroorat hai jitni betiyon ko. POCSO Act 18 saal se kam umar ke har bachche ko protect karta hai, ladkon ko bhi [[pocso-act-2012]].

## Yeh toh family ka kaam hai, school ka kyon?

Yeh dono ka kaam hai. Bachche tab sabse safe hote hain jab unhe ek se zyada bharosemand bado se ek jaisi saaf baat sunne ko mile: parents aur family se, aur teachers se bhi. Family ghar par jaldi shuru kar sakti hai; school yeh pakka karta hai ki koi bachcha chhoot na jaaye.

Akele families yeh kaam nahi kar pa rahi. 2016 mein India ki 88 studies ko milakar ek bada analysis hua, aur usmein sirf 48% teenage ladkiyon ko pehla period aane se pehle uske baare mein bataya gaya tha [[bmjopen-van-eijk-mhm-india-2016]]. Yeh sabse basic baatcheet hai, phir bhi lagbhag aadhi ladkiyon tak yeh time par nahi pahunchi.

Ek aur kadvi wajah hai. 2007 ki study mein 50% abusers aise log the jinhe bachcha jaanta tha, ya jo bharose aur zimmedari ki position mein the [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Jab nuksaan pahunchane wala family ke daayre ke andar ho, toh bachche ko us daayre ke bahar ek safe adult ki zaroorat hoti hai, jaise koi teacher jisne body safety par khulkar baat ki ho. "Stranger danger" wali seekh galat kyon hai, is par hamari data story mein aaj ke police figures hain.

## Kya yeh dharm aur culture ke khilaf hai?

Achhi sexuality education kisi family se uska dharm chhodne ko nahi kehti. Isme yeh baatein aati hain: family aur rishte; respect, consent aur apni body par apna haq; anatomy, puberty aur periods; contraception aur pregnancy; aur HIV samet infections. Respect, sach bolna aur bachchon ko safe rakhna, yeh toh zyada tar families ki apni values hain, chahe unka dharm koi bhi ho. Ghar par parents apni family ki maanyataen bhi jod sakte hain.

"Indian culture ke khilaf" wala argument dekar 2007 mein schools ke programmes ban kiye gaye the; un bans par hamari investigation is argument ko evidence par test karti hai. Tab se India ki apni institutions ulti disha mein chali hain. Health Ministry ka adolescent health programme 7 January 2014 ko launch hua, aur isme sexual aur reproductive health ke saath violence (gender-based violence samet) aur mental health bhi shaamil hai [[nhm-adolescent-health-rksk-page-2026]]. Supreme Court aisi comprehensive sex education ki salah de chuka hai jo consent samjhaye [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]], aur January 2026 mein usne order diya ki schools mein ladkon aur male teachers ko bhi periods ke baare mein sensitise kiya jaaye [[livelaw-sc-jaya-thakur-judgment-2026]]. Yeh bahar se aayi cheez nahi hai. India ki apni courts aur ministries iski maang kar rahi hain.

## Jab koi nahi batata, toh bachche kya seekhte hain?

Seekhte toh woh phir bhi hain: doston se, forwards se aur porn se, jo consent, protection ya care sikhane ke liye banta hi nahi. Woh yeh bhi seekhte hain ki kuch baatein kahi nahi jaatin. 2007 ki study mein jin young adults ke saath bachpan mein sexual assault hua tha, unmein se sirf 26.8% ne kabhi kisi ko bataya [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Aur periods ki wajah se aaj bhi ladkiyon ke school ke din chhootte hain: India mein lagbhag ek-chauthai (24%) teenage ladkiyan periods ke dauraan school nahi gayi [[bmjopen-van-eijk-mhm-india-2016]].

Jo galat baatein school mein koi nahi sudhaarta, woh umar bhar saath reh sakti hain. 2019-21 mein 15-49 saal ke 35.1% Indian mardon ne maana ki contraception auraton ka kaam hai, aur 19.6% ne maana ki contraception use karne wali auratein promiscuous ho sakti hain [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Jis bachche ko kuch nahi bataya jaata, use uski masoomiyat nahi bachaati; woh bas apne sawaalon ke saath akela reh jaata hai. Parents ko har jawab pata hona zaroori nahi. Zaroori yeh hai ki baat woh pehle shuru karein.

sexuality-education-world-vs-india-unesc.en:
Where does a 15-year-old in India learn how bodies, consent and contraception work? The honest answer is that it depends on the state, the school and the teacher. UNESCO's 2021 global status report on sexuality education found that 85% of 155 countries with data report a policy or law on the subject [[unesco-cse-global-status-report-2021]]. On India, it is brief: responsibility is left to the states, and in the whole country UNESCO could name only one state-run programme that had reached scale: Jharkhand's Udaan [[unesco-cse-global-status-report-2021]].

## Policies in 85% of countries

A policy is the easy part. The 85% is what governments reported about themselves, and the key word is "related": UNESCO counts policies, and sometimes laws, *related to* sexuality education, and notes that few countries have a national policy written specifically for it [[unesco-cse-global-status-report-2021]].

A rule in a ministry file does not put a trained teacher in front of a class of 14-year-olds, give that teacher an hour a week, or protect them when a parent complains.

## Policy is not content: what curricula skip

When UNESCO looked at what curricula actually contain, the picture shrank. In 24 sub-Saharan African countries whose curricula were reviewed, only a little more than a quarter had advanced or established content on sexuality and sexual behaviour. In a survey of countries in Asia-Pacific, sub-Saharan Africa and Latin America, the topics least included in secondary-school curricula were access to safe abortion, sexual orientation and gender identity, and online media and technology [[unesco-cse-global-status-report-2021]]. India is not among the 24 countries whose curricula were reviewed.

These are the areas where not knowing hurts young people most. A young woman who has never been told that abortion is legal in India, within the limits of the MTP Act, may wait too long or go to an unsafe provider. A teenager whose class never discussed phones and the internet may not recognise sextortion until the threat arrives. A queer student hears nothing that describes their life; a separate story in this section looks at what that silence teaches.

## India: left to the states

India did try a national push. The Adolescence Education Programme for schools was launched in 2005 by the Ministry of Human Resource Development and the National AIDS Control Organisation [[srhm-pattathil-roy-sexuality-education-india-2023]]. In the 2007 backlash it was banned or refused by somewhere between six and 12 states, depending on the count; a 2020 study puts the number of states that banned all such programmes at 12 [[reprodhealth-plesons-jharkhand-cse-2020]]. Our separate investigation tells how those bans happened. Today the national education policy is silent: NEP 2020 does not once use the words "sex", "sexual" or "sexuality" in its 66 pages [[nep-2020-full-text]].

A subject left to the states produces a map of unequal knowledge. In 2019-21 only 10% of young women aged 15-24 in Bihar had comprehensive knowledge of HIV, against 69% in Mizoram. Among young men it ranged from 14% in West Bengal and Meghalaya to 73% in Goa [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Classrooms are not the only cause of those gaps; poverty, caste and health services all play a part. But the share rises with schooling, from 8.7% among young women with no schooling to 28.0% among those with 12 or more years of school [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Twelve or more years in a classroom, and still only 28.0%: school is where this knowledge could reach almost everyone, and mostly it does not.

The Centre has not left the field completely. Under the School Health and Wellness Programme, whose curriculum was released in February 2020, two teachers in every government and government-aided school are to be trained as Health and Wellness Ambassadors and run one-hour weekly sessions on 11 health themes for 24 weeks a year [[pib-school-health-ambassador-curriculum-2020]]. Private schools are not covered; our explainer on the programme sets out what it promises. In September 2024 the Supreme Court recommended comprehensive sex education that explains consent and the harm of exploitation, and suggested that the Union set up an expert committee on health and sex education [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]]. Those were suggestions, not orders.

## Udaan: the one programme at scale

Udaan is a school-based adolescent education programme that Jharkhand started in its schools in 2006. By September 2019 it had reached over one million students, and UNESCO calls it the only at-scale, state-run initiative of its kind in India [[unesco-cse-global-status-report-2021]].

Three things stand out. First, timing: Udaan began a year before the 2007 backlash and was still running at scale in 2019, through the years when other states banned similar programmes. Second, it is state-run and school-based: it works through an ordinary state education system, not a short pilot. Third, it travelled: UNESCO notes that Udaan served as a blueprint for the national School Health and Wellness Ambassador Initiative [[unesco-cse-global-status-report-2021]].

The title of a 2020 study of Jharkhand's experience sums up the method: build an enabling environment, and respond to resistance [[reprodhealth-plesons-jharkhand-cse-2020]]. The other response, a ban, is the one that other states chose. One caution: the number UNESCO reports is how many students Udaan reached, not what changed for them.

## What 'comprehensive' would add

A biology chapter on reproduction is not comprehensive sexuality education. As WHO describes it, the full version also covers families and relationships; respect, consent and bodily autonomy; anatomy, puberty and menstruation; contraception and pregnancy; and sexually transmitted infections, including HIV. It teaches gender equality, and WHO says children aged 5 to 8 should learn to recognise bullying and violence and understand that these are wrong [[who-cse-qa]].

The evidence for teaching all of it is strong. UNESCO's 2018 guidance found that sexuality education does not increase sexual activity, sexual risk-taking or STI and HIV infection rates [[unesco-itgse-2018]]. Curriculum-based programmes contribute to later first sex, less frequent sex, fewer partners, less risk-taking and more condom and contraceptive use. Abstinence-only programmes do not delay first sex [[unesco-itgse-2018]]. Most of the trials behind those findings were run outside India, so Indian programmes need to be measured too.

A count of policies makes the world look further along than it is. India does not need to top a global ranking. It needs every state to do what one state has already shown can be done inside its own schools.
sexuality-education-world-vs-india-unesc.hg:
India mein ek 15 saal ka teenager kahan se seekhta hai ki body kaise kaam karti hai, consent kya hota hai, aur pregnancy kaise roki jaati hai? Sach bolein toh yeh is par depend karta hai ki woh kis state mein hai, kis school mein hai aur use kaunsa teacher mila. UNESCO ki 2021 ki sexuality education par global status report ke mutabik, jin 155 deshon ka data mila, unmein se 85% ne kaha ki unke paas is par koi policy ya law hai [[unesco-cse-global-status-report-2021]]. India ke baare mein report ki baat chhoti si hai. Yahan zimmedari states par chhod di gayi hai, aur poore desh mein UNESCO ko sirf ek sarkari programme mila jo bade scale tak pahuncha: Jharkhand ka Udaan [[unesco-cse-global-status-report-2021]].

## 85% deshon mein policy hai

Policy banana sabse aasaan kaam hai. 85% wala figure sarkaron ne khud apne baare mein bataya hai, aur ek word pe dhyaan do: "related". Report un policies ko ginti hai, aur kahin-kahin laws ko, jo sexuality education se *related* hain. Report yeh bhi kehti hai ki bahut kam deshon mein sirf iske liye bani alag national policy hai [[unesco-cse-global-status-report-2021]].

Ministry ki file mein likha rule 14 saal ke bachchon ki class mein ek trained teacher khada nahi karta. Na use hafte mein ek ghanta deta hai, na tab uska saath deta hai jab koi parent complain lekar aa jaaye.

## Policy ek baat hai, padhai doosri: syllabus kya chhod dete hain

Jab UNESCO ne dekha ki syllabus mein asal mein kya hai, toh picture aur chhoti ho gayi. 24 sub-Saharan African deshon ke curriculum review hue, aur unmein se sirf ek-chauthai se thode zyada mein sexuality aur sexual behaviour par advanced ya established content tha. Asia-Pacific, sub-Saharan Africa aur Latin America ke deshon ke ek survey mein secondary school curriculum mein sabse kam shaamil topics the: safe abortion tak pahunch, sexual orientation aur gender identity, aur online media aur technology [[unesco-cse-global-status-report-2021]]. India un 24 deshon mein nahi tha jinke curriculum review hue.

Yahi woh topics hain jinke baare mein na jaanna young logon ko sabse zyada nuksaan pahunchata hai. Socho, ek ladki jise kabhi kisi ne nahi bataya ki India mein MTP Act ki limits ke andar abortion legal hai. Woh der kar sakti hai, ya kisi unsafe jagah ja sakti hai. Jis class mein kabhi phone aur internet ki baat nahi hui, wahan ka teenager sextortion ko tab tak nahi pehchaanta jab tak dhamki aa na jaaye. Aur ek queer student ko apni life se judi ek bhi baat sunne ko nahi milti. Yeh chuppi unhe kya sikhaati hai, is par isi section mein ek alag story hai.

## India: faisla states ke haath mein

India ne ek baar national level par koshish ki thi. Schools ke liye Adolescence Education Programme 2005 mein Ministry of Human Resource Development aur National AIDS Control Organisation (NACO) ne launch kiya tha [[srhm-pattathil-roy-sexuality-education-india-2023]]. 2007 ke backlash mein ginti ke hisaab se chhe se 12 states ne ise ban kiya ya lagoo karne se mana kiya; 2020 ki ek study ke mutabik 12 states ne aise saare programmes ban kar diye [[reprodhealth-plesons-jharkhand-cse-2020]]. Yeh bans kaise lage, is par hamari ek alag investigation hai. Aur aaj desh ki education policy is par bilkul chup hai: NEP 2020 ke 66 pages mein "sex", "sexual" ya "sexuality" word ek baar bhi nahi aata [[nep-2020-full-text]].

Jab subject states par chhoda jaata hai, toh knowledge ka map bhi ooncha-neecha ho jaata hai. 2019-21 mein Bihar ki 15-24 saal ki sirf 10% young women ko HIV ki comprehensive knowledge thi, jabki Mizoram mein 69% ko. Young men mein yeh West Bengal aur Meghalaya mein 14% se lekar Goa mein 73% tak tha [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. In gaps ki wajah sirf classroom nahi hai; gareebi, caste aur health services, sabka role hai. Lekin yeh knowledge schooling ke saath badhti hai: jo young women kabhi school nahi gayi, unmein sirf 8.7% ko yeh poori jaankari thi, aur jinhone 12 ya usse zyada saal padhai ki, unmein 28.0% ko [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Socho: 12 ya usse zyada saal class mein baithne ke baad bhi sirf 28.0%. School woh jagah hai jahan se yeh knowledge lagbhag har bachche tak pahunch sakti hai, aur zyada tar pahunchti nahi.

Centre poori tarah peeche bhi nahi hata. School Health and Wellness Programme ka curriculum February 2020 mein jaari hua. Iske under har government aur government-aided school mein do teachers ko Health and Wellness Ambassadors ki training milni hai. Inhe saal mein 24 hafte, har hafte ek ghante ke sessions mein 11 health themes padhane hain [[pib-school-health-ambassador-curriculum-2020]]. Private schools isme cover nahi hain; yeh programme kya promise karta hai, is par hamara alag explainer hai. September 2024 mein Supreme Court ne recommend kiya ki comprehensive sex education ho jo consent aur exploitation ke nuksaan ko samjhaye. Court ne yeh bhi suggest kiya ki Union health aur sex education par ek expert committee banaye [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]]. Yeh suggestions the, orders nahi.

## Udaan: bade scale tak pahuncha akela programme

Udaan ek school-based adolescent education programme hai jo Jharkhand ne 2006 mein apne schools mein shuru kiya. September 2019 tak yeh 10 lakh se zyada students tak pahunch chuka tha. UNESCO ise India mein apni tarah ka akela at-scale, state-run initiative kehta hai [[unesco-cse-global-status-report-2021]].

Teen baatein khaas hain. Pehli, timing: Udaan 2007 ke backlash se ek saal pehle shuru hua aur 2019 mein bhi bade scale par chal raha tha, un saalon mein bhi jab doosre states aise programmes ban kar rahe the. Doosri, ise sarkar chalati hai aur yeh school ke andar chalta hai, yaani state ke normal education system ke through. Yeh koi chhota pilot nahi hai. Teesri, yeh aage tak gaya: UNESCO ke mutabik Udaan national School Health and Wellness Ambassador Initiative ka blueprint bana [[unesco-cse-global-status-report-2021]].

2020 mein Jharkhand ke experience par ek study chhapi, aur uska title hi poora tareeka bata deta hai: enabling environment banao, aur resistance ka jawab do [[reprodhealth-plesons-jharkhand-cse-2020]]. Doosra jawab tha ban, aur doosre states ne wahi chuna. Ek caution bhi zaroori hai. UNESCO ka number batata hai ki Udaan kitne students tak pahuncha, yeh nahi ki unke liye kya badla.

## "Comprehensive" mein aur kya judta hai

Biology ki kitaab ka reproduction wala chapter comprehensive sexuality education nahi hai. WHO ke hisaab se poori sex education mein yeh sab aata hai: family aur rishte; respect, consent aur apni body par apna haq; anatomy, puberty aur periods; contraception aur pregnancy; aur HIV samet sexually transmitted infections. Isme gender equality bhi sikhayi jaati hai, aur WHO ke mutabik 5 se 8 saal ke bachchon ko bullying aur violence pehchaanna aur yeh samajhna sikhaya jaana chahiye ki yeh galat hai [[who-cse-qa]].

Ise padhane ke paksh mein evidence strong hai. UNESCO ki 2018 guidance ke mutabik sexuality education se na sexual activity badhti hai, na risk lena, na STI aur HIV ke infection rates [[unesco-itgse-2018]]. Curriculum-based programmes se pehli baar sex der se hota hai, sex kam baar hota hai, partners kam hote hain aur risk kam liya jaata hai. Condom aur contraception ka use badhta hai. Jo programmes sirf abstinence sikhate hain, woh pehli baar sex ko taal nahi paate [[unesco-itgse-2018]]. In findings ke peeche ke zyada tar trials India ke bahar hue, isliye Indian programmes ko bhi measure karna zaroori hai.

Sirf policies gino, toh duniya asal se zyada aage dikhti hai. India ko kisi global ranking mein top nahi karna. Zaroorat bas itni hai ki har state woh kare jo ek state apne hi schools mein karke dikha chuka hai.

son-preference-after-birth-missing-girls.en:
India's argument about son preference is mostly an argument about ultrasound machines: who runs them, who misuses them, how many girls are never born. That is the larger part of the loss, not all of it. By one analysis that UNFPA cites, sex selection before birth explains about two thirds of India's "missing" girls. Deaths after birth explain about one third [[unfpa-swop-2020]]. Roughly one in three of the missing girls was born, and then lost.

The preference does not stop at infancy either. It shows up again when a marriage is fixed, when dowry is discussed, and in police records of how some of those marriages end.

## 'At least one son': the wish in numbers

In 2014 the International Center for Research on Women and UNFPA surveyed men and women in seven Indian states. 76% of men and 81% of women said it was very important to have at least one son [[icrw-unfpa-masculinity-ipv-son-preference-2014]].

More women than men said so. That does not make women the cause. In many homes the woman answering is the one who gets blamed when no son arrives, so her answer may describe the pressure she lives under as much as her own wish.

The survey covered seven states and is twelve years old, and our verified data hold no newer national measure. What it shows is a ranking inside the family, and the rest of this story is about what it costs the child placed second.

## Two thirds before birth, one third after

UNFPA estimated that about 460,000 girls a year went "missing" at birth in India between 2013 and 2017 [[unfpa-swop-2020]].

The one third lost after birth is a different kind of number. It counts girls dying in greater numbers than they would have if they had been boys, and UNFPA puts both losses in the same count of missing girls [[unfpa-swop-2020]].

Imagine two children in one house with the same fever in the same week. The son is taken to a private doctor that evening. With the daughter, the family waits a few days to see if it passes. No one in that house would say they chose against her. Excess deaths are built from gaps of that size, repeated in many homes over many years.

These are modelled estimates, and they shift with the method chosen, but the split matters. India's law against sex selection is aimed at clinics and scans [[goi-pcpndt-act-1994]]. No inspector can check which child was taken to the doctor first.

## The dowry arithmetic

The ranking has an economic logic that families seldom say aloud. A son is expected to stay, earn and bring a bride into the house. A daughter is expected to leave, and to take money with her.

That money has been illegal since 1961. Under the Dowry Prohibition Act, giving or taking dowry carries at least five years in prison [[indiacode-dowry-prohibition-1961]]. But only 17.4% of the cases decided under the Act in 2024 ended in conviction, and 83,298 cases were still pending at year end [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A law that rarely convicts does not change the price.

UNFPA notes that where the bride's family pays dowry, younger brides typically command smaller dowries, which gives poor parents a reason to marry daughters early [[unfpa-child-marriage-2025]]. This is a general observation, not a measurement of India, and not a verdict on poor parents. It describes what an illegal market does to people who cannot afford its prices.

India's child marriage law counts a bride under 18, or a groom under 21, as a child [[indiacode-pcma-2006]]. In 2023-24, 20.1% of women aged 20-24 had been married before 18, down from 23.3% in 2019-21. In villages the 2023-24 rate was still 23.3%, against 11.4% in cities [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. These provisional figures still mean one young woman in five.

## From child bride to dowry death

UNICEF says girls who marry before 18 are more likely to face domestic violence and less likely to stay in school [[unicef-child-marriage-topic-page]]. The daughter married early to keep the cost down arrives in her husband's home younger, with less schooling, and with less power to refuse anything than she would have had a few years later.

Dowry demands do not always end with the wedding. In 2024 police registered 5,737 dowry-death cases with 5,811 victims, about 16 a day [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A dowry death is a legal category: a woman's death in abnormal circumstances within seven years of marriage, after dowry-linked cruelty [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Deaths recorded as suicide or accident are often not registered under it, so the count is a floor.

None of our verified data tracks how many of those women were married as children. What joins the newborn girl, the bride married before 18 and the woman in the police register is an idea, not a statistic: a daughter is a cost to be kept small, and a son an asset to be secured.

## Raising daughters as equals

Start with the body. A daughter's fever, her plate and her vaccinations deserve the same speed and the same money as a son's.

Then the money. Refuse to give or take dowry, and say so before a match is fixed. Give a daughter the same education, and the same claim on the family's property, that a son is assumed to have. A daughter who can earn and inherit is harder to describe as a cost.

Then the wedding. No marriage before 18 for a woman or 21 for a man. If one is being planned for a child you know, call the Child Helpline 1098 or 112.

Sons learn the ranking at home as well. In the same 2014 study, men raised in families where fathers did household chores were two times more likely to hold gender-equitable attitudes [[icrw-unfpa-masculinity-ipv-son-preference-2014]].

If you are the one being blamed for having daughters, or pressed for dowry, the fault lies with the people making the demand. The Women Helpline and 112 exist for this, and Tele-MANAS on 14416 offers free counselling at any hour.
son-preference-after-birth-missing-girls.hg:
India mein son preference ki bahas zyada tar ultrasound machines ki bahas hai: inhe kaun chalata hai, kaun misuse karta hai, kitni ladkiyan paida hi nahi ho paati. Nuksan ka bada hissa wahi hai, par poora nahi. UNFPA jis analysis ka hawala deta hai, uske mutabik India ki "missing" ladkiyon mein se lagbhag do tihaai ki wajah janm se pehle ka sex selection hai. Lagbhag ek tihaai ki wajah janm ke baad hui mautein hain [[unfpa-swop-2020]]. Yaani missing ladkiyon mein se lagbhag har teesri paida hui thi, aur phir kho gayi.

Yeh soch bachpan par bhi nahi rukti. Yeh phir tab dikhti hai jab rishta pakka hota hai, jab dowry ki baat hoti hai, aur police ke un records mein bhi jo batate hain ki aisi kuch shaadiyan kaise khatam hui.

## 'Kam se kam ek beta': chahat, numbers mein

2014 mein International Center for Research on Women aur UNFPA ne saat Indian states mein men aur women ka survey kiya. 76% men aur 81% women ne kaha ki kam se kam ek beta hona bahut zaroori hai [[icrw-unfpa-masculinity-ipv-son-preference-2014]].

Yeh baat men se zyada women ne kahi. Iska matlab yeh nahi ki wajah women hain. Bahut se gharon mein jawab dene wali aurat wahi hoti hai jis par beta na hone ka ilzaam aata hai. Isliye uska jawab uski apni chahat jitna hi us pressure ko bhi dikha sakta hai jisme woh jeeti hai.

Survey sirf saat states ka tha aur ab barah saal purana hai, aur hamare verified data mein isse naya koi national measure nahi hai. Yeh number jo dikhata hai, woh hai parivaar ke andar ki ek ranking. Is story ka baaki hissa isi baare mein hai ki doosre number par rakhe gaye bachche ko yeh ranking kitni mehngi padti hai.

## Do tihaai janm se pehle, ek tihaai baad mein

UNFPA ka estimate hai ki 2013 se 2017 ke beech India mein har saal lagbhag 460,000 ladkiyan janm par "missing" rahi [[unfpa-swop-2020]].

Janm ke baad khoyi ek tihaai alag tarah ka number hai. Yeh un ladkiyon ki ginti hai jo utni zyada tadaad mein mar gayi jitni woh ladka hone par nahi marti. UNFPA dono nuksan missing ladkiyon ki ek hi ginti mein rakhta hai [[unfpa-swop-2020]].

Socho, ek hi ghar mein do bachchon ko ek hi hafte mein ek jaisa bukhar hai. Bete ko usi shaam private doctor ke paas le jaya jaata hai. Beti ke case mein parivaar kuch din rukta hai, ki shayad apne aap utar jaye. Us ghar mein koi nahi kahega ki humne beti ke khilaf koi faisla kiya. Par janm ke baad ki yeh zyada mautein aise hi chhote-chhote farq se banti hain, jo bahut se gharon mein, bahut saalon tak dohraye jaate hain.

Yeh modelled estimates hain, aur method badalne par yeh badal jaate hain, phir bhi yeh batwara matter karta hai. India ka sex selection ke khilaf kanoon clinics aur scans par nishana lagata hai [[goi-pcpndt-act-1994]]. Koi inspector yeh check nahi kar sakta ki doctor ke paas pehle kaun sa bachcha gaya.

## Dowry ka hisaab

Is ranking ke peeche ek paison wala logic hai jo parivaar kam hi zor se bolte hain. Bete se ummeed hoti hai ki woh ghar mein rahega, kamayega aur bahu layega. Beti se ummeed hoti hai ki woh jayegi, aur apne saath paisa le jayegi.

Yeh paisa 1961 se illegal hai. Dowry Prohibition Act ke tahat dowry dene ya lene par kam se kam paanch saal ki jail hai [[indiacode-dowry-prohibition-1961]]. Lekin 2024 mein is Act ke jin cases ka faisla hua, unme se sirf 17.4% mein conviction hui, aur saal ke end par 83,298 cases pending the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Jo kanoon mushkil se kisi ko saza deta hai, woh daam nahi badalta.

UNFPA kehta hai ki jahan dulhan ka parivaar dowry deta hai, wahan kam umar ki dulhan ke liye aam taur par kam dowry lagta hai, aur isse gareeb maa-baap ko beti ki shaadi jaldi karne ki wajah mil jaati hai [[unfpa-child-marriage-2025]]. Yeh ek general observation hai, India ka koi measurement nahi, aur gareeb maa-baap par koi faisla bhi nahi. Yeh bas yeh batata hai ki ek illegal market un logon ke saath kya karta hai jo uske daam nahi chuka sakte.

India ka child marriage kanoon 18 se kam umar ki dulhan ko, ya 21 se kam umar ke dulhe ko, child maanta hai [[indiacode-pcma-2006]]. 2023-24 mein 20-24 saal ki 20.1% women ki shaadi 18 se pehle ho chuki thi; 2019-21 mein yeh 23.3% tha. Gaon mein 2023-24 ka rate ab bhi 23.3% tha, aur shehron mein 11.4% [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. Yeh provisional figures hain, phir bhi inka matlab hai har paanch mein se ek young woman.

## Child bride se dowry death tak

UNICEF kehta hai ki jin ladkiyon ki shaadi 18 se pehle hoti hai, unke saath domestic violence hone ke chances zyada hote hain aur school mein bane rehne ke chances kam [[unicef-child-marriage-topic-page]]. Jis beti ki shaadi kharcha kam rakhne ke liye jaldi kar di gayi, woh pati ke ghar kam umar mein pahunchti hai, kam padhai ke saath, aur kisi bhi baat ko mana karne ki utni taakat ke bina jitni kuch saal baad uske paas hoti.

Dowry ki maang hamesha shaadi ke saath khatam nahi hoti. 2024 mein police ne 5,737 dowry-death cases register kiye, jinme 5,811 victims the, yaani roz lagbhag 16 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Dowry death ek legal category hai: shaadi ke saat saal ke andar, dowry se judi cruelty ke baad, abnormal haalaat mein hui aurat ki maut [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Jo mautein suicide ya accident ke naam par darj hoti hain, woh aksar isme register nahi hoti, isliye yeh ginti kam se kam ki hai, poori nahi.

Hamare verified data mein kahin yeh nahi hai ki in women mein se kitnon ki shaadi bachpan mein hui thi. Navjaat bachchi, 18 se pehle byahi gayi dulhan aur police register mein darj aurat ko jo cheez jodti hai, woh koi statistic nahi, ek soch hai: beti ek kharcha hai jise chhota rakhna hai, aur beta ek asset hai jise pakka karna hai.

## Betiyon ko barabar ki tarah paalna

Shuruaat body se karo. Beti ka bukhar, uski thaali aur uske vaccination utni hi jaldi aur utne hi paise ke haqdaar hain jitne bete ke.

Phir paisa. Dowry na do, na lo, aur yeh baat rishta pakka hone se pehle hi keh do. Beti ko wahi padhai do, aur parivaar ki property par wahi haq, jo bete ka maan liya jaata hai. Jo beti kama sakti hai aur virasat pa sakti hai, use kharcha kehna mushkil ho jaata hai.

Phir shaadi. Ladki ki shaadi 18 se pehle nahi, ladke ki 21 se pehle nahi. Agar tumhari jaan-pehchaan ke kisi bachche ki shaadi plan ho rahi hai, toh Child Helpline 1098 ya 112 par call karo.

Bete bhi yeh ranking ghar par hi seekhte hain. Usi 2014 ki study mein, jin parivaaron mein papa ghar ka kaam karte the, wahan pale-badhe men ke gender-equitable soch rakhne ke chances do guna the [[icrw-unfpa-masculinity-ipv-son-preference-2014]].

Agar betiyan hone ka blame tum par daala ja raha hai, ya dowry ke liye dabaav hai, toh galti unki hai jo maang kar rahe hain. Women Helpline aur 112 isi ke liye hain, aur Tele-MANAS 14416 par kisi bhi waqt free counselling milti hai.

sports-federations-harassment-committees.en:
A national sports federation decides who is called to camp, who gets on the plane and whose career is over at 19. Since December 2013 the law has also required it to have a committee where a woman can complain of sexual harassment. On 4 May 2023 The Indian Express published what it found when it checked 30 federations: 16 did not comply with the POSH Act, and five of them, including wrestling, had no committee at all [[ie-nsf-icc-investigation-2023]].

## In law, a stadium is a workplace

Sport is not an afterthought in the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013. Its definition of "workplace" names "any sports institute, stadium, sports complex or competition or games venue", along with places visited in the course of work and transport the employer provides [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. The training hall, the tournament venue and the team bus are all inside it.

Nor does the Act ask whether the woman is on a payroll. It protects a woman "of any age whether employed or not" who alleges harassment at a workplace [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. An athlete is rarely anyone's employee. On its plain words, the Act does not shut her out.

Every employer must set up an Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) headed by a senior woman, with at least two employee members and one external member; at least half the members must be women. An employer who does not can be fined up to Rs 50,000 [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].

## 16 of 30 federations

The newspaper reviewed the federations of disciplines in which India competed at the 2018 Asian Games, the Tokyo Olympics and the 2022 Commonwealth Games. The 16 failures were of four kinds [[ie-nsf-icc-investigation-2023]]:
