| What was wrong | Federations |
|---|---|
| No Internal Complaints Committee at all | 5 |
| Fewer members than the law requires | 4 |
| No external member | 6 |
| Two panels, neither with an independent member | 1 |

The external member is not a formality. The Supreme Court's 1997 Vishaka guidelines required a third party, such as an NGO, on every complaints committee to prevent pressure from senior levels [[sc-vishaka-1997]]. In a federation, the senior levels are the people who pick the team. A committee made up only of insiders asks an athlete to complain about the hierarchy to the hierarchy.

Eight days after the newspaper's report, on 12 May 2023, the Supreme Court cited the survey in a judgment that found "serious lapses in the enforcement" of the Act and called it "a sorry state of affairs" [[sc-aureliano-fernandes-2023]].

This is a snapshot from May 2023, and some federations said they were setting up committees. We could not verify a later public audit of all 30.

## Wrestling: the committee that did not exist

In 2023 some of India's top women wrestlers alleged sexual harassment. A government-appointed oversight committee examined the allegations, and flagged as a "major finding" that the Wrestling Federation of India had no Internal Complaints Committee as the law required [[ie-nsf-icc-investigation-2023]].

The official the wrestlers accused has denied the allegations. We do not name people who have not been convicted, or women who report harassment.

Athletes at the top of a national sport had no statutory committee in their own federation to take a complaint to, and it took a government panel to put that on record. If that was the position at the top of the sport, consider the 15-year-old at a district trial.

## Selection, travel, coaches: why athletes stay quiet

Sport gives the people who run it unusual power over the people who play it.

- **Selection.** A coach or official decides who trains, who competes and who is dropped. An athlete who complains about that person is complaining about the one who controls her career.
- **Travel.** Camps and tournaments take athletes, many of them teenagers, away from home for weeks. The adults in charge control food, rooms, transport and the phone call home.
- **Coaches.** A coach works closely on an athlete's body: weight, injuries, technique. That closeness makes a crossed line easy to deny.

Imagine a 17-year-old from a small town at her first national camp. Her family has borrowed money for her kit and diet. The coach who makes sexual remarks is the person who will decide whether she goes to the trials. To speak is to risk the one thing she has worked for since she was ten.

The Supreme Court has described this silence in ordinary jobs: women are reluctant to report, and "many of them even drop out from their job", partly because they do not know whom to approach [[sc-aureliano-fernandes-2023]]. In a federation with no committee, there is no one to approach. And an athlete who drops out cannot simply apply elsewhere.

If the athlete is under 18, the POSH Act is not the only law. POCSO defines a child as anyone under 18 and protects boys and girls alike, which matters because the POSH Act, written for women, gives a boy no committee at all. Anyone who knows of a sexual offence against a child must report it to the police, and the head of an institution who fails to report abuse by a subordinate faces up to one year in prison [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. No coach, physio or academy owner can settle it internally, and no sexual relationship between an adult and an athlete under 18 is legal, whatever the adult calls it.

## Questions to ask before a camp

This is general information, not legal advice. Before joining an academy or a camp, an athlete and her parents can ask, in writing:

1. Who is on your Internal Committee? Ask for names, including the woman who heads it and the external member.
2. How does an athlete complain without going through her own coach?
3. Who travels and stays with the team, and who has access to athletes' rooms?
4. Who is the child-protection contact for athletes under 18?
5. How is selection decided, and where is that written down?

A body that cannot answer the first question probably has no committee. A complaint can still be made on the government's SHe-Box portal [[shebox]] or to the police: sexual harassment is a crime under Section 75 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, punishable with up to three years [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

India counts its medals in public. In May 2023 it took a newspaper to count the committees.
sports-federations-harassment-committees.hg:
National sports federation tay karta hai ki camp mein kise bulaya jaayega, flight mein kaun baithega, aur kiska career 19 ki umr mein khatam ho jaayega. December 2013 se law yeh bhi maangta hai ki uske paas ek committee ho jahan aurat sexual harassment ki complaint kar sake. 4 May 2023 ko The Indian Express ne chhaapa ki 30 federations ko check karne par use kya mila: 16 POSH Act ka paalan nahi kar rahe the, aur unmein se paanch ke paas, wrestling samet, koi committee thi hi nahi [[ie-nsf-icc-investigation-2023]].

## Law ki nazar mein stadium bhi workplace hai

Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013 mein sport koi baad mein joda gaya khayal nahi hai. Iski "workplace" ki definition mein "any sports institute, stadium, sports complex or competition or games venue" ka naam hai, aur saath mein woh jagahein jahan kaam ke silsile mein jaana pade aur employer ka diya hua transport bhi [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Training hall, tournament venue aur team bus, sab iske andar aate hain.

Act yeh bhi nahi poochhta ki aurat kisi ke payroll par hai ya nahi. Yeh us aurat ko protect karta hai jo "of any age whether employed or not" ho, yaani kisi bhi umr ki, employed ho ya nahi, aur workplace par harassment ka ilzaam lagaye [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Athlete aksar kisi ki employee nahi hoti. Law ke shabdon mein use bahar rakhne wali koi baat nahi hai.

Har employer ko ek Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) banani hai, jiski head ek senior woman ho, jismein kam se kam do employee members aur ek external member ho, aur jiske kam se kam aadhe members auratein hon. Jo employer aisa nahi karta, us par Rs 50,000 tak ka fine lag sakta hai [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].

## 30 mein se 16 federations

Akhbaar ne un disciplines ke federations ko review kiya jinmein India ne 2018 Asian Games, Tokyo Olympics aur 2022 Commonwealth Games mein hissa liya tha. 16 federations ki kamiyan chaar tarah ki thin [[ie-nsf-icc-investigation-2023]]:

| Kya galat tha | Federations |
|---|---|
| Internal Complaints Committee thi hi nahi | 5 |
| Law ki zaroorat se kam members | 4 |
| External member nahi | 6 |
| Do panels, dono mein koi independent member nahi | 1 |

External member koi formality nahi hai. Supreme Court ki 1997 ki Vishaka guidelines ne har complaints committee mein ek third party, jaise koi NGO, zaroori ki thi, taaki senior levels ka dabaav roka ja sake [[sc-vishaka-1997]]. Federation mein senior levels wahi log hain jo team chunte hain. Sirf andar ke logon se bani committee athlete se yeh kehti hai ki hierarchy ki complaint hierarchy se hi karo.

Akhbaar ki report ke aath din baad, 12 May 2023 ko, Supreme Court ne is survey ka zikr us judgment mein kiya jismein usne Act ke "serious lapses in the enforcement" paaye, yaani laagu karne mein gambhir kamiyan, aur ise "a sorry state of affairs" kaha [[sc-aureliano-fernandes-2023]].

Yeh May 2023 ka snapshot hai, aur kuch federations ne kaha tha ki woh committees bana rahe hain. Saare 30 ka baad ka koi public audit hum verify nahi kar paaye.

## Wrestling: woh committee jo thi hi nahi

2023 mein India ki kuch top women wrestlers ne sexual harassment ke ilzaam lagaye. Sarkar ki banayi ek oversight committee ne in ilzaamon ki jaanch ki, aur ise "major finding" ke taur par flag kiya ki Wrestling Federation of India ke paas law ke mutabik zaroori Internal Complaints Committee thi hi nahi [[ie-nsf-icc-investigation-2023]].

Jis official par wrestlers ne ilzaam lagaya, usne in ilzaamon se inkaar kiya hai. Hum un logon ka naam nahi chhaapte jinhe court ne convict nahi kiya, aur un auraton ka bhi nahi jo harassment report karti hain.

Ek national sport ke sabse upar ke athletes ke paas apne hi federation mein complaint le jaane ke liye koi statutory committee nahi thi, aur yeh baat record par laane ke liye ek sarkari panel ki zaroorat padi. Agar sport ke sabse upar yeh haal tha, toh district trial mein khadi 15 saal ki ladki ke baare mein sochiye.

## Selection, travel, coaches: athletes chup kyun rehti hain

Sport use chalane walon ko khelne walon par ek alag hi kism ki taaqat deta hai.

- **Selection.** Coach ya official tay karta hai ki kaun train karega, kaun compete karega aur kise drop kiya jaayega. Jo athlete us insaan ki complaint karti hai, woh usi ki complaint kar rahi hai jiske haath mein uska career hai.
- **Travel.** Camps aur tournaments athletes ko, jinmein se kai teenagers hote hain, hafton ke liye ghar se door le jaate hain. Khana, kamre, transport aur ghar par phone, sab in-charge adults ke control mein hota hai.
- **Coaches.** Coach athlete ke shareer par kareeb se kaam karta hai: weight, injuries, technique. Isi nazdeeki ki wajah se line cross hone par use jhuthlaana aasaan ho jaata hai.

Sochiye, ek chhote sheher ki 17 saal ki ek ladki apne pehle national camp mein hai. Uske parivaar ne uski kit aur diet ke liye karz liya hai. Jo coach sexual remarks karta hai, wahi tay karega ki woh trials mein jaayegi ya nahi. Bolne ka matlab hai us ek cheez ko daav par lagana jiske liye woh das saal ki umr se mehnat kar rahi hai.

Supreme Court ne aam naukriyon mein is chuppi ko bayaan kiya hai: auratein report karne se hichkichati hain, aur "many of them even drop out from their job", yaani kai naukri hi chhod deti hain, kyunki unhe pata nahi hota kiske paas jaana hai [[sc-aureliano-fernandes-2023]]. Jis federation mein committee hi nahi hai, wahan jaane ke liye koi hai hi nahi. Aur jo athlete sport chhod deti hai, woh kisi doosri jagah apply karke dobara shuru nahi kar sakti.

Agar athlete ki umr 18 se kam hai, toh POSH Act akela law nahi hai. POCSO 18 se kam umr ke har insaan ko child maanta hai aur ladkon aur ladkiyon dono ko protect karta hai; yeh isliye zaroori hai ki POSH Act auraton ke liye likha gaya hai aur ladke ko koi committee deta hi nahi. Jise bhi child ke khilaaf sexual offence ka pata ho, use police ko report karna hi hoga, aur jo institution head apne subordinate ke abuse ko report nahi karta, use ek saal tak ki jail ho sakti hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Koi coach, physio ya academy owner ise andar hi settle nahi kar sakta, aur kisi adult aur 18 se kam umr ke athlete ke beech koi bhi sexual relationship legal nahi hai, adult use chahe jo naam de.

## Camp se pehle poochhne wale sawaal

Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi. Academy ya camp join karne se pehle athlete aur uske parents likhit mein yeh pooch sakte hain:

1. Aapki Internal Committee mein kaun-kaun hai? Naam maangiye, head karne wali woman aur external member ke bhi.
2. Athlete apne hi coach ke through gaye bina complaint kaise kar sakti hai?
3. Team ke saath kaun travel karta aur rukta hai, aur athletes ke kamron tak kiski pahunch hai?
4. 18 se kam umr ke athletes ke liye child-protection contact kaun hai?
5. Selection kaise tay hota hai, aur yeh kahan likha hua hai?

Jo body pehle sawaal ka jawab nahi de sakti, uske paas shaayad committee hai hi nahi. Tab bhi complaint sarkar ke SHe-Box portal par [[shebox]] ya police mein ki ja sakti hai: sexual harassment Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita ke Section 75 ke tahat crime hai, jismein teen saal tak ki saza ho sakti hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

India apne medals sabke saamne ginta hai. May 2023 mein committees ginne ke liye ek akhbaar ki zaroorat padi.

street-harassment-first-count-odisha.en:
Until its 2024 edition, India's annual crime report had no line for the harassment many women meet in daily life: the comment at the bus stop, the hand in a crowded market. Crime in India 2024 has one. In its first six months the new row filled with 1,469 cases, and 549 of them came from one state, Odisha, more than Uttar Pradesh (184) and Tamil Nadu (136) put together [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Before concluding that Odisha has India's worst streets, look at what the same tables say about its offices and its courts.

## A new category, 1,469 cases

The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita replaced the IPC on 1 July 2024. NCRB's table of sexual harassment cases, which already listed offices, public transport and shelter homes, gained two places for cases registered under the new code: "public places/pathway", and work premises such as shops, factories and homes. So the first street count covers July to December, not a full year [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

The offence itself is old. Section 75 of the BNS punishes sexual harassment with up to three years in prison, and sexually coloured remarks with up to one year [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. What is new is that the police record now says where it happened.

Or says so sometimes. Of the 15,609 sexual harassment cases registered in 2024, 12,592, or 81%, sit under "other places". Public places account for 1,469, work premises 512, public transport 459, office premises 388 and shelter homes 189 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Even in the BNS months, more than three times as many cases went under "other places" as under the street row. Most of the place column is still a blank.

## Why Odisha? Counting versus crime

Odisha is a big-number state across these tables. Its rate of registered crime against women in 2024 was 118.3 per lakh women, third in India behind Delhi (130.7) and Telangana (128.6). It registered 7,299 cases of assault to outrage modesty, second only to Rajasthan's 8,276, at the highest rate in the country: 31.5 per lakh women against a national 7.1 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Two readings fit. Either women in Odisha face more harassment, or Odisha's police write down and label complaints that other forces turn away, settle informally or file under something else. The tables cannot choose between them, and NCRB says so itself. Its note of caution states that "rise in crime" and "increase in registration of crime by police" are "clearly two different things", and that numbers may rise because of an e-FIR facility or women's help desks [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]]. Comparing states on these figures alone, it adds, "will be too simplistic and is best avoided".

Imagine two college students, one in Cuttack and one in Kanpur, each harassed with sexual remarks by men near a bus stand. One finds an officer who writes the complaint and marks it "public place". The other is told to ignore it and change her route. Only the first is among the 1,469. Uttar Pradesh, India's most populous state, recorded 184. That is hard to read as safer streets.

## Zero at the office

The same Odisha police recorded no sexual harassment at office premises in all of 2024. Neither did Rajasthan or West Bengal. Kerala recorded 89, Himachal Pradesh 58 and Maharashtra 57, out of 388 nationwide [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A zero cannot mean that Odisha's offices are free of harassment. It means no FIR carried that label.

So a state can top one table and vanish from the one beside it. Where a case lands depends on what the officer writes and which box gets ticked, and one state's habits can shape the national picture: more than a third of the first street count came from Odisha alone.

Registration is also only the first step. Odisha's courts convicted in 6.3% of the crime-against-women trials they completed in 2024, against 25.7% across India [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. That rate covers every crime against women, not street harassment alone, and it shifts with which trials happen to finish in a year. It still warns against treating a tall stack of FIRs as proof that the system works for the women who file them.

## What the street count still misses

- **Half the year.** Cases from January to June, registered under the IPC, carry no street label.
- **Other sections.** Remarks and gestures can also be booked under Section 79, which punishes words or gestures meant to insult a woman's modesty. Police registered 9,338 such cases in 2024, under a separate head [[ncrb-cii-2024]].
- **Bigger charges.** NCRB counts each FIR once, under its most serious offence. Harassment that came with an assault is counted as the assault.
- **Men and transgender people.** The head counts harassment of women, under a section that by its wording only a man can commit [[indiacode-bns-2023]].
- **Everyone who never filed.** In 2005, 12% of households told the India Human Development Survey that unmarried girls in their neighbourhood were "sometimes" or "often" harassed. Police records implied 0.06% of households, a gap of about 200 times [[aej-iyer-political-voice-2012]]. The comparison is old, but it is a check no police count can run on itself.

## Reading the next new number

New categories will keep appearing in crime tables. Ask four things of each one. How many months does it cover? How much sits under "other"? Does one state supply most of it? And what does the row beside it say?

Then remember how a case enters the row at all: someone files. Under Section 173 of the BNSS, a complaint can be given at any police station, whatever the area, or sent electronically and signed within three days. The FIR copy is free, and a woman's complaint of sexual harassment must be recorded by a woman officer [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. This is general information, not legal advice.

Odisha's 549 is not proof of India's worst streets. It may be the nearest thing in the table to an honest number. The harder questions belong to the states that reported almost nothing.
street-harassment-first-count-odisha.hg:
2024 ke edition se pehle India ki saalana crime report mein us harassment ke liye koi line hi nahi thi jo bahut si aurton ko roz ki zindagi mein jhelna padta hai: bus stop par kasa gaya comment, bheed bhari market mein badhta hua haath. Crime in India 2024 mein yeh line hai. Pehle chhe mahinon mein is nayi row mein 1,469 case aaye, aur inmein se 549 ek hi state Odisha ke the, yaani Uttar Pradesh (184) aur Tamil Nadu (136) ko mila kar bhi usse zyada [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yeh maan lene se pehle ki India ki sabse buri sadkein Odisha mein hain, dekhiye ki wahi tables uske offices aur uski courts ke baare mein kya kehti hain.

## Ek nayi category, 1,469 case

1 July 2024 ko Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita ne IPC ki jagah le li. NCRB ki sexual harassment wali table mein offices, public transport aur shelter homes pehle se the. Naye code ke tahat darj cases ke liye usmein do nayi jagahein judi: "public places/pathway", aur work premises jaise dukaan, factory aur ghar. Isliye sadak ki yeh pehli ginti July se December tak ki hai, poore saal ki nahi [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Offence khud purana hai. BNS ka Section 75 sexual harassment par teen saal tak ki jail deta hai, aur sexually coloured remarks par ek saal tak ki [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Naya bas yeh hai ki police record ab yeh bhi batata hai ki ghatna kahan hui.

Ya kabhi-kabhi batata hai. 2024 mein darj sexual harassment ke 15,609 cases mein se 12,592, yaani 81%, "other places" ke neeche pade hain. Public places ke hisse 1,469 aaye, work premises ke 512, public transport ke 459, office premises ke 388 aur shelter homes ke 189 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. BNS wale mahinon mein bhi "other places" mein sadak wali row se teen guna se zyada case gaye. Jagah wala column abhi bhi zyada tar khaali hi hai.

## Odisha hi kyun? Ginti aur crime ka farq

In tables mein Odisha har jagah bade numbers wala state hai. 2024 mein aurton ke khilaaf darj crime ka uska rate har lakh aurton par 118.3 tha, India mein teesra, Delhi (130.7) aur Telangana (128.6) ke baad. Usne assault to outrage modesty ke 7,299 case darj kiye, jo sirf Rajasthan ke 8,276 se kam the, aur rate desh mein sabse upar tha: har lakh aurton par 31.5, jabki national rate 7.1 hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Iske do matlab ho sakte hain. Ya toh Odisha mein aurton ko zyada harassment jhelna padta hai, ya Odisha ki police woh complaints likhti aur label karti hai jinhe doosri jagah ki police lauta deti hai, bina likhe "settle" kara deti hai ya kisi aur heading mein daal deti hai. Tables in dono mein se ek ko chun nahi sakti, aur yeh baat NCRB khud kehta hai. Uska note of caution kehta hai ki "rise in crime" aur "increase in registration of crime by police" "clearly two different things" hain, aur numbers e-FIR facility ya women's help desk jaise kadamon ki wajah se bhi badh sakte hain [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]]. Sirf in figures par states ki tulna karna, woh aage kehta hai, "will be too simplistic and is best avoided", yaani bahut simplistic hoga aur isse bachna hi behtar hai.

Sochiye, do college students hain, ek Cuttack mein aur ek Kanpur mein, aur dono par bus stand ke paas kuch aadmi sexual remarks kaste hain. Ek ko aisa officer milta hai jo complaint likhta hai aur us par "public place" mark karta hai. Doosri se kaha jaata hai ki ignore karo aur raasta badal lo. Un 1,469 mein sirf pehli hai. Uttar Pradesh, India ka sabse zyada aabaadi wala state, ne 184 case darj kiye. Ise zyada safe sadkein maan lena mushkil hai.

## Office mein zero

Usi Odisha police ne poore 2024 mein office premises par sexual harassment ka ek bhi case darj nahi kiya. Rajasthan aur West Bengal ne bhi nahi. Kerala ne 89 darj kiye, Himachal Pradesh ne 58 aur Maharashtra ne 57, poore desh ke 388 mein se [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Zero ka yeh matlab nahi ho sakta ki Odisha ke offices mein harassment hota hi nahi. Iska matlab bas yeh hai ki kisi FIR par woh label nahi laga.

Yaani ek state ek table mein sabse upar ho sakta hai aur bagal wali table se gaayab. Case kis row mein pahunchta hai, yeh is par tika hai ki officer kya likhta hai aur kaun sa box tick hota hai, aur ek state ki aadatein poore desh ki tasveer badal sakti hain: sadak ki pehli ginti ka ek-tihaai se zyada hissa akele Odisha se aaya.

Aur registration toh sirf pehla kadam hai. 2024 mein Odisha ki courts ne aurton ke khilaaf crime ke jitne trial poore kiye, unmein se 6.3% mein conviction hui, jabki poore India mein yeh 25.7% tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yeh rate aurton ke khilaaf har crime ka hai, sirf street harassment ka nahi, aur is par bhi tika hai ki saal mein kaun se trial khatam hue. Phir bhi yeh ek chetaavni hai: FIRs ka ooncha dher is baat ka saboot nahi ki system un aurton ke liye kaam karta hai jo complaint likhwati hain.

## Sadak ki ginti mein abhi bhi kya chhoot jaata hai

- **Aadha saal.** January se June tak ke case IPC ke tahat darj hue, aur un par sadak wala label hai hi nahi.
- **Doosre sections.** Remarks aur ishaare Section 79 ke tahat bhi darj ho sakte hain, jo aurat ki modesty ka apmaan karne wale shabdon ya gestures par saza deta hai. 2024 mein police ne aise 9,338 case darj kiye, ek alag head ke neeche [[ncrb-cii-2024]].
- **Bade charge.** NCRB har FIR ko ek hi baar ginta hai, uske sabse serious offence ke neeche. Jis harassment ke saath assault bhi hua, woh assault mein gina jaata hai.
- **Mard aur transgender log.** Yeh head aurton ke harassment ko ginta hai, aur woh bhi ek aise section ke tahat jo apne shabdon ke hisaab se sirf koi mard hi kar sakta hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].
- **Woh sab jinhone kabhi complaint ki hi nahi.** 2005 mein 12% households ne India Human Development Survey ko bataya ki unke mohalle mein unmarried ladkiyon ko "sometimes" ya "often" harass kiya jaata hai. Police records ke hisaab se yeh sirf 0.06% households banta tha, yaani qareeb 200 guna ka farq [[aej-iyer-political-voice-2012]]. Yeh tulna purani hai, lekin yeh aisi jaanch hai jo police ki koi ginti khud apne upar nahi kar sakti.

## Agla naya number kaise padhein

Crime tables mein nayi categories aati rahengi. Har ek se chaar sawaal poochhiye. Yeh kitne mahine cover karti hai? "Other" mein kitna pada hai? Kya iska zyada tar hissa ek hi state se aa raha hai? Aur iske bagal wali row kya kehti hai?

Phir yaad rakhiye ki koi case us row mein pahunchta kaise hai: koi complaint likhwata hai. BNSS ke Section 173 ke tahat complaint kisi bhi police station mein di ja sakti hai, ghatna chaahe kisi bhi area ki ho, ya electronically bheji ja sakti hai jis par teen din ke andar sign karna hota hai. FIR ki copy free milti hai, aur aurat ki sexual harassment ki complaint mahila officer ko hi record karni hoti hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

Odisha ke 549 is baat ka saboot nahi hain ki India ki sabse buri sadkein wahin hain. Ho sakta hai poori table mein yahi number sachchai ke sabse qareeb ho. Zyada mushkil sawaal un states se poochhe jaane chahiye jinhone lagbhag kuch bhi report nahi kiya.

why-didnt-she-speak-up-earlier.en:
"Itne saal chup kyun rahi?" It is what women who speak late keep hearing, and it is said as a challenge: if it were true, you would have spoken. The question has an answer. A Delhi trial court, the Supreme Court, a government study and a judicial committee in Kerala have all written it down.

## Why did she wait so long?

Because most people do. In 2021 a Delhi court, acquitting a journalist of criminal defamation over a #MeToo allegation, wrote: "Most of the women who suffer abuse do not speak up about it or against it for simple reason 'The Shame' or the social stigma attached with the sexual harassment and abuse." [[delhi-court-metoo-defamation-judgment-2021]]

The Supreme Court's 2023 Handbook on Combating Gender Stereotypes calls the belief that a woman who delays reporting is lying a stereotype, and explains that "lack of familial support or fear of repercussions may cause a survivor / victim to delay their reporting" [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

In the government's 2007 Study on Child Abuse, 72.1% of the children who said they had been sexually assaulted had told no one, and only 3.4% had gone to the police [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. The study covered 13 states, was not nationally representative and predates the POCSO Act. Among adult women, NFHS-5 found that 77.2% of those who had faced physical or sexual violence had never sought help or told anyone [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

A child who tells no one at nine is an adult "speaking late" at twenty-nine. The delay is not a hole in her account. It is the most common part of it.

## Why did she stay in touch with him?

Because he was already in her life. In 96.8% of rape cases registered in India in 2024, the offender was known to the victim [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. He is the relative at every family function, or the manager who signs her appraisal. Cutting him off means explaining why, to the very people she is not ready to tell.

The handbook lists as a stereotype the belief that a genuine survivor never speaks to the accused again. "There is no 'correct' or 'appropriate' way in which a survivor or victim behaves," it says [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

Imagine a 24-year-old analyst in Gurugram whose harasser is her reporting manager. For two years she answers his messages with "Sure sir, will send it today", because her salary and reference letter pass through him. Later those messages are produced as proof that nothing happened. They prove that she needed the job.

Many of the people the Hema Committee approached in the Malayalam film industry were at first afraid to speak because they feared losing work. As its study went on, the committee wrote, "we realised it was well-founded", and it was concerned for their safety and that of their close relatives [[bbc-hema-report-2024]].

## Why didn't she go to the police?

Often because she did not know where to go, or did not believe a formal complaint would help. In 2023 the Supreme Court, in a judgment on the workplace harassment law, observed that women harassed at work are often reluctant to report it. "Many of them even drop out from their job," it wrote, and it gave two reasons: "uncertainty about who to approach" and "lack of confidence in the process and its outcome" [[sc-aureliano-fernandes-2023]].

Among women in NFHS-5 who did seek help after violence, 60.9% turned to their own family and 6.3% went to the police [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Parliament has accepted that the police station can be a closed door. In 2013 it made it a crime for a police officer to refuse to record an FIR for rape [[indiacode-cla-2013]]. The rule continues as Section 199 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, with six months to two years in prison [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Nobody writes that law for a problem that does not exist.

For men and for transgender and queer survivors the door is narrower still: the code's rape section covers only a man assaulting a woman [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

## Why speak now?

Often the answer is that whatever enforced the silence has changed. She has left the job. He no longer controls her salary or her home. Someone else spoke first. None of this makes her account less true.

The Delhi court dealt with timing directly: "The woman has a right to put her grievance at any platform of her choice and even after decades" [[delhi-court-metoo-defamation-judgment-2021]]. That is a trial court's ruling, and it has been appealed to the Delhi High Court [[livelaw-akbar-appeal-2026]].

The law's own clock pushes late speech into public. Under the POSH Act a written complaint must be made within three months of the incident, or of the last in a series, extendable by at most three more [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. A woman who needs two years to find the words has lost the workplace forum before she can use it. What is left is the police, or saying it aloud.

Institutions wait too. The Hema Committee gave its report to the Kerala government in December 2019. It was made public only on 19 August 2024, nearly five years later [[nie-hema-report-release-2024]]. On 10 September 2024 the Kerala High Court asked why the state had been "inactive or silent" on it since 31 December 2019 [[livelaw-kerala-hc-hema-sit-2024]]. That is the question pointed the right way: at the institution with the power to act.

## What to say instead of 'why didn't you'

"Why didn't you" asks her to defend herself. Try sentences that ask nothing of her:

- "I believe you."
- "It was not your fault."
- "What do you need right now?"

A police complaint can be given at any police station, whatever the area, and she must get a free copy of the FIR [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Time limits depend on the offence, so ask a lawyer before assuming it is too late.

If the person telling you is under 18, do not promise secrecy: the POCSO Act requires anyone who knows of child sexual abuse to report it [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Say you will stay with them, and call Child Helpline 1098. This is general information, not legal advice.

The answer to "why didn't she speak up earlier" is already on record. The more useful question is who made it unsafe to speak.
why-didnt-she-speak-up-earlier.hg:
"Itne saal chup kyun rahi?" Der se bolne wali auraton ko yahi baar-baar suna jaata hai, aur ek challenge ki tarah kaha jaata hai: sach hota toh tum pehle bolti. Is sawaal ka jawab hai. Delhi ki ek trial court, Supreme Court, bachchon par sarkar ki ek study aur Kerala ki ek judicial committee, sabne ise likh kar rakha hai.

## Usne itni der kyun ki?

Kyunki zyadatar log der hi karte hain. 2021 mein Delhi ki ek court ne ek journalist ko #MeToo allegation par chale criminal defamation ke case mein bari karte hue likha: "Most of the women who suffer abuse do not speak up about it or against it for simple reason 'The Shame' or the social stigma attached with the sexual harassment and abuse." Yaani abuse jhelne wali zyadatar auratein ek seedhi si wajah se nahi bolti: 'sharm', ya woh kalank jo samaaj sexual harassment aur abuse ke saath jod deta hai [[delhi-court-metoo-defamation-judgment-2021]].

Supreme Court ki 2023 ki Handbook on Combating Gender Stereotypes is soch ko stereotype kehti hai ki der se report karne wali aurat jhooth bol rahi hai, aur samjhati hai ki "lack of familial support or fear of repercussions may cause a survivor / victim to delay their reporting", yaani parivaar ka saath na milna ya nateejon ka darr survivor se der karwa sakta hai [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

Sarkar ki 2007 ki Study on Child Abuse mein jin bachchon ne study mein bataya ki unka sexual assault hua tha, unme se 72.1% ne kisi ko nahi bataya tha, aur sirf 3.4% police ke paas gaye the [[mwcd-study-child-abuse-2007]]. Ye study 13 states mein hui thi, poore desh ki representative nahi thi, aur POCSO Act se pehle ki hai. Adult auraton mein, NFHS-5 ne paaya ki physical ya sexual violence jhelne waliyon mein se 77.2% ne kabhi madad nahi maangi aur kisi ko bataya nahi [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Jo bachcha nau saal ki umar mein kisi ko nahi batata, wahi untees ki umar mein "der se bolne wala" adult ban jaata hai. Ye der uski baat mein koi chhed nahi hai. Ye uski kahani ka sabse aam hissa hai.

## Woh us aadmi se baat kyun karti rahi?

Kyunki woh pehle se uski zindagi mein tha. 2024 mein India mein darj rape cases mein se 96.8% mein offender victim ka jaan-pehchaan wala tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Woh har family function mein aane wala rishtedaar hai, ya woh manager jo uske appraisal par sign karta hai. Usse rishta todne ka matlab hai wajah batana, aur wajah unhi logon ko batani padegi jinhe batane ke liye woh abhi taiyaar nahi hai.

Handbook is soch ko stereotype maanti hai ki 'asli' survivor accused se phir kabhi baat nahi karti. Woh kehti hai, "There is no 'correct' or 'appropriate' way in which a survivor or victim behaves", yaani survivor ya victim ke bartaav ka koi 'sahi' ya 'uchit' tareeka nahi hota [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

Sochiye Gurugram ki ek 24 saal ki analyst ke baare mein, jise harass karne wala uska apna reporting manager hai. Do saal tak woh uske messages ka jawab "Sure sir, will send it today" likh kar deti hai, kyunki uski salary aur uska reference letter usi ke haath se guzarte hain. Baad mein yahi messages is baat ke saboot ki tarah pesh kiye jaate hain ki kuch hua hi nahi. Ye messages bas itna saabit karte hain ki use naukri ki zaroorat thi.

Hema Committee ne Malayalam film industry ke jin logon se baat karni chaahi, unme se kai shuru mein bolne se darte the, kyunki unhe kaam chhin jaane ka darr tha. Committee ne likha ki jaise-jaise study aage badhi, "we realised it was well-founded", yaani hum samajh gaye ki ye darr bebuniyaad nahi tha, aur use un logon aur unke kareebi rishtedaaron ki safety ki fikar thi [[bbc-hema-report-2024]].

## Woh police ke paas kyun nahi gayi?

Aksar isliye ki use pata nahi tha kahan jaana hai, ya use yakeen nahi tha ki formal complaint se kuch hoga. 2023 mein Supreme Court ne workplace harassment ke law par diye ek judgment mein kaha ki kaam ki jagah par harass hone wali auratein aksar report karne se jhijhakti hain. "Many of them even drop out from their job," court ne likha, yaani kai toh naukri hi chhod deti hain, aur do wajah batayi: "uncertainty about who to approach", yaani ye pata na hona ki kiske paas jaayein, aur "lack of confidence in the process and its outcome", yaani process aur uske nateeje par bharosa na hona [[sc-aureliano-fernandes-2023]].

NFHS-5 mein jin auraton ne violence ke baad madad maangi bhi, unme se 60.9% apne hi parivaar ke paas gayi aur 6.3% police ke paas [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Parliament khud maan chuki hai ki police station ka darwaza band mil sakta hai. 2013 mein usne ise crime bana diya ki koi police officer rape ki FIR likhne se mana kare [[indiacode-cla-2013]]. Ye rule ab Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita ka Section 199 hai, jisme chheh mahine se do saal tak ki jail hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Aisa law us problem ke liye koi nahi likhta jo hoti hi na ho.

Mardon ke liye, aur transgender aur queer survivors ke liye, ye darwaza aur bhi tang hai: code ka rape wala section sirf us case ko cover karta hai jisme ek aadmi ek aurat par assault kare [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

## Ab kyun bol rahi hai?

Aksar jawab ye hota hai ki jo cheez use chup rakhe hue thi, woh badal gayi. Usne woh naukri chhod di. Ab uski salary ya uska ghar us aadmi ke haath mein nahi hai. Kisi aur ne pehle bol diya. In mein se koi bhi baat uski kahani ko kam sach nahi banati.

Delhi ki court ne timing par seedha kaha: "The woman has a right to put her grievance at any platform of her choice and even after decades", yaani aurat ko haq hai ki woh apni shikaayat apni marzi ke kisi bhi platform par rakhe, dashkon baad bhi [[delhi-court-metoo-defamation-judgment-2021]]. Ye ek trial court ka faisla hai, aur iske khilaaf Delhi High Court mein appeal ki gayi hai [[livelaw-akbar-appeal-2026]].

Law ki apni ghadi der se bolne wali aurat ko public mein bolne ki taraf dhakel deti hai. POSH Act ke under written complaint incident ke teen mahine ke andar deni hoti hai, ya kai incidents hon toh aakhri incident ke teen mahine ke andar, aur ye waqt zyada se zyada teen mahine aur badh sakta hai [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Jis aurat ko apni baat kehne ke shabd dhoondhne mein do saal lagte hain, woh workplace ka forum use karne se pehle hi kho chuki hoti hai. Bachta hai police ke paas jaana, ya khul kar bol dena.

Institutions bhi der karte hain. Hema Committee ne apni report December 2019 mein Kerala sarkar ko di. Report 19 August 2024 ko jaakar public hui, lagbhag paanch saal baad [[nie-hema-report-release-2024]]. 10 September 2024 ko Kerala High Court ne poocha ki state 31 December 2019 se is report par "inactive or silent", yaani nishkriya ya chup, kyun rahi [[livelaw-kerala-hc-hema-sit-2024]]. Sawaal ki sahi disha yahi hai: us institution ki taraf jiske paas kuch karne ki taakat thi.

## 'Tumne kyun nahi' ki jagah kya kahein

"Tumne kyun nahi bataya" usse apni safai maangta hai. Aise sentences boliye jo usse kuch nahi maangte:

- "Mujhe tum par yakeen hai."
- "Ye tumhari galti nahi thi."
- "Tumhe abhi kya chahiye?"

Police complaint kisi bhi police station mein di ja sakti hai, ilaaka koi bhi ho, aur FIR ki free copy use milni hi chahiye [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Time limit offence par depend karti hai, isliye ye maan lene se pehle ki ab bahut der ho gayi, kisi lawyer se poochiye.

Agar batane wala 18 saal se chhota hai, toh raaz rakhne ka vaada mat kijiye: POCSO Act ke under jise bhi bachche ke sexual abuse ka pata ho, use report karna zaroori hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Kahiye ki aap uske saath rahenge, aur Child Helpline 1098 par call kijiye. Ye general information hai, legal advice nahi.

"Usne pehle kyun nahi bola" ka jawab pehle se record par hai. Zyada kaam ka sawaal ye hai ki bolna unsafe kisne banaya.

women-officers-as-far-as-practicable.en:
Imagine a 19-year-old in a district town who walks into a police station after midnight to report that she was raped. The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), the 2023 law on criminal procedure, promises her a woman at almost every step: at the desk, during her statement, before the magistrate and in court. It cannot promise that a woman will be there. Three of those four promises carry the same four words: "as far as practicable".

## The law's four requests for a woman

The first request is firm. When a woman reports rape, sexual harassment, stalking, voyeurism or an acid attack, her information must be recorded by a woman police officer or any woman officer (Section 173) [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. There is no "if possible" in that sentence.

The other three are softer. A rape survivor's statement must be taken at her home or a place she chooses, "as far as practicable" by a woman officer, and may be recorded on video, even on a phone (Section 176) [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. A magistrate, as far as practicable a woman, must record her statement as soon as police learn of the offence (Section 183(6)). The trial must be held in camera, as far as practicable before a woman judge (Section 366(2)) [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Children get a similar promise: under Section 24 of the POCSO Act, the child's statement is taken at home or a place the child chooses, by an officer out of uniform, and as far as practicable by a woman officer not below sub-inspector rank [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

These rules have a history. In 1978 the Supreme Court acquitted two policemen accused of raping a minor girl inside a police station in Maharashtra (AIR 1979 SC 185) [[sc-tukaram-maharashtra-1978]]. Protests over that judgment led to the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 1983, which moved rape trials behind closed doors [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. The police station was where the law first saw the danger.

## 'As far as practicable': the escape clause

"As far as practicable" means: if it can be done. It turns a right into a request. If no woman officer is free, a man can take the statement. Only one clause names a fallback: without a woman magistrate, a male magistrate records the statement in the presence of a woman [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

What does a survivor lose when the clause is used? Often, her words. Describing a sexual assault to a man in uniform, with other men walking in and out, can make it far harder to speak at all. A frightened statement can later be read in court as an "inconsistency".

One protection does not depend on staffing. Under Section 179(1), police cannot require a woman to come anywhere other than where she lives, though she may go to the station if she chooses [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. The officers can come to her.

The courtroom faces harder arithmetic. At the end of 2024, 1,85,785 rape cases were pending trial, 89.8% of the 2,06,777 before Indian courts that year [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Each is meant to be heard in camera, as far as practicable by a woman judge. Whether that happens depends on the court a case lands in.

## Help desks: 14,658 and counting

At the police end, the government has tried to build women into the system. In December 2019 the Ministry of Home Affairs sanctioned Rs 100 crore from the Nirbhaya Fund for Women Help Desks in police stations, a first point of contact for any woman who walks in, staffed mainly by women officers [[pib-mha-women-help-desks-2019]]. By March 2025, 14,658 help desks had been set up, 13,743 of them headed by women officers [[pib-nirbhaya-fund-2025]].

That is real progress, but it counts desks, not shifts. A desk headed by a woman officer does not mean a woman is on duty at 2 am, when the young woman in our example walks in. Nor does it count magistrates or judges.

## What changed where women ran the station

Does a woman at the desk change anything? Research on all-women police stations in Indian cities found that opening them was associated with a 29% rise in police reports of crimes against women, mainly domestic violence, while killings of women did not change [[iza-amaral-women-police-stations-2021]]. The authors read this as more reporting, not more violence.

That matters because most women never reach a police station. Among women who faced physical or sexual violence and sought help, only 6% went to the police; 61% turned to their own family (NFHS-5, 2019-21) [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. The gap between 61% and 6% is where a woman officer can matter most. For a wife reporting her husband, or a niece reporting an uncle, the first face at the station decides whether she speaks at all.

NCRB itself warns that steps such as women help desks can push registered crime up [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A rise after a desk opens may simply be the desk working, as our myth-buster on rising rape numbers explains.

These rules are written for women. Men and transgender survivors fall outside them, and they too deserve an officer who listens without mockery.

## What to ask for when no woman is on duty

This is general information, not legal advice.

- **Ask for a woman to write it down.** For a woman reporting a sexual offence, Section 173 has no "if possible". Ask for the women help desk.
- **Do not accept being turned away.** An officer who fails to record an FIR for rape or sexual assault faces six months to two years of rigorous imprisonment under Section 199 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) [[indiacode-bns-2023]].
- **Choose the place.** Ask for your statement to be recorded at home or somewhere you feel safe.
- **Before the magistrate**, ask for a woman magistrate, or else for a woman to be present.
- **At trial**, ask your lawyer or the public prosecutor to request a woman judge.

One Stop Centres offer support under one roof to women facing violence; in July 2026, 985 of the 1,033 approved centres were operational [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-07]]. In an emergency, call 112 or the Women Helpline.
women-officers-as-far-as-practicable.hg:
Sochiye, ek district town ki 19 saal ki ladki aadhi raat ke baad police station pahunchti hai, yeh report karne ki uska rape hua hai. Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), yaani criminal procedure ka 2023 ka law, usse lagbhag har step par ek woman ka vaada karta hai: desk par, statement ke waqt, magistrate ke saamne aur court mein. Lekin law yeh vaada nahi kar sakta ki woh woman wahan hogi bhi. In chaar mein se teen vaadon ke saath wahi chaar shabd jude hain: "as far as practicable".

## Law ki chaar maangein: har step par ek woman

Pehli maang pakki hai. Jab koi woman rape, sexual harassment, stalking, voyeurism ya acid attack report karti hai, toh uski information ek woman police officer ya kisi bhi woman officer ko hi record karni hai (Section 173) [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Is line mein "agar ho sake" jaisa kuch nahi likha.

Baaki teen maangein naram hain. Rape survivor ka statement uske ghar par ya uski pasand ki jagah par liya jaana hai, "as far as practicable" ek woman officer ke zariye, aur ise video par record kiya ja sakta hai, phone par bhi (Section 176) [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Jaise hi police ko offence ka pata chale, ek magistrate ko uska statement record karna hai, aur jahan tak ho sake woh magistrate woman ho (Section 183(6)). Trial in camera, yaani band kamre mein hona hai, aur jahan tak ho sake woman judge ke saamne (Section 366(2)) [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Bachchon ke liye bhi aisa hi vaada hai: POCSO Act ki Section 24 ke tahat bachche ka statement uske ghar par ya uski pasand ki jagah par liya jaata hai, aisa officer leta hai jo uniform mein na ho, aur "as far as practicable" woh ek woman officer ho jo sub-inspector se neeche ki rank ki na ho [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

In rules ke peeche ek itihaas hai. 1978 mein Supreme Court ne un do policewalon ko bari kar diya jin par Maharashtra ke ek police station ke andar ek minor ladki ke rape ka aarop tha (AIR 1979 SC 185) [[sc-tukaram-maharashtra-1978]]. Us judgment ke khilaaf hue protests ke baad Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 1983 aaya, jisne rape trials ko band darwazon ke peeche kar diya [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. Law ne khatra sabse pehle police station mein hi dekha tha.

## 'As far as practicable': bach nikalne ka raasta

"As far as practicable" ka matlab hai: agar ho sake toh. Yeh shabd ek haq ko request bana dete hain. Agar koi woman officer free nahi hai, toh statement ek aadmi le sakta hai. Sirf ek clause mein doosra raasta likha hai: woman magistrate na ho, toh male magistrate ek woman ki maujoodgi mein statement record karega [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Jab yeh clause istemaal hota hai, toh survivor kya khoti hai? Aksar, apne shabd. Uniform pehne ek aadmi ko sexual assault ke baare mein batana, jab doosre aadmi kamre mein aa-ja rahe hon, bolna hi bahut mushkil bana sakta hai. Darr mein diya gaya statement baad mein court mein "inconsistency" ki tarah padha ja sakta hai.

Ek protection staff par depend nahi karti. Section 179(1) ke tahat police kisi woman ko uske rehne ki jagah ke alawa kahin aur aane ke liye majboor nahi kar sakti, haan woh khud chahe toh station ja sakti hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Officers uske paas aa sakte hain.

Courtroom ka hisaab aur mushkil hai. 2024 ke end mein rape ke 1,85,785 cases trial ke intezaar mein the, yaani us saal Indian courts ke saamne aaye 2,06,777 cases ka 89.8% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Har ek ki sunwai in camera honi hai, aur jahan tak ho sake woman judge ke saamne. Aisa hoga ya nahi, yeh is par depend karta hai ki case kis court mein pahunchta hai.

## Help desks: 14,658, aur ginti jaari hai

Police ke level par sarkar ne system ke andar women ko jagah dene ki koshish ki hai. December 2019 mein Ministry of Home Affairs ne Nirbhaya Fund se Rs 100 crore police stations mein Women Help Desks ke liye sanction kiye. Yeh desk station mein aane wali kisi bhi woman ke liye pehla contact point hai, aur ise zyada tar women officers chalati hain [[pib-mha-women-help-desks-2019]]. March 2025 tak 14,658 help desks ban chuke the, jinmein se 13,743 ki head women officers thi [[pib-nirbhaya-fund-2025]].

Yeh asli progress hai, lekin yeh desks ki ginti hai, shifts ki nahi. Kisi desk ki head woman officer hai, iska matlab yeh nahi ki raat ke 2 baje bhi koi woman duty par hogi, jab hamare example wali ladki andar aati hai. Aur is ginti mein magistrates ya judges shaamil nahi hain.

## Jahan station women ne chalaya, wahan kya badla

Desk par ek woman ke hone se kuch badalta hai kya? Indian cities ke all-women police stations par hui research ne paaya ki inke khulne ke baad women ke khilaaf crimes ki police reports 29% badhi, zyada tar domestic violence ki, jabki women ki hatya ke cases mein koi badlaav nahi aaya [[iza-amaral-women-police-stations-2021]]. Researchers ne iska matlab yeh nikala ki reporting badhi, violence nahi.

Yeh isliye zaroori hai kyunki zyada tar women kabhi police station tak pahunchti hi nahi. Jin women ne physical ya sexual violence jhela aur help maangi, unmein se sirf 6% police ke paas gayi; 61% apni family ke paas gayi (NFHS-5, 2019-21) [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. 61% aur 6% ke beech ka yahi gap woh jagah hai jahan ek woman officer sabse zyada farq daal sakti hai. Pati ko report karne wali patni ho ya chacha-mama ko report karne wali bhatiji-bhanji, station par dikhne wala pehla chehra tay karta hai ki woh bolegi bhi ya nahi.

NCRB khud warn karta hai ki women help desks jaise steps se registered crime ke numbers badh sakte hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Desk khulne ke baad numbers badhein, toh ho sakta hai desk bas apna kaam kar raha ho, jaisa rape ke badhte numbers par hamara myth-buster samjhata hai.

Yeh rules women ke liye likhe gaye hain. Men aur transgender survivors inke daayre se bahar hain, aur unhe bhi aisa officer milna chahiye jo bina mazaak udaaye unki baat sune.

## Jab duty par koi woman na ho, toh kya maangein

Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

- **Maangiye ki likhne wali ek woman ho.** Sexual offence report karne wali woman ke liye Section 173 mein "agar ho sake" nahi likha. Women help desk ke baare mein poochiye.
- **Lautaye jaane ko accept mat kijiye.** Jo officer rape ya sexual assault ki FIR record nahi karta, use Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ki Section 199 ke tahat chhe mahine se do saal tak ki rigorous imprisonment ho sakti hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].
- **Jagah aap chuniye.** Maangiye ki statement ghar par ya wahan record ho jahan aap safe mehsoos karti hain.
- **Magistrate ke saamne**, woman magistrate maangiye, ya phir yeh ki ek woman wahan maujood rahe.
- **Trial mein**, apne lawyer ya public prosecutor se kahiye ki woh woman judge ki request karein.

One Stop Centres violence jhel rahi women ko ek hi chhat ke neeche support dete hain; July 2026 mein 1,033 approved centres mein se 985 chal rahe the [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-07]]. Emergency mein 112 par ya Women Helpline par call kijiye.

women-safety-public-space-myths.en:
Ask an Indian family how to keep a daughter safe and the rules come quickly: be home by seven, don't take the bus, share your live location. Ask a government and the answer is usually a camera. Both assume that the danger is a stranger in a public place, and that the fix is to watch women or to keep them away from it. Here are five of the commonest beliefs about women's safety in public, checked against the data and the law.

## Myth 1: 'Cameras make a city safe'

Surveillance is where the announcements go. Delivery is another matter. According to a Rajya Sabha reply reported in July 2026, a Nirbhaya Fund pilot to put AI-based facial recognition at seven railway stations was listed as "ongoing" with zero spending. So was a programme to sensitise men on women's issues through panchayats. A proposal for CCTV cameras at village panchayats was still awaiting financial approval [[theprint-nirbhaya-fund-rajya-sabha-2026]].

The fund's Safe City projects had received Rs 1,686.73 crore by July 2026, all of it for eight cities [[theprint-nirbhaya-fund-rajya-sabha-2026]]. A woman in a small town or a village is not on that map.

**Truth:** A camera can help identify a man after a woman complains. It cannot make an officer write her complaint down, and it does not look inside a home, a classroom or a phone. The programme meant to change men's behaviour had the same record as the facial-recognition pilot: nothing spent.

## Myth 2: 'If harassment were common, the police numbers would show it'

In 2005 the India Human Development Survey asked households directly. 12% said unmarried girls in their neighbourhood were "sometimes" or "often" harassed. NCRB's records implied 0.06% of households, a gap of about 200 times [[aej-iyer-political-voice-2012]].

That comparison is old. The newer police numbers are still tiny. In all of 2024, police across India registered 459 cases of sexual harassment in public transport, and Delhi registered 18. A new category for harassment at public places and pathways recorded 1,469 cases in the whole country in the second half of 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Imagine a 19-year-old in Indore who is touched without her consent on a crowded city bus. To enter the statistics she must give up a day of college, find a police station, be believed and get an FIR registered. Many women in her place go to class instead. Silence is the norm even for graver violence: in NFHS-5, 77.2% of women who had faced physical or sexual violence had never sought help or told anyone [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

**Truth:** Police numbers count the complaints that were written down. A low number can mean a safe street or a silent one, and the survey evidence points to silence.

## Myth 3: 'It's only eve teasing'

The phrase makes a crime sound like flirting. The Supreme Court's 2023 Handbook on Combating Gender Stereotypes tells judges to stop writing "eve teasing" and write "street sexual harassment". The same glossary replaces "provocative clothing" with simply "clothing" [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

The law already treats it as a crime. Under the BNS, sexual harassment carries up to three years in prison, sexually coloured remarks up to one year, stalking up to three years on a first conviction, and words or gestures meant to insult a woman's modesty up to three years [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. These sections are written around a man harassing a woman, so men and transgender people harassed in public have thinner cover here. This is general information, not legal advice.

**Truth:** When a family says "ignore it, it's just teasing", the girl is being asked to absorb a crime so that nobody else has to act. The cost lands on her: a changed route, a dropped coaching class, an earlier curfew. The man's evening stays the same.

## Myth 4: 'Keeping women at home keeps them safe'

Home is where the numbers are largest. In NFHS-5, 29.3% of ever-married women aged 18-49 reported physical or sexual violence by a husband [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. In police data, the offender was known to the victim in 96.8% of rape cases registered in 2024: 28,597 of 29,536 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

**Truth:** A curfew guards against the stranger on the road, who is the rarer threat in these figures, and does nothing about the commoner one. It can also cost a woman the things that help her leave a violent home: her own income, her friends, a city she knows how to cross.

## Myth 5: 'She can just take an auto'

This is the modern curfew: go out, but buy your own safety. A World Bank survey in Mumbai in 2019 shows who pays. As public transport worsened, women shifted to auto-rickshaws and taxis, which cost more. The report calls this a "pink tax" on women's mobility [[worldbank-mumbai-gender-transport-2021]]. A domestic worker or a first-year student cannot pay that tax twice a day, so the advice protects only women who already have money.

The same survey tests another assumption: that fear of the road is what mainly keeps women out of jobs. Of 2,388 non-working women, 31% said commuting was a barrier to working, mostly because of domestic duties (19%) and childcare (13%). Only 1.6% named unsafe commuting [[worldbank-mumbai-gender-transport-2021]]. Mumbai is seen as one of India's safer cities, so safety may weigh more elsewhere.

**Truth:** Private transport is a fee charged to women for a public failure. And among the women who called commuting a barrier, the usual reason was not danger on the road. It was the unpaid work waiting at home.

Put the five checks together and safety stops looking like a camera and a curfew. It looks like buses and trains that women can afford and rely on; a police station where a harassment complaint is written down by a woman officer, as the BNSS requires [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]; and families that call harassment a crime and ask the man to change. It also means giving violence inside homes the attention the street already gets.
women-safety-public-space-myths.hg:
Kisi Indian family se poochhiye ki beti ko safe kaise rakhein, toh rules turant aa jaate hain: saat baje tak ghar aa jao, bus mat lo, live location share karo. Sarkar se poochhiye, toh jawaab aksar ek camera hota hai. Dono yeh maan kar chalte hain ki khatra public jagah par khada koi anjaan aadmi hai, aur ilaaj yeh hai ki aurton par nazar rakhi jaaye ya unhe wahan se door rakha jaaye. Yahan public mein aurton ki safety ke baare mein paanch sabse aam beliefs hain, data aur kaanoon ke saamne rakh kar check kiye gaye.

## Myth 1: 'Cameras se sheher safe ho jaata hai'

Elaan surveillance ke hote hain. Zameen par kaam hona alag baat hai. July 2026 mein report hue ek Rajya Sabha reply ke mutaabiq, saat railway stations par AI-based facial recognition lagaane ka Nirbhaya Fund ka pilot "ongoing" likha tha, aur us par kharch zero tha. Panchayaton ke zariye mardon ko aurton ke muddon par sensitise karne wale programme ka bhi yahi haal tha. Gaon ki panchayaton mein CCTV cameras lagaane ka proposal abhi tak financial approval ka intezaar kar raha tha [[theprint-nirbhaya-fund-rajya-sabha-2026]].

Fund ke Safe City projects ko July 2026 tak Rs 1,686.73 crore mil chuke the, aur yeh saara paisa aath shehron ke liye tha [[theprint-nirbhaya-fund-rajya-sabha-2026]]. Kisi chhote kasbe ya gaon ki aurat us naqshe par hai hi nahi.

**Sach:** Camera kisi aurat ki complaint ke baad aadmi ko pehchaanne mein madad kar sakta hai. Woh kisi officer se uski complaint nahi likhwa sakta, aur woh ghar, classroom ya phone ke andar nahi dekhta. Mardon ka bartaav badalne wale programme ka record bhi facial-recognition pilot jaisa hi nikla: kharch kuch nahi.

## Myth 2: 'Agar harassment itna aam hota, toh police ke numbers mein dikhta'

2005 mein India Human Development Survey ne seedhe households se poochha. 12% ne kaha ki unke mohalle mein unmarried ladkiyon ko "sometimes" ya "often" harass kiya jaata hai. NCRB ke records ke hisaab se yeh 0.06% households banta tha, yaani qareeb 200 guna ka farq [[aej-iyer-political-voice-2012]].

Yeh tulna purani hai. Lekin police ke naye numbers bhi bahut chhote hain. Poore 2024 mein poore India ki police ne public transport mein sexual harassment ke 459 case darj kiye, aur Delhi ne 18. Public places aur raaston par harassment ki ek nayi category mein 2024 ke doosre half mein poore desh se 1,469 case aaye [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Sochiye, Indore ki ek 19 saal ki ladki ko bheed bhari city bus mein uski marzi ke bina chhua jaata hai. Statistics mein aane ke liye use college ka ek din chhodna hoga, police station dhoondhna hoga, apni baat par yaqeen dilwana hoga aur FIR darj karwani hogi. Uski jagah bahut si aurtein seedhe class chali jaati hain. Chuppi toh isse zyada gambhir violence mein bhi aam hai: NFHS-5 mein physical ya sexual violence jhel chuki 77.2% aurton ne kabhi madad nahi maangi thi aur kisi ko bataya bhi nahi tha [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

**Sach:** Police ke numbers un complaints ko ginte hain jo likhi gayi. Chhote number ka matlab safe sadak bhi ho sakta hai aur chup sadak bhi, aur surveys ka saboot chuppi ki taraf ishaara karta hai.

## Myth 3: 'Yeh toh bas eve teasing hai'

Yeh phrase ek crime ko flirting jaisa bana deta hai. Supreme Court ki 2023 ki Handbook on Combating Gender Stereotypes judges se kehti hai ki "eve teasing" likhna band karein aur "street sexual harassment" likhein. Wahi glossary "provocative clothing" ki jagah sirf "clothing" likhne ko kehti hai [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

Kaanoon ise pehle se crime maanta hai. BNS ke tahat sexual harassment par teen saal tak ki jail hai, sexually coloured remarks par ek saal tak, stalking par pehli conviction mein teen saal tak, aur aurat ki modesty ka apmaan karne wale shabdon ya gestures par teen saal tak [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Yeh sections is tarah likhe gaye hain ki ek mard ek aurat ko harass kar raha hai, isliye public mein harass hone wale mardon aur transgender logon ke liye yahan suraksha kamzor hai. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

**Sach:** Jab family kehti hai "ignore karo, bas teasing hai", toh ladki se kaha ja raha hota hai ki woh ek crime ko chup-chaap seh le, taaki kisi aur ko kuch karna na pade. Qeemat wahi chukaati hai: badla hua raasta, chhooti hui coaching class, aur jaldi wala curfew. Us aadmi ki shaam waisi ki waisi rehti hai.

## Myth 4: 'Aurton ko ghar par rakhne se woh safe rehti hain'

Sabse bade numbers ghar ke hi hain. NFHS-5 mein 18-49 saal ki 29.3% ever-married aurton ne pati ki taraf se physical ya sexual violence report ki [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Police data mein, 2024 mein darj rape cases mein se 96.8% mein offender victim ka jaan-pehchaan wala tha: 29,536 mein se 28,597 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

**Sach:** Curfew sadak ke anjaan aadmi se bachata hai, jo in figures mein kam milne wala khatra hai, aur zyada aam khatre ka kuch nahi karta. Woh aurat se woh cheezein bhi chheen sakta hai jo use ek violent ghar se nikalne mein madad karti hain: apni kamaai, apne dost, aur ek aisa sheher jise woh akele paar karna jaanti hai.

## Myth 5: 'Woh auto le le na'

Yeh aaj ke zamaane ka curfew hai: bahar jao, lekin apni safety khud khareedo. World Bank ka 2019 ka Mumbai survey dikhata hai ki iski qeemat kaun chukaata hai. Jaise-jaise public transport ki haalat bigdi, aurtein auto-rickshaw aur taxi ki taraf gayi, jo zyada mehange padte hain. Report ise aurton ki mobility par "pink tax" kehti hai [[worldbank-mumbai-gender-transport-2021]]. Koi domestic worker ya first-year student yeh tax din mein do baar nahi bhar sakti, isliye yeh salaah sirf un aurton ko bachaati hai jinke paas pehle se paisa hai.

Wahi survey ek aur maanyata ko parakhta hai: ki aurton ko naukri se door rakhne wali sabse badi cheez sadak ka darr hai. 2,388 non-working aurton mein se 31% ne kaha ki commuting kaam karne mein rukaavat hai, aur zyada tar ne wajah ghar ke kaam (19%) aur childcare (13%) batayi. Sirf 1.6% ne unsafe commuting ka naam liya [[worldbank-mumbai-gender-transport-2021]]. Mumbai ko India ke zyada safe shehron mein gina jaata hai, isliye ho sakta hai doosri jagah safety ka wazan zyada ho.

**Sach:** Private transport ek aisi fees hai jo ek public naakaami ke liye aurton se wasooli jaati hai. Aur jin aurton ne commuting ko rukaavat bataya, unke liye aam wajah sadak ka khatra nahi tha. Wajah thi ghar par intezaar karta unpaid kaam.

In paanchon checks ko saath rakhiye, toh safety camera aur curfew jaisi dikhna band ho jaati hai. Woh aisi buses aur trains jaisi dikhti hai jinka kiraaya aurtein de sakein aur jin par bharosa kar sakein; aise police station jaisi jahan harassment ki complaint mahila officer likhe, jaisa BNSS kehta hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]; aur aisi families jaisi jo harassment ko crime kahein aur aadmi se badalne ko kahein. Iska matlab yeh bhi hai ki ghar ke andar ki violence par utna hi dhyaan diya jaaye jitna sadak ko pehle se milta hai.

women-work-harassment-by-the-numbers.en:
In 2017-18, 23.3% of Indian women aged 15 and above were in the labour force. In 2023-24 the figure was 41.7% [[mospi-plfs-annual-2023-24]]. It is the number quoted to show that Indian women are, at last, going out to work.

The same survey holds other numbers that complicate the story, and the law on sexual harassment at work reaches only some of these women in practice. Read together, they show whom the law can reach, whom it cannot, and what harassment costs.

## 23.3% to 41.7%: the rise

The Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) puts the female labour force participation rate at 23.3% in 2017-18, 24.5% in 2018-19, 30.0% in 2019-20, 32.5% in 2020-21, 32.8% in 2021-22, 37.0% in 2022-23 and 41.7% in 2023-24. For men it was 78.8% in 2023-24 [[mospi-plfs-annual-2023-24]].

The measure is "usual status", which counts a woman who did even subsidiary work in the year, including unpaid help in a family enterprise. On the survey's "current weekly status" measure, the female rate in 2023-24 was 35.6% [[mospi-plfs-annual-2023-24]]. And after six years of rise, the rate for men is still nearly twice the rate for women.

## 28.0% in the cities

| Women aged 15+ in the labour force | 2017-18 | 2023-24 |
|---|---|---|
| Rural | 24.6% | 47.6% |
| Urban | 20.4% | 28.0% |
| All India | 23.3% | 41.7% |

The rural rate nearly doubled. The urban rate moved from 20.4% to 28.0% [[mospi-plfs-annual-2023-24]]. Cities are where the salaried jobs, the offices, the long commutes and the Internal Committees are, and there fewer than three in ten women are in the labour force.

Is it fear? Not in any simple way. A 2019 World Bank survey in Mumbai found that 31% of 2,388 non-working women called commuting a barrier to working, mostly because of domestic duties (19%) and childcare (13%). Only 1.6% named unsafe commuting. But as public transport worsened, women shifted to costlier auto-rickshaws and taxis, a "pink tax" on their mobility [[worldbank-mumbai-gender-transport-2021]]. Safety does not always show up in a survey as fear. Sometimes it shows up as a fare. This is one city, and one seen as among India's safer ones for women.

## Self-employed and unsalaried

In 2023-24, 73.5% of rural women workers were self-employed and just 7.8% had regular salaried jobs [[mospi-plfs-annual-2023-24]]. A newer quarterly figure, measured differently, points the same way: in July-September 2025 only 10.8% of employed rural women held regular wage or salaried jobs, while 37.5% were own-account workers or employers and 34.2% were helpers in household enterprises [[es-2025-26-employment-chapter]].

Imagine one of those helpers: a woman at the counter of her in-laws' shop, harassed by a relative who runs it or a supplier who visits every week. There is no HR department, no colleague to sit on a committee, often no wage to lose because there was never a wage.

On paper the law has an answer. The Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013 (the POSH Act) tells each district's District Officer to set up a Local Committee for workplaces with fewer than ten workers, or where the complaint is against the employer, and its definition of a workplace reaches as far as "a dwelling place or a house" [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. But affidavits before the Supreme Court in May 2025 left Local Committee compliance unclear in Delhi, Haryana, Jharkhand and Kerala [[sc-posh-order-2025-05-21]].

## 2.0 points, or 4.2: what harassment costs

In 2017 the International Labour Office estimated how far particular barriers lower a woman's probability of taking part in the labour market. In low-income countries, abuse, harassment or discrimination at work lowers it by 4.2 percentage points, and limited access to safe transport by 16.5 points. For middle-income countries, the group that includes India, its estimates were 2.0 and 5.7 points [[ilo-weso-trends-women-2017]].

The 4.2 figure is the one that travels, under the label "developing countries". In the ILO's grouping it is not India's number; 2.0 is. Both are cross-country estimates from survey data, not Indian measurements [[ilo-weso-trends-women-2017]].

Two points is still a lot where 28.0% of urban women are in the labour force. And no estimate captures the woman who had a job and left it. The Supreme Court observed in 2023 that women harassed at work are often reluctant to report, and "many of them even drop out from their job" [[sc-aureliano-fernandes-2023]]. In the participation rate she is simply one fewer woman. The rate does not record why.

Police data cannot fill the gap. In 2024 police registered 388 cases of sexual harassment at office premises in all of India, and 512 at other work premises such as shops, malls, factories and homes in the second half of the year, when that category began [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Most workplace complaints go to Internal Committees, a civil process, and never become FIRs.

## Where the law reaches, and where it does not

The POSH Act requires every employer with ten or more workers at an office or branch to constitute an Internal Complaints Committee headed by a senior woman, with an external member, and protects any woman "of any age whether employed or not" at a workplace [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. It covers women only; for men and transgender workers, a committee route depends on the employer's own policy. That design fits an office with a payroll, the kind of job that fewer than one in ten rural women workers had in 2023-24.

Even there, enforcement is thin. On 12 May 2023 the Supreme Court found "serious lapses in the enforcement" of the Act a decade after it was passed [[sc-aureliano-fernandes-2023]]. In December 2024 it ordered a survey of Internal Committees in private as well as government institutions; by August 2025 it was told that only the Andaman and Nicobar Islands had completed one [[livelaw-posh-district-survey-2025]].

> "If the authorities/managements/employers cannot assure them a safe and secure work place, they will fear stepping out of their homes to make a dignified living" (Supreme Court, 2023)

By early 2026 around 22 states and union territories allowed women to work night shifts in factories, and 33 in commercial establishments [[es-2025-26-employment-chapter]]. Every new shift is a workplace that needs a committee its workers can find.

If you work for someone, in an office, a shop, a factory or a home, find out now who your Internal Committee is, or where your district's Local Committee sits; a written complaint is due within three months of an incident [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. If you employ people, set the committee up and tell them who is on it. And the next time 41.7% appears in a headline, ask where those women work. This is general information, not legal advice.
women-work-harassment-by-the-numbers.hg:
2017-18 mein 15 saal aur usse upar ki 23.3% Indian women labour force mein thi. 2023-24 mein yeh figure 41.7% tha [[mospi-plfs-annual-2023-24]]. Yeh dikhane ke liye ki Indian women aakhirkaar ghar se bahar kaam par nikal rahi hain, yahi number quote hota hai.

Usi survey mein kuch aur numbers bhi hain jo is kahani ko itna seedha nahi rehne dete, aur kaam ki jagah par sexual harassment ka law asal mein in mein se kuch hi women tak pahunchta hai. Saath rakh kar padho toh dikhta hai ki law kis tak pahunch sakta hai, kis tak nahi, aur harassment ki keemat kya hai.

## 23.3% se 41.7%: badhat

Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) ke hisaab se female labour force participation rate 2017-18 mein 23.3% tha, 2018-19 mein 24.5%, 2019-20 mein 30.0%, 2020-21 mein 32.5%, 2021-22 mein 32.8%, 2022-23 mein 37.0% aur 2023-24 mein 41.7%. Men ke liye yeh 2023-24 mein 78.8% tha [[mospi-plfs-annual-2023-24]].

Yeh measure "usual status" hai, jo us woman ko bhi ginta hai jisne saal mein thoda-sa subsidiary kaam bhi kiya ho, family enterprise mein bina paise ki madad bhi. Survey ke "current weekly status" measure par 2023-24 mein female rate 35.6% tha [[mospi-plfs-annual-2023-24]]. Aur chhah saal ki badhat ke baad bhi men ka rate women ke rate ka lagbhag double hai.

## Shehron mein 28.0%

| Labour force mein 15+ women | 2017-18 | 2023-24 |
|---|---|---|
| Rural | 24.6% | 47.6% |
| Urban | 20.4% | 28.0% |
| All India | 23.3% | 41.7% |

Rural rate lagbhag double ho gaya. Urban rate 20.4% se 28.0% tak pahuncha [[mospi-plfs-annual-2023-24]]. Salaried jobs, offices, lambe commutes aur Internal Committees shehron mein hi hain, aur wahin das mein se teen se bhi kam women labour force mein hain.

Kya wajah darr hai? Itna seedha nahi. 2019 mein World Bank ke Mumbai survey mein 2,388 non-working women mein se 31% ne kaha ki commuting kaam karne mein rukawat hai, zyada tar gharelu zimmedariyon (19%) aur childcare (13%) ki wajah se. Sirf 1.6% ne unsafe commuting ka naam liya. Lekin jaise-jaise public transport kharab hua, women mehange auto-rickshaws aur taxis ki taraf shift hui, yaani unki mobility par ek "pink tax" [[worldbank-mumbai-gender-transport-2021]]. Safety survey mein hamesha darr ban kar nahi dikhti. Kabhi-kabhi woh kiraye ke roop mein dikhti hai. Yeh sirf ek shehar hai, aur aisa shehar jise women ke liye India ke zyada safe shehron mein gina jaata hai.

## Self-employed aur bina salary ke

2023-24 mein 73.5% rural women workers self-employed thi, aur sirf 7.8% ke paas regular salaried job thi [[mospi-plfs-annual-2023-24]]. Ek naya quarterly figure, jo alag tareeke se measure hota hai, isi taraf ishara karta hai: July-September 2025 mein sirf 10.8% employed rural women ke paas regular wage ya salaried job thi, jabki 37.5% own-account workers ya employers thi aur 34.2% household enterprises mein helpers thi [[es-2025-26-employment-chapter]].

Socho, un helpers mein se ek: apne sasural ki dukaan ke counter par baithi ek woman, jise dukaan chalane wala koi rishtedar ya har hafte aane wala supplier harass karta hai. Wahan na HR department hai, na koi colleague jo committee mein baithe, aur aksar khone ke liye salary bhi nahi, kyunki salary kabhi thi hi nahi.

Kaagaz par law ke paas jawab hai. Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013 (POSH Act) har district ke District Officer se kehta hai ki un workplaces ke liye Local Committee banao jahan das se kam workers hain ya jahan complaint employer ke hi khilaf hai, aur uski workplace ki definition "a dwelling place or a house", yaani ghar tak pahunchti hai [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Lekin May 2025 mein Supreme Court ke saamne aaye affidavits se Delhi, Haryana, Jharkhand aur Kerala mein Local Committee ka compliance saaf nahi hua [[sc-posh-order-2025-05-21]].

## 2.0 points, ya 4.2: harassment ki keemat

2017 mein International Labour Office ne estimate kiya ki alag-alag rukawatein ek woman ke labour market mein hissa lene ki probability kitni ghatati hain. Low-income countries mein kaam par abuse, harassment ya discrimination ise 4.2 percentage points ghatata hai, aur safe transport tak limited access 16.5 points. Middle-income countries ke liye, jis group mein India aata hai, uske estimates 2.0 aur 5.7 points the [[ilo-weso-trends-women-2017]].

Charcha mein zyada tar 4.2 wala figure hi chalta hai, "developing countries" ke label ke saath. ILO ki grouping mein woh India ka number nahi hai; India ka number 2.0 hai. Dono hi survey data se nikle cross-country estimates hain, India ke apne measurements nahi [[ilo-weso-trends-women-2017]].

Jahan sirf 28.0% urban women labour force mein hain, wahan do points bhi bahut hain. Aur koi estimate us woman ko nahi pakadta jiske paas job thi aur usne chhod di. Supreme Court ne 2023 mein kaha tha ki kaam par harassment jhelne wali women aksar report karne se hichkichati hain, aur "many of them even drop out from their job", yaani kai toh job hi chhod deti hain [[sc-aureliano-fernandes-2023]]. Participation rate mein woh bas ek kam woman ban jaati hai. Rate yeh record nahi karta ki kyun.

Police data yeh gap nahi bhar sakta. 2024 mein police ne poore India mein office premises par sexual harassment ke 388 cases register kiye, aur doosre work premises jaise shops, malls, factories aur gharon par 512 cases, woh bhi saal ke doosre half mein, jab yeh category shuru hui [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Zyada tar workplace complaints Internal Committees ke paas jaati hain, jo ek civil process hai, aur kabhi FIR nahi banti.

## Law kahan tak pahunchta hai, aur kahan nahi

POSH Act har us employer se, jiske office ya branch mein das ya usse zyada workers hain, kehta hai ki Internal Complaints Committee banao, jiski head ek senior woman ho aur jismein ek external member ho, aur woh workplace par har us aurat ko protect karta hai jo "of any age whether employed or not" ho, yaani kisi bhi umar ki, chahe employed ho ya nahi [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Yeh Act sirf women ko cover karta hai; men aur transgender workers ke liye committee ka rasta employer ki apni policy par depend karta hai. Yeh design payroll wale office par fit baithta hai, aur 2023-24 mein aisi job das mein se ek se bhi kam rural women workers ke paas thi.

Wahan bhi enforcement kamzor hai. 12 May 2023 ko Supreme Court ne paaya ki Act banne ke ek dashak baad bhi uske enforcement mein "serious lapses" hain [[sc-aureliano-fernandes-2023]]. December 2024 mein Court ne private aur government, dono tarah ke institutions mein Internal Committees ka survey karne ko kaha; August 2025 tak use bataya gaya ki sirf Andaman and Nicobar Islands ne survey poora kiya hai [[livelaw-posh-district-survey-2025]].

> "If the authorities/managements/employers cannot assure them a safe and secure work place, they will fear stepping out of their homes to make a dignified living" (Supreme Court, 2023). Yaani agar employers women ko safe workplace ka bharosa nahi de sakte, toh woh izzat ki kamai ke liye ghar se nikalne mein darengi.

Early 2026 tak lagbhag 22 states aur union territories ne women ko factories mein night shift karne ki ijazat de di thi, aur 33 ne commercial establishments mein [[es-2025-26-employment-chapter]]. Har nayi shift ek aisa workplace hai jise aisi committee chahiye jo uske workers ko mil sake.

Agar tum kisi ke liye kaam karti ho, office, shop, factory ya ghar mein, toh abhi pata karo ki tumhari Internal Committee mein kaun hai, ya tumhare district ki Local Committee kahan baithti hai; written complaint incident ke teen mahine ke andar deni hoti hai [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Agar tum logon ko kaam par rakhte ho, toh committee banao aur unhe batao ki usmein kaun hai. Aur agli baar jab headline mein 41.7% dikhe, toh poocho ki yeh women kaam kahan karti hain. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

youth-session-guide-peer-educators.en:
Many young Indians piece together what they know about sex from friends, phones and guesswork, and the gaps show. In 2019-21, 46% of women aged 15-49 did not know that HIV cannot spread through a mosquito bite, and 55% did not know it cannot spread by sharing food with a person who has AIDS [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. If you are a peer educator, an NSS volunteer or the person your college club asked for "a session on safety", this guide is for you.

## Why peers can say what adults won't

India's adolescent health programme, the Rashtriya Kishor Swasthya Karyakram (RKSK), launched on 7 January 2014 [[nhm-adolescent-health-rksk-page-2026]], is built on this idea. It plans four "Saathiya" peer educators, two boys and two girls, for every village or 1,000 people, each running a weekly one- to two-hour session for 15 to 20 adolescents [[nhm-peer-education-page-2026]].
